title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
皇明取士之制率三歲一舉於鄉正
德庚午適賓興之年維時廣東
藩臬重臣先事走聘才等俾司
文衡至期巡按御史王旻實監
臨之合提學副使李麟所簡士
一千五百有奇鎖院而三試焉
===
分房校藝務拔殊尤於其文之
明徹純粹者取焉渾雄雋拔者
取焉宏博中正者取焉深茂典
雅者取焉其贍而不蕪平而不
弱豪縱而不揚簡質而有體者
亦取焉凡得士七十有五人爰
列其名第并彙所著文爲鄉試
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

皇明取士之制，率三歲一舉於鄉。正德庚午，適賓興之年。維時廣東藩臬重臣，先事走聘才等，俾司文衡。至期，巡按御史王旻實監臨之，合提學副使李麟所簡士一千五百有奇，鎖院而三試焉。分房校藝，務拔殊尤。於其文之明徹純粹者取焉，渾雄雋拔者取焉，宏博中正者取焉，深茂典雅者取焉。其贍而不蕪、平而不弱、豪縱而不揚、簡質而有體者，亦取焉。凡得士七十有五人，爰列其名第，并彙所著文爲鄉試
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Under the illustrious Ming dynasty’s system for recruiting officials, a Provincial Examination is generally held every three years. The gengwu year of the Zhengde reign [1510] duly fell in a year for recommending worthy men. At that time, the senior officials of Guangdong’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions sent invitations in advance to myself, Cai 才, and my colleagues, charging us with judging the examination writings. When the appointed time arrived, Regional Inspector Wang Min 王旻 served as Supervising Official. More than fifteen hundred candidates selected by Li Lin 李麟, Vice Surveillance Commissioner in charge of education, were assembled, and the examination compound was locked for the three examination sessions.

The examiners assessed the writings in separate groups, striving to select those of outstanding merit. We accepted compositions that were lucid and pure; those that were forceful, accomplished, and distinguished; those that were broad in learning, balanced, and correct; and those that were profound, rich, classically grounded, and elegant. We also accepted those that were ample without being overgrown, plain without being weak, bold and free without being ostentatious, and concise and unadorned while maintaining proper form. In all, seventy-five men were selected. We then listed their names and ranks and collected their compositions to form the Provincial Examination…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
錄以
獻甚盛典也於乎廣東逺落荒裔
而一時詞華之盛廼克間邁中
邦何哉詎非總督都御史林廷
選廓靖方維使庠序樂於教育
歟總鎮太監潘忠提督市舶太
監畢真總兵東寧伯焦淇崇重
===
儒紳致舒翹揚英之有加歟監
察御史郁侃劉祥江萬實鮮冕
奉公是邦風紀丕振有以起末
學之嚮往歟抑經理于內若右
參議王秩李希顏副使鄭岳僉
事江潮以及諸執事咸殫厥心
使文場筆札罔不罄其所長於
punctuated: 錄，以獻，甚盛典也。於乎！廣東逺落荒裔，而一時詞華之盛，廼克間邁中邦，何哉？詎非總督都御史林廷選廓靖方維，使庠序樂於教育歟？總鎮太監潘忠、提督市舶太監畢真、總兵東寧伯焦淇崇重儒紳，致舒翹揚英之有加歟？監察御史郁侃、劉祥、江萬實、鮮冕奉公是邦，風紀丕振，有以起末學之嚮往歟？抑經理于內，若右參議王秩、李希顏，副使鄭岳，僉事江潮，以及諸執事，咸殫厥心，使文場筆札罔不罄其所長於
translation_en: …a Record, to be presented to the throne: a most splendid observance indeed! Ah! Guangdong lies far away on the uncultivated fringes, yet the brilliance of its literary achievement at this moment can sometimes surpass that of the central regions. Why is this? Is it not because Lin Tingxuan, Supreme Commander and Censor-in-Chief, has brought peace throughout the region, allowing the schools to delight in teaching and nurturing their students? Is it because Pan Zhong, the eunuch Grand Defender; Bi Zhen, the eunuch Superintendent of Maritime Trade; and Jiao Qi, Earl of Dongning and Regional Commander, have honored the Confucian gentry, further enabling outstanding talent to unfold and flourish? Is it because the Investigating Censors Yu Kan, Liu Xiang, Jiang Wanshi, and Xian Mian have served the public interest in this province, greatly strengthening official discipline and thereby inspiring the aspirations of junior scholars? Or is it because those managing affairs within the examination compound—such as Wang Zhi and Li Xiyan, Assistant Administration Commissioners of the Right; Zheng Yue, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Jiang Chao, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and all the other functionaries—have devoted their utmost care, enabling every candidate writing in the examination hall to exercise his abilities to the full at…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一日歟防範于外若左布政使
李思明按察使任漢左參政羅
榮右參政鄒虞副使詹璽左參
議翁茂南右參議董鉦僉事李
瑾夏璲趙繼宗譏察周詳絕乘
凌蔽欺之弊而締構靡怠心留
念歟是雖所司有輕重詳略之
===
殊其爲人才之助則一爾然予
猶以爲未焉粤自應聘而來度
庾關抵韶廣旁觀聳視第見竒
峯疊嶂卷阿大阜蜿蜒迤邐如
鳥獸之騰舞巀嶭孤撑蓊鬱蒼
翠若雲矗而氣浮則夫扶輿磅
礴之所鍾殆非紛葩瑰麗之物
punctuated:
一日歟？防範于外，若左布政使李思明、按察使任漢、左參政羅榮、右參政鄒虞、副使詹璽、左參議翁茂南、右參議董鉦、僉事李瑾、夏璲、趙繼宗，譏察周詳，絕乘凌蔽欺之弊，而締構靡怠心留念歟？是雖所司有輕重詳略之殊，其爲人才之助則一爾。
然予猶以爲未焉。粤自應聘而來，度庾關，抵韶廣，旁觀聳視，第見竒峯疊嶂、卷阿大阜，蜿蜒迤邐，如鳥獸之騰舞；巀嶭孤撑，蓊鬱蒼翠，若雲矗而氣浮。則夫扶輿磅礴之所鍾，殆非紛葩瑰麗之物
translation_en:
… in a single day? As for precautions outside the examination compound, there were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Siming, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Ren Han, Left Provincial Vice Administration Commissioner Luo Rong, Right Provincial Vice Administration Commissioner Zou Yu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhan Xi, Left Provincial Assistant Administration Commissioner Weng Maonan, Right Provincial Assistant Administration Commissioner Dong Zheng, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Li Jin, Xia Sui, and Zhao Jizong. Were they not thorough and meticulous in their inspections, eliminating abuses of encroachment, intimidation, concealment, and deception, and tireless in making arrangements and keeping these matters in mind [?]? Although their respective responsibilities differed in importance and in the detail of their involvement, their contribution to fostering talent was the same.
Yet I still consider this insufficient. Since coming in response to the invitation, I have crossed Yu Pass and reached Shaozhou and Guangzhou. Looking about and gazing upward, I have seen extraordinary peaks and overlapping ridges, winding hillsides and great mounds, twisting and extending like birds and beasts leaping and dancing. Lofty, precipitous heights stand alone, luxuriant and verdant, like towering clouds and floating vapors. Surely that in which these vast, all-pervading energies of the earth concentrate cannot be merely things of luxuriant bloom and magnificent beauty …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得而獨當也其壤地之廣輪聚
落畦塍動亘數百里而浮嵐秀
水率映照上下城郭里市雖涉
喧囂而其間陂池林麓亦罔不
可亭可廬則夫玩心觀理有不
待入中條傍月泉然後得而靜
專也其川流之委會滇湟東注
===
呀呷溯湃飛湍激淙瞬息數十
里巨溟南匯波濤日夕盪潏而
魚龍神恠倏隱見飇突則又有
不待望五湖闚洛汭而後可以
發其豪懷藻思者矧荷
祖宗治化涵煦之久
今上政教漸被之深猶嘉木美箭培
punctuated: 得而獨當也。其壤地之廣輪，聚落畦塍，動亘數百里，而浮嵐秀水率映照上下。城郭里市雖涉喧囂，而其間陂池林麓亦罔不可亭可廬，則夫玩心觀理，有不待入中條、傍月泉，然後得而靜專也。其川流之委會，滇湟東注，呀呷溯湃，飛湍激淙，瞬息數十里；巨溟南匯，波濤日夕盪潏，而魚龍神恠倏隱見、飇突，則又有不待望五湖、闚洛汭，而後可以發其豪懷藻思者。矧荷祖宗治化涵煦之久，今上政教漸被之深，猶嘉木美箭培
translation_en: …could alone lay claim to it. Across the breadth and length of this land, settlements, fields, and their embankments commonly extend for hundreds of li, while drifting mountain mists and beautiful waters mirror one another above and below. Although the walled towns and neighborhood markets are bustling and noisy, the ponds, woods, and wooded foothills among them all offer places for pavilions and dwellings. Thus, to nurture the mind and contemplate principle, one need not enter the Zhongtiao Mountains or settle beside Yuequan before attaining tranquillity and concentration. Its rivers gather and converge; the Dian and Huang [?] pour eastward, roaring and surging, with flying rapids and crashing torrents covering tens of li in an instant. The vast sea receives them to the south, its waves heaving day and night, while fish, dragons, spirits, and strange creatures suddenly appear and disappear, darting forth like whirlwinds. Here, too, one need not gaze upon the Five Lakes or peer at the bend of the Luo River before stirring lofty feelings and ornate literary thoughts. Moreover, this land has long enjoyed the nurturing influence of the imperial ancestors’ civilizing rule and has been deeply imbued with the governance and instruction of His present Majesty, like fine trees and excellent arrow bamboo being cultivated…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
植不置枝幹固碩茂而杪末尤
曄暢敷華者嶺服之地為然也
夫若是如之何其不郁郁乎迥
邁疇昔也哉雖然蛟龍騰翥徧
雨八荒騏驥就駕一日千里諸
士登薦鄉書部
廷之進有階而嚮用且有日顧可
===
泥尋常効圭撮而已耶大而經
世宰物康國寧民次而典司曹
局循良州邑要皆自其所以盛
者舉而措之可也是不惟上荅
聖朝作養之恩下彰主司知人之鑑
而已嶺表山川土壤亦與有光
焉若舎此而他求則非予之所
punctuated: 植不置，枝幹固碩茂，而杪末尤曄暢敷華者，嶺服之地為然也。夫若是，如之何其不郁郁乎迥邁疇昔也哉！雖然，蛟龍騰翥，徧雨八荒；騏驥就駕，一日千里。諸士登薦鄉書，部廷之進有階，而嚮用且有日，顧可泥尋常、効圭撮而已耶？大而經世宰物，康國寧民；次而典司曹局，循良州邑。要皆自其所以盛者，舉而措之可也。是不惟上荅聖朝作養之恩，下彰主司知人之鑑而已，嶺表山川土壤亦與有光焉。若舎此而他求，則非予之所
translation_en:
…unceasingly cultivated, their branches and trunks are indeed stout and luxuriant, while their uppermost shoots flourish with particular brilliance and burst into flower: such is the land of Lingnan. This being so, how could its abundant flourishing fail to surpass former times by far!

Nevertheless, when dragons soar aloft, they rain upon all eight reaches of the world; when fine steeds are harnessed, they travel a thousand li in a day. You scholars have been entered in the provincial register of recommended candidates. You now have a stepping-stone toward advancement through the ministry and the court, and the day when your talents will be employed is approaching. Could you remain confined to the commonplace and offer only a trifling measure of service? At the highest level, you should order the world and govern its affairs, bring well-being to the state and peace to the people; at the next, you should oversee administrative offices and serve as conscientious, benevolent officials in prefectures and counties. In every case, you need only put into practice those qualities in which you excel. This will not merely repay the sagely dynasty’s kindness in nurturing you and demonstrate the presiding examiners’ discernment of talent: the mountains, rivers, and soil of Lingnan will also share in your glory. If you abandon this and seek elsewhere, that is not what I…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知矣諸士其敬念之哉
直隸常州府儒學教授劉才謹
序
punctuated:
知矣，諸士其敬念之哉！

直隸常州府儒學教授劉才謹序。
translation_en:
…understand. May you scholars bear this reverently in mind!

Preface respectfully written by Liu Cai, Professor of the Confucian School of Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:

punctuated:
正德五年廣東鄉試

監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史王昊〔汝欽，湖廣衡陽縣人，癸丑進士〕。

廣東等處承宣布政使司右參議李希顏〔原復，直隸華亭縣人，癸丑進士〕。

廣東等處提刑按察司副使鄭岳〔汝華，福建莆田縣人，癸丑進士〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事江潮〔大信，江西貴溪縣人，己未進士〕。

translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, Fifth Year of Zhengde (1510)

Supervising Official
Wang Hao, Investigating Censor on巡 inspection of Guangdong, courtesy name Ruqin, was a native of Hengyang County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the guichou year.

Proctors
Wang Zhi, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Xunbo, was a native of Kunshan County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.
Li Xiyan, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Huating County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Zheng Yue, Vice Surveillance Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Ruhua, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.
Jiang Chao, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Daxin, was a native of Guixi County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.

Examiners
Liu Cai, Professor at the Confucian School of Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Shangyong, was a native of Anfu County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.
He Qia, Instructor at the Confucian School of Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, courtesy name Yunren, was a native of Fuyang County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.

Associate Examiners
Min Yinfang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Deqing, was a native of Fuliang County, Jiangxi, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the jiyou year.
Jiang Wanyu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Qin'an County, Qinzhou Subprefecture, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi, courtesy name Rupu, was a native of Dazhu County, Sichuan, and a tribute student of the dingmao year.
Zhuang Wenxuan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Tonglu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Shusheng, was a native of Changle County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the yimao year.
Lin Kuan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Gao'an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Renliang, was a native of Huai'an County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the dingmao year.
Gu Qin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Bocheng, was a native of Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and a tribute student of the wuwu year.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
生財有大道生之者衆食之者寡爲之者
疾用之者舒則財恒足矣仁者以財發
身
君子喻於義
夏曰校殷曰序周曰庠學則三代共之皆
所以明人倫也人倫明於上小民親於
下
===
易
天且弗違而况於人乎
告公從以益志也
履信思乎順又以尚賢也是以自天祐之
吉无不利也
動萬物者莫疾乎雷撓萬物者莫疾乎風
燥萬物者莫熯乎火說萬物者莫說乎
澤潤萬物者莫潤乎水終萬物始萬物
者莫盛乎艮
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

生財有大道：生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒，則財恒足矣。仁者以財發身。

君子喻於義。

夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠，學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。

易

天且弗違，而况於人乎？

告公從，以益志也。

履信，思乎順，又以尚賢也。是以自天祐之，吉，无不利也。

動萬物者莫疾乎雷，撓萬物者莫疾乎風，燥萬物者莫熯乎火，說萬物者莫說乎澤，潤萬物者莫潤乎水，終萬物、始萬物者莫盛乎艮。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

There is a great way to produce wealth: let those who produce it be numerous and those who consume it few; let its production be swift and its expenditure slow. Then wealth will always be sufficient. The benevolent person uses wealth to develop his person.

The gentleman understands righteousness.

In the Xia dynasty they were called xiao; in the Yin, xu; and in the Zhou, xiang. As for xue, all three dynasties used that name. All these schools served to clarify human relationships. When human relationships are made clear above, the common people below are affectionate toward one another.

Book of Changes

Even Heaven does not oppose him; how much less would human beings do so?

“He reports to the duke, who follows his counsel”: this serves to advance his purpose.

He treads the path of trustworthiness, turns his thoughts toward compliance, and also honors the worthy. Thus Heaven itself blesses him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.

Of what sets the myriad things in motion, nothing is swifter than thunder. Of what stirs the myriad things, nothing is swifter than wind. Of what dries the myriad things, nothing is more drying than fire. Of what delights the myriad things, nothing is more delightful than the marsh. Of what moistens the myriad things, nothing is more moistening than water. Of what brings the myriad things to their end and gives them their beginning, nothing surpasses Gen, the Mountain trigram.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
侯以明之撻以□□書用識哉欲並生哉
四海之内咸仰朕德時乃風股肱惟人良
臣惟聖
曰雨曰暘曰燠曰寒曰風曰時
其作大邑其自時配皇天毖祀于上下其
自時中乂
詩
于以盛之維筐及筥于以湘之維錡及釡
===
南有嘉魚烝然汕汕君子有酒嘉賓式燕
以衎
江漢湯湯武夫洸洸經營四方告成于王
四方旣平王國庶定時靡有爭王心載
寧江漢之滸王命召虎式辟四方徹我
疆土匪疚匪棘王國來極于疆于理至
于南海王命召虎來旬來宣文武受命
召公維翰無曰予小子召公是似肇敏
戎公用錫爾祉釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣告
punctuated:
書
侯以明之，撻以□□，書用識哉，欲並生哉。
四海之内咸仰朕德，時乃風。股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。
曰雨，曰暘，曰燠，曰寒，曰風，曰時。
其作大邑，其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下，其自時中乂。

詩
于以盛之？維筐及筥。于以湘之？維錡及釡。
南有嘉魚，烝然汕汕。君子有酒，嘉賓式燕以衎。
江漢湯湯，武夫洸洸。經營四方，告成于王。四方旣平，王國庶定。時靡有爭，王心載寧。江漢之滸，王命召虎：「式辟四方，徹我疆土。匪疚匪棘，王國來極。于疆于理，至于南海。」王命召虎：「來旬來宣。文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣，告
translation_en:
Book of Documents
Use the archery targets to make their merits clear; use flogging to [two illegible characters]; use written records to preserve the account. The wish is that all may live.
All within the four seas look up to my virtue: this is owing to your influence. Arms and legs make a man complete; worthy ministers make a sage complete.
These are rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind, each arriving in its proper season.
Let him build a great city. From here let him worthily serve August Heaven, carefully offering sacrifices to the powers above and below; from here let him govern with due balance.

Book of Odes
In what shall we hold them? In square baskets and round baskets. In what shall we boil them? In tripod cauldrons and cooking pots.
In the south there are fine fish, swimming in shoals. The lord has wine; his honored guests feast and rejoice.
The Jiang and Han rivers flow mightily; the warriors are valiant. They bring order to the four quarters and report their success to the king. The four quarters are pacified; the royal realm is all but settled. There is no more contention, and the king’s heart is at peace. On the banks of the Jiang and Han, the king commands Shao Hu: “Open up the four quarters and define the boundaries of our lands. Cause neither suffering nor haste; let the royal realm be the center to which all turn. Mark out the boundaries and put the lands in order, reaching as far as the southern sea.” The king commands Shao Hu: “Come, make your rounds and proclaim my commands. When Wen and Wu received the Mandate, the Duke of Shao was their mainstay. Do not say, ‘I am but a young man’; emulate the Duke of Shao. Begin diligently upon your great service, and I shall bestow blessings upon you. I grant you a jade libation ladle and one vessel of fragrant black-millet wine, to make report …

text:

載戢干戈載櫜弓矢

漷東田及沂西田癸巳叔孫州仇仲孫

禮記
故唯聖人為知禮之不可以已也
灌以圭璋用玉氣也
樂者為同禮者為異同則相親異則相敬
樂勝則流禮勝則離合情飾貌者禮樂
之事也禮義立則貴賤等矣樂文同則
上下和矣好惡著則賢不肖別矣刑禁
punctuated:
于文人，錫山土田。于周受命，自召祖命。載戢干戈，載櫜弓矢。

春秋
荆人來聘，荘公二十三年。
盟于召陵，僖公四年。公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。諸侯遂救許，僖公六年。
大蒐于比蒲，昭公十一年。
季孫斯、叔孫州仇、仲孫何忌帥師伐邾，取漷東田及沂西田。癸巳，叔孫州仇、仲孫何忌及邾子盟于句繹，哀公二年。

禮記
故唯聖人為知禮之不可以已也。
灌以圭璋，用玉氣也。
樂者為同，禮者為異。同則相親，異則相敬。樂勝則流，禮勝則離。合情飾貌者，禮樂之事也。禮義立，則貴賤等矣；樂文同，則上下和矣；好惡著，則賢不肖別矣；刑禁
translation_en:
…to your cultured ancestor; mountains, lands, and fields are bestowed upon you. Receive the mandate at Zhou, continuing the mandate of your ancestor, the Duke of Shao. Then put away shields and dagger-axes, and place bows and arrows in their cases.

Spring and Autumn Annals
Men of Jing came on a diplomatic visit. Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang.
A covenant was concluded at Shaoling. Fourth year of Duke Xi. The duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng and besieging Xincheng. The assembled lords then went to the aid of Xu. Sixth year of Duke Xi.
A great hunt and military review was held at Bipu. Eleventh year of Duke Zhao.
Jisun Si, Shusun Zhouchou, and Zhongsun Heji led an army against Zhu, taking the lands east of the Huo River and west of the Yi River. On the guisi day, Shusun Zhouchou and Zhongsun Heji concluded a covenant with the Viscount of Zhu at Gouyi. Second year of Duke Ai.

Book of Rites
Thus only the sage understands that ritual cannot be dispensed with.
Libations are poured using gui and zhang jade implements, drawing upon the vital essence of jade.
Music creates unity; ritual establishes distinctions. Unity brings mutual affection; distinctions bring mutual respect. When music predominates, there is dissipation; when ritual predominates, there is estrangement. Harmonizing feelings and refining outward conduct are the functions of ritual and music. When ritual and righteousness are established, noble and lowly have their proper ranks. When musical forms are shared, superiors and inferiors are in harmony. When approval and disapproval are made clear, the worthy are distinguished from the unworthy. Punishments prohibit…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
暴爵舉賢則政均矣仁以愛之義以正
之如此則民治行矣
故君子與其使食浮於人也寧使人浮於
食
第貳場
論
聖人之道猶天然
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢勸農桑禁采黃金珠玉詔景帝後二年
===
擬唐加房玄齡太子少師誥貞觀十三年
擬宋以孔宜襲封文宣公謝表太平興國三年
判語五條
官吏給由
典買田宅
上書陳言
飛報軍情
辯明冤枉
第參場
punctuated:
暴，爵舉賢，則政均矣。仁以愛之，義以正之，如此則民治行矣。
故君子與其使食浮於人也，寧使人浮於食。
第貳場
論：聖人之道猶天然。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢勸農桑禁采黃金珠玉詔，景帝後二年。
擬唐加房玄齡太子少師誥，貞觀十三年。
擬宋以孔宜襲封文宣公謝表，太平興國三年。
判語五條：官吏給由；典買田宅；上書陳言；飛報軍情；辯明冤枉。
第參場
translation_en:
…violence, and ranks are used to advance the worthy, then government becomes equitable. Love them with benevolence and correct them with righteousness; in this way, the people are brought to order.
Thus the gentleman would rather have people exceed the food provided than have the food provided exceed the people’s worth.
Second Session
Discourse: “The Way of the Sage Is Like Heaven.”
One topic from among imperial edicts, imperial mandates, and memorials [?].
Compose an imperial edict in the manner of the Han dynasty encouraging agriculture and sericulture and prohibiting the extraction of gold, pearls, and jade: the second year of Emperor Jing’s latter reign period.
Compose an imperial mandate in the manner of the Tang dynasty conferring on Fang Xuanling the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent: the thirteenth year of Zhenguan.
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for Kong Yi’s succession to the enfeoffed title Duke for Propagating Culture: the third year of Taiping Xingguo.
Five legal judgments: issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks; mortgaging and purchasing fields and houses; submitting written statements to the throne; urgently reporting military intelligence; and establishing the truth of wrongful accusations.
Third Session

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第五道
問自古帝王渙汗其大號所以推是心而
布之天下者也若典謨訓誥誓命之文
是已維持國脉統繫人心咸於是乎在
我
祖宗
列聖中天而興
明詔在天下固家傳而人誦矣
聖天子嗣位益隆太平之治迺今歲夏四月偶
===
因邊陲小警誕告多方海濱萬里之外
俯聽仰思知
聖天子有敬
天法
祖之心有勤民恤物之心有神武不殺之心是
心也上與
祖宗
列聖合遠與古帝王合漢去古未遠後之稱詔
者以漢爲首漢之賢君若高文景武果
punctuated:
第五道

問：自古帝王渙汗其大號，所以推是心而布之天下者也。若典謨訓誥誓命之文，是已。維持國脉，統繫人心，咸於是乎在。我祖宗列聖中天而興，明詔在天下，固家傳而人誦矣。聖天子嗣位，益隆太平之治。迺今歲夏四月，偶因邊陲小警，誕告多方。海濱萬里之外，俯聽仰思，知聖天子有敬天法祖之心，有勤民恤物之心，有神武不殺之心。是心也，上與祖宗列聖合，遠與古帝王合。漢去古未遠，後之稱詔者以漢爲首。漢之賢君，若高文景武，果
translation_en:
Question Five

Question: From antiquity, emperors and kings have widely issued their great proclamations as a means of extending their intentions throughout the realm. Such are the texts of the canons, counsels, instructions, announcements, oaths, and charges. Sustaining the lifeblood of the state and binding together the hearts of the people both depend upon these. Our founding ancestors and successive sage sovereigns arose at Heaven’s zenith; their luminous edicts circulated throughout the realm, transmitted in every household and recited by everyone. Since succeeding to the throne, the sagely Son of Heaven has further enhanced the governance of Great Peace. Now, in the fourth month of this year, in summer, a minor alarm on the frontier occasioned a proclamation addressed to all regions. Here on the seacoast, ten thousand li away, we listen humbly and reflect reverently, knowing that the sagely Son of Heaven has a heart that reveres Heaven and takes his ancestors as models, that labors for the people and cares for all beings, and that possesses divine martial prowess without resorting to killing. This heart accords with those of our founding ancestors and successive sage sovereigns above, and with those of the emperors and kings of remote antiquity. The Han was not far removed from antiquity, and later generations discussing edicts have ranked those of the Han foremost. Did such worthy Han rulers as Gao, Wen, Jing, and Wu indeed …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
能有是心乎抑能有是詔乎其間亦有
粗合夫一二者乎諸生遭際
明時獲沾
聖化久矣有能鋪張揚厲述此
盛德以昭示無疆者乎華國之才吾將爲爾
薦之
問諸子之書亦儒者之所嘗讀也班固作
漢藝文志分爲諸子十家然所謂十家
者有出於司徒者有出於史官者有出
===
於羲和者有出於理官者又有出於掌
禮之官清廟之官行人之官者又有出
於擬議之官農稷之官稗闔之官者皆
可得而言歟孟堅於諸子十家之外又
刪劉歆七略之說而有四家後世分四
部之書而諸子百家皆列於子部豈亦
倣孟堅之體歟十家之書有鹽鐵論潛
夫論荆楚歲時記秦中歲時記昌言申
鑒中論法訓之書風俗通義群書治要
punctuated:
能有是心乎？抑能有是詔乎？其間亦有粗合夫一二者乎？諸生遭際明時，獲沾聖化久矣，有能鋪張揚厲，述此盛德，以昭示無疆者乎？華國之才，吾將爲爾薦之。

問：諸子之書，亦儒者之所嘗讀也。班固作《漢藝文志》，分爲諸子十家。然所謂十家者，有出於司徒者，有出於史官者，有出於羲和者，有出於理官者，又有出於掌禮之官、清廟之官、行人之官者，又有出於擬議之官、農稷之官、稗闔之官者，皆可得而言歟？孟堅於諸子十家之外，又刪劉歆《七略》之說，而有四家。後世分四部之書，而諸子百家皆列於子部，豈亦倣孟堅之體歟？十家之書，有《鹽鐵論》、《潛夫論》、《荆楚歲時記》、《秦中歲時記》、《昌言》、《申鑒》、《中論》、《法訓》之書，《風俗通義》、《群書治要》
translation_en:
…could they possess such a heart? Or could they issue such edicts? Among them, were there any who roughly fulfilled even one or two of these qualities? You students have encountered an enlightened age and have long benefited from the sage emperor’s transforming influence. Can any of you expound and extol this abundant virtue, making it manifest for all time? Those with the talent to bring glory to the state—I shall recommend you.

Question: The writings of the various philosophical masters are also works that Confucian scholars have read. When Ban Gu compiled the Bibliographical Treatise of the History of the Han, he divided the masters into ten schools. Among these ten schools, some originated with the Minister of Education, some with the historiographers, some with Xi and He, the astronomical officials, and some with judicial officials. Others originated with officials responsible for ritual, officials of the ancestral temple, and diplomatic envoys; still others with deliberative officials, agricultural officials, and minor officials [?]. Can you explain all of these origins? Besides the ten schools of masters, Mengjian [Ban Gu] also abridged Liu Xin’s account in the Seven Summaries, producing four further categories. Later generations divided books into four divisions, placing all the various philosophical schools in the Masters division. Was this likewise modeled on Mengjian’s arrangement? Among the books of the ten schools are the Discourses on Salt and Iron, Discourses of a Recluse, Record of Seasonal Observances in Jingchu, Record of Seasonal Observances in Qinzhong, Forthright Words, Extended Reflections, Discourses on the Mean, and Model Instructions, as well as the Comprehensive Meaning of Customs and the Essentials of Government from the Collected Books…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
古今說苑管氏指要論衡說林世說類
林之集斯皆作於誰歟他如鬼谷子尉
繚子抱朴子廣成子金樓子鶡冠子鄧
析子尹文子魯連子淮南子胡非子鬻
子田子宣子陸子黔婁子之數子者抑
果何許人而其所著果為何家書歟學
者若能脩六藝之術而觀此十家之言
亦可以通萬方之略矣願詳陳之毋隱
問文章可以潤身政事可以及物後世之
===
士亦各以其盛者稱鮮有能兼之者若
唐之時有韓愈宋之時有歐陽修皆以
文章名一代而論其文者乃謂奧衍閎
深佐佑六經醇深炳蔚渾然天質又謂
韓愈之才自視司馬遷揚雄歐陽修為
今之韓愈其果然歟今其遺文具在其
間議論關涉義理之大者尚可指其一
二而評之歟槩之以聖人之道亦皆有
所見歟愈為裴晉公所知然卒不能薦
punctuated:
《古今》《說苑》《管氏指要》《論衡》《說林》《世說》《類林》之集，斯皆作於誰歟？他如《鬼谷子》《尉繚子》《抱朴子》《廣成子》《金樓子》《鶡冠子》《鄧析子》《尹文子》《魯連子》《淮南子》《胡非子》《鬻子》《田子》《宣子》《陸子》《黔婁子》之數子者，抑果何許人，而其所著果為何家書歟？學者若能脩六藝之術，而觀此十家之言，亦可以通萬方之略矣。願詳陳之，毋隱。

問：文章可以潤身，政事可以及物。後世之士亦各以其盛者稱，鮮有能兼之者。若唐之時有韓愈，宋之時有歐陽修，皆以文章名一代。而論其文者乃謂「奧衍閎深，佐佑六經」「醇深炳蔚，渾然天質」，又謂「韓愈之才，自視司馬遷、揚雄」「歐陽修為今之韓愈」，其果然歟？今其遺文具在，其間議論關涉義理之大者，尚可指其一二而評之歟？槩之以聖人之道，亦皆有所見歟？愈為裴晉公所知，然卒不能薦
translation_en:
…the collections Ancient and Modern Matters (Gujin) [?], Garden of Discourses (Shuoyuan), Essential Teachings of Master Guan (Guanshi zhiyao), Balanced Discourses (Lunheng), Forest of Discourses (Shuolin), Accounts of the World (Shishuo), and Forest of Classified Materials (Leilin): who wrote all these? Then there are such masters as the Master of Ghost Valley (Guiguzi), Master Wei Liao (Weiliaozi), the Master Who Embraces Simplicity (Baopuzi), Master Guangcheng (Guangchengzi), the Master of the Golden Tower (Jinlouzi), the Pheasant-Cap Master (Heguanzi), Master Deng Xi (Deng Xizi), Master Yin Wen (Yin Wenzi), Master Lu Lian (Lu Lianzi), the Master of Huainan (Huainanzi), Master Hu Fei (Hu Feizi), Master Yu (Yuzi), Master Tian (Tianzi), Master Xuan (Xuanzi), Master Lu (Luzi), and Master Qian Lou (Qian Louzi). Who, in fact, were these men, and to which schools did their writings belong? If students can cultivate the arts of the Six Arts and examine the teachings of these ten schools, they may thereby gain a comprehensive understanding of the methods of every quarter. Please set this out fully, withholding nothing.

Question: Literary composition can refine the person, while government service can benefit others. Scholars of later ages have each won renown for whichever of these they excelled in; few have combined both. There were Han Yu in the Tang and Ouyang Xiu in the Song, each renowned in his age for literary composition. Those who discuss their writings have described them as “profound, expansive, broad, and deep, supporting the Six Classics” and “pure and profound, brilliant and luxuriant, possessing an integral, natural quality.” They have also said, “In talent, Han Yu ranked himself with Sima Qian and Yang Xiong,” and “Ouyang Xiu is the Han Yu of our day.” Is this indeed so? Their surviving writings are all available today. Can you identify and assess one or two passages whose arguments concern major questions of moral principle? Measured against the Way of the sages, do they each possess genuine insight? Han Yu was appreciated by Pei, Duke of Jin, yet in the end the duke was unable to recommend…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之於朝至韓魏公之薦修乃曰韓愈唐
之名士天下望以為相而竟不用使愈
為之未必有補於唐而談者至今以為
謗今不用修臣恐謗必及國然則使唐
誠能用愈果皆無所補歟其後修嘗為
執政矣一時建白亦有補於宋否歟抑
二子功業掩於文章而卒不可得而兼
歟請極論之以觀嚮往先哲之志
問治天下以正風俗得賢才為本然風俗
===
可易而正賢才可易而得耶其轉移化
導之機亦存乎其人耳夫輿圖之大姑
未枚舉子粤產也請以粤論粤自交州
置郡之後淳風古俗豈無可稱者歟在
漢唐宋時有質直尚信民得華風者有
習尚淳樸士多愿慤者有此郡文物不
下他州者亦可以為美矣不知其地可
乎風氣既開之後長材秀民豈無間出
者歟在漢唐宋時有累徵不起志趣高
punctuated:
之於朝。至韓魏公之薦修，乃曰：「韓愈，唐之名士，天下望以為相，而竟不用。使愈為之，未必有補於唐，而談者至今以為謗。今不用修，臣恐謗必及國。」然則使唐誠能用愈，果皆無所補歟？其後修嘗為執政矣，一時建白亦有補於宋否歟？抑二子功業掩於文章，而卒不可得而兼歟？請極論之，以觀嚮往先哲之志。

問：治天下以正風俗、得賢才為本，然風俗可易而正，賢才可易而得耶？其轉移化導之機，亦存乎其人耳。夫輿圖之大，姑未枚舉。子粤產也，請以粤論。粤自交州置郡之後，淳風古俗豈無可稱者歟？在漢唐宋時，有質直尚信、民得華風者，有習尚淳樸、士多愿慤者，有此郡文物不下他州者，亦可以為美矣。不知其地可乎？風氣既開之後，長材秀民豈無間出者歟？在漢唐宋時，有累徵不起、志趣高
translation_en:
…him for appointment at court. When Han, Duke of Wei, recommended Ouyang Xiu, he said: “Han Yu was a celebrated scholar of the Tang. All under Heaven hoped that he would be made chief minister, yet in the end he was not employed. Had Han Yu held that office, he might not necessarily have benefited the Tang; nevertheless, commentators to this day treat this as grounds for reproach. If Ouyang Xiu is not employed now, I fear that reproach will surely fall upon the state.” If, then, the Tang had indeed employed Han Yu, would he really have contributed nothing? Later, Ouyang Xiu did hold high office in government. Did the proposals he submitted at that time benefit the Song? Or were these two men’s achievements in public service overshadowed by their literary writings, so that ultimately they could not attain both? Discuss this fully, so that we may discern your aspiration to emulate the wise men of earlier times.

Question: Governing all under Heaven rests upon rectifying customs and securing worthy talent. But can customs easily be rectified, and worthy talent easily be secured? The key to bringing about change and guiding moral transformation lies in the people responsible. For the moment, let us refrain from enumerating cases throughout the vast territory of the empire. You are a native of Yue; please discuss the matter with reference to Yue. Since commanderies were established in Jiaozhou, have there been no pure manners and ancient customs in Yue worthy of praise? During the Han, Tang, and Song, there were places described as “straightforward in character and valuing trustworthiness, their people having acquired the cultivated ways of Chinese civilization”; others where “customs were pure and simple, and scholars were mostly sincere and honest”; and others of which it was said, “This commandery’s cultural attainments are no less than those of other prefectures.” These may indeed be considered admirable. Can you fail to know which places they were? Once the cultural climate had opened up, did people of outstanding ability and distinction not emerge from time to time? During the Han, Tang, and Song, there were those who repeatedly declined summonses to office, whose aspirations were lofty…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
尚者有録上金鑑坐貶荊州者有屢言
邊情三使契丹者亦可以爲賢矣不知
其人可乎
聖朝敷德海隅丕冒俗宜無不正也然未變如
信巫淫祀喪用樂之類其故何在抑可
諉諸夷否耶才固無不生也然繼出如
關敏鄧顒陳鼎之徒其行何居抑可班
諸賢否耶夫政由俗革魯多君子信乎
有開必先也閩之先有常衮蜀之先有
===
文翁吳之先有言偃楚之先有陳良固
也凡在嶺表類是而先者果何郡何人
歟亦有事類而實弗類者歟諸生以賢
才抱藝而來他日均有移風易俗之責
者盍各言之以觀厥志
問書曰民惟邦本詩曰用戒戎作則卹民
馭兵皆國之所恃以安而不可緩焉者
試以策之諸士昔人留意卹民有以理
其稅歛進戒其君者有以輕稅薄征諷
punctuated:
尚者，有録上金鑑、坐貶荊州者，有屢言邊情、三使契丹者，亦可以爲賢矣。不知其人可乎？聖朝敷德，海隅丕冒，俗宜無不正也。然未變如信巫、淫祀、喪用樂之類，其故何在？抑可諉諸夷否耶？才固無不生也，然繼出如關敏、鄧顒、陳鼎之徒，其行何居？抑可班諸賢否耶？夫政由俗革，魯多君子，信乎有開必先也。閩之先有常衮，蜀之先有文翁，吳之先有言偃，楚之先有陳良，固也。凡在嶺表，類是而先者，果何郡何人歟？亦有事類而實弗類者歟？諸生以賢才抱藝而來，他日均有移風易俗之責者，盍各言之，以觀厥志？

問：書曰：「民惟邦本。」詩曰：「用戒戎作。」則卹民馭兵，皆國之所恃以安而不可緩焉者。試以策之諸士：昔人留意卹民，有以理其稅歛進戒其君者，有以輕稅薄征諷
translation_en:
…lofty in their aspirations; there were those who submitted a Golden Mirror and were consequently demoted to Jingzhou, and those who repeatedly reported on frontier conditions and went three times as envoys to the Khitan. These, too, may be called worthy men. Can one remain ignorant of these people? Our sagely dynasty spreads its virtue, abundantly extending its shelter to the remotest coastal lands; surely no customs should remain unrectified. Yet such practices as trusting shamans, offering improper sacrifices, and using music at funerals remain unchanged. Why is this? Can these simply be attributed to the non-Han peoples? Talent certainly arises everywhere. Yet among those who subsequently emerged, such as Guan Min, Deng Yong, and Chen Ding, how should their conduct be assessed? Can they be ranked among the worthies? Customs change through government, and Lu had many gentlemen: surely every flowering has its pioneers. Min had Chang Gun as a pioneer, Shu had Wen Weng, Wu had Yan Yan, and Chu had Chen Liang—this is established. Throughout Lingbiao, which commanderies and which men provided comparable pioneers? Were there also cases similar in outward circumstances but different in substance? You students have come with worthy talents and cultivated learning, and in the future you will all bear responsibility for transforming customs. Why not each set forth your views, so that your aspirations may be seen?

Question: The Book of Documents says, “The people are the foundation of the state.” The Book of Odes says, “Thereby guard against the outbreak of war.” Thus caring for the people and controlling the troops are both things upon which the state depends for its security, and neither can be neglected. Let us put this to you gentlemen as a policy question. Among men of the past who devoted attention to caring for the people, some admonished their rulers to regulate the collection of taxes; others indirectly remonstrated with them about reducing taxes and lightening levies…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諫其君者又有論惜元氣在輕賦役者
立紀綱須寛民力者其人可悉數歟昔
人留意馭兵有四萬騎分屯九郡而單
于引去者有十一軍控制二邊而南詔
請還者又有監博州軍脩治器械虜人
不入者閱延州兵日夜訓練敵人相戒
者其人可歷指歟方
今堯封一統禹貢攸同萬方惟正之供軍士
樂於用戰比年以來湖湘遇歉或竭府
===
庫或停起運以賑卹之設或諸路旱澇
相仍不知若何而濟襄漢有警或調土
兵或募民兵以應援之設或他處盜賊
繼起不知若何而禦宋儒有謂斯民之
休戚係守令之賢否又有謂天下無必
勝之兵而有不可敗之將則守令將帥
任兵民之責不可以不擇也兹欲各得
其人而盡卹民馭兵之道必如之何而
後可昔人在布衣時視天下事皆爲分
punctuated: 諫其君者，又有論惜元氣在輕賦役者、立紀綱須寛民力者，其人可悉數歟？昔人留意馭兵，有四萬騎分屯九郡而單于引去者，有十一軍控制二邊而南詔請還者，又有監博州軍、脩治器械、虜人不入者，閱延州兵、日夜訓練、敵人相戒者，其人可歷指歟？方今堯封一統，禹貢攸同，萬方惟正之供，軍士樂於用戰。比年以來，湖湘遇歉，或竭府庫，或停起運，以賑卹之。設或諸路旱澇相仍，不知若何而濟？襄漢有警，或調土兵，或募民兵，以應援之。設或他處盜賊繼起，不知若何而禦？宋儒有謂斯民之休戚係守令之賢否，又有謂天下無必勝之兵，而有不可敗之將，則守令、將帥任兵民之責，不可以不擇也。兹欲各得其人，而盡卹民馭兵之道，必如之何而後可？昔人在布衣時，視天下事皆爲分
translation_en:
… remonstrated with their rulers. Others argued that conserving the state's vital energies depended on lightening taxes and labor services, or that establishing governing principles and discipline required easing burdens on the people's resources. Can you enumerate all these men? Among men of the past who devoted attention to commanding troops, one stationed forty thousand cavalry across nine commanderies, causing the chanyu to withdraw; another controlled two frontiers with eleven armies, so that Nanzhao requested permission to return. Another supervised the troops at Bozhou and repaired weapons and equipment, so that enemy forces did not invade; another inspected the troops at Yanzhou and trained them day and night, so that the enemy warned one another to beware. Can you identify these men one by one?

Today, the realm bounded by Yao is united, and the lands described in the Tribute of Yu share a common order. All regions furnish their regular tribute, and the soldiers gladly serve in battle. In recent years, when the Hu-Xiang region suffered poor harvests, relief was provided either by exhausting government treasuries or by suspending the dispatch of revenues. But supposing droughts and floods were to recur across the various regions, how could relief be provided? When alarms arose in the Xiang-Han region, reinforcements were supplied either by transferring native troops or by recruiting militia. But supposing bandits were to rise in succession elsewhere, how could they be resisted?

A Song Confucian said that the well-being or suffering of the people depends on whether their prefects and district magistrates are worthy. Another said that there are no troops in the world certain of victory, but there are generals who cannot be defeated. Thus prefects, district magistrates, and military commanders bear responsibility for soldiers and civilians, and must be carefully chosen. If we now wish to obtain the right person for each post and fully realize the proper ways of caring for the people and commanding troops, what must be done to achieve this? Men of the past, while still commoners, regarded all affairs of the realm as falling within their…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
内而况兵食二者尤今日之先務臣子
憂國愛民之心所不能自己者請詳言
之以觀用世之學
punctuated: 内，而况兵食二者，尤今日之先務，臣子憂國愛民之心所不能自己者。請詳言之，以觀用世之學。
translation_en: …within their own responsibilities. How much more, then, do military affairs and provisions—the most pressing tasks of the present day—compel the concern of those who serve the throne, whose care for the state and love for the people cannot be restrained. Please discuss these matters in detail, so that we may assess your learning for practical service.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
生財有大道生之者衆食之者寡爲之者
疾用之者舒則財恒足矣仁者以財發
身
黃佐
同考試官敎諭莊批此題舊以理財之效散財
之效對待言之殊失曾子立言之意蓋生財有道
而不自專惟仁者能之此作獨得其旨是用錄出
===
同考試官敎諭江批融會傳意發揮明白如此
篇者蓋不多得
考試官學正何批詞氣雅健可嘉
考試官敎授劉批大學義似此蓋頴出矣
大學旣詳言理天下之財自周於用必指言公
天下之財自得乎民甚矣財之有繫於天下也
理之固有其道而散之者豈有不得乎民哉曾
子傳大學之十章論平天下在絜矩而推廣其
意如此謂夫人君富有天下而恒慮其財之不
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

生財有大道：生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒，則財恒足矣。仁者以財發身。

黃佐

同考試官敎諭莊批：此題舊以理財之效、散財之效對待言之，殊失曾子立言之意。蓋生財有道而不自專，惟仁者能之。此作獨得其旨，是用錄出。

同考試官敎諭江批：融會傳意，發揮明白，如此篇者蓋不多得。

考試官學正何批：詞氣雅健，可嘉。

考試官敎授劉批：大學義似此，蓋頴出矣。

大學旣詳言理天下之財，自周於用，必指言公天下之財，自得乎民。甚矣，財之有繫於天下也！理之固有其道，而散之者豈有不得乎民哉？曾子傳大學之十章，論平天下在絜矩，而推廣其意如此。謂夫人君富有天下，而恒慮其財之不
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

There is a great way to produce wealth: let those who produce it be many, those who consume it few, those who make it work swiftly, and those who use it spend slowly; then wealth will always be sufficient. The benevolent person uses wealth to develop his person.

Huang Zuo

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor (jiaoyu): Earlier treatments of this topic have juxtaposed the effects of managing wealth and those of distributing wealth, seriously missing Zengzi’s intention in framing these words. For only a benevolent person can produce wealth according to the proper way without reserving it exclusively for himself. This composition alone grasps that meaning; hence its selection for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor (jiaoyu): Compositions like this, which integrate the meaning of the commentary and expound it clearly, are indeed seldom found.

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor (xuezheng): Its language and expressive force are refined and vigorous: commendable.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor (jiaoshou): An exposition of the meaning of the Great Learning such as this is truly outstanding.

Having explained in detail that managing the wealth of all under Heaven naturally ensures sufficient resources for expenditure, the Great Learning must explicitly state that sharing the wealth of all under Heaven naturally wins the people’s allegiance. How profoundly wealth bears upon all under Heaven! Managing it certainly has its proper way; and how could one who distributes it fail to win the people’s allegiance? In the tenth chapter of his commentary on the Great Learning, Zengzi discusses how bringing peace to all under Heaven rests upon the principle of the measuring square, and extends its meaning in this way. His point is that a ruler possesses all the wealth under Heaven, yet constantly worries that his wealth will not …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
□者顧未得生財之大道耳其道維何蓋天下
之財以生而裕以食而耗也故必在國也農工
商賈各事其業而無游惰之民在朝也公卿大
夫皆惟其人而無幸致之位則財之生者衆而
食者寡矣天下之財爲之難成用之易竭也故
必念稼穡之艱難凡有興作而不奪其時計貨
利之出入凡有經費而不踰其節則財之爲者
疾而用者舒矣夫如是則旣務本以開財之源
而又節用以止財之流府庫充而供億之有餘
===
倉廩實而荒歉之有備何患於財之不足乎夫
生財有道如此而能公其財者誰歟蓋惟仁者
至公無我知千萬人之心卽一人之心利不獨
專也以一人之心爲千萬人之心財不私蓄也
藏富於民而不急於誅求取民有制而不事於
掊克雖未嘗分我所有以與之也而民得以樂
其樂者自然愛戴歸往尊之爲天子矣雖未嘗
出吾所有以益之也而民得以利其利者自爾
忻慕感悅戴之爲元后矣何有於民之不得乎
punctuated: □者，顧未得生財之大道耳。其道維何？蓋天下之財，以生而裕，以食而耗也。故必在國也，農工商賈各事其業，而無游惰之民；在朝也，公卿大夫皆惟其人，而無幸致之位，則財之生者衆而食者寡矣。天下之財，爲之難成，用之易竭也。故必念稼穡之艱難，凡有興作而不奪其時；計貨利之出入，凡有經費而不踰其節，則財之爲者疾而用者舒矣。夫如是，則旣務本以開財之源，而又節用以止財之流，府庫充而供億之有餘，倉廩實而荒歉之有備，何患於財之不足乎？夫生財有道如此，而能公其財者誰歟？蓋惟仁者，至公無我，知千萬人之心卽一人之心，利不獨專也；以一人之心爲千萬人之心，財不私蓄也。藏富於民而不急於誅求，取民有制而不事於掊克。雖未嘗分我所有以與之也，而民得以樂其樂者，自然愛戴歸往，尊之爲天子矣；雖未嘗出吾所有以益之也，而民得以利其利者，自爾忻慕感悅，戴之爲元后矣。何有於民之不得乎？
translation_en:
…[illegible] is merely because he has not yet grasped the great way of producing wealth. What is this way? The wealth of the realm grows abundant through production and is depleted through consumption. Thus, throughout the realm, farmers, artisans, and merchants must each pursue their occupations, with no idle people; at court, dukes, ministers, and grandees must all be suitable men, with no offices gained through undeserved good fortune. Then those who produce wealth will be many, and those who consume it few. The wealth of the realm is difficult to create but easily exhausted in use. Thus one must keep in mind the hardships of sowing and reaping, ensuring that no undertaking encroaches upon the farmers’ working time; one must reckon the receipts and outlays of goods and revenue, ensuring that regular expenditures never exceed proper limits. Then wealth will be produced swiftly and consumed slowly. In this way, one both attends to the fundamental occupation of agriculture to open the sources of wealth and economizes in expenditure to restrain its outflow. Treasuries and storehouses will be full, with more than enough to meet provisioning needs; granaries will be well stocked, with reserves against famine and poor harvests. What fear need there be that wealth will prove insufficient?

Such is the way of producing wealth; but who can make that wealth serve the common good? Only the benevolent ruler, utterly impartial and without selfishness. He knows that the hearts of the myriad people are the heart of the one ruler, and so does not monopolize benefits; he makes his own heart the heart of the myriad people, and so does not hoard wealth for himself. He lodges wealth among the people, without pressing them for exactions; he takes from them within prescribed limits, without pursuing oppressive extraction. Although he has never divided his own possessions to give to them, the people, enabled to enjoy what brings them joy, naturally love him, attach themselves to him, and turn to him, honoring him as the Son of Heaven. Although he has never drawn upon his own possessions to enrich them, the people, enabled to benefit from what brings them benefit, naturally admire him with delight and respond with gratitude and gladness, upholding him as their sovereign. How could he fail to win the people’s allegiance?

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
然則為治者可不知所以足國之道而顧以專
利為哉大抵財用國家所急而不可一日缺者
也然或斂之無道而徒朘削於民未有不失民
之心者故曾子於此論足國之道而必歸之仁
人豈非萬世君天下者之明法歟他日孟軻氏
有曰無政事則財用不足又曰王如好貨與百
姓同之於王何有其亦曾子之意歟
君子喻於義
薛侃
===
同考試官教諭賴批喻義分明就知上說諸士子多於
行義上說多殊戾本旨此作卓有所見而詞亦雅贍錄之
同考試官教諭閔批說理文字不冗則晦求其體認
親切而善於措辭者無踰此篇
考試官學正何批整潔可誦
考試官教授劉批文有理致
聖人論有德者深知夫天理之所宜也蓋君子
之心一於理而已則其所喻者豈有外於理之
所宜哉聖人論君子之異於小人者如此謂夫
punctuated:
然則為治者可不知所以足國之道，而顧以專利為哉？大抵財用，國家所急而不可一日缺者也。然或斂之無道，而徒朘削於民，未有不失民之心者。故曾子於此論足國之道，而必歸之仁人，豈非萬世君天下者之明法歟？他日孟軻氏有曰：「無政事則財用不足。」又曰：「王如好貨，與百姓同之，於王何有？」其亦曾子之意歟？

君子喻於義
薛侃

同考試官教諭賴批：喻義分明，就知上說。諸士子多於行義上說，多殊戾本旨。此作卓有所見，而詞亦雅贍，錄之。
同考試官教諭閔批：說理文字，不冗則晦。求其體認親切而善於措辭者，無踰此篇。
考試官學正何批：整潔可誦。
考試官教授劉批：文有理致。

聖人論有德者深知夫天理之所宜也。蓋君子之心一於理而已，則其所喻者豈有外於理之所宜哉？聖人論君子之異於小人者如此，謂夫
translation_en:
Then can those who govern fail to understand the way to make the state prosperous, and instead devote themselves to monopolizing profit? Financial resources are urgently needed by the state and cannot be dispensed with for even a day. Yet those who gather them improperly, merely draining and despoiling the people, invariably lose the people’s allegiance. Thus, when Zengzi discusses here the way to enrich the state, he necessarily attributes it to the benevolent person. Is this not a clear model for all who rule the realm in ages to come? Later, Meng Ke said, “Without proper administration, financial resources will be insufficient.” He also said, “If Your Majesty loves wealth, share it with the common people: what difficulty would there be in becoming a true king?” Was this not also Zengzi’s meaning?

“The Gentleman Understands Righteousness”
Xue Kan

Comment by Associate Examiner Lai, Instructor: The explanation of understanding righteousness is clear and treats it in terms of knowledge. Most candidates discuss it in terms of practicing righteousness, often departing markedly from the original meaning. This composition displays outstanding insight, and its language is also elegant and ample. I select it for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Min, Instructor: Writing that expounds principles tends to be either verbose or obscure. For an intimate grasp of the subject combined with skill in expression, no essay surpasses this one.

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: Orderly and polished; worthy of recitation.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: The writing conveys the subtleties of principle.

The Sage explains that the virtuous deeply understand what accords with Heavenly principle. The gentleman’s mind is wholly devoted to principle; how, then, could what he understands lie outside what accords with principle? Such is the Sage’s account of how the gentleman differs from the petty man. His meaning is that …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人品不同則其所喻亦異惟所謂君子者氣質
清明而其所造詣者蓋極其深德性渾全而其
所識見者一出於正天下之事開闔常變莫不
各有當然之則君子則不昧於所從焉天下之
物大小精粗莫不各有自然之理君子則能審
其所向焉無適無莫於凡義之所比者知之極
其精而他岐不足以惑之不信不果於凡義之
所在者見之極其明而外物不得以蔽之大而
一身之進退小而一物之取予在我之權度精
===
切而所以處之者確乎不差矣翅龜卜而蓍筮
邪大而死生之故小而食息之微在我之方寸
虛明而所以辨之者的然不惑矣翅燭照而數
計邪吁君子之喻於義者如此若夫小人則反
是矣學者其可不知所以擇之乎大抵天下之
道二義與利耳出乎此則入乎彼幾微之際蓋
有未易辨者尚父之戒武王而曰義勝欲者從
欲勝義者凶孟子亦曰舜與蹠之分善與利之
間而已毫釐之不審天淵之懸隔聖賢每於是
punctuated: 人品不同，則其所喻亦異。惟所謂君子者，氣質清明，而其所造詣者蓋極其深；德性渾全，而其所識見者一出於正。天下之事，開闔常變，莫不各有當然之則，君子則不昧於所從焉；天下之物，大小精粗，莫不各有自然之理，君子則能審其所向焉。無適無莫，於凡義之所比者，知之極其精，而他岐不足以惑之；不信不果，於凡義之所在者，見之極其明，而外物不得以蔽之。大而一身之進退，小而一物之取予，在我之權度精切，而所以處之者確乎不差矣，翅龜卜而蓍筮邪？大而死生之故，小而食息之微，在我之方寸虛明，而所以辨之者的然不惑矣，翅燭照而數計邪？吁！君子之喻於義者如此，若夫小人則反是矣。學者其可不知所以擇之乎？大抵天下之道二，義與利耳。出乎此，則入乎彼，幾微之際，蓋有未易辨者。尚父之戒武王而曰：「義勝欲者從，欲勝義者凶。」孟子亦曰：「舜與蹠之分，善與利之間而已。」毫釐之不審，天淵之懸隔，聖賢每於是
translation_en:
…people differ in character, and so what they understand also differs. Those called gentlemen possess a clear and luminous psychophysical constitution, and their attainments are exceedingly profound; their moral nature is whole and complete, and their understanding proceeds entirely from what is correct. All affairs under Heaven, in their unfolding and closing, constancy and change, have their proper standards, and the gentleman is never unclear about what to follow. All things under Heaven, great or small, fine or coarse, have their inherent principles, and the gentleman can discern where to direct himself. With neither fixed preferences nor fixed refusals, he understands with utmost precision whatever accords with righteousness, and divergent paths cannot confuse him. Without insisting on keeping his word or carrying an undertaking through regardless of circumstances, he sees with utmost clarity wherever righteousness lies, and external things cannot obscure his understanding. In matters as great as his own advancement or withdrawal, or as small as taking or giving a single object, his inner capacity to weigh and measure is precise and exact, and his handling of them is assuredly without error. Is this merely divination by tortoise shell or milfoil stalks [?]? In matters as great as life and death, or as slight as eating and resting, his heart is open and clear, and his discernment is certain and free from confusion. Is this merely illumination by a candle or reckoning by numbers [?]? Ah! Such is the gentleman’s understanding of righteousness; the petty man is the reverse. Can students fail to understand how to choose between them?

Broadly speaking, there are two paths under Heaven: righteousness and profit, and nothing more. To leave one is to enter the other, and at their most subtle juncture they are not always easily distinguished. Shangfu admonished King Wu, saying: “When righteousness overcomes desire, things proceed smoothly [?]; when desire overcomes righteousness, misfortune follows.” Mengzi also said: “The distinction between Shun and Zhi lies simply in the difference between goodness and profit.” A failure to discern a hair’s breadth produces a separation as vast as that between Heaven and the depths. The sages and worthies, whenever addressing these…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
二者對舉而互言之其垂訓之意至矣厥後宋
儒張子有曰無所為而為之者義也有所為而
為之者利也朱子謂其擴前聖所未發是又後
學之所當知
夏曰校殷曰序周曰庠學則三代共之皆
所以明人倫也人倫明於上小民親於
下
陳世美
同考試官訓導陳批三代立學教民成俗之意具
於此數語而能鋪叙有法僅見此篇
===
同考試官訓導楊批平平說去而步驟自然中節
蓋必養之有素者
考試官學正何批文字有機軸
考試官教授劉批講語精確
大賢詳舉三代之學必指其教之所以立而及
其化之所由成也蓋人倫者立教之本也三代
以是教民而民豈有不化者哉昔孟子答滕文
公為國之問及此若曰政莫要於教民法莫善
punctuated:
二者對舉而互言之，其垂訓之意至矣。厥後宋儒張子有曰：「無所為而為之者，義也；有所為而為之者，利也。」朱子謂其擴前聖所未發，是又後學之所當知。

夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠，學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。

陳世美

同考試官訓導陳批：三代立學教民成俗之意，具於此數語，而能鋪叙有法，僅見此篇。

同考試官訓導楊批：平平說去，而步驟自然中節，蓋必養之有素者。

考試官學正何批：文字有機軸。

考試官教授劉批：講語精確。

大賢詳舉三代之學，必指其教之所以立，而及其化之所由成也。蓋人倫者，立教之本也。三代以是教民，而民豈有不化者哉？昔孟子答滕文公為國之問，及此，若曰：「政莫要於教民，法莫善
translation_en:
…set these two side by side and discussed each in relation to the other: their intention in leaving instruction to posterity was most profound. Later, the Song Confucian Master Zhang said: “To act without an ulterior purpose is righteousness; to act with an ulterior purpose is profit.” Master Zhu said that this expanded upon what the earlier sages had left unexpressed. This, too, is something later students should understand.

“In the Xia they were called xiao; in the Yin, xu; and in the Zhou, xiang. As for xue, all three dynasties shared that designation. All served to clarify human relationships. When human relationships are made clear above, the common people below live in mutual affection.”

Chen Shimei

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: The intention behind the Three Dynasties’ establishment of schools—to teach the people and shape their customs—is fully contained in these few words. Yet this is the only essay I have seen that develops the subject with such method.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: The exposition proceeds evenly, yet its successive steps naturally strike the proper measure. Surely this comes from long cultivation.

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: The writing has an organizing conception.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: The exposition is precise.

When the great worthy enumerated the schools of the Three Dynasties in detail, he necessarily pointed out how their teaching was established and went on to explain how its transforming influence was accomplished. Human relationships are the foundation upon which teaching is established. Since the Three Dynasties taught the people through these relationships, how could the people fail to be transformed? Formerly, when Mencius answered Duke Wen of Teng’s question about governing a state, he touched upon this, as if to say: “In government, nothing is more essential than teaching the people; among models, none is better…”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於三代彼其都鄙鄉遂之地必有鄉學夏之鄉
學則取教民之義名之曰校殷之鄉學則取習
射之義名之曰序周之鄉學則謂之庠蓋有取
於養老之義焉是皆所謂小學也至於王畿首
善之地必有國學則殷因於夏而稱之無異名
周因於殷而名之無異義是則所謂大學也夫
以庠序學校之設如此而其所以爲教者夫豈
求之民性之外哉蓋以父子之親君臣之義人
之大倫也然或奪於情而牽於愛則日就晦蝕
===
矣必於學而講明之夫婦之別長幼之序朋友
之信亦人之大倫也然或溺於私而流於俗則
日就昏昧矣必於學而開發之本之於躬行心
得之餘加之以鼓舞作興之道親義之倫明於
上而天下之爲父子君臣者各得其分翕然相
敬而相愛雍穆之化行矣序別信之倫明於上
而天下之爲夫婦長幼朋友者各止其所怡然
相信而相悅和順之俗作矣化行於上俗美於
下三代教民之善如此文公爲國舍是將誰法
punctuated: 於三代。彼其都鄙鄉遂之地，必有鄉學。夏之鄉學，則取教民之義，名之曰校；殷之鄉學，則取習射之義，名之曰序；周之鄉學，則謂之庠，蓋有取於養老之義焉。是皆所謂小學也。至於王畿首善之地，必有國學，則殷因於夏而稱之無異名，周因於殷而名之無異義，是則所謂大學也。夫以庠序學校之設如此，而其所以爲教者，夫豈求之民性之外哉？蓋以父子之親、君臣之義，人之大倫也。然或奪於情而牽於愛，則日就晦蝕矣，必於學而講明之。夫婦之別、長幼之序、朋友之信，亦人之大倫也。然或溺於私而流於俗，則日就昏昧矣，必於學而開發之。本之於躬行心得之餘，加之以鼓舞作興之道，親義之倫明於上，而天下之爲父子君臣者各得其分，翕然相敬而相愛，雍穆之化行矣。序別信之倫明於上，而天下之爲夫婦長幼朋友者各止其所，怡然相信而相悅，和順之俗作矣。化行於上，俗美於下，三代教民之善如此。文公爲國，舍是將誰法
translation_en:
…than those of the Three Dynasties. Throughout their cities, outlying districts, and rural communities, there were necessarily local schools. The local schools of the Xia were named xiao, taking their meaning from teaching the people; those of the Yin were named xu, taking their meaning from practicing archery; those of the Zhou were called xiang, drawing their meaning from caring for the elderly. These were all what are called elementary schools. In the royal domain, the foremost place of moral excellence, there was necessarily a school of the state. The Yin followed the Xia, retaining the same designation; the Zhou followed the Yin, using a name with the same meaning. This was what is called the higher school.

With schools of these various kinds established in this way, could the substance of their teaching possibly have been sought outside the people’s own nature? Affection between father and son and righteousness between ruler and subject are cardinal human relationships. Yet when people are overpowered by emotion and swayed by attachment, these become increasingly obscured and impaired. They must therefore be explained and clarified in school. Distinction between husband and wife, precedence between elder and younger, and trustworthiness between friends are likewise cardinal human relationships. Yet when people become immersed in selfishness and drift along with prevailing customs, these become increasingly obscure. They must therefore be elucidated and brought to light in school.

Once a foundation has been laid through personal practice and understanding gained in one’s own heart, methods of encouragement and inspiration are added. When the relationships of affection and righteousness are made clear above, fathers and sons, rulers and subjects throughout the realm each fulfill their allotted roles. United in mutual respect and affection, they bring about a transformation toward harmony and reverence. When the relationships of precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness are made clear above, husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends throughout the realm each abide in their proper places. Gladly trusting and delighting in one another, they establish customs of harmony and concord. Moral transformation proceeds from above, and customs become good below. Such was the excellence of the Three Dynasties’ teaching of the people. In governing his state, if Duke Wen abandoned this, whom would he take as his model…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉抑論戰國之時三代之教盡廢區區小國之
君如滕文者尚何望其能興三代之治然而孟
子拳拳以是告之亦獨何哉蓋聖賢之所學者
三代之法也齊梁之君地大民衆足以有為既
嘗以是語之而卒不見用滕文有志則亦安得
不為之告邪□□於此可見聖賢之用心矣
易
天且弗違而況於人乎
潘濂
===
同考試官訓導陳批作者多將天且弗違兼後天
說況於人乎作利見說惟此篇於天人處體認真切錄之
同考試官訓導楊批題本明白學者多體認不真
此篇理順詞暢是用錄之為治易者式
考試官學正何批詞理俱到
考試官教授劉批得本義旨
道所由出者既從乎大人道所同具者必從乎
大人夫道出於天而具於人也大人所為皆道
天既從之矣人豈有不從者哉文言釋乾九五
punctuated:
哉？抑論戰國之時，三代之教盡廢，區區小國之君如滕文者，尚何望其能興三代之治？然而孟子拳拳以是告之，亦獨何哉？蓋聖賢之所學者，三代之法也。齊梁之君，地大民衆，足以有為，既嘗以是語之，而卒不見用。滕文有志，則亦安得不為之告邪？□□於此，可見聖賢之用心矣。

易
天且弗違，而況於人乎？
潘濂

同考試官訓導陳批：作者多將「天且弗違」兼後天說，「況於人乎」作利見說。惟此篇於天人處體認真切，錄之。

同考試官訓導楊批：題本明白，學者多體認不真。此篇理順詞暢，是用錄之，為治易者式。

考試官學正何批：詞理俱到。

考試官教授劉批：得本義旨。

道所由出者，既從乎大人；道所同具者，必從乎大人。夫道出於天，而具於人也。大人所為皆道，天既從之矣，人豈有不從者哉？文言釋乾九五
translation_en:
…indeed? Yet consider the Warring States period: the teachings of the Three Dynasties had been entirely abandoned. What hope could there still be that the ruler of a mere small state, such as Duke Wen of Teng, could revive the governance of the Three Dynasties? Why, then, did Mengzi so earnestly instruct him in these matters? Because what sages and worthies studied were the methods of the Three Dynasties. The rulers of Qi and Liang possessed extensive territories and large populations, sufficient to accomplish something. Mengzi had already spoken to them of these methods, but in the end his counsel was not adopted. Since Duke Wen of Teng had the aspiration, how could Mengzi refrain from instructing him as well? [Two illegible characters] Here we can see the intentions of sages and worthies.

Book of Changes
“Even Heaven does not oppose him; how much less would human beings?”
Pan Lian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: Most writers explain “Even Heaven does not oppose him” by also incorporating the passage about acting after Heaven, and explain “how much less would human beings?” in terms of “it is beneficial to see [the great man].” This essay alone shows a genuine and precise understanding of Heaven and humanity. I have selected it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: The topic itself is clear, but students often fail to grasp it accurately. This essay’s reasoning is coherent and its language fluent. I have therefore selected it as a model for those studying the Book of Changes.

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: It captures the purport of the Original Meaning [of the Book of Changes].

Since that from which the Way issues follows the great man, those who alike possess the Way must follow the great man. The Way issues from Heaven and is possessed by human beings. Everything the great man does accords with the Way. Since Heaven follows him, how could human beings fail to follow him? The Commentary on the Words of the Text explains the nine in the fifth place of Qian…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文義至此謂夫九五大人至公无私以道爲體
是以天理民彜天固不能无頼於大人也彼則
聰明以開其先凡心之所經畫者卽天之所默
成天且從之而不違民生日用天固不能无望
於大人也彼則沉幾以創其始凡意之所建立
者卽天之所默定天且順之而不拂觀其通變
神化也則祐之以吉无不利裁成輔相也則因
之而无過不及天豈能違之哉天且弗違如此
況人之生也藐然有身其心卽天之心也於大
===
人所經畫者必遵之以寡過混然中處其道卽
天之道也於大人所建立者必宜之而不倦在
當世則曰立我烝民莫匪爾極出入惟順帝之
則而已求其自用自專者何有在後世則曰佑
啓後人以正罔缺曰罔惟遵王之道而已求其
不信不從者蔑如人又豈能違之哉吁大人所
爲建之於天而天不悖徵之於人而人必從如
此是其道德之純絕无有我之私允爲人類之
首而爲人所利見也歟雖然分而二之天之事
punctuated: 文義至此，謂夫九五大人至公无私，以道爲體。是以天理民彜，天固不能无頼於大人也。彼則聰明以開其先，凡心之所經畫者，卽天之所默成，天且從之而不違。民生日用，天固不能无望於大人也。彼則沉幾以創其始，凡意之所建立者，卽天之所默定，天且順之而不拂。觀其通變神化也，則祐之以吉，无不利；裁成輔相也，則因之而无過不及。天豈能違之哉？天且弗違如此，況人之生也，藐然有身，其心卽天之心也，於大人所經畫者，必遵之以寡過；混然中處，其道卽天之道也，於大人所建立者，必宜之而不倦。在當世則曰：「立我烝民，莫匪爾極。」出入惟順帝之則而已，求其自用自專者何有？在後世則曰：「佑啓後人，以正罔缺。」曰：「罔惟遵王之道。」而已，求其不信不從者蔑如。人又豈能違之哉？吁！大人所爲，建之於天而天不悖，徵之於人而人必從，如此，是其道德之純，絕无有我之私，允爲人類之首，而爲人所利見也歟！雖然，分而二之，天之事
translation_en:
…At this point, the meaning of the text is that the great man of the nine in the fifth place is perfectly impartial and without selfishness, embodying the Way. Thus, in matters of Heaven’s principles and the constant norms of human relations, Heaven assuredly cannot dispense with reliance upon the great man. Through his perceptiveness he takes the lead: whatever his mind plans is precisely what Heaven silently brings to completion. Even Heaven follows him without opposition. In matters of the people’s livelihood and daily needs, Heaven assuredly cannot cease to place its hopes in the great man. Through profound discernment of incipient developments, he initiates undertakings: whatever his intention establishes is precisely what Heaven silently determines. Even Heaven accords with him without resistance. Consider how he comprehends change and brings about wondrous transformation: Heaven blesses him with good fortune, and nothing is unfavorable. In shaping and completing, assisting and supporting the work of Heaven and Earth, he follows their workings, with neither excess nor deficiency. How could Heaven oppose him?

If even Heaven offers no opposition in this way, how much more must this apply to human beings? Born with their tiny individual bodies, their minds are nevertheless the mind of Heaven itself. They must therefore follow what the great man plans, so as to lessen their faults. Dwelling amidst the undifferentiated whole [?], their Way is the Way of Heaven itself. They must therefore conform tirelessly to what the great man establishes. Of those living in his own age it is said: “You establish us, the multitude of the people; none fails to take you as his standard.” In all their comings and goings, they simply follow the rules of the Lord on High. Where could one find anyone relying solely on himself or acting on his own authority? Of later generations it is said: “Aid and enlighten those who come after, through rectitude without deficiency.” It is also said: “None but follow the king’s Way” [?]. That is all. Those who neither trust nor follow him are nowhere to be found. How, then, could people oppose him?

Ah! What the great man does can be set before Heaven, and Heaven does not reject it; it can be tested among people, and people invariably follow it. Such is the purity of his Way and virtue, utterly free of selfish concern for himself. Surely he is worthy to stand at the head of humankind, the one whom it benefits people to see! Nevertheless, if Heaven and humanity are distinguished as two, the affairs of Heaven…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
違人必不違也合而一之則天之視聽皆在於
人人之從違即天之從違也是故觀天命者每
卜諸人心善言天者必有驗於人外乎人以求
天不可也噫安得學貫天人者而與之言易哉
履信思乎順又以尚賢也是以自天祐之
吉无不利也
蔡士儲
同考試官訓導陳批說出大有上九滿而不溢
明白簡當較之衆作自別本房殆無出其右者
===
同考試官訓導楊批此題卦爻本義明白作者
多無根據晚得此卷讀之令人嘆賞
考試官學正何批得潔淨精微之旨
考試官教授劉批理明詞到
能盡處有之道斯享所有之福聖人釋大有爻
義然也夫有大者不可以盈也上九處之盡其
道則其獲天之祐不亦宜乎大傳釋大有上九
爻辭如此意謂上九所以自天祐之吉無不利
者何哉蓋其大有之世以剛居上而能下從六
punctuated:
違，人必不違也。合而一之，則天之視聽皆在於人，人之從違即天之從違也。是故觀天命者，每卜諸人心；善言天者，必有驗於人。外乎人以求天，不可也。噫！安得學貫天人者，而與之言《易》哉！
履信思乎順，又以尚賢也，是以自天祐之，吉无不利也。
蔡士儲
同考試官訓導陳批：說出大有上九滿而不溢，明白簡當，較之衆作自別，本房殆無出其右者。
同考試官訓導楊批：此題卦爻本義明白，作者多無根據。晚得此卷，讀之令人嘆賞。
考試官學正何批：得潔淨精微之旨。
考試官教授劉批：理明詞到。
能盡處有之道，斯享所有之福，聖人釋大有爻義然也。夫有大者，不可以盈也。上九處之盡其道，則其獲天之祐，不亦宜乎？《大傳》釋大有上九爻辭如此，意謂上九所以自天祐之、吉無不利者，何哉？蓋其大有之世，以剛居上，而能下從六
translation_en:
…oppose; people certainly will not oppose. Taken together as one, however, Heaven’s seeing and hearing reside entirely in the people: the people’s assent or opposition is precisely Heaven’s assent or opposition. Thus those who observe Heaven’s mandate always ascertain it through the people’s hearts; those who speak well of Heaven must find confirmation among the people. To seek Heaven apart from the people is impossible. Ah! Where might I find someone whose learning encompasses Heaven and humanity, with whom to discuss the Book of Changes?
“He practices trustworthiness, considers compliance, and also honors the worthy. Therefore Heaven helps him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.”
Cai Shichu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: “He explains how the top Nine of Great Possession is full without overflowing. Clear, concise, and apt, this essay stands apart from the others. Among the papers in this examining room, scarcely any surpasses it.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: “The original meaning of this topic’s hexagram and line is clear, yet most writers offer no grounded interpretation. I received this paper late; reading it inspires admiration.”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “It captures the purport of purity and refinement, subtlety and profundity.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “The principles are clear, and the wording fully conveys them.”
Only by fully realizing the Way of living amid possessions can one enjoy the blessings of what one possesses. Such is the sage’s explanation of the line meaning in Great Possession. One who possesses much must not become overfull. Since the top Nine fully realizes the Way of occupying this position, is it not fitting that it receives Heaven’s help? This is how the Great Commentary explains the line statement for the top Nine of Great Possession. Its meaning is this: why does the top Nine receive Heaven’s help and attain good fortune, with nothing unfavorable? Because, in the time of Great Possession, it occupies the highest position with firmness, yet can follow the Six below…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
□則是五之虛中有信之德也彼則能履其信
凡措諸躬行者信以發志未嘗恃有而放誕五
之柔巽有順之德也彼則能思其順凡存諸念
慮者卑以自牧未嘗挾有而驕矜匪惟履信而
已又能降志以尊尚乎六五之賢不自作其聰
明焉匪惟思順而已又能致恭以崇重乎六五
之德不自用其賢智焉夫上九能盡處有之道
如此將見天眷來於信順之餘而所以祐之者
有隆而無替帝心簡於尚賢之後而所以福之
===
者方進而未巳滿而不溢位之受於先者猶鞏
用黃牛之革吉於我乎得矣何所往而不利哉
大而不盈禄之得於舊者有繫于苞桑之固吉
於我乎獲矣何所適而不宜哉吁盡道於巳獲
福於天上九其善於處有歟嗟夫謙則受益滿
則招損大有上九所有既極使非持盈守滿之
有道則如乾上九亢龍之悔旅上九喪牛之凶
將不免矣尚望其吉無不利而保所有於終哉
噫有大能謙必豫窮大者必失其居孔子之意
punctuated: □，則是五之虛中有信之德也，彼則能履其信。凡措諸躬行者，信以發志，未嘗恃有而放誕。五之柔巽有順之德也，彼則能思其順。凡存諸念慮者，卑以自牧，未嘗挾有而驕矜。匪惟履信而已，又能降志以尊尚乎六五之賢，不自作其聰明焉；匪惟思順而已，又能致恭以崇重乎六五之德，不自用其賢智焉。夫上九能盡處有之道如此，將見天眷來於信順之餘，而所以祐之者有隆而無替；帝心簡於尚賢之後，而所以福之者方進而未巳。滿而不溢，位之受於先者猶鞏用黃牛之革，吉於我乎得矣，何所往而不利哉？大而不盈，禄之得於舊者有繫于苞桑之固，吉於我乎獲矣，何所適而不宜哉？吁！盡道於巳，獲福於天，上九其善於處有歟！嗟夫！謙則受益，滿則招損。大有上九，所有既極，使非持盈守滿之有道，則如乾上九亢龍之悔、旅上九喪牛之凶，將不免矣。尚望其吉無不利，而保所有於終哉？噫！有大能謙必豫，窮大者必失其居，孔子之意
translation_en:
…[illegible character] Thus the fifth line, being empty at its center, possesses the virtue of trustworthiness, and the top line can put that trustworthiness into practice. In everything it carries out in person, it expresses its purpose through trustworthiness, never relying on its possessions to behave without restraint. The fifth line, being yielding and compliant, possesses the virtue of obedience, and the top line can keep that obedience in mind. In all its thoughts and deliberations, it cultivates itself through humility, never using its possessions as grounds for arrogance. It not only practices trustworthiness but also lowers its aspirations to honor the worthiness of the six in the fifth place, never presuming upon its own intelligence. It not only keeps obedience in mind but also shows reverence to exalt the virtue of the six in the fifth place, never relying exclusively on its own worth and wisdom.

Since the nine at the top so fully realizes the Way of conducting oneself amid abundance, Heaven’s favor will surely follow upon its trustworthiness and obedience, and the aid bestowed upon it will increase without decline. Once it has honored the worthy, it will be distinguished in the mind of the Lord on High, and the blessings bestowed upon it will continue to advance without ceasing. Full yet not overflowing, it will hold the position previously conferred upon it as securely as though bound with yellow oxhide. Good fortune is thus attained: wherever it goes, how could anything fail to be favorable? Great yet not overfull, it will hold its long-standing emoluments as securely as though tied to a clump of mulberry trees. Good fortune is thus gained: wherever it turns, how could anything fail to be fitting? Ah! By fully realizing the Way in itself, it obtains blessings from Heaven. How well the nine at the top conducts itself amid abundance!

Alas! Humility brings benefit; self-satisfaction invites loss. In the top nine of Great Possession, what one possesses has already reached its utmost extent. Unless one has a proper way to sustain fullness and preserve abundance, one will inevitably incur something like the regret of the ‘overreaching dragon’ in the top nine of The Creative, or the misfortune of ‘losing the ox’ in the top nine of The Wanderer. Could one still hope for good fortune with nothing unfavorable, and preserve one’s possessions to the end? Ah! Those who possess greatness and can remain humble will surely enjoy ease; those who push greatness to its limit will surely lose their dwelling. Confucius’s meaning…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
又於序卦發之合而觀之則保有之道可得矣
書
侯以明之撻以記之書用識哉欲並生哉
蕭汝爲
同考試官教諭顧批題本不難解而作者鋪叙
多至晦澁詞不費而意自到無喻此篇
同考試官教諭閔批圓轉條暢經義似此者絶少
考試官學正何批意思周匝
考試官教授劉批説出有虞不輕棄人處宛
===
然在目
聖世於未化之人詳有以教之者欲有以全之
也甚矣聖世不輕於棄人也則於侯明撻記而
書識之者豈非欲化其善而全其生也哉昔帝
舜告禹之意若曰臣鄰之責在汝無負固可以
爲忠直之勸矣然一有頑愚讒説出於其間則
爲盛治之累矣可無道以處之乎是故射所以
觀德也於是取彼射侯試以射藝若使容體不
比於禮而其發也或不能中節奏不比於樂而
punctuated:
又於《序卦》發之。合而觀之，則保有之道可得矣。
書
「侯以明之，撻以記之，書用識哉，欲並生哉。」
蕭汝爲
同考試官教諭顧批：「題本不難解，而作者鋪叙多至晦澁。詞不費而意自到，無喻此篇。」
同考試官教諭閔批：「圓轉條暢，經義似此者絶少。」
考試官學正何批：「意思周匝。」
考試官教授劉批：「説出有虞不輕棄人處，宛然在目。」
聖世於未化之人，詳有以教之者，欲有以全之也。甚矣，聖世不輕於棄人也！則於侯明、撻記而書識之者，豈非欲化其善而全其生也哉？昔帝舜告禹之意若曰：臣鄰之責，在汝無負，固可以爲忠直之勸矣。然一有頑愚讒説出於其間，則爲盛治之累矣，可無道以處之乎？是故射所以觀德也。於是取彼射侯，試以射藝。若使容體不比於禮，而其發也或不能中；節奏不比於樂，而
translation_en:
…He also expounded this in the Sequence of the Hexagrams. Considered together, these teachings reveal the way to preserve what one possesses.

Book of Documents

“Use the archery target to make them manifest; use flogging to make them remember; use writing to record them. The wish is that all should live.”

Xiao Ruwei

Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: “The topic is not inherently difficult to explain, yet writers often elaborate upon it until it becomes obscure. For economy of words and fullness of meaning, nothing surpasses this essay.”

Associate Examiner Min, Instructor, comments: “The transitions are smooth, and the exposition lucid and orderly. Essays interpreting the Classics that match this are exceedingly rare.”

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The thought is comprehensive.”

Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “It explains so vividly how the sovereign of Youyu was reluctant to abandon anyone that the scene seems present before our eyes.”

In a sage age, those who have not yet been transformed receive painstaking instruction because the aim is to preserve them. How great is the reluctance of a sage age to abandon anyone! Thus, making their character manifest through the archery target, making them remember through flogging, and recording their faults in writing—are these not intended to transform them toward goodness and preserve their lives?

The meaning of Emperor Shun’s words to Yu in former times was as follows: The responsibilities of a minister, the ruler’s close companion, rest with you; do not fail them. This certainly suffices to encourage loyalty and uprightness. Yet if obstinacy, ignorance, or slander should arise among the ministers, it would encumber flourishing government. Could there be no way to deal with this?

Therefore, archery is a means of observing virtue. Set up the archery target and test them in the art of shooting. If their bearing does not accord with ritual propriety, their shots may fail to hit the target; if their rhythm does not accord with the music, and …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其中也亦不能多則其心之不正而爲頑愚讒
說也無疑矣然於此而遂釋之不可也故必施
夫夏楚而治之以學校之刑使其備嘗折辱於
膚體之間庶幾記憶於心不至於或忘焉於此
而遂置之不可也又必錄其過惡而揭之於簡
冊之書于以暴著事迹於耳目之表庶幾愧念
於心不能以自已焉然其所以教之之詳如此
者果何意哉蓋以頑愚不攺勢不免於刑誅矣
所以侯明而撻記之者非忍外之也蓋欲啓其
===
憤發其悱變頑愚而爲忠直而與濟濟臣工並
生於天地之間不爲盛世之棄人矣讒說不悛
勢必至於滅絕矣所以撻記而書識之者非故
薄之也蓋欲攺其惡遷於善變讒說而爲臣鄰
而與烝烝士庶並生於覆載之内不爲太平之
棄物矣吁教之詳可以見聖人之義待之至可
以見聖人之仁宜乎史臣詳載之於書也抑觀
有虞之世萬邦咸寧可謂盛矣近而九德咸事
遠而黎獻共臣尚何庶頑讒說之足慮哉觀舜
punctuated:
其中也亦不能多，則其心之不正而爲頑愚讒說也無疑矣。然於此而遂釋之，不可也。故必施夫夏楚，而治之以學校之刑，使其備嘗折辱於膚體之間，庶幾記憶於心，不至於或忘焉。於此而遂置之，不可也。又必錄其過惡，而揭之於簡冊之書，于以暴著事迹於耳目之表，庶幾愧念於心，不能以自已焉。然其所以教之之詳如此者，果何意哉？蓋以頑愚不攺，勢不免於刑誅矣。所以侯明而撻記之者，非忍外之也，蓋欲啓其憤，發其悱，變頑愚而爲忠直，而與濟濟臣工並生於天地之間，不爲盛世之棄人矣。讒說不悛，勢必至於滅絕矣。所以撻記而書識之者，非故薄之也，蓋欲攺其惡，遷於善，變讒說而爲臣鄰，而與烝烝士庶並生於覆載之内，不爲太平之棄物矣。

吁！教之詳，可以見聖人之義；待之至，可以見聖人之仁。宜乎史臣詳載之於書也！抑觀有虞之世，萬邦咸寧，可謂盛矣。近而九德咸事，遠而黎獻共臣，尚何庶頑讒說之足慮哉？觀舜
translation_en:
…and their hits on the target are also few, then there can be no doubt that their hearts are not upright and that they are obstinate, foolish, and given to slander. Yet simply to let them go at this point would not do. Thus the wooden rod and thorn switch must be applied, disciplining them with the punishments of the schools and making them experience humiliation and pain fully in their flesh, so that they may remember in their hearts and never forget. Nor would it do simply to leave them alone at this point. Their faults and misdeeds must also be recorded and displayed in written registers, making their conduct manifest for all to hear and see, so that they may feel shame in their hearts and be unable to put it aside. But what, indeed, is the intention behind such painstaking instruction? If the obstinate and foolish do not reform, they will inevitably face punishment and execution. Revealing their faults through the archery target and impressing them upon their memory through flogging does not mean that the ruler can bear to cast them out. Rather, he wishes to enlighten them when they struggle to understand and help them express what they cannot yet articulate, transforming their obstinacy and foolishness into loyalty and uprightness. Thus they may live alongside the assembled officials between Heaven and Earth, without becoming people cast aside by a flourishing age. If those given to slander do not repent, they will inevitably come to destruction. Impressing their faults upon their memory through flogging and setting them down in writing does not mean deliberately treating them with contempt. Rather, he wishes them to reform their evil ways and turn toward goodness, changing from slanderers into ministers and close aides. Thus they may live alongside the multitude of gentlemen and common people beneath Heaven’s canopy and upon Earth’s support, without becoming beings cast aside in an age of peace.

Ah! In the thoroughness of this instruction we can see the sage’s righteousness; in the utmost care with which he treats them we can see the sage’s benevolence. Fitting indeed that the court historians recorded this in detail in the Book of Documents! Consider, moreover, the age of Youyu: all the myriad states were at peace, and it could indeed be called an age of flourishing rule. Close at hand, men possessing the nine virtues all served in office; far away, the worthy among the people all served as subjects. What cause could there still be to worry about the obstinate multitude and slanderers? Consider Shun…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之命龍而欲審於出納防其漸也至此復以命
禹而欲詳於教導化其惡也蓋深慮讒邪之害
治而欲謹之於微焉夫子告顏淵之為邦而曰
遠佞人其意不猶是歟
其作大邑其自時配皇天毖祀于上下其
自時中乂
蘇信
同考試官教諭顧批講王者宅洛事辭意嚴整
蓋精於經學者宜錄以為式
===
同考試官教諭閔批詞簡而意自見可以矯經
生浮冗支離之習矣
考試官學正何批不蔓不腐自是作手
考試官教授劉批講語精切
建天下之大業以行天下之大事大臣言作洛
之意也蓋建都王業之大也奉天祀神治民之
事咸於是乎行焉夫豈徒建也哉昔召公告成
王宅洛而舉周公之言如此其意蓋曰不言王
者居洛之事不知王者作洛之意彼擇地以中
punctuated:
之命龍而欲審於出納，防其漸也。至此復以命禹而欲詳於教導，化其惡也。蓋深慮讒邪之害治，而欲謹之於微焉。夫子告顏淵之為邦而曰：「遠佞人。」其意不猶是歟？

「其作大邑，其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下，其自時中乂。」
蘇信

同考試官教諭顧批：講王者宅洛事，辭意嚴整，蓋精於經學者，宜錄以為式。
同考試官教諭閔批：詞簡而意自見，可以矯經生浮冗支離之習矣。
考試官學正何批：不蔓不腐，自是作手。
考試官教授劉批：講語精切。

建天下之大業，以行天下之大事，大臣言作洛之意也。蓋建都，王業之大也；奉天、祀神、治民之事，咸於是乎行焉。夫豈徒建也哉？昔召公告成王宅洛，而舉周公之言如此。其意蓋曰：不言王者居洛之事，不知王者作洛之意。彼擇地以中
translation_en:
…in instructing Long, Shun wished him to scrutinize what was communicated to and from the throne, guarding against the first signs of such harm. Here he again instructed Yu, wishing him to provide thorough teaching and guidance so as to transform their wickedness. Deeply concerned that slander and depravity would harm good government, he wished to exercise vigilance while their manifestations were still slight. When the Master instructed Yan Yuan on governing a state, he said, “Keep flatterers at a distance.” Was his intention not the same?

“Let him build the great city; from here let him worthily match August Heaven and reverently offer sacrifices to the powers above and below; from here let him govern from the center.”
Su Xin

Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: “In explaining the sovereign’s establishment of his residence at Luo, the wording and ideas are rigorous and orderly. The writer is evidently proficient in classical learning; this should be recorded as a model.”
Associate Examiner Min, Instructor, comments: “The wording is concise, yet the meaning emerges clearly. It can correct the superficial verbosity and disjointedness habitual among students of the Classics.”
Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: “Neither rambling nor stale: clearly an accomplished writer.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “The exposition is precise and pertinent.”

To establish the great enterprise of the realm so as to carry out the great affairs of the realm: this is what the great minister meant when he spoke of founding Luo. Establishing a capital is a great undertaking of kingship; the affairs of serving Heaven, sacrificing to the spirits, and governing the people are all conducted there. Surely it is not merely a matter of construction! In former times, when the Duke of Shao advised King Cheng about taking up residence at Luo, he cited these words of the Duke of Zhou. His meaning was this: unless one explains what the sovereign is to do while residing at Luo, one cannot understand his purpose in founding Luo. He selected a site for its central position…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
基之定之王城中建足以來百辟之朝會體勢
何尊嚴也趨事以民經之營之下都外拓足以
奠四民之居止規模何宏遠也是豈麗宮室而
事游幸哉亦豈輕改作而圖壯觀哉蓋皇矣上
帝天子配之自是可以體元居正臨萬國於覆
幬之下天維顯思仰之不愧也天神地祇天子
祭之自是可以執圭奉幣舉大禮於郊社之時
神之格思祭之不黷也至若和恒居師天子主
之自是可以中天下而立謹身率物惟誠和之
===
治是圖焉定四海之民敬德祈天惟撫綏之政
是修焉吁洛邑之不徒作也如此人君於洛其
可以易而為之哉周公之意深矣抑洛邑之作
豈真舍鎬京之舊而慕新造之樂耶蓋將有所
寧也是意也周公知之召公知之恐成王之不
盡知也故周有中乂之言召復繼以自服土中
焉召肯以周固言之乃更其說以自異耶故周
公曰襄我二人汝有合哉噫此二公之所以同
心輔政也
punctuated: 基之定之，王城中建，足以來百辟之朝會，體勢何尊嚴也！趨事以民，經之營之，下都外拓，足以奠四民之居止，規模何宏遠也！是豈麗宮室而事游幸哉？亦豈輕改作而圖壯觀哉？蓋皇矣上帝，天子配之，自是可以體元居正，臨萬國於覆幬之下，「天維顯思」，仰之不愧也。天神地祇，天子祭之，自是可以執圭奉幣，舉大禮於郊社之時，「神之格思」，祭之不黷也。至若和恒居師，天子主之，自是可以中天下而立，謹身率物，惟誠和之治是圖焉；定四海之民，敬德祈天，惟撫綏之政是修焉。吁！洛邑之不徒作也如此，人君於洛，其可以易而為之哉？周公之意深矣！抑洛邑之作，豈真舍鎬京之舊而慕新造之樂耶？蓋將有所寧也。是意也，周公知之，召公知之，恐成王之不盡知也。故周有中乂之言，召復繼以自服土中焉。召肯以周固言之，乃更其說以自異耶？故周公曰：「襄我二人，汝有合哉！」噫！此二公之所以同心輔政也。
translation_en:
…laying its foundations and establishing it, the royal city was built at the center, sufficient to draw the many lords to court assemblies. How imposing and majestic its configuration! Mobilizing the people for the work, planning and constructing it, the lower capital expanded outward, sufficient to settle the four occupational groups in their dwellings. How grand and far-reaching its design! Was this merely to embellish palaces and indulge in pleasure excursions? Was it to undertake alterations lightly and seek a magnificent spectacle?

August is the Lord on High, and the Son of Heaven serves as his counterpart. From this seat he could embody the primal principle and occupy his rightful position, presiding over the myriad states beneath Heaven’s covering canopy. “Heaven is manifestly illustrious”: he could look up to it without shame. The Son of Heaven sacrifices to the spirits of Heaven and Earth. From this seat he could hold the jade tablet and present silk offerings, performing the great rites at the suburban sacrifices and the altar of soil. “The spirits arrive”: he could sacrifice to them without irreverence. As for bringing harmony and constancy to the resident multitudes [?], the Son of Heaven presides over them. From this seat he could stand at the center of all under Heaven, be circumspect in his own conduct, and lead others by example, seeking only government marked by sincerity and harmony. He could settle the people within the Four Seas, revere virtue and pray to Heaven, and practice only government that comforts and pacifies.

Ah! Such were the purposes for which Luoyi was built; it was no idle undertaking. Could a ruler treat his responsibilities at Luo lightly? The Duke of Zhou’s intention was profound! Yet was the construction of Luoyi really a matter of abandoning the old capital at Haojing and coveting the pleasures of a newly built city? Rather, it was intended to provide a place of settled peace. The Duke of Zhou understood this intention, and the Duke of Shao understood it; they feared that King Cheng did not fully understand it. Thus Zhou spoke of governing from the center, and Shao followed this with words about exercising authority from the center of the land. Would Shao, merely because Zhou had already spoken of it, alter his explanation to distinguish himself? Thus the Duke of Zhou said: “In the assisting work of us two, may you act in accord! [?]” Ah! This is how these two dukes assisted the government with a common purpose.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詩
江漢湯湯武夫洸洸經營四方告成于王
四方旣平王國庶定時靡有爭王心載
寧江漢之滸王命召虎式辟四方徹我
疆土匪疚匪棘王國來極于疆于理至
于南海王命召虎來旬來宣文武受命
召公維翰無曰予小子召公是似肇敏
戎公用錫爾祉釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣告
于文人錫山土田于周受命自召祖命
===
同□□官教諭莊批長題難於包括此作明白
整齊且深得詩人稱美召穆公之旨佳士也健
羨健羨
同考試官教諭江批大雅題場中作者多體認
失真僅得此篇理明辭暢其葩經中之傑然者是
用錄出
考試官學正何批分截明白詞語平正戛異諸作
考試官教授劉批不枯不腴雅義正如此
punctuated:
詩

江漢湯湯，武夫洸洸。經營四方，告成于王。四方旣平，王國庶定。時靡有爭，王心載寧。江漢之滸，王命召虎：式辟四方，徹我疆土。匪疚匪棘，王國來極。于疆于理，至于南海。王命召虎：來旬來宣。文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣，告于文人。錫山土田，于周受命，自召祖命。

同□□官教諭莊批：長題難於包括，此作明白整齊，且深得詩人稱美召穆公之旨，佳士也。健羨健羨！

同考試官教諭江批：大雅題，場中作者多體認失真，僅得此篇理明辭暢，其葩經中之傑然者，是用錄出。

考試官學正何批：分截明白，詞語平正，戛異諸作。

考試官教授劉批：不枯不腴，雅義正如此。
translation_en:
Book of Odes

The Jiang and Han rivers flow in mighty torrents; the warriors are valiant. They bring order to the four quarters and report their success to the king. The four quarters are now pacified; the royal realm may at last be settled. There is no longer any strife, and the king’s heart is at peace. On the banks of the Jiang and Han, the king commands Shao Hu: “Open up the four quarters and demarcate our territory. Neither afflict the people nor act precipitately; let the royal realm be their standard. Establish boundaries and put the land in order, as far as the southern sea.” The king commands Shao Hu: “Go forth to inspect and proclaim my rule. When Kings Wen and Wu received the Mandate, the Duke of Shao was their supporting pillar. Do not say, ‘I am but a young man’; emulate the Duke of Shao. You have begun diligently to accomplish your great work, and for this I bestow blessings upon you. I grant you a jade-handled libation ladle and a vessel of black-millet sacrificial wine: announce this to your cultivated ancestors. I grant you hills, lands, and fields. Receive your charge at Zhou, following the charge given to your ancestor, the Duke of Shao.”
