Comment by Zhuang, Instructor and Associate [??] Official: “A long topic is difficult to encompass fully. This composition is clear and well ordered, and it also profoundly grasps the poet’s intention in praising Duke Mu of Shao. This is a worthy scholar. How greatly I admire him!”

Comment by Jiang, Instructor and Associate Examiner: “On this topic from the Greater Odes, most candidates in the examination hall failed to grasp the true meaning. Only this essay was found to have lucid reasoning and fluent expression. It is an outstanding piece on the Book of Odes, and for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”

Comment by He, Instructor and Examiner: “The divisions are clear, and the wording balanced and sound. It stands distinctly apart from the other compositions.”

Comment by Liu, Professor and Examiner: “Neither dry nor overrich: this is precisely the meaning of the Odes.”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詩人美世臣歷建其功必詳述王者命之切而
報之厚也蓋建功者臣之職報功者君之禮也
君臣兩盡其道非盛世其能然哉昔宣王命召
穆公平淮南之夷詩人美之意謂惟我召虎受
命南征瞻彼江漢之水湯湯然而深廣率此武
夫之衆洸洸然而奮揚來求來鋪于以經營乎
四方不矜不伐將以告成于天子當是時王國
靡定以四方之未平也今旣平矣王國於是而
大定焉王心匪寧以天下之有爭也今靡爭矣
===
===
王心於是而載寧焉若此者皆召虎之功也江
漢旣平王又命召虎視四方之侵地未闢要皆
闢之以復其舊按疆土之徹法弗行要皆徹之
以行其法固非病彼之民亦非急我之欲也但
使其來取正於王國合人心於一統耳於是遂
疆之而至於南海則大界之定截然矣理之而
止於海邦則溝塗之分井然矣若此者亦召虎
之功也然豈無所激勸哉蓋王初命召虎來此
江漢之滸國事則徧治也王命則宣布也乃謂
punctuated: 詩人美世臣歷建其功，必詳述王者命之切而報之厚也。蓋建功者臣之職，報功者君之禮也。君臣兩盡其道，非盛世其能然哉？昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之夷，詩人美之，意謂惟我召虎受命南征，瞻彼江漢之水，湯湯然而深廣；率此武夫之衆，洸洸然而奮揚。來求來鋪，于以經營乎四方；不矜不伐，將以告成于天子。當是時，王國靡定，以四方之未平也；今旣平矣，王國於是而大定焉。王心匪寧，以天下之有爭也；今靡爭矣，王心於是而載寧焉。若此者，皆召虎之功也。江漢旣平，王又命召虎視四方之侵地未闢，要皆闢之以復其舊；按疆土之徹法弗行，要皆徹之以行其法。固非病彼之民，亦非急我之欲也，但使其來取正於王國，合人心於一統耳。於是遂疆之而至於南海，則大界之定截然矣；理之而止於海邦，則溝塗之分井然矣。若此者，亦召虎之功也。然豈無所激勸哉？蓋王初命召虎來此江漢之滸，國事則徧治也，王命則宣布也，乃謂：
translation_en:
When the poet praises a hereditary minister for his successive achievements, he invariably recounts in detail the urgency of the king’s charge to him and the generosity of his rewards. For achieving merit is the minister’s duty, and rewarding merit is the ruler’s proper observance of ritual. Could ruler and minister each fully fulfill his proper role except in an age of flourishing government?

Long ago, King Xuan ordered Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the Yi peoples south of the Huai River. The poet praised him, conveying this meaning: Our Shao Hu received the command to campaign southward. He gazed upon the waters of the Jiang and Han, surging, deep, and broad; he led his host of warriors, martial and spirited. They came to seek out and deploy, thereby bringing order to the four quarters. Neither conceited nor boastful, he would report the completion of his task to the Son of Heaven. At that time, the royal realm was unsettled because the four quarters had not been pacified. Now that they were pacified, the royal realm attained great stability. The king’s heart was uneasy because there was strife in the world. Now that strife had ceased, the king’s heart at last found peace. All these were Shao Hu’s achievements.

Once the Jiang and Han region had been pacified, the king further ordered Shao Hu to inspect lands in the four quarters that had been encroached upon and not yet reclaimed: all were to be reclaimed and restored to their former condition. He was to investigate territories where the che system of land taxation was not being practiced: all were to implement it in accordance with its rules. This certainly was not to afflict those people, nor to press for the satisfaction of his own desires. It was simply to have them take their standard of correct government from the royal realm and unite the people’s hearts under a single rule. Thus Shao Hu established boundaries as far as the southern sea, clearly fixing the great territorial divisions. He ordered the land as far as the coastal states, systematically laying out the divisions of ditches and roads. These, too, were Shao Hu’s achievements.

Yet could he have lacked any source of encouragement? When the king first commanded Shao Hu to come to the banks of the Jiang and Han, affairs of state were to be attended to throughout the region, and royal commands were to be proclaimed. He then said: …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昔我祖文武受命于天惟汝祖召公爲周之翰
今汝勿曰予小子故也但當似汝召公可焉汝
能開敏其功果無愧於召公之維翰則我當錫
汝以福必不靳於文武之褒崇然豈徒空言爲
哉今王賜以策命念其祀先思孝也則釐爾圭
瓚秬鬯一卣使得以祀其先祖知其封邑未廣
也則告于文人錫山土田使得以廣其封邑然
命不苟受必使往岐周興王之地而受之往不
徒行必從祖康公受命之所以寵之一以昭報
===
賜之厚恩非出於今也一以表世臣之賢功無
替於先也吁臣有功而不負君之命君有賜而
不負臣之功此有周之所以中興也歟嗟夫君
臣相遇自古爲難周至宣王內脩外攘志在恢
復誠可謂有道之賢君矣時則有若吉甫方叔
召穆公者出南征北伐各獻其功亦皆名世之
賢佐也噫雲龍相從風虎相就中興之盛是豈
偶然者哉
載戢干戈載櫜弓矢
punctuated:
「昔我祖文武受命于天，惟汝祖召公爲周之翰。今汝勿曰予小子故也，但當似汝召公可焉。汝能開敏其功，果無愧於召公之維翰，則我當錫汝以福，必不靳於文武之褒崇。」然豈徒空言爲哉？今王賜以策命，念其祀先思孝也，則釐爾圭瓚、秬鬯一卣，使得以祀其先祖；知其封邑未廣也，則告于文人，錫山土田，使得以廣其封邑。然命不苟受，必使往岐周興王之地而受之；往不徒行，必從祖康公受命之。所以寵之，一以昭報賜之厚恩非出於今也，一以表世臣之賢功無替於先也。吁！臣有功而不負君之命，君有賜而不負臣之功，此有周之所以中興也歟！嗟夫！君臣相遇，自古爲難。周至宣王，內脩外攘，志在恢復，誠可謂有道之賢君矣。時則有若吉甫、方叔、召穆公者出，南征北伐，各獻其功，亦皆名世之賢佐也。噫！雲龍相從，風虎相就，中興之盛，是豈偶然者哉！

載戢干戈，載櫜弓矢。
translation_en:
…“Formerly, my ancestors, Kings Wen and Wu, received Heaven’s mandate, and your ancestor, the Duke of Shao, was a pillar of Zhou. Now do not excuse yourself by saying, ‘I am but a young man.’ You need only emulate your Duke of Shao. If you can energetically advance your achievements [?] and truly prove worthy of the Duke of Shao’s service as a pillar of the dynasty, I shall bestow blessings upon you, certainly no less generously than Kings Wen and Wu bestowed their honors.” But could these have been mere empty words? Now the king grants him a written investiture. Mindful of his desire to sacrifice to his ancestors and express his filial devotion, he declares, “I bestow upon you a jade libation ladle and one vessel of fragrant black-millet wine,” enabling him to sacrifice to his ancestors. Knowing that his fief is not yet extensive, the king announces this to the cultivated ancestor and bestows mountains and fields, enabling him to enlarge his fief. Yet the charge must not be received casually: he must go to Qizhou, the place where the royal house arose, to receive it. Nor is this journey undertaken without purpose: he must receive the charge in accordance with his ancestor, Duke Kang [?]. These honors serve, first, to show that the generous favor expressed in these rewards did not originate only in the present age; and, second, to demonstrate that the worthy achievements of a hereditary servant have not declined from those of his forebears. Ah! The minister achieves merit and does not betray his ruler’s charge; the ruler bestows rewards and does not fail to recognize his minister’s achievements. Was this not how Zhou attained its restoration?

Alas! Since antiquity, it has been difficult for a ruler and minister to find their fitting counterparts. When Zhou reached the reign of King Xuan, he cultivated good government within and repelled enemies without, setting his heart on restoration. He may truly be called a worthy ruler who possessed the Way. At that time, men such as Jifu, Fang Shu, and Duke Mu of Shao came forward, campaigning south and north, each contributing his achievements. They too were worthy assistants renowned in their age. Ah! Clouds follow the dragon, and winds draw near the tiger. Could the splendor of this restoration have come about by chance?

“Then they put away shields and halberds; then they cased their bows and arrows.”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批寫出武王偃武之意宛
在目宜錄之以式學者
同考試官教諭江批作此題者多不就巡狩上
說且綴緝陳語可厭晚得此篇形容武王巡狩偃武
之意親切可愛宜冠本房
考試官學正何批詞贍氣充必有學之士也允
宜高薦
考試官教授劉批得頌體
===
王者巡狩而藏乎武備正欲以偃乎武事也蓋
用武非聖人之得已也周王巡狩而欲偃武焉
武備安得而不藏之哉此巡狩而朝會祭告之
樂歌也其意若謂非武無以定天下徒武無以
致太平彼當陳師牧野之時固嘗稱干而比戈
矣今朝會一行而諸侯聽命干戈其可以弗戢
乎會兵孟津之日固嘗張弓而挾矢矣今祭告
一舉而百神受職弓矢其可以弗櫜乎於是大
開明堂渙頒號令意以干戈雖堅且利也自今
punctuated:
黃佐

同考試官教諭莊批：寫出武王偃武之意，宛在目，宜錄之以式學者。

同考試官教諭江批：作此題者多不就巡狩上說，且綴緝陳語，可厭。晚得此篇，形容武王巡狩偃武之意，親切可愛，宜冠本房。

考試官學正何批：詞贍氣充，必有學之士也，允宜高薦。

考試官教授劉批：得頌體。

王者巡狩而藏乎武備，正欲以偃乎武事也。蓋用武非聖人之得已也。周王巡狩而欲偃武焉，武備安得而不藏之哉？此巡狩而朝會祭告之樂歌也。其意若謂：非武無以定天下，徒武無以致太平。彼當陳師牧野之時，固嘗稱干而比戈矣。今朝會一行，而諸侯聽命，干戈其可以弗戢乎？會兵孟津之日，固嘗張弓而挾矢矣。今祭告一舉，而百神受職，弓矢其可以弗櫜乎？於是大開明堂，渙頒號令，意以干戈雖堅且利也，自今
translation_en:
Huang Zuo

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: It depicts King Wu’s intention to lay warfare to rest as vividly as if it were before our eyes. It should be included as a model for students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Most who write on this topic fail to discuss it in terms of the royal inspection tour, and merely stitch together stale phrases—a tiresome practice. This essay came to hand late; its depiction of King Wu’s intention to lay warfare to rest during his inspection tour is apt and pleasing. It should rank first in this examining room.

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: Rich in expression and full of vigor: its author must be a man of learning. He certainly deserves a high recommendation.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: It captures the style of a sacrificial hymn.

When a king goes on an inspection tour and puts away his military equipment, his very purpose is to lay warfare to rest. For a sage resorts to arms only when he has no alternative. When the king of Zhou went on his inspection tour intending to lay warfare to rest, how could he fail to put away his military equipment? This is the ceremonial song for the court assembly and sacrificial announcement during that inspection tour. Its meaning seems to be this: without military force, there is no way to settle the realm; through military force alone, there is no way to achieve supreme peace. When the troops were arrayed at Muye, shields were indeed raised and dagger-axes drawn up in ranks. Now that the court assembly has been held and the regional lords obey his commands, how could shields and dagger-axes remain unstored? On the day the troops assembled at Mengjin, bows were indeed drawn and arrows held ready. Now that the sacrificial announcement has been made and the hundred spirits have received their duties, how could bows and arrows remain uncase​d? Thereupon he opened wide the Hall of Enlightenment and broadly promulgated his commands, conveying this intention: though shields and dagger-axes are stout and sharp, from this time onward …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以始藏諸府庫毋復稱之比之以擾吾民弓矢
雖強且鈞也自是而後抗諸鞬服勿復張焉挾
焉以方吾命干戈戢之非於鑠之師終於弛而
弗張誠以大統旣集尚文不尚武也於此不戢
則武流於黷矣何以慰商民之宿望哉弓矢櫜
之非虎賁之士恃其安而忘危誠以四海旣清
耀德不耀兵也於此不櫜則兵幾於窮矣何以
昭我周之新命哉吁用武於天下未平之初固
王者之大義偃武於天下旣平之後尤王者之
===
至仁仁義並行文教斯舉此武王所以為受命
之聖君也天其不子之乎大抵事有定理兵無
常形時乎用則用時乎藏則藏聖人何容心於
其間哉一於用秦皇之黷武也一於藏晉武之
銷兵也之二君者胥失之矣乃若唐之太宗比
迹湯武其庶幾乎惜夫殿廷非習射之所也噫
武王其盡美者耶
春秋
荆人來聘〔莊公二十三年〕
punctuated:
以始，藏諸府庫，毋復稱之、比之，以擾吾民。弓矢雖強且鈞也，自是而後，抗諸鞬服，勿復張焉、挾焉，以方吾命。干戈戢之，非於鑠之師終於弛而弗張，誠以大統旣集，尚文不尚武也。於此不戢，則武流於黷矣，何以慰商民之宿望哉？弓矢櫜之，非虎賁之士恃其安而忘危，誠以四海旣清，耀德不耀兵也。於此不櫜，則兵幾於窮矣，何以昭我周之新命哉？吁！用武於天下未平之初，固王者之大義；偃武於天下旣平之後，尤王者之至仁。仁義並行，文教斯舉，此武王所以為受命之聖君也。天其不子之乎？大抵事有定理，兵無常形，時乎用則用，時乎藏則藏，聖人何容心於其間哉？一於用，秦皇之黷武也；一於藏，晉武之銷兵也。之二君者，胥失之矣。乃若唐之太宗，比迹湯武，其庶幾乎？惜夫殿廷非習射之所也！噫！武王其盡美者耶？

春秋

荆人來聘〔莊公二十三年〕
translation_en:
…from this time onward, store them in the government repositories. No longer raise the shields and array the spears to trouble my people. Though the bows and arrows are strong and well balanced, henceforth put them away in their cases and quivers. No longer draw the bows or grasp the arrows in defiance of my command. To put away shields and spears does not mean that the splendid army is finally to relax and never again make ready. Rather, now that rule over the realm has been secured, civil culture is to be esteemed above military force. If weapons are not put away at this point, warfare will degenerate into wanton aggression. How then could the long-held hopes of the people of Shang be fulfilled? To encase bows and arrows does not mean that the tiger-brave warriors are to rely on present security and forget danger. Rather, now that all within the Four Seas has been pacified, virtue is to be displayed, rather than arms. If weapons are not encased at this point, military force will verge on being used to exhaustion. How then could the new Mandate of our Zhou be made manifest? Ah! To employ military force when the realm has yet to be pacified is indeed the great righteousness of a true king; to lay down arms once the realm is at peace is especially the utmost benevolence of a true king. When benevolence and righteousness proceed together, moral and cultural instruction flourishes. This is why King Wu was a sage ruler who received the Mandate. Would Heaven not treat him as its son? In general, affairs have fixed principles, but military action has no constant form. When the time calls for using arms, use them; when it calls for storing them, store them. How could a sage interpose his own preferences? To insist solely on using arms is the First Emperor of Qin’s wanton militarism; to insist solely on storing them is Emperor Wu of Jin’s abolition of armaments. Both these rulers erred. As for Emperor Taizong of Tang, whose deeds approached those of Tang and King Wu, did he perhaps come close to the ideal? Yet regrettably, the palace court was no place for archery practice! Ah! Was King Wu not perfect in every respect?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“Men of Jing came on a diplomatic visit.” 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang〕

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
盧金潤
考試官學正何批春秋義謹嚴如此作者絕少
考試官教授劉批題本胡傳作者體認欠眞
下筆多牽滯此作明白簡瑩是用錄出
春秋於外交內而進之嘉其事之善而原其類
之善也此荆之聘魯遂以人稱聖人樂與人爲
善而重絕人之意寓焉且荆楚嘗僭號不臣矣
又嘗猾夏不恭矣春秋狄之宜也今而遣使聘
魯遂以人稱所謂謹華夷之辨內夏外夷義安
===
在乎蓋中國諸侯之事朝聘之禮爲重也荆楚
一旦革其固陋求以自通駟牡之駕不遠千里
玉帛之將恭奠兩觀禽父之澤慰於仰止者不
少禮樂之化得於觀感者必多非如入蔡伐鄭
狼貪蠶食亂我中華之無厭也借曰假禮行詐
不可測焉聖人樂與人爲善不追其旣往不逆
其將來與其潔而與其進以是心至斯受之矣
況先王封建之國聖賢之後不遺也荆楚上世
祝融垂裕熊繹襲封苗裔之昌延於百世茅土
punctuated:
盧金潤

考試官學正何批：春秋義謹嚴如此，作者絕少。

考試官教授劉批：題本胡傳，作者體認欠眞，下筆多牽滯。此作明白簡瑩，是用錄出。

春秋於外交內而進之，嘉其事之善，而原其類之善也。此荆之聘魯，遂以人稱，聖人樂與人爲善而重絕人之意寓焉。且荆楚嘗僭號不臣矣，又嘗猾夏不恭矣，春秋狄之，宜也。今而遣使聘魯，遂以人稱，所謂謹華夷之辨、內夏外夷，義安在乎？蓋中國諸侯之事，朝聘之禮爲重也。荆楚一旦革其固陋，求以自通，駟牡之駕不遠千里，玉帛之將恭奠兩觀，禽父之澤慰於仰止者不少，禮樂之化得於觀感者必多，非如入蔡伐鄭，狼貪蠶食，亂我中華之無厭也。借曰假禮行詐，不可測焉，聖人樂與人爲善，不追其旣往，不逆其將來，與其潔而與其進，以是心至，斯受之矣。況先王封建之國，聖賢之後不遺也。荆楚上世，祝融垂裕，熊繹襲封，苗裔之昌延於百世，茅土
translation_en:
Lu Jinrun

Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: Very few writers produce interpretations of the Spring and Autumn Annals as exacting and rigorous as this.

Examiner Liu, School Director, comments: The topic derives from Hu’s Commentary. Writers often fail to grasp its meaning fully, and their writing becomes strained and impeded. This composition is clear, concise, and polished, and has therefore been selected for inclusion.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals advances an outsider who establishes relations with the inner realm, it commends the goodness of his deeds and traces the goodness of his lineage. In this instance, when Jing paid a diplomatic visit to Lu, it was accordingly designated by the term “men.” Herein lies the sage’s willingness to help others do good and his reluctance to cut them off. Jing, or Chu, had previously usurped a royal title and refused allegiance; it had also disturbed the Xia states and acted disrespectfully. It was fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should treat it as barbarian. Yet now, upon its sending an envoy to visit Lu, it was designated by the term “men.” Where, then, is the principle of carefully distinguishing Hua from Yi, treating the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders?

Among the affairs of the lords of the central states, court audiences and diplomatic visits hold particular ritual importance. Once Jing-Chu abandoned its ingrained narrowness and sought to establish relations, its teams of four stallions thought nothing of travelling a thousand li, and its offerings of jade and silk were respectfully laid before the paired gate towers. Many who looked up in reverence found solace in the beneficent legacy of Qinfu; surely much was gained through observing and responding to the transforming influence of rites and music. This was unlike its incursions into Cai and attacks upon Zheng, when, ravenous as a wolf and encroaching like a silkworm, it disrupted our central realm without ever being satisfied. Even supposing that it used ritual as a pretext for deceit, its intentions being unfathomable, the sage was willing to help others do good. He did not pursue their past faults or prejudge their future conduct; he approved their purification and their advancement. If they came with such a disposition, he accepted them.

Moreover, among the states enfeoffed by the former kings, the descendants of sages and worthies were not neglected. Among Jing-Chu’s distant ancestors, Zhurong bequeathed a rich legacy, and Xiong Yi inherited an enfeoffment. Their flourishing descendants continued for a hundred generations; the thatch and earth of enfeoffment …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之邦列於五等元德顯功通于周室若夫泯衣
裳冠帶視之百辟也何殊豈若西戎北狄狼子
野心非我族類之可比也借曰以夷變夏方且
膺之然聖人猶不欲絕其類不使與中國同不
使與夷狄均推可遠而引可來苟可善焉斯進
之矣故特書曰荆人來聘傳曰嘉其慕義自通
故進之也又曰諸夏之變於夷者故書法如此
聖人宅心忠恕於茲不具見乎雖然聖人宅心
雖恕而立法則嚴後世之君能以聖人之心為
===
心則與天地相似凡變於夷者叛則懲其不恪
而威之以刑來則嘉其慕義而接之以禮邇人
安遠者服矣噫春秋所以為天子之事百王之
法為萬世之準繩也歟
盟于召陵僖公四年公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛
侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城 諸侯遂救許僖
公六年
李卿
考試官學正何 批體貼傳意辭不費而意
punctuated:
之邦，列於五等，元德顯功，通于周室。若夫泯衣裳冠帶，視之百辟也何殊？豈若西戎北狄，狼子野心，非我族類之可比也？借曰以夷變夏，方且膺之，然聖人猶不欲絕其類，不使與中國同，不使與夷狄均，推可遠而引可來，苟可善焉，斯進之矣。故特書曰：「荆人來聘。」傳曰：「嘉其慕義自通，故進之也。」又曰：「諸夏之變於夷者。」故書法如此。聖人宅心忠恕，於茲不具見乎？雖然，聖人宅心雖恕，而立法則嚴。後世之君能以聖人之心為心，則與天地相似。凡變於夷者，叛則懲其不恪，而威之以刑；來則嘉其慕義，而接之以禮。邇人安，遠者服矣。噫！春秋所以為天子之事、百王之法，為萬世之準繩也歟！
盟于召陵，僖公四年。公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。諸侯遂救許，僖公六年。
李卿
考試官學正何批：體貼傳意，辭不費而意
translation_en:
…a state enfeoffed with thatch and soil, ranked among the five grades of nobility, whose great virtue and illustrious achievements were known to the royal house of Zhou. As for their robes, caps, and girdles [?], how did they differ in appearance from the other lords? How could they be compared with the Western Rong and Northern Di, with their wolfish hearts, who are not of our kind? Suppose it is said that they were transforming the Xia through barbarian ways and were therefore about to be chastised. Yet the Sage still did not wish to cut off their kind altogether. He neither treated them as identical with the Central States nor placed them on the same footing as the barbarians. They could be pushed away or drawn near; if they were capable of goodness, he advanced them.
Thus he specifically wrote: “The men of Jing came on a diplomatic visit.” The Commentary says: “He commended their admiration for righteousness and their initiative in establishing relations, and therefore advanced them.” It also says: “Those of the Xia states who had changed into barbarians.” Hence this manner of recording the event. Is not the Sage’s disposition of conscientiousness and reciprocity fully apparent here? Nevertheless, although the Sage’s disposition was forbearing, his establishment of rules was strict. If rulers of later ages could take the Sage’s heart as their own, they would resemble Heaven and Earth. Whenever those who had adopted barbarian ways rebelled, the rulers would punish their lack of respect and overawe them with penalties; when they came, the rulers would commend their admiration for righteousness and receive them with ritual propriety. Those nearby would be at peace, and those far away would submit. Ah! Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals constitutes the business of the Son of Heaven, the law for the hundred kings, and the standard for all ages?
“A covenant was made at Shaoling”—the fourth year of Duke Xi. “The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao to attack Zheng and besiege Xincheng. The lords then went to the rescue of Xu”—the sixth year of Duke Xi.
Li Qing.
Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: “Closely attuned to the meaning of the Commentary; the wording is economical, while the meaning…”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
定蓋嘗精於是經者
考試官教授劉批說出聖人與桓之意整嚴
可觀讀之令人起敬
春秋旣予伯主得用師待敵之道尤予伯主得
討罪卹患之義此見齊桓召陵之師討鄭救許
之事所以爲善也且夫盟者諸侯之所不得爲
也春秋於齊桓召陵之盟何以予之耶蓋自荆
楚伐鄭其勢浸强于時齊桓主伯志在攘夷八
國南征楚人畏懾若可乘勝一鼓而直搗其墟
===
===
矣桓則以爲大兵之後狃於一勝而不知止如
萬全之道何楚人悔禍屈完請成若可以俘執
□問而釁之鼓矣桓則以爲敵旣來歸不招之
以禮而一其心如柔遠之道何於是載戢干戈
而退舍召陵之地載敦玉帛而徼惠屈完之盟
於此見師雖强桓公能以律用之而不暴楚已
服桓公能以禮下之而不驕庶幾王者之師矣
春秋書盟于召陵于次陘之下傳曰序桓績也
聖人予桓之意明矣至若兵者聖人之所甚重
punctuated:
定，蓋嘗精於是經者。

考試官教授劉批：說出聖人與桓之意，整嚴可觀，讀之令人起敬。

春秋旣予伯主得用師待敵之道，尤予伯主得討罪卹患之義。此見齊桓召陵之師、討鄭救許之事，所以爲善也。且夫盟者，諸侯之所不得爲也。春秋於齊桓召陵之盟，何以予之耶？蓋自荆楚伐鄭，其勢浸强。于時齊桓主伯，志在攘夷，八國南征，楚人畏懾，若可乘勝一鼓而直搗其墟矣。桓則以爲，大兵之後，狃於一勝而不知止，如萬全之道何？楚人悔禍，屈完請成，若可以俘執□問而釁之鼓矣。桓則以爲，敵旣來歸，不招之以禮而一其心，如柔遠之道何？於是載戢干戈，而退舍召陵之地；載敦玉帛，而徼惠屈完之盟。於此見師雖强，桓公能以律用之而不暴；楚已服，桓公能以禮下之而不驕，庶幾王者之師矣。春秋書「盟于召陵」于「次陘」之下，傳曰：「序桓績也。」聖人予桓之意明矣。至若兵者，聖人之所甚重
translation_en:
…definite; surely this is someone who has studied this Classic deeply.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: He brings out the Sage’s intention in approving Huan. The composition is orderly and rigorous, worthy of attention; reading it inspires respect.

The Spring and Autumn Annals approves the hegemon’s grasp of the proper way to employ armies and deal with enemies; still more does it approve his grasp of the righteousness of punishing wrongdoing and relieving distress. This shows why Duke Huan of Qi’s campaign at Shaoling and his actions in attacking Zheng and rescuing Xu were deemed good. Now, making covenants was something the feudal lords were not entitled to do. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve Duke Huan of Qi’s covenant at Shaoling? Ever since Jing-Chu attacked Zheng, its power had gradually grown. At that time Duke Huan of Qi held the hegemony and aimed to repel the barbarians. Eight states marched south, and the people of Chu were terrified. It seemed possible to press the advantage, advance at a single beat of the drums, and strike directly at their capital. Huan, however, considered: after a great military expedition, if one becomes complacent over a single victory and does not know when to stop, what becomes of the way to ensure complete security?

The people of Chu regretted the calamity, and Qu Wan requested peace. It seemed possible to seize him, subject him to questioning [?], and smear the drums with his blood. Huan, however, considered: when the enemy has already come to submit, if one does not receive him with ritual courtesy and thereby secure his wholehearted allegiance, what becomes of the way to conciliate distant peoples? Thus he put away the weapons and withdrew to encamp at Shaoling; he generously supplied jade and silk offerings and sought the favor of a covenant with Qu Wan. Here we see that, although his army was powerful, Duke Huan could employ it with discipline and without violence; although Chu had submitted, Duke Huan could defer to it with ritual courtesy and without arrogance. His army came close to being that of a true king. The Spring and Autumn Annals records “made a covenant at Shaoling” after “encamped at Xing.” The Commentary says: “This sets forth Huan’s achievements.” The Sage’s intention in approving Huan is clear. As for warfare, it is something to which the Sage attaches the greatest weight…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也春秋於齊桓伐鄭救許之師何以予之耶蓋
自鄭與楚合首止逃盟是時齊桓憂之急於討
貳兵連六國執詞伐鄭宜若振槁然桓則以爲
妤攻樂殺於罪爲大是可忍心爲之哉許受楚
攻朝不保暮宜若倒懸然桓則以爲救患分災
於禮爲急是可坐視不爲哉於是寧遺力而不
盡新城之下卽解兵而遠赴許人之圍於此見
鄭可討桓公以義討之而不暴許可救桓公以
義救之而不緩庶幾君子之道矣春秋書救許
===
於伐鄭圍新城之下傳曰善之尤也聖人予桓
之心亦著矣吁盟非美事而召陵之盟在春秋
所宜有兵本凶器而伐鄭救許之兵在春秋不
可無然則聖人之予之豈得已耶大抵伯者莫
難於立功功旣成則其志驕志驕則其行荒行
荒則其業怠故陽穀之會于卞之會肆於寵樂
緣陵之城于匡之次楚之伐黃狄之侵衞忽於
簡書而視召陵之盟救許之兵不可同日語矣
先儒謂其量淺而器不宏又曰假之不久而遽
punctuated:
也。春秋於齊桓伐鄭救許之師，何以予之耶？蓋自鄭與楚合，首止逃盟，是時齊桓憂之，急於討貳，兵連六國，執詞伐鄭，宜若振槁。然桓則以爲妤攻樂殺，於罪爲大，是可忍心爲之哉？許受楚攻，朝不保暮，宜若倒懸。然桓則以爲救患分災，於禮爲急，是可坐視不爲哉？於是寧遺力而不盡新城之下，卽解兵而遠赴許人之圍。於此見鄭可討，桓公以義討之而不暴；許可救，桓公以義救之而不緩，庶幾君子之道矣。春秋書救許於伐鄭圍新城之下，傳曰：「善之尤也。」聖人予桓之心亦著矣。
吁！盟非美事，而召陵之盟在春秋所宜有；兵本凶器，而伐鄭救許之兵在春秋不可無。然則聖人之予之，豈得已耶？大抵伯者莫難於立功，功旣成則其志驕，志驕則其行荒，行荒則其業怠。故陽穀之會、于卞之會，肆於寵樂；緣陵之城、于匡之次、楚之伐黃、狄之侵衞，忽於簡書，而視召陵之盟、救許之兵，不可同日語矣。先儒謂其量淺而器不宏，又曰：「假之不久而遽
translation_en:
…indeed. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve of Duke Huan of Qi’s campaign against Zheng and his relief of Xu? Ever since Zheng had allied with Chu and evaded the covenant at Shouzhi, Duke Huan had been troubled by this and eager to punish its divided allegiance. Joining the forces of six states, he advanced against Zheng with declared grounds for punishment; it should have been as easy as shaking down withered leaves. Yet Duke Huan considered delighting in attacks [?] and taking pleasure in killing to be grave offenses. Could he harden his heart and do such things? Xu was under attack by Chu: safe in the morning, it could not be sure of surviving until evening, and its plight was like that of someone hanging upside down. Duke Huan considered rescuing those in distress and sharing the burden of calamity urgent obligations of ritual propriety. Could he sit and watch without acting? Thus, rather than expend all his strength beneath the walls of Xincheng, he withdrew his troops and marched far away to relieve the siege of Xu. Here we see that, although Zheng deserved punishment, Duke Huan punished it according to righteousness without brutality; and, since Xu deserved rescue, he rescued it according to righteousness without delay. He thus came close to the way of the gentleman. The Spring and Autumn Annals records the relief of Xu after the attack on Zheng and the siege of Xincheng. The commentary says: “This was an especially good deed.” The Sage’s intention to approve of Duke Huan is also evident here.
Ah! Covenants are no splendid thing, yet the covenant at Shaoling was fitting for the Spring and Autumn period. Weapons are inherently instruments of ill omen, yet the campaign against Zheng and the relief of Xu could not be dispensed with in that age. Could the Sage, then, have withheld his approval? In general, nothing is harder for a hegemon than establishing achievements. Once his achievements are secured, his ambitions grow arrogant; arrogance leads to dissolute conduct, and dissolute conduct to neglect of his undertakings. Thus, at the meetings at Yanggu and Bian, he indulged in favoritism and pleasure; in the fortification of Yuanling, the encampment at Kuang, Chu’s attack on Huang, and the Di invasion of Wei, he neglected the written calls to duty. These cannot be spoken of in the same breath as the covenant at Shaoling and the relief of Xu. Earlier scholars said that his measure was shallow and his capacity limited. They also said: “He borrowed it for only a short time and then abruptly …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
歸是足以槩桓之顛末矣使其慎終如始而敦
不息之誠則進於王德而不為聖門之所不道
也
禮記
樂者為同禮者為異同則相親異則相敬
樂勝則流禮勝則離合情飾貌者禮樂
之事也禮義立則貴賤等矣樂文同則
上下和矣好惡著則賢不肖别矣刑禁
暴爵舉賢則政均矣仁以愛之義以正
===
之如此則民治行矣
葉孟
同考試官教諭林批說先王用禮樂治民情及民
治行處前後照應明白是宜錄之以式學者
考試官學正何批理明詞順
考試官教授劉批得旨
禮樂異其用而民心所由感禮樂濟其偏而民
化所由成夫禮樂之足以感民也尚矣但不能
無偏勝之弊耳偏而能濟化豈有不成哉且先
punctuated:
歸，是足以槩桓之顛末矣。使其慎終如始，而敦不息之誠，則進於王德，而不為聖門之所不道也。

禮記

樂者為同，禮者為異。同則相親，異則相敬。樂勝則流，禮勝則離。合情飾貌者，禮樂之事也。禮義立則貴賤等矣，樂文同則上下和矣，好惡著則賢不肖别矣，刑禁暴、爵舉賢則政均矣。仁以愛之，義以正之，如此則民治行矣。

葉孟

同考試官教諭林批：說先王用禮樂治民情及民治行處，前後照應明白，是宜錄之以式學者。
考試官學正何批：理明詞順。
考試官教授劉批：得旨。

禮樂異其用，而民心所由感；禮樂濟其偏，而民化所由成。夫禮樂之足以感民也尚矣，但不能無偏勝之弊耳。偏而能濟，化豈有不成哉？且先
translation_en:
…return it: this suffices to summarize Duke Huan’s course from beginning to end. Had he been as careful at the end as at the beginning and cultivated unceasing sincerity, he would have advanced toward the virtue of a true king and would not have been someone whom the followers of the Sage declined to discuss.

Book of Rites (Liji)

Music creates unity; ritual creates distinctions. Unity brings mutual affection; distinctions bring mutual respect. When music predominates, people become unrestrained; when ritual predominates, they become estranged. Bringing feelings together and refining outward deportment are the tasks of ritual and music. When the principles of ritual are established, the noble and the lowly have their proper ranks. When the patterns of music are shared, superiors and inferiors are harmonious. When likes and dislikes are made clear, the worthy are distinguished from the unworthy. When punishments restrain violence and ranks elevate the worthy, government is equitable. Love them through benevolence and correct them through righteousness: in this way, the governance of the people takes effect.

Ye Meng

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: His discussion of how the former kings used ritual and music to regulate the people’s feelings, and of how governance of the people takes effect, connects the beginning and the end clearly. This deserves to be recorded as a model for students.
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: Clear reasoning and fluent expression.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: Grasps the essential meaning.

Ritual and music differ in their functions, yet through them the people’s hearts are moved; ritual and music compensate for each other’s one-sided tendencies, and through them the moral transformation of the people is accomplished. The power of ritual and music to move the people has long been recognized. Yet they cannot escape the drawback of one predominating over the other. If such imbalance can be corrected, how could moral transformation fail to be accomplished? Moreover, first …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
因人情而作禮樂慮其乖而不同也則導以
樂之和而凡聲容節奏之翕然者皆所以統同
也慮其混而無異也則導以禮之序而凡儀文
度數之截然者皆所以辨異也唯統同則情敦
而雍睦之風作矣民不由之而相親乎唯辨異
則分定而侵陵之患息矣民不由之而相敬乎
夫禮樂之有以感民也固如此使樂過於同禮
過於異則偏勝而有流離之弊矣於此將何以
救之亦唯合情於內而救其離之失此樂以和
===
禮之事也飾貌於外而救其流之失此禮以節
樂之事也禮以節樂而禮之義以立則貴賤秩
然其有等矣樂以和禮而樂之文以同則上下
藹然其協和矣賢否無別非所以輔禮樂也賢
者從而好之不肖者從而惡之而賢否曾有不
別乎政事不均非所以輔禮樂也暴者刑禁之
必及賢者爵舉之無遺而政事曾有不均乎然
猶未也仁以愛之使辨異之中一吾心之至誠
□者存義以正之使統同之中一吾心之□□
punctuated: 因人情而作禮樂，慮其乖而不同也，則導以樂之和，而凡聲容節奏之翕然者，皆所以統同也；慮其混而無異也，則導以禮之序，而凡儀文度數之截然者，皆所以辨異也。唯統同，則情敦而雍睦之風作矣，民不由之而相親乎？唯辨異，則分定而侵陵之患息矣，民不由之而相敬乎？夫禮樂之有以感民也，固如此。使樂過於同，禮過於異，則偏勝而有流離之弊矣。於此將何以救之？亦唯合情於內而救其離之失，此樂以和禮之事也；飾貌於外而救其流之失，此禮以節樂之事也。禮以節樂，而禮之義以立，則貴賤秩然其有等矣；樂以和禮，而樂之文以同，則上下藹然其協和矣。賢否無別，非所以輔禮樂也。賢者從而好之，不肖者從而惡之，而賢否曾有不別乎？政事不均，非所以輔禮樂也。暴者刑禁之必及，賢者爵舉之無遺，而政事曾有不均乎？然猶未也。仁以愛之，使辨異之中一吾心之至誠□者存；義以正之，使統同之中一吾心之□□
translation_en:
…created ritual and music in accordance with human feelings. Concerned that these feelings might diverge and fail to unite, they guided them through the harmony of music: the concord of sounds, movements, rhythms, and tempos all served to bring about unity. Concerned that these feelings might become confused and lose their distinctions, they guided them through the ordering of ritual: the clear divisions of ceremonial forms, measures, and prescribed numbers all served to distinguish differences. Through unity, feelings become generous and a spirit of concord arises. Would the people not thereby come to cherish one another? Through distinctions, stations become fixed and the troubles caused by encroachment and oppression cease. Would the people not thereby come to respect one another?

Such indeed is the power of ritual and music to move the people. But if music goes too far in unifying, and ritual too far in distinguishing, one prevails excessively, producing the evils of unrestrained indulgence and estrangement. How are these to be remedied? Simply by bringing feelings together within, one remedies the fault of estrangement: this is the work of music in harmonizing ritual. By refining outward comportment, one remedies the fault of indulgence: this is the work of ritual in regulating music. When ritual regulates music and the principles of ritual are established, noble and lowly take their orderly places in a hierarchy. When music harmonizes ritual and the forms of music are brought into accord, superior and subordinate unite in warm harmony.

Failure to distinguish the worthy from the unworthy cannot support ritual and music. If the worthy are accordingly cherished and the unworthy accordingly disliked, could the worthy and unworthy remain undistinguished? Uneven administration cannot support ritual and music. If punishments and prohibitions invariably reach the violent, and no worthy person is overlooked in conferring rank and promotion, could administration remain uneven? Yet this is still not enough. Through benevolence, love them, so that amid the distinguishing of differences the utmost sincerity of my heart may be preserved [?]; through righteousness, correct them, so that amid the bringing about of unity, my heart’s [two illegible characters] …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
割斷制者在此又以仁義爲禮樂之輔也夫然
則所以救其偏弊者亦無不至矣自是民之漸
被於禮樂者同焉能異自相親而不至於流異
焉能同自相敬而不至於離民治豈有不行哉
至是則化成矣抑先王之作禮樂也效法天地
而又有和敬之德以爲之本故推之於治宜乎
民無不化矣豈唯民化而已哉位天地育萬物
要皆此禮樂之所爲也後世人君不務出此往
往因陋就簡以圖一時之近功耳宋儒歐陽氏
===
有曰三代而上治出於一而禮樂達于天下三
代而下治出於二而禮樂爲虛名者此之謂也
爲治者盍亦知所務哉
故君子與其使食浮於人也寧使人浮於
食
葉孟
同考試官教諭林批寫出君子耻食浮之意儘
是親切他日見用殆非竊禄者矣
考試官學正何批明鬯
punctuated:
割斷制者在，此又以仁義爲禮樂之輔也。夫然，則所以救其偏弊者亦無不至矣。自是民之漸被於禮樂者，同焉能異，自相親而不至於流；異焉能同，自相敬而不至於離。民治豈有不行哉？至是則化成矣。抑先王之作禮樂也，效法天地，而又有和敬之德以爲之本，故推之於治，宜乎民無不化矣。豈唯民化而已哉？位天地，育萬物，要皆此禮樂之所爲也。後世人君不務出此，往往因陋就簡，以圖一時之近功耳。宋儒歐陽氏有曰：「三代而上，治出於一，而禮樂達于天下；三代而下，治出於二，而禮樂爲虛名。」者，此之謂也。爲治者盍亦知所務哉？

故君子與其使食浮於人也，寧使人浮於食。

葉孟

同考試官教諭林批：「寫出君子耻食浮之意，儘是親切。他日見用，殆非竊禄者矣。」

考試官學正何批：「明鬯。」
translation_en:
…that which distinguishes and decides is present [?]. This, moreover, makes benevolence and righteousness auxiliaries to rites and music. Thus every provision is made to remedy their one-sided tendencies and attendant defects. Thereafter, as the people gradually come under the influence of rites and music, they can preserve distinctions within their unity: they naturally cherish one another without lapsing into excess. They can preserve unity within their distinctions: they naturally respect one another without becoming estranged. How could good government of the people fail to prevail? At this point, their transformation is complete. Moreover, in creating rites and music, the former kings modeled them on Heaven and Earth and grounded them in the virtues of harmony and reverence. When these were extended to government, it was fitting that none of the people should remain untransformed. Yet was the transformation of the people their only achievement? Giving Heaven and Earth their proper places and nurturing the myriad things—all these, in essence, are accomplished through rites and music. Rulers of later ages have failed to pursue this course, often making do with crude and makeshift arrangements merely to seek immediate results. The Song Confucian scholar Ouyang said: “During the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source, and rites and music reached all under Heaven. After the Three Dynasties, government issued from two sources, and rites and music became empty names.” This is what he meant. Should those who govern not also recognize what they ought to pursue?

“Thus the gentleman would rather have his worth exceed his emolument than let his emolument exceed his worth.”

Ye Meng

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “He brings out the gentleman’s sense of shame at receiving emoluments exceeding his worth, expressing it with great aptness. If appointed to office in the future, he will surely not be one who draws a salary without earning it.”

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: “Clear and lucid.”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授劉批文理通暢
君子之仕也不欲厚其所受於君者唯欲厚其
所事於君者夫事君之才德薄而受祿厚則其
仕也苟祿耳曾謂君子而肯爲此哉夫子之言
如此其意謂夫古之君子未嘗不欲仕而其仕
也亦曷嘗以苟祿爲哉彼如才僅可以爲士而
君以大夫之祿予之德僅可以爲大夫而君以
公卿之祿予之則食浮於人矣人情於此孰不
利之君子必曰君之所以祿我者如此固足以
===
自富矣報踰其分獨不有負於君乎賞過其功
獨不有愧於巳乎與其受之而使食浮於人不
若辭之而使人浮於食也如德可以爲公卿而
但受大夫之祿德可以爲大夫而但受士之祿
則人浮於食矣人情於此雖若不堪君子必曰
君之所以祿我者如此亦足以代耕矣吾唯盡
其職耳位不滿其德何計哉吾唯敬其事耳祿
不稱其功何恤哉君子之仕如此則其受於君
者薄而事於君者厚所謂辭貴不辭賤辭富不
punctuated:
考試官教授劉批：文理通暢。

君子之仕也，不欲厚其所受於君者，唯欲厚其所事於君者。夫事君之才德薄而受祿厚，則其仕也苟祿耳。曾謂君子而肯爲此哉？夫子之言如此，其意謂夫古之君子未嘗不欲仕，而其仕也亦曷嘗以苟祿爲哉？彼如才僅可以爲士，而君以大夫之祿予之；德僅可以爲大夫，而君以公卿之祿予之，則食浮於人矣。人情於此，孰不利之？君子必曰：「君之所以祿我者如此，固足以自富矣。報踰其分，獨不有負於君乎？賞過其功，獨不有愧於巳乎？與其受之而使食浮於人，不若辭之而使人浮於食也。」如德可以爲公卿，而但受大夫之祿；德可以爲大夫，而但受士之祿，則人浮於食矣。人情於此，雖若不堪，君子必曰：「君之所以祿我者如此，亦足以代耕矣。吾唯盡其職耳，位不滿其德，何計哉？吾唯敬其事耳，祿不稱其功，何恤哉？」君子之仕如此，則其受於君者薄，而事於君者厚。所謂辭貴不辭賤，辭富不
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Liu, Prefectural School Instructor: The writing and reasoning are lucid and fluent.

When a gentleman takes office, he does not seek to increase what he receives from his ruler; he seeks only to increase the service he renders to his ruler. If his ability and virtue in serving the ruler are meager, yet his stipend is generous, then he holds office merely to draw a stipend without deserving it. Could anyone suppose that a gentleman would consent to this? Such are the Master's words. Their meaning is that the gentlemen of antiquity certainly wished to hold office, but when did they ever do so merely to draw an undeserved stipend? If, for example, a man's ability qualifies him only to be a serviceman, yet the ruler grants him the stipend of a grand master, or his virtue qualifies him only to be a grand master, yet the ruler grants him the stipend of a duke or minister, then his emoluments exceed his worth. Who, following ordinary human inclinations, would not see an advantage in this? Yet the gentleman would surely say: “What the ruler grants me as a stipend is certainly enough to enrich me. But if my recompense exceeds my due, would I not be failing my ruler? If my rewards exceed my achievements, would I not feel ashamed before myself? Rather than accept them and let my emoluments exceed my worth, I would do better to decline them and let my worth exceed my emoluments.”

If a man's virtue qualifies him to be a duke or minister, but he receives only the stipend of a grand master, or his virtue qualifies him to be a grand master, but he receives only the stipend of a serviceman, then his worth exceeds his emoluments. Though ordinary human inclinations might find this intolerable, the gentleman would surely say: “What the ruler grants me as a stipend is still enough to provide a livelihood in place of farming. I seek only to fulfill my duties. Why should I concern myself if my rank falls short of my virtue? I seek only to attend reverently to my service. Why should I worry if my stipend does not match my achievements?” If a gentleman holds office in this way, then what he receives from his ruler is modest, while the service he renders is substantial. This is what is meant by declining high station but not low station, declining wealth but not…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
辭貧者在是矣政事豈有不脩而風俗豈有不
美哉大抵三代以前君之爵人也唯恐不得其
人臣之受命也唯恐不稱其職故有虞咨岳命
官當時在廷之臣類皆推賢讓能而不敢直以
爲已任也世降春秋儋爵食祿者不過藉此以
媒富貴耳辭富貴而寧處貧賤者幾何此所以
爭奪之禍作矣噫夫子言此其亦有所感也夫
第貳場
論
===
聖人之道猶天然
馮徽
同考試官訓導陳批論題正大士子類能道之
但多模擬形似而無親切意味令人厭觀晚得此
篇議論平妥而理致明白决非疎淺之學所能到
也是用錄出
同考試官訓導楊批議論層出而抑揚中度非
老於文學者不能爲也健羨健羨
考試官學正何批文思清潤而氣象悠揚若
punctuated:
辭貧者，在是矣。政事豈有不脩，而風俗豈有不美哉？大抵三代以前，君之爵人也，唯恐不得其人；臣之受命也，唯恐不稱其職。故有虞咨岳命官，當時在廷之臣，類皆推賢讓能，而不敢直以爲已任也。世降春秋，儋爵食祿者，不過藉此以媒富貴耳。辭富貴而寧處貧賤者幾何？此所以爭奪之禍作矣。噫！夫子言此，其亦有所感也夫！

第貳場
論

聖人之道猶天然
馮徽

同考試官訓導陳批：「論題正大，士子類能道之，但多模擬形似，而無親切意味，令人厭觀。晚得此篇，議論平妥，而理致明白，决非疎淺之學所能到也，是用錄出。」

同考試官訓導楊批：「議論層出，而抑揚中度，非老於文學者不能爲也。健羨！健羨！」

考試官學正何批：「文思清潤，而氣象悠揚，若
translation_en:
…yet do not decline poverty: this is what is meant. How could governmental affairs fail to be well ordered, and customs fail to be good? Generally, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, when rulers conferred ranks, their sole concern was lest they fail to find the right men; when ministers accepted appointments, their sole concern was lest they prove unequal to their duties. Thus, when the sovereign of Youyu consulted the Four Mountains and appointed officials, the ministers then at court generally recommended the worthy and yielded to the able, not daring simply to regard the responsibility as their own. As the ages declined into the Spring and Autumn period, those who bore rank and received stipends merely used these to procure wealth and eminence. How many declined wealth and eminence, preferring poverty and humble station? This is why the calamities of contention and strife arose. Alas! When the Master said this, he too must have been moved by something he had witnessed!

Second Session
Discourse

“The Way of the Sage Is Like Heaven”
By Feng Hui

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不竟其說者可以占其中之所存矣
考試官敎授劉批詞有根據作性理論當如是
道至聖人而止也論聖道而必擬諸天其善於
立言者矣何也道莫全於聖人也道以聖人而
全亦以聖人而止窮天下後世無以復加者也
自其跡觀之聖人亦天地間一人耳自其道論
之則聖人未始不爲天而天未始不爲聖人也
夫豈可以差殊觀之哉程子曰聖人之道猶天
然門弟子親炙而冀及之然後知其高且遠也
===
味斯言也程子不惟知聖人亦知天矣其善於
立言者歟且聖人之道何道也中庸率性之謂
也原於天命之正具於人心之微其體則仁義
禮智其用則喜怒哀樂其倫則父子君臣夫婦
長幼朋友其法則禮樂刑政其文則詩書易春
秋其爲道易明而其爲敎易行也是道也人皆
有之而獨以聖人爲言者何哉蓋道之得於天
者雖同而其成於人者自異衆人有之而不知
賢者踐之而未盡聖人獨能盡之而無餘故擧
punctuated:
不竟其說者，可以占其中之所存矣。

考試官敎授劉批：詞有根據，作性理論當如是。

道至聖人而止也。論聖道而必擬諸天，其善於立言者矣。何也？道莫全於聖人也。道以聖人而全，亦以聖人而止，窮天下後世，無以復加者也。自其跡觀之，聖人亦天地間一人耳；自其道論之，則聖人未始不爲天，而天未始不爲聖人也。夫豈可以差殊觀之哉？程子曰：「聖人之道猶天然，門弟子親炙而冀及之，然後知其高且遠也。」味斯言也，程子不惟知聖人，亦知天矣。其善於立言者歟！且聖人之道何道也？《中庸》率性之謂也。原於天命之正，具於人心之微。其體則仁義禮智，其用則喜怒哀樂，其倫則父子、君臣、夫婦、長幼、朋友，其法則禮樂刑政，其文則《詩》《書》《易》《春秋》。其爲道易明，而其爲敎易行也。是道也，人皆有之，而獨以聖人爲言者，何哉？蓋道之得於天者雖同，而其成於人者自異。衆人有之而不知，賢者踐之而未盡，聖人獨能盡之而無餘，故擧
translation_en:
…as though he had not exhausted what he had to say: from this one may discern what he holds within.

Examiner Liu, Prefectural School Professor, comments: “The wording has a firm foundation. A discourse on human nature and principle should be written like this.”

The Way reaches its ultimate point in the sage. To discuss the sage’s Way and invariably compare it to Heaven is indeed to formulate one’s words well. Why? Nowhere is the Way more complete than in the sage. Through the sage the Way attains completeness, and in the sage it also reaches its ultimate point. Throughout the world and all subsequent ages, nothing further can be added to it. Viewed through his outward deeds, the sage is merely one person between Heaven and Earth. Considered in terms of his Way, however, the sage has never been other than Heaven, and Heaven has never been other than the sage. How could they be regarded as different? Master Cheng said: “The sage’s Way is like Heaven. His disciples receive his teaching in person and hope to attain it; only then do they understand its height and remoteness.” Savoring these words, we see that Master Cheng understood not only the sage but also Heaven. How well he formulated his words!

Moreover, what is the sage’s Way? It is what the Doctrine of the Mean calls following one’s nature. It originates in the correctness of Heaven’s mandate and is fully present in the subtle workings of the human mind. Its substance is benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom; its functioning is joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure. Its relationships are those between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends. Its institutions are rites, music, punishments, and government; its literary expressions are the Book of Odes, the Book of Documents, the Book of Changes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals. As a Way it is easy to understand, and as a teaching it is easy to practice. Everyone possesses this Way; why, then, is it spoken of exclusively in connection with the sage? Although the Way received from Heaven is the same, its realization in human beings naturally differs. Ordinary people possess it without knowing it; the worthy practice it without fully realizing it. The sage alone can realize it completely, leaving nothing unfulfilled. Thus it is taken in its entirety…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而歸諸聖人也然聖人之道亦不過循其性之
自然盡其理之當然而初非外此而別有所增益
也論聖道而必以天為言者何哉蓋天之所賦
於我者本如是其渾全也吾於是而偏曲之則
人矣而非天也本如是其博大也吾於是而狹
小之則人矣而非天也本如是其精純粹美也
吾於是而矯揉駁雜之則人矣而非天也聖人
於其所謂渾全者而渾全之博大者而博大之
精純粹美者而精純粹美之不偏曲也不狹小
===
也不矯揉駁雜也一全其天之本體而無虧焉
則善繼善述而克肖乎天矣克肖乎天者天固
天也聖人亦天也其道不亦高矣乎不亦遠矣
乎聖人之心亦非故欲為此高遠以絕人也蓋
其生也聖由天縱性本天成氣極其清質極其
粹所謂渾全者博大者純粹精美者自然凝聚
厥躬無少疵類無少間斷仁義禮智以立其體
喜怒哀樂以達其用父子君臣夫婦長幼朋友
以敦其倫禮樂刑政以立其法詩書易春秋以
punctuated: 而歸諸聖人也。然聖人之道，亦不過循其性之自然，盡其理之當然，而初非外此而別有所增益也。論聖道而必以天為言者，何哉？蓋天之所賦於我者，本如是其渾全也，吾於是而偏曲之，則人矣，而非天也；本如是其博大也，吾於是而狹小之，則人矣，而非天也；本如是其精純粹美也，吾於是而矯揉駁雜之，則人矣，而非天也。聖人於其所謂渾全者而渾全之，博大者而博大之，精純粹美者而精純粹美之，不偏曲也，不狹小也，不矯揉駁雜也。一全其天之本體而無虧焉，則善繼善述，而克肖乎天矣。克肖乎天者，天固天也，聖人亦天也。其道不亦高矣乎？不亦遠矣乎？聖人之心，亦非故欲為此高遠以絕人也。蓋其生也，聖由天縱，性本天成，氣極其清，質極其粹，所謂渾全者、博大者、純粹精美者，自然凝聚厥躬，無少疵類，無少間斷。仁義禮智以立其體，喜怒哀樂以達其用，父子、君臣、夫婦、長幼、朋友以敦其倫，禮樂刑政以立其法，《詩》《書》《易》《春秋》以
translation_en: …and attribute it to the sages. Yet the Way of the sages consists merely in following what is spontaneous in their nature and fully realizing what its principles require; it does not involve going beyond these to add anything else. Why must discussion of the sages’ Way always invoke Heaven? What Heaven has endowed us with is originally so complete and undivided. If we make it partial and distorted, it becomes something human, no longer heavenly. It is originally so broad and great. If we make it narrow and small, it becomes something human, no longer heavenly. It is originally so refined, pure, unalloyed, and beautiful. If we force and adulterate it, it becomes something human, no longer heavenly. The sages preserve the completeness of what is complete, the breadth and greatness of what is broad and great, and the refinement, purity, and beauty of what is refined, pure, and beautiful. They neither distort it nor narrow it, neither force it nor adulterate it. They preserve wholly intact the original substance bestowed by Heaven, without any impairment. Thus they skillfully carry on and transmit what they have received, and can truly resemble Heaven. When they can truly resemble Heaven, Heaven is of course Heaven, and the sages too are Heaven. Is their Way not lofty? Is it not far-reaching? Nor do the sages deliberately seek such loftiness and remoteness in order to cut themselves off from others. At their birth, their sagehood is Heaven’s gift, and their nature is formed by Heaven; their vital energy is supremely clear and their constitution supremely pure. What we call completeness, breadth and greatness, purity, refinement, and beauty naturally coalesces in their persons, without the slightest blemish or interruption. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom establish the substance of their Way; joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure give expression to its functioning; the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends give depth to its human bonds; rites, music, punishments, and government establish its norms; the Book of Odes, Book of Documents, Book of Changes, and Spring and Autumn Annals serve to…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
□其文至於動靜語默之間食息起居之際無
一事而非道也無一事而非道則無一事而非
天矣故淪於卑者自見其道之高不可及也狃
於近者自見其道之遠不可即也吾嘗合天與
聖人而觀之聖道之所謂一本者即維天之命
於穆不已也聖道之所謂萬殊者即乾道變化
各正性命也意必固我之絕無其太虛之明淨
乎仕止久速之適可其四時之錯行乎老者安
而少者懷一物各付物之妙也用則行而舍則
===
藏一盈虛消息之理也聖人之所以為聖人者
如此是蓋靜與天游也動與天俱也易曰先天
而天弗違後天而奉天時朱子曰孔子其太極
邵子曰聖人與昊天為一道皆此意也程子之
言其弗信矣乎抑非程子之言也夫子之不可
及也猶天之不可階而升也子貢嘗有是言矣
天何言哉四時行焉百物生焉吾夫子亦嘗以
天自謂矣惜乎當時門人默契此道者僅見顏
曾二子而已其他如子貢者無言之教猶不能
punctuated: □其文。至於動靜語默之間，食息起居之際，無一事而非道也。無一事而非道，則無一事而非天矣。故淪於卑者，自見其道之高不可及也；狃於近者，自見其道之遠不可即也。吾嘗合天與聖人而觀之：聖道之所謂一本者，即維天之命，於穆不已也；聖道之所謂萬殊者，即乾道變化，各正性命也。意必固我之絕無，其太虛之明淨乎？仕止久速之適可，其四時之錯行乎？老者安而少者懷，一物各付物之妙也；用則行而舍則藏，一盈虛消息之理也。聖人之所以為聖人者如此，是蓋靜與天游也，動與天俱也。《易》曰：「先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。」朱子曰：「孔子其太極。」邵子曰：「聖人與昊天為一道。」皆此意也。程子之言，其弗信矣乎？抑非程子之言也。「夫子之不可及也，猶天之不可階而升也。」子貢嘗有是言矣。「天何言哉？四時行焉，百物生焉。」吾夫子亦嘗以天自謂矣。惜乎當時門人默契此道者，僅見顏曾二子而已。其他如子貢者，無言之教猶不能
translation_en: …[illegible] its cultural expression [?]. As for activity and stillness, speech and silence, eating and resting, rising and retiring, there is nothing that is not the Way. If nothing is other than the Way, then nothing is other than Heaven. Thus those sunk in lowliness naturally see the height of the sage’s Way as unattainable; those habituated to what is near naturally see its remoteness as beyond their reach. I have considered Heaven and the sage together: what is called the single source of the sage’s Way is precisely “Heaven’s mandate—ah, profound and unceasing!” What are called its myriad differentiations are precisely “the transformations of the Creative, through which each thing receives its proper nature and destiny.” His utter freedom from conjecture, insistence, obstinacy, and self-centeredness—is this not the brightness and purity of the Great Void? His perfect appropriateness in taking office or withdrawing, remaining long or departing quickly—is this not the alternating course of the four seasons? Bringing peace to the old and cherishing the young embodies the same subtle working by which each thing is left to fulfill its own nature. Acting when employed and withdrawing when set aside embodies the same principle of fullness and emptiness, waning and waxing. Such is what makes the sage a sage: in stillness he communes with Heaven; in movement he proceeds together with Heaven. The Book of Changes says: “When he precedes Heaven, Heaven does not oppose him; when he follows Heaven, he observes Heaven’s seasons.” Master Zhu said: “Confucius is the Supreme Ultimate.” Master Shao said: “The sage and August Heaven constitute one Way.” All express this meaning. Can Master Cheng’s words, then, be unworthy of belief? Yet these are not merely Master Cheng’s words. “The Master cannot be equaled, just as Heaven cannot be ascended by a stairway.” Zigong once said this. “What does Heaven say? The four seasons proceed, and the myriad things are born.” Our Master, too, once spoke of himself in terms of Heaven. Alas, among his disciples at that time, only Yan and Zeng are seen to have attained a tacit understanding of this Way. Others, such as Zigong, were still unable to understand the teaching without words…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
喻况其下者乎有隱之疑宜乎諸弟子所不能
免矣於戲聖人作止語默無非教也亦猶天之
四時行百物生無非天理發見流行之實也曾
何有隱而亦何待於言哉學者果能悟夫子無
隱之言力求其實而因以得其無言之妙則高
者可及而遠者可即矣此固程子之意也
表
擬宋以孔宜襲封文宣公謝表太平興國三年
黃佐
===
同考試官教諭莊批表體駢儷學者類能為之
求其意婉而厚語贍而莊寓忠愛於稱謝間者僅見此篇
同考試官教諭江批文辭典則氣象渾厚寫出崇
德象賢之意可佳
考試官學正何批四六中用事切當錄之
考試官教授劉批溫純整潔可誦
臣宜言今月某日某官某奉宣
詔旨以臣宜為右賛善大夫襲封文宣公者臣
誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言
punctuated:
喻，况其下者乎？有隱之疑，宜乎諸弟子所不能免矣。於戲！聖人作止語默，無非教也；亦猶天之四時行、百物生，無非天理發見流行之實也。曾何有隱，而亦何待於言哉？學者果能悟夫子無隱之言，力求其實，而因以得其無言之妙，則高者可及，而遠者可即矣。此固程子之意也。
表
擬宋以孔宜襲封文宣公謝表，太平興國三年。
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批：表體駢儷，學者類能為之。求其意婉而厚、語贍而莊、寓忠愛於稱謝間者，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭江批：文辭典則，氣象渾厚，寫出崇德象賢之意，可佳。
考試官學正何批：四六中用事切當，錄之。
考試官教授劉批：溫純整潔，可誦。
臣宜言：今月某日，某官某奉宣詔旨，以臣宜為右賛善大夫、襲封文宣公者。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：
translation_en:
…understand it; how much less could those below him? It was only natural that the disciples could not escape the suspicion that something was being concealed. Ah! The sage’s actions and repose, speech and silence, are all instruction. They are just like Heaven’s procession of the four seasons and generation of the myriad things: all are concrete manifestations of heavenly principle revealing itself and flowing forth. What could possibly be concealed, and what need could there be for words? If learners can truly understand the Master’s statement that he conceals nothing, earnestly seek its substance, and thereby grasp the subtle wonder of his wordless teaching, then what is high can be reached, and what is distant can be approached. This is indeed Master Cheng’s meaning.
Memorial
A model memorial of thanks on the Song court’s granting Kong Yi hereditary succession to the title Duke of Propagating Culture (Wenxuan), in the third year of Taiping Xingguo.
By Huang Zuo.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: “The memorial form uses parallel prose, which students can generally compose. But in seeking one whose meaning is tactful yet substantial, whose language is ample yet dignified, and which conveys loyalty and devotion amid its expressions of thanks, I have found only this piece.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The language is classical and well regulated, and the overall bearing full and substantial. It expresses the intention of honoring virtue and emulating the worthy. Commendable.”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “The allusions in this four-and-six prose are aptly employed. Include it in the record.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “Gentle and pure, orderly and polished; worthy of recitation.”
Your servant Yi states: On such-and-such a day of this month, such-and-such an official respectfully proclaimed the imperial decree appointing your servant Yi Grand Master for Assisting Virtue of the Right and granting him hereditary succession to the title Duke of Propagating Culture. Your servant, in deepest awe and trepidation, bows his head to the ground and kowtows, respectfully submitting these words: …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝德重華開萬世文明之象儒門有慶荷
九天錫命之光道尊素王恩及苗裔建官作
一人之輔列爵居五等之先家學淵源世遠敢
忘似續
皇仁浩博才微幸獲涵容
綸綍下頒箕裘內愧茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
沉幾先物
英斷合天河洛圖書夙嘗授之
宣廟範疇福德蚤巳占之
藝皇四海
帝臣龍行雲擁萬方王會虎步風生閔農事戒
田荒心欲所其無逸抑禎符絕遠物治必
保其有終大哉
中國聖人允矣
太平天子明昭定烈不一再朞崇德象賢越四
十世上爵賜繇隋帝嘉名制自唐宗監彼
儀文畀茲朽質重輔導俾兼其職輕征傜
punctuated: 帝德重華，開萬世文明之象；儒門有慶，荷九天錫命之光。道尊素王，恩及苗裔。建官作一人之輔，列爵居五等之先。家學淵源，世遠敢忘似續；皇仁浩博，才微幸獲涵容。綸綍下頒，箕裘內愧。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，沉幾先物，英斷合天。河洛圖書，夙嘗授之宣廟；範疇福德，蚤巳占之藝皇。四海帝臣，龍行雲擁；萬方王會，虎步風生。閔農事，戒田荒，心欲所其無逸；抑禎符，絕遠物，治必保其有終。大哉，中國聖人！允矣，太平天子！明昭定烈，不一再朞；崇德象賢，越四十世。上爵賜繇隋帝，嘉名制自唐宗。監彼儀文，畀茲朽質。重輔導，俾兼其職；輕征傜，
translation_en:
Imperial virtue renews the splendor of Shun, opening a prospect of civilization for ten thousand generations; rejoicing has come to the Confucian household, which receives the radiance of an appointment bestowed from the Nine Heavens. The Way exalts the Uncrowned King, and favor reaches his descendants. An office is established to provide an assistant to the Son of Heaven; a noble rank is conferred that stands foremost among the five degrees. Our family learning has deep sources: though generations stretch far back, how could I forget to carry it on? Imperial benevolence is vast: despite my meager talents, I have fortunately received its indulgence. The imperial command descends, while inwardly I feel ashamed of my inadequacy to continue the ancestral calling.
This is because I have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [an unresolved honorific placeholder], whose profound discernment anticipates events and whose sagacious decisions accord with Heaven. The charts and writings of the Yellow River and Luo River were long ago bestowed upon Xuanmiao [?]; the blessings and virtues of the categories of the Great Plan were already foretold for Emperor Yi [?]. Within the Four Seas, all are imperial subjects: the dragon advances, surrounded by clouds. From every quarter, rulers assemble at court: the tiger strides, and winds arise. You care for farming and warn against leaving fields waste, desiring in your heart to abide in freedom from ease [?]. You restrain the presentation of auspicious portents and refuse exotic goods from distant lands, determined to preserve good government to its conclusion. Great indeed is the sage of the Central Realm! Truly, you are the Son of Heaven of an age of peace! Your illustrious achievements have been established in scarcely one or two years; your honoring of virtue and recognition of worth in a sage’s descendants reach across more than forty generations. The exalted noble rank was bestowed by a Sui emperor; the honored designation was instituted by a Tang sovereign. Following those ceremonial precedents, you confer them upon this decrepit person. Esteeming the work of guidance, you have me hold that office concurrently; lightening taxes and corvée obligations, …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
用復其家岱嶽滄溟高揭仲尼日月魯邦
兗土弘開夫子宮墻延賞無窮
君恩已極受爵不讓臣罪何辭竊念臣宜下第
乾德之初征商星子之鎭遠違廊廟久涉
江湖詣
闕上書迹頗似於韓愈還
朝獻賦文不類於相如詎意菲封謬登鼎俎
仰天有愧俯地何從敢不砥礪廉隅期無
負於
===
明詔纘承統緒求不忝於前人啓沃之心尚
圖夙夜將順之美莫補涓埃三祝華封
堯仁曷能想像載歌天保
周德難以形容伏願五星永聚奎躔人文與
天文並耀六籍大明
聖世
國統與道統同尊臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
punctuated: 用復其家。岱嶽滄溟，高揭仲尼日月；魯邦兗土，弘開夫子宮墻。延賞無窮，君恩已極；受爵不讓，臣罪何辭？竊念臣宜下第乾德之初，征商星子之鎭，遠違廊廟，久涉江湖。詣闕上書，迹頗似於韓愈；還朝獻賦，文不類於相如。詎意菲封，謬登鼎俎。仰天有愧，俯地何從？敢不砥礪廉隅，期無負於明詔；纘承統緒，求不忝於前人。啓沃之心，尚圖夙夜；將順之美，莫補涓埃。三祝華封，堯仁曷能想像；載歌天保，周德難以形容。伏願五星永聚奎躔，人文與天文並耀；六籍大明聖世，國統與道統同尊。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉
translation_en:
…thereby exempting his household from service obligations. As lofty as Mount Tai and as vast as the blue sea, you raise high the sun and moon of Zhongni; in the land of Lu and the territory of Yan, you greatly extend the walls of the Master's palace. Rewards reach onward without end; Your Majesty's grace has reached its utmost. Having accepted the rank without declining it, how can your servant plead against his guilt?

I humbly reflect that I, your servant Yi, failed the examination at the beginning of the Qiande era and collected commercial taxes in the town of Xingzi. Far removed from the court, I long wandered among rivers and lakes. In approaching the palace to submit a letter, my actions somewhat resembled those of Han Yu; in returning to court to present a rhapsody, my writing bore no resemblance to that of Xiangru. Who could have imagined that my humble enfeoffment [?] would undeservedly find a place among the sacrificial cauldrons and stands? Looking up at Heaven, I feel ashamed; looking down at the earth, where can I turn? How dare I fail to temper my integrity, hoping not to disappoint your illustrious edict, and to carry forward the ancestral succession, seeking not to disgrace my predecessors? With a heart intent on nourishing your wisdom, I still aspire to serve morning and night; yet in supporting and furthering your worthy purposes, I cannot contribute even a drop of water or a speck of dust.

Even the three blessings offered by the border warden of Hua could scarcely convey the benevolence of Yao; even singing Heaven Protects You could hardly describe the virtue of Zhou. I humbly wish that the five planets may forever gather in the celestial station of Kui, so that human culture and the patterns of Heaven shine together; and that the Six Classics may shine brightly in your sagely age, so that the imperial succession and the succession of the Way are equally honored. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sageliness, cannot contain his utmost fervor and trembling awe, and respectfully presents…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批
朝廷盛德大業默寓
===
詔旨此策發揚殆盡末復以古人自期遠大之到吾切有望於子
同考試官教諭江批能鋪張我
聖天子至仁盛德之實誦之不覺嘆賞至再況五策翩翩氣充詞贍吾
意此子殆不止魁一省而已健羨健羨
考試官學正何批我
朝詔令如天難名子能詳悉無遺則才之宏博有可占矣華國之薦
舍子其誰
考試官教授劉批此策議論閎闊揄揚得體
有士如此真足以薦
punctuated:
表稱謝以聞。
第叁場，策五道。第一問。黃佐。
同考試官教諭莊批：朝廷盛德大業，默寓詔旨。此策發揚殆盡，末復以古人自期，遠大之到，吾切有望於子。
同考試官教諭江批：能鋪張我聖天子至仁盛德之實，誦之不覺嘆賞至再。況五策翩翩，氣充詞贍，吾意此子殆不止魁一省而已。健羨，健羨！
考試官學正何批：我朝詔令，如天難名。子能詳悉無遺，則才之宏博有可占矣。華國之薦，舍子其誰？
考試官教授劉批：此策議論閎闊，揄揚得體。有士如此，真足以薦
translation_en:
…this memorial expressing thanks, for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session: Five Policy Essays. First Question. Huang Zuo.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: The court’s abundant virtue and great achievements are implicitly embodied in the imperial edict. This policy essay brings them out almost exhaustively. At the end, you further take the ancients as the standard to which you aspire. Such lofty attainment [?] gives me earnest hopes for you.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: You can expound fully the actual manifestations of our sagely Son of Heaven’s supreme benevolence and abundant virtue. Reading this aloud, I could not help voicing my admiration repeatedly. Moreover, all five policy essays are graceful, vigorous in spirit, and rich in expression. I think this young man will probably do more than merely rank first in a single province. How enviable, how enviable!

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: Our dynasty’s edicts, like Heaven, are difficult to describe adequately. Your ability to explain them thoroughly, omitting nothing, reveals the breadth of your talent. In recommending someone who will bring lustre to the realm, whom could we choose but you?

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: This policy essay’s arguments are broad in scope, and its praise is fittingly expressed. A scholar like this truly deserves to be recommended…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
上矣
聖人之感人心也有所以立天下之本有
所以示天下之機有其本則允德協下而
感之也深有其機則嘉言孔彰而應之也
速是故問其德曰天下之大本也問其言
曰天下之大機也聖人者作操其本握其
機言出而天下從之夫天下豈可以空言
感動之哉愚因反覆明問而有以知
聖世
===
皇言之大足以配帝王而陋西漢矣敬陳其槩
粵自戊申春正月我
太祖高皇帝首以
卽位詔天下則
上帝
祖考之靈建元定號之正續中國帝王之統開
億萬載無疆之休其精神命脉固已潜孚
於天下矣乃若求遺書定律令定文武科
取士之法出師以定中原馳檄以諭齊魯
punctuated:
上矣。

聖人之感人心也，有所以立天下之本，有所以示天下之機。有其本，則允德協下而感之也深；有其機，則嘉言孔彰而應之也速。是故問其德，曰天下之大本也；問其言，曰天下之大機也。聖人者作，操其本，握其機，言出而天下從之。夫天下豈可以空言感動之哉？愚因反覆明問，而有以知聖世皇言之大，足以配帝王而陋西漢矣。敬陳其槩。

粵自戊申春正月，我太祖高皇帝首以卽位詔天下，則上帝祖考之靈、建元定號之正、續中國帝王之統、開億萬載無疆之休，其精神命脉固已潜孚於天下矣。乃若求遺書、定律令、定文武科取士之法、出師以定中原、馳檄以諭齊魯
translation_en:
…to the throne.

In moving people’s hearts, the sage has the means to establish the foundation of the realm and to reveal its moving impulse. With that foundation, his genuine virtue brings those below into harmony, and he moves them profoundly; with that impulse, his fine words shine forth, and their response is swift. Thus, if asked about his virtue, one says: it is the great foundation of the realm. If asked about his words, one says: they are the great moving impulse of the realm. When a sage arises, he holds that foundation and grasps that impulse; his words go forth, and all under Heaven follow him. How could all under Heaven be moved by empty words? Having repeatedly pondered your illuminating question, I have come to understand that the grandeur of imperial utterances in this sagely age is sufficient to rival the ancient emperors and kings and to make the Western Han appear inferior. I respectfully present an outline.

Beginning in the first month of spring in the wushen year [1368], our Emperor Taizu Gao first proclaimed his accession to all under Heaven. The divine efficacy of the Lord on High and his ancestors, the rightful establishment of an era and designation of the dynasty, the continuation of the succession of China’s emperors and kings, and the inauguration of boundless blessings for countless ages—the animating spirit and vital force of these had already quietly won the trust of all under Heaven. As for seeking out lost writings, establishing statutes and ordinances, determining the methods of recruiting men through the civil and military examinations, dispatching armies to pacify the Central Plain, and sending proclamations at speed to instruct Qi and Lu…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
河洛燕薊秦晉之人此
令行於立國之初者也先之以農桑學校繼
之以求言又繼之以赦宥存恤免姑孰金
陵免唐鄧秦隴等處田租諭山東山西省
臣諭元舊相諭高麗安南日本諸國此
詔頒於一統之後者也嗣是而
太宗之入正大統
仁宗
宣宗之纘緒
===
英宗之復辟
憲宗
孝宗之繼體守文莫不有
詔惟繼天立極之德無一而不備故經天緯
地之文無一而不周萬世遵之萬世之治
也迺今庚午夏四月
聖天子特下
明詔命討寧夏之罪首舉法天立政卽堯之
欽若昊天湯之祗承上帝而敬
punctuated:
河洛燕薊秦晉之人，此令行於立國之初者也。先之以農桑學校，繼之以求言，又繼之以赦宥存恤，免姑孰金陵、免唐鄧秦隴等處田租，諭山東山西省臣，諭元舊相，諭高麗安南日本諸國，此詔頒於一統之後者也。嗣是而太宗之入正大統，仁宗、宣宗之纘緒，英宗之復辟，憲宗、孝宗之繼體守文，莫不有詔。惟繼天立極之德，無一而不備，故經天緯地之文，無一而不周。萬世遵之，萬世之治也。
迺今庚午夏四月，聖天子特下明詔，命討寧夏之罪，首舉法天立政，卽堯之欽若昊天、湯之祗承上帝，而敬
translation_en:
…the people of Heluo, Yan, Ji, Qin, and Jin: these were commands put into effect at the founding of the dynasty. First came measures concerning agriculture, sericulture, and schools; next came the solicitation of counsel; and then pardons, clemency, relief, and care for those in need. Land taxes were remitted in Gushu and Jinling, and in Tang, Deng, Qin, Long, and other places. Instructions were issued to the provincial officials of Shandong and Shanxi, to the former chief councillors of the Yuan, and to the countries of Gaoli, Annan, and Riben. These were edicts promulgated after unification. Thereafter, when Taizong assumed his rightful place in the imperial succession, when Renzong and Xuanzong succeeded to the imperial line, when Yingzong was restored to the throne, and when Xianzong and Xiaozong inherited the throne and upheld the established institutions, each issued edicts. Because they possessed every virtue required to succeed Heaven and establish the supreme standard, their writings, which ordered Heaven and Earth, were comprehensive in every respect. If followed for ten thousand generations, they would ensure good government for ten thousand generations.
Now, in the fourth month of summer in the gengwu year, the sagely Son of Heaven has specially issued an illustrious edict commanding a punitive campaign against the wrongdoing in Ningxia. It begins by invoking the principle of modeling government on Heaven: this is precisely Yao’s reverent conformity to August Heaven and Tang’s respectful service to the Lord on High, and his reverence…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天之心何至也上念
祖宗付託即高宗之監于成憲成王之對揚耿
光而法
祖之心何至也以同仁之政布天下即堯之協
和萬邦湯之輯寧邦家也而勤民恤物之
心至矣以問罪之師告天下即舜之徂征
有苗啓之用剿有扈也而神武不殺之心
至矣回視漢之高祖約法三章似得文王
慎罰之意也文帝田租賜半似得大禹養
===
民之意也宣帝之戒脩職似得成王訓官
之意也武帝之罷輪臺似得太甲悔過之
意也然究其本則漢之君無精一執中之
傳而漢之詔豈復有虞夏商周四代之書
之氣象耶我
聖天子有
祖宗
列聖之德發而爲
祖宗
punctuated: 天之心何至也！上念祖宗付託，即高宗之監于成憲、成王之對揚耿光，而法祖之心何至也！以同仁之政布天下，即堯之協和萬邦、湯之輯寧邦家也，而勤民恤物之心至矣！以問罪之師告天下，即舜之徂征有苗、啓之用剿有扈也，而神武不殺之心至矣！回視漢之高祖約法三章，似得文王慎罰之意也；文帝田租賜半，似得大禹養民之意也；宣帝之戒脩職，似得成王訓官之意也；武帝之罷輪臺，似得太甲悔過之意也。然究其本，則漢之君無精一執中之傳，而漢之詔豈復有虞夏商周四代之書之氣象耶？我聖天子有祖宗列聖之德，發而爲祖宗
translation_en:
…how consummate is his reverence for Heaven! [?] His Majesty bears in mind the trust committed to him by his ancestors, just as Gaozong looked to established statutes and King Cheng acknowledged and magnified the brilliant legacy; how consummate is his resolve to emulate his ancestors! [?] He proclaims throughout the realm a government of impartial benevolence, just as Yao brought the myriad states into harmony and Tang brought peace to his domains. His concern for the people and care for all beings are indeed consummate! He announces to the realm an army sent to punish wrongdoing, just as Shun marched against the Youmiao and Qi used force to destroy the Youhu. His resolve to exercise divine martial power without killing is indeed consummate!

Looking back at the Han, Gaozu’s covenant reducing the laws to three articles seems to have captured King Wen’s intent to exercise caution in punishment. Emperor Wen’s remission of half the land tax seems to have captured Yu the Great’s intent to nourish the people. Emperor Xuan’s admonition to officials to attend to their duties seems to have captured King Cheng’s intent in instructing his officers. Emperor Wu’s abandonment of the Luntai undertaking seems to have captured Tai Jia’s intent in repenting his errors. Yet, when we examine their foundations, the Han rulers lacked the transmitted teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the Mean. How, then, could Han edicts possess the grandeur of the documents of the four dynasties—Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou?

Our sage Son of Heaven possesses the virtue of his ancestors, the succession of sage sovereigns, and gives it expression in the words of his ancestors…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列聖之言有二帝三王之德發而為典謨訓誥
誓命之文故曰聖人之心見於書猶化工
之妙著於物非精深不能識也天下之人
沐其德而莫知其本誦其言而莫測其機
草茅何足以形容之然愚於漢而有感焉
趙佗嘗帝越矣尺書南下佗即稱臣奉貢
而何感之易耶漢文恭儉之風卑遜謙抑
之語海濱父老至于今猶能道之漢詔之
感人蓋不止於山東之民扶杖而往聽也
===
而况我
聖天子之詔乎愚生也晚當鼓舞振作之下而
誦習久矣茲欲鋪張揚厲以昭
聖德神功於罔極則自有燕許大筆在而愚愧
非其人也惟進教之幸甚
第二問
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊 批 策問諸子之書塲中善對者
少惟此一卷考據精詳評論切當且以六經折衷其說
punctuated:
列聖之言，有二帝三王之德，發而為典謨訓誥誓命之文。故曰：「聖人之心見於書，猶化工之妙著於物，非精深不能識也。」天下之人沐其德而莫知其本，誦其言而莫測其機。草茅何足以形容之？然愚於漢而有感焉。趙佗嘗帝越矣，尺書南下，佗即稱臣奉貢，而何感之易耶？漢文恭儉之風，卑遜謙抑之語，海濱父老至于今猶能道之。漢詔之感人，蓋不止於山東之民扶杖而往聽也，而况我聖天子之詔乎？愚生也晚，當鼓舞振作之下，而誦習久矣。茲欲鋪張揚厲，以昭聖德神功於罔極，則自有燕許大筆在，而愚愧非其人也。惟進教之幸甚！

第二問
黃佐

同考試官教諭莊批：策問諸子之書，塲中善對者少，惟此一卷，考據精詳，評論切當，且以六經折衷其說。
translation_en:
…the words of the successive sage emperors; possessing the virtue of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, he gives it expression in writings of the kinds called Canons, Counsels, Instructions, Announcements, Oaths, and Charges. Thus it is said: “The sage’s mind is revealed in his writings, just as the marvels of the work of transformation are manifested in things; without profound discernment, one cannot comprehend it.” All under Heaven enjoy his virtue without knowing its source, and recite his words without fathoming their workings. How could a humble scholar outside office adequately describe this? Yet the Han gives me cause for reflection. Zhao Tuo once proclaimed himself emperor in Yue, but when a brief letter went south, he at once acknowledged himself a subject and presented tribute. How was he moved so readily? The reverent and frugal conduct of Emperor Wen of Han, and his humble, deferential words, are still recounted today by the elders along the seacoast. The power of Han edicts to move people was surely not confined to the people east of the mountains, who went leaning on their staffs to hear them. How much more powerful, then, are the edicts of our sage Son of Heaven! Born in this later age, I have long recited and studied them under their inspiring and invigorating influence. If their excellence is now to be expansively celebrated, making manifest without limit his sagely virtue and divine achievements, there are already great pens such as those of Yan and Xu to do so. I am ashamed that I am not such a person. I would count it a great blessing to receive your instruction!

Second Question
Huang Zuo

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: The policy question concerns the books of the various masters. Few in the examination hall answered it well. This paper alone is meticulous and precise in its examination of evidence, apt in its judgments, and furthermore uses the Six Classics as the standard by which to assess their doctrines…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得士如此亦可以自慶矣
同考試官教諭江批晚得此策獨能於周秦漢
唐上下千餘年間所紀之書所作之人歴歴陳說無
遺披閱之次不覺為之斂袵
考試官學正何批條答有據而文亦清致其
空谷之足音歟
考試官教授劉批考究旣詳折衷尤當蓋學
之博而知其要者也
對欲博極夫諸子之書必折衷以六經之
===
旨蓋諸子之書各以所見為說駁而不醇
雜而無統其於聖人之道背馳焉者多矣
茲欲遍考其書而不以六經之旨折衷其
說則其為道之蔽也豈淺淺哉故曰眾言
殽亂折諸聖其是之謂乎先儒有言不觀
非聖之書又曰學不博則不能約則夫諸
子之書固儒者之所當知請因明問而歴
陳之可乎聖人之道載在六經如日月之
中天萬古常明六經之外而有諸子諸子
punctuated:
得士如此，亦可以自慶矣。

同考試官教諭江批：晚得此策，獨能於周秦漢唐上下千餘年間所紀之書、所作之人，歴歴陳說無遺。披閱之次，不覺為之斂袵。

考試官學正何批：條答有據，而文亦清致，其空谷之足音歟！

考試官教授劉批：考究旣詳，折衷尤當，蓋學之博而知其要者也。

對：欲博極夫諸子之書，必折衷以六經之旨。蓋諸子之書，各以所見為說，駁而不醇，雜而無統，其於聖人之道背馳焉者多矣。茲欲遍考其書，而不以六經之旨折衷其說，則其為道之蔽也，豈淺淺哉？故曰：「眾言殽亂，折諸聖。」其是之謂乎？先儒有言：「不觀非聖之書。」又曰：「學不博則不能約。」則夫諸子之書，固儒者之所當知。請因明問而歴陳之，可乎？聖人之道，載在六經，如日月之中天，萬古常明。六經之外而有諸子，諸子
translation_en:
…To obtain a scholar such as this is indeed cause for congratulating ourselves.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: I came upon this policy essay late. It alone clearly sets forth, without omission, the books recorded and the people who composed them over more than a thousand years, spanning the Zhou, Qin, Han, and Tang. As I read it, I could not help straightening my robes in respect.

Comment by Examiner He, Schoolmaster: The answers to the individual points are well grounded, and the writing is also lucid and elegant. Is this not the sound of footsteps in an empty valley—a rare and welcome discovery!

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: His investigation is thorough, and his judgments are especially apt. Here is someone whose learning is broad and who understands its essentials.

Reply: To gain comprehensive knowledge of the writings of the various masters, one must judge them by the purport of the Six Classics. Each master's writings propound views based on what he himself has perceived; they are mixed rather than pure, miscellaneous and lacking a unifying principle. Much in them runs counter to the Way of the sages. If one now seeks to examine all these writings without judging their doctrines by the purport of the Six Classics, could the resulting obscuration of the Way be slight? Thus it is said: “When the many teachings are confused, judge them against the sages.” Is this not what that means? An earlier Confucian said: “Do not read books that are not by sages.” Yet it is also said: “Unless one's learning is broad, one cannot grasp its essentials.” The writings of the various masters are therefore certainly something that Confucian scholars ought to know. May I take your illuminating question as the occasion to set them forth in turn? The Way of the sages is recorded in the Six Classics. Like the sun and moon in mid-heaven, it shines eternally through all ages. Beyond the Six Classics there are the various masters; the various masters…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之書如燭照室輝光所及不越尋丈而戶
牖之外即為幽暗故六經稱經者萬世之
典也諸子稱子者一家之言也漢之時太
史談為六家要指劉歆則有七略迨夫班
孟堅作藝文志而十家之名布在簡冊儒
家道家陰陽家則出於司徒史官羲和法
家名家墨家則出於理官禮官清廟又有
縱橫之家非出於行人之官捭闔之官乎
又有曰雜曰農之家非出於擬議之官農
===
稷之官乎孟堅於諸子十家之外刪劉歆
七略之說又備以兵法天文五行醫經四
家後世分四部之書列諸子於子部然其
紀載之體蓋亦倣於孟堅隋書之志經籍
唐史之志藝文諸家之書多與班同而陰
陽之家不列於目唐志又始以雜藝術類
然後百家之書於此而咸備矣若夫十家
之書各有所著桓寬有鹽鐵論王符有潜
夫論荆楚歲時記作於宗懔秦中歲時記
punctuated: 之書，如燭照室，輝光所及不越尋丈，而戶牖之外即為幽暗。故六經稱經者，萬世之典也；諸子稱子者，一家之言也。漢之時，太史談為《六家要指》，劉歆則有《七略》。迨夫班孟堅作《藝文志》，而十家之名布在簡冊。儒家、道家、陰陽家，則出於司徒、史官、羲和；法家、名家、墨家，則出於理官、禮官、清廟。又有縱橫之家，非出於行人之官、捭闔之官乎？又有曰雜曰農之家，非出於擬議之官、農稷之官乎？孟堅於諸子十家之外，刪劉歆《七略》之說，又備以兵法、天文、五行、醫經四家。後世分四部之書，列諸子於子部，然其紀載之體蓋亦倣於孟堅。《隋書》之志經籍，《唐史》之志藝文，諸家之書多與班同，而陰陽之家不列於目。唐志又始以雜藝術類，然後百家之書於此而咸備矣。若夫十家之書，各有所著：桓寬有《鹽鐵論》，王符有《潜夫論》，《荆楚歲時記》作於宗懔，《秦中歲時記》
translation_en:
…the writings of the various masters are like a candle lighting a room: their radiance reaches no farther than a few feet, while beyond the doors and windows all is darkness. Thus the Six Classics are called “classics” because they are standards for all ages; the various masters are called “masters” because each represents the teachings of a single school. During the Han, the Grand Astrologer Tan composed the Essential Purport of the Six Schools, while Liu Xin produced the Seven Summaries. When Ban Mengjian compiled the Treatise on Literature, the names of the ten schools were set down in the written record. The Confucian, Daoist, and Yin-Yang schools derived respectively from the Minister of Education, the historiographers, and the astronomical officials Xi and He; the Legalist, Names, and Mohist schools derived respectively from judicial officials, ritual officials, and the ancestral temple. There was also the school of diplomatic strategists: did it not derive from diplomatic messengers and officials concerned with opening and closing negotiations [?]? There were also the Miscellaneous and Agricultural schools: did they not derive from officials charged with deliberation [?] and those responsible for agriculture and grain?

Beyond the ten schools of masters, Mengjian abridged the account in Liu Xin’s Seven Summaries and supplemented it with four further categories: military methods, astronomy, the Five Phases, and medical classics. Later generations divided books into four divisions, placing the various masters in the Masters division; their manner of recording and organizing these works likewise followed Mengjian. The Treatise on the Classics and Other Writings in the History of the Sui and the Treatise on Literature in the History of the Tang largely agreed with Ban in their classification of the schools’ writings, but did not list the Yin-Yang school among their headings. The Tang treatise also first classified miscellaneous arts [?]; only then were the writings of the hundred schools fully included.

As for the writings of the ten schools, each had its own works: Huan Kuan wrote the Discourses on Salt and Iron; Wang Fu wrote the Discourses of a Recluse; the Record of Seasonal Customs in Jingchu was written by Zong Lin; the Record of Seasonal Customs in Qinzhong…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
士鄧析子則鄭人與子産同時者尹文子
則宋人與宋鈃同遊者魯連子則六國之
仲連淮南子則劉漢之王安胡非子非墨
翟之弟子乎黔婁子非齊國之隱士乎鬻
子則爲鬻熊田子則爲田駢宣子則爲宣
聘陸子則爲陸雲論其人之所産不過秦
漢上下之人論其所著之書不出藝文十
家之外然皆起于王道旣衰聖人旣沒之
後時君世主好尚殊方是以十家之術蠭
===
然並作各持其說取合諸侯論其書雖有
蔽短之不同要其歸豈無梗槩之可取使
其人遭際明時設學校而陶鎔之以道德
而表正之會其同而變其異取其純而去
其謬則皆可爲六經之羽翼矣學者若能
脩六藝之術以觀此諸家之書又豈不能
通萬方之略而爲游藝之一助乎愚也無
高睨千古之見乏貫串百家之學孤陋寡
聞對揚明問固不能免夫掛一漏萬之誚
punctuated: 士。鄧析子則鄭人，與子産同時者；尹文子則宋人，與宋鈃同遊者；魯連子則六國之仲連；淮南子則劉漢之王安。胡非子非墨翟之弟子乎？黔婁子非齊國之隱士乎？鬻子則爲鬻熊，田子則爲田駢，宣子則爲宣聘，陸子則爲陸雲。論其人之所産，不過秦漢上下之人；論其所著之書，不出藝文十家之外。然皆起于王道旣衰、聖人旣沒之後，時君世主好尚殊方，是以十家之術蠭然並作，各持其說，取合諸侯。論其書，雖有蔽短之不同，要其歸，豈無梗槩之可取？使其人遭際明時，設學校而陶鎔之，以道德而表正之，會其同而變其異，取其純而去其謬，則皆可爲六經之羽翼矣。學者若能脩六藝之術，以觀此諸家之書，又豈不能通萬方之略，而爲游藝之一助乎？愚也無高睨千古之見，乏貫串百家之學，孤陋寡聞，對揚明問，固不能免夫掛一漏萬之誚。
translation_en:
… scholar [?]. Master Deng Xi was a native of Zheng and a contemporary of Zichan; Master Yin Wen was a native of Song who associated with Song Xing; Master Lu Lian was Zhonglian of the Six States; and the Master of Huainan was An, a prince of the Liu house of Han. Was Master Hu Fei not a disciple of Mo Di? Was Master Qian Lou not a recluse of the state of Qi? Master Yu was Yu Xiong; Master Tian was Tian Pian; Master Xuan was Xuan Pin [?]; and Master Lu was Lu Yun [?]. As for when these men lived, they belonged to the periods around the Qin and Han; as for the books they wrote, these fall within the ten schools of the bibliographical treatise. Yet all arose after the Way of the Kings had declined and the sages had passed away. The rulers of those times differed in their tastes and preferences, and thus the teachings of the ten schools arose together like a swarm of bees, each upholding its own doctrines and seeking the favor of the feudal lords. Although their books differ in their limitations and shortcomings, when one considers their ultimate purport, surely there are broad principles worth adopting?

Had these men encountered an enlightened age, with schools established to mold them and the Way and virtue employed to guide and correct them, their common ground could have been brought together and their divergences transformed, their sound teachings retained and their errors removed. They could then all have served as aids to the Six Classics. If students could cultivate the disciplines of the Six Arts and use them to examine the writings of these various schools, could they not comprehend the essentials of myriad approaches and thereby gain an aid to their cultivation of the arts? In my foolishness, I lack the vision to survey the ages from a lofty vantage, and lack the learning to connect and comprehend the hundred schools. Isolated in my learning and limited in what I have heard, in answering your illuminating question I surely cannot escape the reproach of mentioning one thing while omitting ten thousand.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
作於李綽昌言則作於仲長統申鑒則作
於荀悅氏中論作於魏之徐幹法訓作於
蜀之譙周應劭有風俗通義之書魏證有
群書治要之典李吉甫則有古今說苑杜
佑則有管氏指要論衡說林非作於王充
孔衍乎世說類林非作於義慶子野乎他
如鬼谷子則周世之隱士尉繚子則六國
之時人抱朴子則爲葛洪金樓子則爲梁
元廣成子則爲商路公鶡冠子則爲齊隱
===
矣
第三問
廖任
同考試官教諭莊批評二公文章政事以道為主
而折以程朱之論可謂有見且先後布置俱合法程
同考試官教諭江批閱此一策考據詳明斷制精
蓋嶺南之佳士也
考試官學正何批此策於韓歐二公文章事業
確豈嘗熟讀二公之文而尚論其世者歟
punctuated:
作於李綽，《昌言》則作於仲長統，《申鑒》則作於荀悅氏。《中論》作於魏之徐幹，《法訓》作於蜀之譙周。應劭有《風俗通義》之書，魏證有《群書治要》之典。李吉甫則有《古今說苑》，杜佑則有《管氏指要》。《論衡》《說林》非作於王充、孔衍乎？《世說》《類林》非作於義慶、子野乎？他如《鬼谷子》，則周世之隱士；《尉繚子》，則六國之時人；《抱朴子》，則爲葛洪；《金樓子》，則爲梁元；《廣成子》，則爲商路公；《鶡冠子》，則爲齊隱矣。
第三問
廖任
同考試官教諭莊批：「評二公文章政事，以道為主，而折以程朱之論，可謂有見，且先後布置俱合法程。」
同考試官教諭江批：「閱此一策，考據詳明，斷制精，蓋嶺南之佳士也。」
考試官學正何批：「此策於韓歐二公文章事業確，豈嘗熟讀二公之文而尚論其世者歟？」
translation_en:
…was written by Li Chuo; Forthright Discourse (Changyan) was written by Zhongchang Tong, and Mirror of Admonitions (Shenjian) by Xun Yue. Discourses on the Mean (Zhonglun) was written by Xu Gan of Wei, and Exemplary Instructions (Faxun) by Qiao Zhou of Shu. Ying Shao wrote Comprehensive Interpretations of Customs (Fengsu tongyi), and Wei Zheng compiled Essentials of Governance from the Collected Books (Qunshu zhiyao). Li Jifu had Garden of Sayings, Ancient and Modern (Gujin shuoyuan) [?], and Du You had Essential Purport of Master Guan (Guanshi zhiyao) [?]. Were Balanced Discourses (Lunheng) and Forest of Sayings (Shuolin) not written by Wang Chong and Kong Yan? Were Tales of the World (Shishuo) and Forest of Categories (Leilin) not written by Yiqing and Ziye? As for other works, Master of Ghost Valley (Guiguzi) was by a recluse of the Zhou age; Master Wei Liao (Weiliaozi), by a man of the Six States period; Master Who Embraces Simplicity (Baopuzi), by Ge Hong; Master of the Golden Tower (Jinlouzi), by Emperor Yuan of Liang; Master Guangcheng (Guangchengzi), by Shang Lugong [?]; and Pheasant-Cap Master (Heguanzi), by a recluse of Qi.
Third Policy Question
Liao Ren
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: “In assessing the literary writings and governmental affairs of these two gentlemen, he takes the Way as his guiding principle and adjudicates by the teachings of Cheng and Zhu. This may indeed be called insightful. Moreover, the arrangement throughout accords with the prescribed standards.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “On reading this policy essay, I find its evidential research detailed and clear, and its judgments discerning. He is surely an outstanding scholar of Lingnan.”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “This essay is sound concerning the literary writings and achievements of the two gentlemen, Han and Ouyang [?]. Could its author be someone who has thoroughly read their writings and critically considered the age in which they lived?”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
評品停當足見學識
考試官敎授劉批詞氣舂容而議論切實當
是策手
對文章政事出於道則隨所用而咸備文
章政事離於道則隨所就而難兼盖文章
不可徒為政事不可徒施要必有道以為
之本本有未至隨其才力之所就則優於
此者未必能兼於彼而文章政事始岐而
為二矣請因明問而陳其槩易曰言之無
===
文行之不遠則文章固足以潤身書曰道
洽政治澤潤生民則政事固足以及物然
自三代而上士以脩身體道為本文章乃
其餘事學以窮理盡性為先政事乃其末
節伊尹之德協于克一而伐夏救民之功
伊訓太甲之書後世未有能及之者尹吉
甫之德萬邦為憲而攘夷安夏之功崧高
烝民之什後世未有能過之者世變日下
道學不明則所謂文章者藝焉而已而非
punctuated:
評品停當，足見學識。
考試官敎授劉批：詞氣舂容，而議論切實，當是策手。
對：文章政事出於道，則隨所用而咸備；文章政事離於道，則隨所就而難兼。盖文章不可徒為，政事不可徒施，要必有道以為之本。本有未至，隨其才力之所就，則優於此者未必能兼於彼，而文章政事始岐而為二矣。請因明問而陳其槩。《易》曰：「言之無文，行之不遠。」則文章固足以潤身。《書》曰：「道洽政治，澤潤生民。」則政事固足以及物。然自三代而上，士以脩身體道為本，文章乃其餘事；學以窮理盡性為先，政事乃其末節。伊尹之德，協于克一，而伐夏救民之功、《伊訓》《太甲》之書，後世未有能及之者。尹吉甫之德，萬邦為憲，而攘夷安夏之功、《崧高》《烝民》之什，後世未有能過之者。世變日下，道學不明，則所謂文章者，藝焉而已，而非
translation_en:
… His assessments are well judged, amply demonstrating his learning and discernment.
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: His language and cadence are composed and expansive, while his arguments are pertinent and substantial. He must be an accomplished writer of policy essays.
In reply: When literary composition and governmental affairs proceed from the Way, both are fully available as circumstances require. When they depart from the Way, achievement in one makes it difficult to excel in both. Literary composition must not be undertaken merely for its own sake, nor governmental measures simply put into practice without a foundation: both must have the Way as their basis. If that foundation is imperfect, achievement follows the limits of one’s talent and strength; someone who excels in one field may not also excel in the other.
