Thus literary composition and governmental affairs begin to diverge into two separate pursuits. Allow me to set forth the broad outlines in response to your illuminating question.
The Book of Changes says: “If words lack literary refinement, they will not travel far.” Literary composition can thus indeed adorn one’s person. The Book of Documents says: “The Way prevails and government is well ordered; beneficence enriches the lives of the people.” Governmental affairs can thus indeed bring benefits to others. Yet in the Three Dynasties and earlier, scholars took cultivating themselves and embodying the Way as their foundation; literary composition was a secondary undertaking. Learning gave priority to fathoming principle and fully realizing one’s nature; governmental affairs were its subordinate details.
Yi Yin’s virtue accorded with the ability to remain single-minded. His achievement in overthrowing Xia and saving the people, and the writings “The Instructions of Yi” and “Tai Jia,” have never been equaled by anyone in later ages. Yin Jifu’s virtue served as a model for the myriad states. His achievement in repelling the Yi peoples and securing the Xia realm, and the odes “Lofty Mountains” and “The Multitude of the People,” have never been surpassed by anyone in later ages. As the world changed and declined day by day, learning devoted to the Way became obscure. What was called literary composition then became merely an art, rather than …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
載道之具所謂政事者法焉而已而非正
已之推才性有通塞功力有疎密優於此
者或劣於彼求其能兼之者實難其人試
以韓歐二子論之唐之文章承八代之後
專以雕琢綺麗爲工而氣象萎薾陳子昻
甞欲變之矣而力弗逮至元和間韓愈者
出力去陳言務追古作宋庠謂其奧衍閎
深佐佑六經史臣謂愈之才自視司馬遷
揚雄殆非虛語矣然遷於愈固相上下雄
===
之命意措詞短局滯澁不若愈之肆意有
作不煩繩削則愈於雄似爲過之也宋之
文章承五代之後專以聲律對偶爲事而
文體卑弱穆修甞欲變之矣而才不及至
景祐間歐陽修者出深黜險譎務趨平淡
曾鞏謂其醇深炳鬱渾然天質蘇軾謂修
爲今之韓子亦非過論也然修初得韓文
於故壁破簏之中披閱校讎至老不懈雖
未甞規規追躡其故步而體裁矩矱自成
punctuated:
載道之具；所謂政事者，法焉而已，而非正已之推。才性有通塞，功力有疎密，優於此者或劣於彼，求其能兼之者，實難其人。
試以韓歐二子論之。唐之文章，承八代之後，專以雕琢綺麗爲工，而氣象萎薾。陳子昻甞欲變之矣，而力弗逮。至元和間，韓愈者出，力去陳言，務追古作。宋庠謂其奧衍閎深，佐佑六經；史臣謂愈之才自視司馬遷、揚雄，殆非虛語矣。然遷於愈固相上下，雄之命意措詞，短局滯澁，不若愈之肆意有作，不煩繩削，則愈於雄似爲過之也。
宋之文章，承五代之後，專以聲律對偶爲事，而文體卑弱。穆修甞欲變之矣，而才不及。至景祐間，歐陽修者出，深黜險譎，務趨平淡。曾鞏謂其醇深炳鬱，渾然天質；蘇軾謂修爲今之韓子，亦非過論也。然修初得韓文於故壁破簏之中，披閱校讎，至老不懈。雖未甞規規追躡其故步，而體裁矩矱自成
translation_en:
…a means of conveying the Way; what is called government is merely a matter of methods, rather than an extension of rectifying oneself. Natural abilities may be perceptive or obtuse, and effort may be cursory or thorough. Those who excel in one may fall short in the other; someone capable of combining both is truly difficult to find.
Let us consider Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu. Tang prose inherited the legacy of the Eight Dynasties: its sole measure of accomplishment was elaborate ornament and gorgeous diction, while its spirit was feeble. Chen Zi’ang once sought to change this, but his powers proved insufficient. During the Yuanhe era, Han Yu emerged, striving to eliminate stale expressions and emulate ancient writings. Song Xiang described his writing as profound, expansive, broad, and deep, supporting the Six Classics. The official historian said that Han Yu considered his own talent comparable to that of Sima Qian and Yang Xiong. These were surely no empty words. Yet while Sima Qian and Han Yu were indeed comparable, Yang Xiong’s conception and phrasing were cramped, constrained, labored, and obscure. They did not match Han Yu’s freely flowing compositions, which required no laborious trimming to fit prescribed rules. Han Yu thus seems to have surpassed Yang Xiong.
Song prose inherited the legacy of the Five Dynasties: it concerned itself exclusively with tonal patterns and parallel phrasing, while its style was low and weak. Mu Xiu once sought to change this, but his talent proved insufficient. During the Jingyou era, Ouyang Xiu emerged, firmly rejecting strained and peculiar expression and striving for simplicity and naturalness. Zeng Gong described his writing as pure and profound, brilliant and richly wrought, its natural qualities forming a seamless whole. Su Shi called him the Han Yu of his own day; this too was no exaggerated judgment. Yet Ouyang Xiu first obtained Han Yu’s writings from a broken bamboo chest by an old wall. He read and collated them, never slackening even in old age. Although he never scrupulously retraced Han Yu’s footsteps, in literary form and standards he established his own…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一家則修於愈庶乎及之矣今考其遺文
愈之原道原性師說等篇發明天地人物
之理往往有前人所未發者程子所謂不
可漫觀者是已惜其因文見道而無格致
之學故以博愛為仁則語用而遺體性有
三品則泝流而失源揆之以聖人之道不
能無牴牾焉修之本論易童子問詩本義
諸作發明古今名物之理往往有經傳所
未及者朱文公所謂平易說理者是已惜
===
其專意業文而無濂洛之學故以繫辭非
孔子之經周禮非周公所作揆之於聖人
之道不能無枘鑿焉愈性鯁直李逢吉皇
甫鎛輩深忌之晚為裴度所知然卒不能
薦之於朝議者深為之惜然觀其始論宮
市繼論佛骨刺潮州而以文行化俗使魏
博而以口舌解圍其見於樹立者卓有可
觀使唐果能相愈亦豈無所補乎修性狷
介彭思永蔣之奇輩屢譖之晚用韓琦之
punctuated:
一家，則修於愈庶乎及之矣。今考其遺文，愈之《原道》《原性》《師說》等篇，發明天地人物之理，往往有前人所未發者，程子所謂不可漫觀者是已。惜其因文見道，而無格致之學，故以博愛為仁，則語用而遺體；性有三品，則泝流而失源。揆之以聖人之道，不能無牴牾焉。修之《本論》《易童子問》《詩本義》諸作，發明古今名物之理，往往有經傳所未及者，朱文公所謂平易說理者是已。惜其專意業文，而無濂洛之學，故以《繫辭》非孔子之經，《周禮》非周公所作。揆之於聖人之道，不能無枘鑿焉。
愈性鯁直，李逢吉、皇甫鎛輩深忌之，晚為裴度所知，然卒不能薦之於朝，議者深為之惜。然觀其始論宮市，繼論佛骨，刺潮州而以文行化俗，使魏博而以口舌解圍，其見於樹立者，卓有可觀。使唐果能相愈，亦豈無所補乎？修性狷介，彭思永、蔣之奇輩屢譖之，晚用韓琦之
translation_en:
…a school of his own; thus Ouyang Xiu came close to matching Han Yu. Examining their surviving writings, we find that Han Yu’s essays Inquiry into the Way, Inquiry into Human Nature, and On Teachers elucidate the principles of Heaven, Earth, human beings, and things, often revealing what earlier writers had not brought to light. These are what Master Cheng meant when he said that they must not be read casually. Regrettably, Han apprehended the Way through literary composition but lacked learning in the investigation of things and extension of knowledge. Thus, in defining benevolence as universal love, he spoke of its functioning while overlooking its substance; in maintaining that human nature has three grades, he traced the current but missed its source. Measured against the Way of the sages, his views inevitably contain contradictions. Ouyang Xiu’s works, including On Fundamentals, Questions of a Youth about the Changes, and The Original Meaning of the Odes, elucidate the principles underlying institutions and things, past and present, often addressing matters untouched by the classics and their commentaries. These exemplify what Zhu Xi, Duke Wen, called explaining principles in plain and accessible language. Regrettably, Ouyang devoted himself exclusively to literary composition and lacked the learning of Lianxi and the Luo school. Thus he held that the Appended Statements was not a canonical text by Confucius and that the Rites of Zhou was not written by the Duke of Zhou. Measured against the Way of the sages, his views inevitably fit as poorly as mismatched tenons and mortises.
Han Yu was forthright by nature, and men such as Li Fengji and Huangfu Bo deeply resented him. Late in life he gained Pei Du’s appreciation, yet Pei ultimately failed to recommend him to the court, which commentators have greatly regretted on Han’s behalf. Yet consider how he first remonstrated against palace purchases and later against the Buddha’s bone; how, as Prefect of Chaozhou, he transformed local customs through his writings and conduct; and how, as an envoy to Weibo, he resolved a siege through persuasion. His concrete achievements were outstanding and worthy of admiration. Had the Tang indeed made Han Yu a chief councilor, could he have failed to contribute? Ouyang Xiu was uncompromising and upright by nature, and men such as Peng Siyong and Jiang Zhiqi repeatedly slandered him. Late in life, through Han Qi’s…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
薦而與同登政府不可謂之不遇及觀其
遺司諫之書進朋黨之論議麟州之屯田
阻六塔之河道其見於建白者綽有可紀
則修之用於宋亦可謂無負矣然要其所
至則愈以文章名於唐而身繫安危如裴
度者終非愈之所優修以文章名於宋而
功在社稷如韓琦者每爲修之所服則天
下後世之公論不可誣矣愚生幸際
明時思樂泮水固將假文字以進身而欲效
===
其所欲爲者也其於韓歐二子未敢以爲
終身之地而於商之伊尹周之吉甫竊有
志焉執事幸毋以爲僭
第四問
蕭汝爲
同考試官教諭顧批粤中風俗人才評品精覈
而篇末數語尤精采動人非積學之士不能也
同考試官教諭閔批此策條荅詳明措辭清雅篇
終又含蓄感慨不盡之意蓋尚友古人者也錄之以考其後
punctuated:
薦，而與同登政府，不可謂之不遇。及觀其遺司諫之書、進朋黨之論、議麟州之屯田、阻六塔之河道，其見於建白者，綽有可紀，則修之用於宋，亦可謂無負矣。然要其所至，則愈以文章名於唐，而身繫安危如裴度者，終非愈之所優；修以文章名於宋，而功在社稷如韓琦者，每爲修之所服，則天下後世之公論不可誣矣。愚生幸際明時，思樂泮水，固將假文字以進身，而欲效其所欲爲者也。其於韓、歐二子，未敢以爲終身之地，而於商之伊尹、周之吉甫，竊有志焉。執事幸毋以爲僭。

第四問

蕭汝爲

同考試官教諭顧批：粤中風俗人才，評品精覈，而篇末數語，尤精采動人，非積學之士不能也。

同考試官教諭閔批：此策條荅詳明，措辭清雅，篇終又含蓄感慨不盡之意，蓋尚友古人者也。錄之以考其後。
translation_en:
…on Han Qi’s recommendation, and entered the highest councils of government alongside him: one cannot say that he lacked opportunities. Consider his letter to the Remonstrator, his discourse on factions submitted to the throne, his proposals concerning agricultural colonies at Linzhou, and his opposition to the Liuta river channel project. His policy proposals offer ample achievements worth recording; thus Ouyang Xiu’s service under the Song may also be said to have fulfilled the trust placed in him. Yet, to assess their ultimate attainments, Han Yu won fame through his literary writings under the Tang, but bearing responsibility for the state’s security, as Pei Du did, was ultimately not his strength. Ouyang Xiu won fame through his literary writings under the Song, but he consistently deferred to men such as Han Qi for their contributions to the state. The impartial judgment of the world and posterity cannot be gainsaid.

I, an unworthy student, am fortunate to live in an enlightened age and rejoice in the learning of the schools, as in the ode “The Waters of the Pan.” Certainly I intend to advance through literary accomplishment and put my aspirations into practice. As for Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu, I would not presume to make their attainments the limit of my lifelong endeavor; rather, I privately aspire to emulate Yi Yin of the Shang and Jifu of the Zhou. I hope that you, honored examiners, will not consider this presumptuous.

Fourth Question

Xiao Ruwei

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: His assessment of Guangdong’s customs and talented men is precise and discerning. The few sentences at the end are especially brilliant and moving. Only a man of accumulated learning could achieve this.

Comment by Associate Examiner Min, Instructor: This policy essay answers each point thoroughly and clearly, with lucid and elegant phrasing. Its ending also conveys restrained reflections and emotions whose implications are inexhaustible. He is surely one who takes the ancients as his friends. I select this essay for inclusion so that his subsequent progress may be assessed.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正何批博雅之才具見此策嶺南
佳士吾當於子拭目
考試官教授劉批辭嚴義正深得儒先探本
之意是用錄出
對風俗因地而異同知有以變之則無不
可同之地賢才因時而盛衰知有以興之
則無不可盛之時蓋風俗賢才固未可以
地與時論也亦在變之興之何如耳有化
導之方有轉移之術培植之旣固漸摩之
===
===
旣久則異可同衰可盛自有不言而化之
妙此其機也而神其機者固執事所謂存
乎其人也傳曰爲政在人經曰遐不作人
其有見於此歟敢摭其說以對風俗不以
人而變乎何東郊頑民乃卒化於三后協
心之日賢才不以人而興乎何孔門諸賢
乃並起於東魯洙泗之鄉是必有故矣今
之東廣古南粤地也而廣州等十府卽漢
交州所部南海等郡是已其地多民夷雜
punctuated:
考試官學正何批：博雅之才，具見此策。嶺南佳士，吾當於子拭目。
考試官教授劉批：辭嚴義正，深得儒先探本之意，是用錄出。
對：風俗因地而異同，知有以變之，則無不可同之地；賢才因時而盛衰，知有以興之，則無不可盛之時。蓋風俗賢才，固未可以地與時論也，亦在變之興之何如耳。有化導之方，有轉移之術，培植之旣固，漸摩之旣久，則異可同，衰可盛，自有不言而化之妙。此其機也，而神其機者，固執事所謂存乎其人也。傳曰：「爲政在人。」經曰：「遐不作人。」其有見於此歟？敢摭其說以對。風俗不以人而變乎？何東郊頑民，乃卒化於三后協心之日？賢才不以人而興乎？何孔門諸賢，乃並起於東魯洙泗之鄉？是必有故矣。今之東廣，古南粤地也，而廣州等十府，卽漢交州所部南海等郡是已。其地多民夷雜
translation_en:
Examiner He, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “The writer’s broad learning and refined abilities are fully displayed in this policy essay. Among the outstanding scholars of Lingnan, I shall watch you with particular expectation.”
Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: “The language is rigorous and the principles correct. It deeply grasps the intent of earlier Confucian masters in probing fundamentals. For this reason, it has been selected for inclusion.”
Reply: Customs differ or resemble one another according to place; if one knows how to transform them, there is no place where they cannot be brought into conformity. Worthy talent flourishes or declines according to the times; if one knows how to foster it, there is no time when it cannot flourish. Thus customs and worthy talent cannot properly be judged by place and time alone. Everything also depends on how they are transformed and fostered. With methods of moral instruction and techniques for effecting change, once cultivation is firmly established and gradual refinement has continued long enough, differences can be brought into conformity and decline can turn to flourishing. There naturally emerges the subtle efficacy of transformation without words. This is the crucial mechanism; what makes its operation wondrous is precisely what you, honored examiners, mean by saying that it rests with the person. The commentary says, “The conduct of government rests with the person.” The classic says, “Why should he not nurture men?” Do these sayings not show insight into this? I venture to draw upon their meaning in my reply.
Are customs not transformed through people? Why, then, were the obstinate people of the eastern suburbs finally transformed when the three rulers acted with one heart? Is worthy talent not fostered through people? Why, then, did the many worthies of Confucius’s school arise together in eastern Lu, in the region of the Zhu and Si rivers? There must surely be reasons for this. Present-day Guangdong is the territory of ancient Nanyue, and its ten prefectures, including Guangzhou, correspond to Nanhai and the other commanderies administered by Jiaozhou under the Han. In this territory, many commoners and non-Han peoples intermingle…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
處其風俗不同自其變者言之廣之俗則
質直尚信韶之俗則淳樸愿愨惠之俗則
文物有加焉若他郡之美具載圖誌固不
得而盡述也自其未變者言之如信巫淫
祀喪用樂之類雖當
聖朝誕敷文德之時鄉士夫固敦尚名教矣其
比閭族黨之間深山邊海之區亦或有不
免者其故何哉以變之無其人耳使如執
事所謂常衮文翁者置為長民之吏則變
===
而通之革而信之尚何風俗之不與化推
移耶昔韓愈之治潮州也師延趙德潮人
化之遂篤於文行張紘之治雷州也禮明
宗子雷人化之悉更其舊習執是而徵諸
常衮文翁蓋先後一揆焉嗚呼先民不作
遺矩猶存安得若人者而為風俗之指南
哉其地多山川靈秀其人才間出自其賢
者觀之在漢則有若董正之高潔在唐則
有若張九齡之相業在宋則有若余靖之
punctuated:
處，其風俗不同。自其變者言之，廣之俗則質直尚信，韶之俗則淳樸愿愨，惠之俗則文物有加焉。若他郡之美，具載圖誌，固不得而盡述也。自其未變者言之，如信巫淫祀、喪用樂之類，雖當聖朝誕敷文德之時，鄉士夫固敦尚名教矣，其比閭族黨之間、深山邊海之區，亦或有不免者。其故何哉？以變之無其人耳。使如執事所謂常衮、文翁者，置為長民之吏，則變而通之，革而信之，尚何風俗之不與化推移耶？昔韓愈之治潮州也，師延趙德，潮人化之，遂篤於文行；張紘之治雷州也，禮明宗子，雷人化之，悉更其舊習。執是而徵諸常衮、文翁，蓋先後一揆焉。嗚呼！先民不作，遺矩猶存，安得若人者而為風俗之指南哉？

其地多山川靈秀，其人才間出。自其賢者觀之，在漢則有若董正之高潔，在唐則有若張九齡之相業，在宋則有若余靖之
translation_en:
…living intermingled, their customs differ. Speaking of those that have undergone transformation, the customs of Guangzhou are straightforward and prize trustworthiness; those of Shaozhou are simple, honest, and sincere; and those of Huizhou display still greater cultural refinement. The admirable features of the other prefectures are fully recorded in maps and gazetteers and cannot all be recounted here. Speaking of those that have not yet changed, there are such practices as trusting shamans, offering unauthorized sacrifices, and using music at funerals. Although our sagely dynasty is now spreading its civil virtues far and wide, and local gentlemen certainly esteem and uphold the moral teachings, such practices may still persist among neighborhood and lineage communities and in remote mountain and coastal districts. Why is this? Simply because the right people are lacking to transform them. If men like Chang Gun and Wen Weng, whom you have mentioned, were appointed as officials to govern the people, they would bring about change and make it effective, reform practices and win trust. What customs could then fail to change with their transforming influence? Formerly, when Han Yu governed Chaozhou, he invited Zhao De to serve as a teacher. The people of Chaozhou were transformed by this and became devoted to literary learning and moral conduct. When Zhang Hong governed Leizhou, he honored Ming Zongzi [?]; the people of Leizhou were transformed and entirely changed their old habits. If these examples are compared with Chang Gun and Wen Weng, the earlier and later cases followed the same principle. Alas! Those men of old will not rise again, but the standards they left remain. Where can we find men like them to guide the customs of the people?

This region abounds in spiritually potent mountains and beautiful rivers, and talented men emerge from time to time. Considering its worthy men, under the Han there was the lofty integrity of Dong Zheng; under the Tang, the achievements of Zhang Jiuling as chief councilor; and under the Song, there was Yu Jing’s…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
邊功焉其事行之詳具載史傳亦不得而
槩舉也自其賢而繼出者觀之如關敏鄧
顒陳鼎之輩正值
聖朝開國承家之日關敏固闔門死忠矣而鄧
顒委身濟難之烈陳鼎蹇諤不阿之行是
皆人所難者其故何哉以興之有其人耳
誠如執事所謂董逸民張文獻者首開南
粤之荒則高山仰止景行行止尚何賢才
之不項背相望耶昔言偃載道而南至宋
===
范仲淹諸賢輩出而吳遂爲文物之望陳
良游學於北至宋周茂叔大儒特起而楚
遂爲道學之邦執是而徵之董正九齡蓋
古今一律焉嗚呼不有先覺孰開我人安
得數公者而爲人物之標的哉愚也仰往
哲之孤高悼末俗之簡陋而欲振衣於千
仞之崗久矣倘與其進吾將過闕里而弔
古循東郊而問俗不知尚有往日其人否
乎謹對
punctuated:
邊功焉。其事行之詳，具載史傳，亦不得而槩舉也。自其賢而繼出者觀之，如關敏、鄧顒、陳鼎之輩，正值聖朝開國承家之日。關敏固闔門死忠矣，而鄧顒委身濟難之烈、陳鼎蹇諤不阿之行，是皆人所難者。其故何哉？以興之有其人耳。誠如執事所謂董逸民、張文獻者，首開南粤之荒，則「高山仰止，景行行止」，尚何賢才之不項背相望耶？昔言偃載道而南，至宋范仲淹諸賢輩出，而吳遂爲文物之望；陳良游學於北，至宋周茂叔大儒特起，而楚遂爲道學之邦。執是而徵之董正、九齡，蓋古今一律焉。

嗚呼！不有先覺，孰開我人？安得數公者而爲人物之標的哉？愚也仰往哲之孤高，悼末俗之簡陋，而欲振衣於千仞之崗久矣。倘與其進，吾將過闕里而弔古，循東郊而問俗，不知尚有往日其人否乎？謹對。
translation_en:
… achievements on the frontier. The details of their deeds and conduct are fully recorded in the histories and biographies; I cannot enumerate even their broad outlines here. Looking at the worthy men who followed them, such figures as Guan Min, Deng Yong, and Chen Ding lived precisely when our sagely dynasty was founding its state and establishing its ruling house. Guan Min, together with his entire household, died in loyalty. Deng Yong’s heroic devotion to relieving the crisis and Chen Ding’s forthright, unbending conduct were likewise things difficult for anyone to accomplish. Why was this so? Because there were men to inspire them.

Indeed, as you, honored sir, have said, Dong the Recluse and Zhang Wenxian first opened up the uncultivated region of Nanyue. Thus, “We look up to the lofty mountain; we follow the great road.” How could worthy talents then fail to follow one another in close succession? Long ago, Yan Yan carried the Way southward. By the Song, Fan Zhongyan and other worthies emerged in succession, and Wu consequently became a region renowned for its cultural accomplishments. Chen Liang traveled north to study. By the Song, the great Confucian Zhou Maoshu rose to particular prominence, and Chu consequently became a land of the Learning of the Way. If we use these examples to examine Dong Zheng and Zhang Jiuling, the same pattern holds in antiquity and in later times.

Alas! Without those who awaken first, who would enlighten our people? Where can we find men like these gentlemen to serve as models for others? In my humble person, I admire the lofty independence of the wise men of the past and lament the crudeness of the customs of this declining age. I have long wished to shake out my robes upon a ridge a thousand ren high. If you approve my advancement, I shall visit Queli to pay homage to antiquity and travel through the eastern outskirts to inquire into local customs. I wonder whether men like those of former days may still be found. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第五問
潘濂
同考試官訓導陳批時務一策正欲觀士子識
見何如此答者究得實處置有方决非迂腐之士也
同考試官訓導楊批論馭兵恤民二事援古證今
卓有所見所謂識時務者在俊傑子足當之矣
考試官學正何批議處時事俱合機宜足見
學識
考試官教授劉批論時事有根據有識見
===
凡士哉
天下之事所以防其患者在有其道所以
任其責者在得其人夫法敝而為之立患
生而為之防此理也亦勢也然非得人以
任之則膠膠擾擾紛變於吾前者日不知
其幾而天下之事始多矣自今觀之民惟
邦本本固邦寧民不可以不恤也天下雖
安忘戰則危兵不可以不馭也今之談者
動曰恤民在守令而難其人馭兵在將帥
punctuated:
第五問
潘濂
同考試官訓導陳批：時務一策，正欲觀士子識見何如。此答者究得實，處置有方，决非迂腐之士也。
同考試官訓導楊批：論馭兵恤民二事，援古證今，卓有所見。所謂識時務者在俊傑，子足當之矣。
考試官學正何批：議處時事，俱合機宜，足見學識。
考試官教授劉批：論時事，有根據，有識見，凡士哉！
天下之事，所以防其患者在有其道，所以任其責者在得其人。夫法敝而為之立，患生而為之防，此理也，亦勢也。然非得人以任之，則膠膠擾擾、紛變於吾前者，日不知其幾，而天下之事始多矣。自今觀之，民惟邦本，本固邦寧，民不可以不恤也；天下雖安，忘戰則危，兵不可以不馭也。今之談者動曰：恤民在守令，而難其人；馭兵在將帥，
translation_en:
Fifth Policy Question
Pan Lian
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: This policy question on current affairs was intended precisely to ascertain the candidates’ judgment. This respondent gets to the substance of the matter and proposes sound measures. He is certainly no pedantic scholar.
Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: In discussing the two matters of controlling troops and caring for the people, he draws on antiquity to substantiate his arguments about the present, displaying outstanding insight. As the saying goes, those who understand the needs of the times are men of exceptional talent. You fully deserve that description.
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: His proposals for handling current affairs all suit the circumstances, amply demonstrating his learning and judgment.
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: His discussion of current affairs is well grounded and insightful. An ordinary scholar indeed! [?]
In the affairs of the realm, preventing troubles depends on having the proper methods, and entrusting responsibility depends on finding the right people. To establish laws when existing ones have deteriorated, and to take preventive measures when troubles arise, accords both with principle and with the demands of circumstances. Yet unless the right people are found to undertake these responsibilities, disturbances and bewildering changes will arise before us in untold numbers each day, and the realm’s difficulties will multiply. Looking at the present, the people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is secure, the state is at peace. Thus the people must be cared for. Though the realm be peaceful, forgetting warfare brings danger. Thus the troops must be controlled. Those who discuss these matters today constantly say: caring for the people rests with prefects and magistrates, but finding the right people is difficult; controlling the troops rests with military commanders …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而難其人此非天下之通論也天生一世
之材自足以效一世之用顧在任之何如
爾載觀古之人孝武窮征遠討海内虚耗
而東方朔進薄其賦斂之言德宗剛愎自
任藩鎮離心而陸贄獻輕稅薄征之諫元
氣欲惜賦斂當輕此胡安國上時政之忠
議也紀綱欲立民力湏寬此朱熹應直言
之正論也是數君子其知國之所恃在民
民之所恃在守令者乎趙充國以四萬騎
===
屯沿邊九郡而單于引去李德裕以十一
軍控制西北二邊而南詔請還監博州郡
脩治器械而虜人遠遁此馬知節之謀略
可嘉也閱延州兵日夜訓練而敵人相戒
此范仲淹之威望可畏也是數君子其知
民之所衛在兵兵之所馭在將帥者乎方
今
皇風清穆海宇輯寧干戈積府庫之塵閭里興
載芟之頌太平之治復見於
punctuated:
而難其人，此非天下之通論也。天生一世之材，自足以效一世之用，顧在任之何如爾。載觀古之人，孝武窮征遠討，海内虚耗，而東方朔進薄其賦斂之言；德宗剛愎自任，藩鎮離心，而陸贄獻輕稅薄征之諫。元氣欲惜，賦斂當輕，此胡安國上時政之忠議也；紀綱欲立，民力湏寬，此朱熹應直言之正論也。是數君子，其知國之所恃在民，民之所恃在守令者乎？趙充國以四萬騎屯沿邊九郡，而單于引去；李德裕以十一軍控制西北二邊，而南詔請還。監博州郡，脩治器械，而虜人遠遁，此馬知節之謀略可嘉也；閱延州兵，日夜訓練，而敵人相戒，此范仲淹之威望可畏也。是數君子，其知民之所衛在兵，兵之所馭在將帥者乎？
方今皇風清穆，海宇輯寧，干戈積府庫之塵，閭里興《載芟》之頌，太平之治復見於
translation_en:
…yet finding the right men is difficult. This is no sound general judgment of the affairs of the realm. Heaven produces talent in each age sufficient to serve that age’s needs; the question is simply how it is employed. Looking further at men of antiquity: when Emperor Xiaowu pursued distant campaigns to exhaustion and depleted the resources of the realm, Dongfang Shuo urged him to reduce tax exactions. When Emperor Dezong obstinately trusted his own judgment and the regional military commands became estranged, Lu Zhi presented remonstrances urging lighter taxation and reduced levies. To preserve the state’s vital energies, tax exactions must be light: this was Hu Anguo’s loyal counsel in his submission on current government. To establish governing order and discipline, the people’s resources must be spared: this was Zhu Xi’s sound argument in response to a call for frank advice. Did not these gentlemen understand that the state depends upon the people, and the people upon prefects and magistrates?
Zhao Chongguo stationed forty thousand cavalry in nine frontier commanderies, and the chanyu withdrew. Li Deyu used eleven armies to command the northwestern frontier regions, and Nanzhao requested permission to return [?]. Supervising the prefecture of Bo [?], repairing and putting weapons and equipment in order, and thereby causing the enemy to flee far away—such was Ma Zhijie’s praiseworthy strategy. Inspecting the troops of Yanzhou and training them day and night, so that the enemy warned one another against him—such was Fan Zhongyan’s awe-inspiring prestige. Did not these gentlemen understand that the people are protected by soldiers, and soldiers are controlled by generals?
Today, the imperial influence is pure and harmonious, and the realm is united and tranquil. Shields and spears gather dust in the government storehouses, while the villages raise the praises of “They Cleared Away the Grass” (Zai shan). An age of great peace is once again witnessed in…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今日矣往年湖湘歲歉致厪
當宁之憂於是竭府庫停起運而所以賑恤
吾民者至矣執事猶懷意外之患而以諸
路水旱為慮愚以為人君有憂勤惕厲之
心自足以感召和氣固無是矣萬一有之
則古人救荒之政具在或發倉廩以賑乏
或為粥溢以救殍或興工作以聚失業或
弛刑禁以釋無辜罷不急之務去無名之
征募商糶粟可行也諸路借運可行也何
===
患救荒之無其策哉近時襄漢有警致煩
宵旰之憂於是調土兵募民兵而所以捍衞
吾民者至矣執事猶抱意外之虞而以他
處盜賊繼起為念愚以為人君有神武不
殺之威自足以戡定禍亂固無是矣萬一
有之則古人禦寇之法具在先加威武以
懾其心次示招安以弛其計多方間諜擣
虛攻盈居則謹烽堠出則禁侵掠賊勢少
緩則一路之兵可捍禦也賊勢衆大則諸
punctuated:
今日矣。往年湖湘歲歉，致厪當宁之憂。於是竭府庫，停起運，而所以賑恤吾民者至矣。執事猶懷意外之患，而以諸路水旱為慮。愚以為人君有憂勤惕厲之心，自足以感召和氣，固無是矣。萬一有之，則古人救荒之政具在：或發倉廩以賑乏，或為粥溢以救殍，或興工作以聚失業，或弛刑禁以釋無辜。罷不急之務，去無名之征，募商糶粟可行也，諸路借運可行也，何患救荒之無其策哉？

近時襄漢有警，致煩宵旰之憂。於是調土兵，募民兵，而所以捍衞吾民者至矣。執事猶抱意外之虞，而以他處盜賊繼起為念。愚以為人君有神武不殺之威，自足以戡定禍亂，固無是矣。萬一有之，則古人禦寇之法具在：先加威武以懾其心，次示招安以弛其計，多方間諜，擣虛攻盈；居則謹烽堠，出則禁侵掠。賊勢少緩，則一路之兵可捍禦也；賊勢衆大，則諸
translation_en:
…today. In past years, poor harvests in Huxiang caused the sovereign anxious concern. The government thereupon exhausted its treasuries and storehouses and suspended shipments of tax revenues, doing everything possible to relieve our people. Yet you, sir, still harbor fears of unforeseen troubles and worry about floods and droughts in the various regions. In my humble opinion, when the ruler is concerned and diligent, vigilant and watchful, this alone suffices to call forth harmonious influences, and such calamities surely will not occur. Should they nevertheless occur, the famine-relief measures of the ancients are all available: opening granaries to relieve those in want; preparing gruel [?] to save the starving; undertaking public works to gather and employ those who have lost their livelihoods; or relaxing penal prohibitions to release the innocent. Suspend tasks that are not urgent and abolish levies without justification. Recruiting merchants to sell grain is practicable; arranging for grain to be borrowed and transported among the various regions is also practicable. Why fear that there are no policies for relieving famine?

Recently, disturbances in Xianghan caused the sovereign such anxiety that he rose before dawn and ate only late in the day. The government thereupon mobilized native troops and recruited militia, doing everything possible to protect our people. Yet you, sir, still fear unforeseen dangers and worry that bandits will arise in succession elsewhere. In my humble opinion, when the ruler possesses the awe-inspiring power of divine martial prowess that subdues without killing, this alone suffices to quell calamity and disorder, and such troubles surely will not occur. Should they nevertheless occur, the methods of the ancients for resisting bandits are all available: first deploy military might to strike fear into their hearts, then offer amnesty and submission to loosen their resolve. Employ spies in many ways; strike where they are weak and attack where they are concentrated. When stationed, maintain vigilant beacon posts; when advancing, prohibit incursions and plundering. If the bandits’ strength abates somewhat, the troops of a single region can hold them off; if their forces are numerous and powerful, then the various…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
路之兵可召集也孰謂禦寇之無其略哉
雖然此特其法爾而所以行夫法者顧在
於得人耳先儒謂斯民之休戚係守令之
賢否方今天下民力之匱竭不但湖湘爲
然也若郡縣之守令果得人如召信臣之
在南陽爲民興利而躬勸農桑卓茂之在
密邑勞心撫字而視民如子賈琮之在交
趾蠲復徭役而謳歌四起則必有以培植
乎元氣而黎民享其安矣先儒謂天下無
===
必勝之兵而有不可敗之將方今天下軍
士之消耗不但襄漢爲然也若邊陲之將
帥果得人如郭子儀之屯涇陽馭下以恕
而將士樂用李光弼之代朔方號令精明
而人心自服曹彬監征蜀之軍申令戢下
而所在秋毫無犯則必有以振揚乎威武
而軍士樂於用矣然守令之賢否將帥之
勇怯則又在乎
朝廷慎選作興何如耳此廟堂密勿之至計
punctuated: 路之兵可召集也。孰謂禦寇之無其略哉？雖然，此特其法爾，而所以行夫法者，顧在於得人耳。先儒謂：「斯民之休戚，係守令之賢否。」方今天下民力之匱竭，不但湖湘爲然也。若郡縣之守令果得人，如召信臣之在南陽，爲民興利而躬勸農桑；卓茂之在密邑，勞心撫字而視民如子；賈琮之在交趾，蠲復徭役而謳歌四起，則必有以培植乎元氣，而黎民享其安矣。先儒謂：「天下無必勝之兵，而有不可敗之將。」方今天下軍士之消耗，不但襄漢爲然也。若邊陲之將帥果得人，如郭子儀之屯涇陽，馭下以恕而將士樂用；李光弼之代朔方，號令精明而人心自服；曹彬監征蜀之軍，申令戢下而所在秋毫無犯，則必有以振揚乎威武，而軍士樂於用矣。然守令之賢否、將帥之勇怯，則又在乎朝廷慎選作興何如耳。此廟堂密勿之至計
translation_en:
…the troops of the various circuits can be summoned and assembled. Who could say that there is no strategy for resisting bandits? Yet these are merely methods; putting them into practice depends on finding the right men. Earlier Confucian scholars said: “The well-being or suffering of the people depends on whether their prefects and magistrates are worthy.” Today, the exhaustion of the people’s resources throughout the realm is by no means confined to the Hu-Xiang region. If the prefectures and counties truly obtain the right men as prefects and magistrates—men like Shao Xinchen in Nanyang, who promoted measures benefiting the people and personally encouraged farming and sericulture; Zhuo Mao in Mi, who devoted himself to nurturing the people and regarded them as his children; and Jia Cong in Jiaozhi, who remitted corvée obligations, so that songs of praise arose everywhere—then there will assuredly be a means to nurture the fundamental vitality of the realm, and the common people will enjoy peace.

Earlier Confucian scholars said: “There are no armies under Heaven certain of victory, but there are generals who cannot be defeated.” Today, the depletion of military manpower throughout the realm is by no means confined to the Xiang-Han region. If the frontier commands truly obtain the right men as generals—men like Guo Ziyi when stationed at Jingyang, who governed his subordinates with forbearance, so that officers and soldiers gladly served him; Li Guangbi when taking over command at Shuofang [?], whose orders were precise and clear, so that men willingly submitted; and Cao Bin, who supervised the army campaigning against Shu, reiterating his orders and restraining his subordinates, so that wherever they went they did not encroach upon so much as an autumn hair—then there will assuredly be a means to invigorate military might, and the soldiers will serve willingly. Yet whether prefects and magistrates are worthy or unworthy, and generals brave or cowardly, depends in turn on how carefully the court selects and encourages them. This is a matter of the utmost importance for the court’s confidential deliberations…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下經乆之遠圖顧草茅賤士何足以語
此然竊有志焉惟執事進教之可也
punctuated: 天下經乆之遠圖。顧草茅賤士，何足以語此？然竊有志焉，惟執事進教之可也。
translation_en: …and a far-reaching plan for the enduring stability of the realm. Yet how could a lowly scholar from the countryside be qualified to speak of this? Nevertheless, I humbly aspire to contribute to it, and ask only that you, honored officials, favor me with your instruction.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
我
太祖高皇帝奄有天下之初規畫庶
務而於設科取士則尤加之意
焉是故三載一舉行之其制大
備于洪武甲子條貫截然著為
令典歷世守之而無敝也迺今
===
正德庚午適當天下鄉試之期
洽膺聘而来濫竽取士之柄事
既竣刻士之邑里名氏并文之
粹者與夫内外執事之職名為
鄉試錄將獻諸
天子傳之天下洽竊序其後曰惟天
生賢與賢之用世要皆非偶然
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

我太祖高皇帝奄有天下之初，規畫庶務，而於設科取士則尤加之意焉。是故三載一舉行之，其制大備于洪武甲子，條貫截然，著為令典，歷世守之而無敝也。迺今正德庚午，適當天下鄉試之期，洽膺聘而来，濫竽取士之柄。事既竣，刻士之邑里名氏，并文之粹者，與夫内外執事之職名，為《鄉試錄》，將獻諸天子，傳之天下。洽竊序其後曰：惟天生賢，與賢之用世，要皆非偶然
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

When our Emperor Taizu Gao first took possession of all under Heaven, he laid plans for the many affairs of government, giving particular attention to establishing examinations for the selection of scholars. Accordingly, these were held once every three years. The system was fully elaborated in the jiazi year of Hongwu [1384], its provisions clearly delineated and promulgated as authoritative regulations. Successive generations observed them without their falling into disrepair. Now, in the gengwu year of Zhengde [1510], the appointed time for Provincial Examinations throughout the realm has arrived. I, Qia, came in response to an invitation and, despite my inadequacy, assumed responsibility for selecting scholars. Once the work was completed, the scholars’ home localities and names, together with their finest compositions and the official titles and names of those serving within and outside the examination compound, were engraved for printing as the Record of the Provincial Examination, to be presented to the Son of Heaven and circulated throughout the realm. I, Qia, venture to append this postface: Heaven’s bringing forth worthy men, and worthy men’s service in the world, are surely neither matters of chance…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者東廣古南粵地也歷秦與漢
土地開拓積數百年而文獻張
公出焉東南文運藉是一倡自
夫辨邪之智識事君之忠藎當
時人物卒難並埒又積數百年
而忠襄余公出焉其文章尚矣
在朝也著蹇諤之風在邕州也
===
收經營之績至今人誦之不已
要之天有意於二公故其出而
用世也如此夫豈偶然者哉矧
我
國家
聖聖相承道化浹洽天心克眷畀以
才賢宜乎數十年来賢人君子
punctuated: 者。東廣，古南粵地也。歷秦與漢，土地開拓，積數百年，而文獻張公出焉。東南文運，藉是一倡。自夫辨邪之智識、事君之忠藎，當時人物卒難並埒。又積數百年，而忠襄余公出焉。其文章尚矣，在朝也，著蹇諤之風；在邕州也，收經營之績。至今人誦之不已。要之，天有意於二公，故其出而用世也如此，夫豈偶然者哉？矧我國家，聖聖相承，道化浹洽，天心克眷，畀以才賢。宜乎數十年來，賢人君子
translation_en:
… Eastern Guangdong was the territory of ancient Nanyue. Through the Qin and Han dynasties, its territory was opened up and expanded. After several hundred years, Lord Zhang, posthumously titled Wenxian, emerged there. Through him, the literary fortunes of the southeast received their first great impetus. In his discernment of wickedness and his wholehearted loyalty in serving his ruler, the men of his time could scarcely equal him. Several hundred more years passed, and Lord Yu, posthumously titled Zhongxiang, emerged. His literary achievements were outstanding. At court, he distinguished himself by his forthright remonstrance; in Yongzhou, he achieved success in administering and developing the region. To this day, people continue to praise him. In sum, Heaven had a purpose for these two men; hence their emergence and service to the world took this form. How could this have been accidental?
How much more is this true of our dynasty! Sage sovereign has succeeded sage sovereign, and the transforming influence of the Way has spread everywhere. Heaven has graciously favored it, bestowing talented and worthy men upon it. It is fitting, then, that over the past several decades, worthy men and gentlemen …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以文章魁天下類是者恒多夷
考其政事參預館閣職司臺諫
者足以羽儀乎
天朝布列方嶽分牧郡縣者又足以
鎮重乎外服故嘗論天下士必
先焉論科目得人而莫敢少焉
諸士子獲取於是矣行將角天
===
下士則夫奉
廷對服官序實昉於此將何以為
之地耶必曰不徒以文章為也
行檢其郛郭不徒以政事為也
學術其基本近師之今之前輩
是也遠師之文獻忠襄公是也
等而上之則雖伊傅周召亦吾
punctuated: 以文章魁天下，類是者恒多。夷考其政事，參預館閣、職司臺諫者，足以羽儀乎天朝；布列方嶽、分牧郡縣者，又足以鎮重乎外服。故嘗論天下士，必先焉；論科目得人，而莫敢少焉。諸士子獲取於是矣，行將角天下士，則夫奉廷對、服官序，實昉於此，將何以為之地耶？必曰：不徒以文章為也，行檢其郛郭；不徒以政事為也，學術其基本。近師之，今之前輩是也；遠師之，文獻、忠襄公是也。等而上之，則雖伊、傅、周、召，亦吾
translation_en:
…who have led all under Heaven in literary accomplishment: men of this kind have always been numerous. Examining their achievements in government, those serving in the Hanlin Academy and other scholarly offices, or holding posts as censors and remonstrance officials, have lent distinction to the imperial court; those stationed throughout the provinces and governing prefectures and counties have likewise brought stability and dignity to the outlying territories. Thus, whenever scholars throughout the realm are discussed, these men must be ranked foremost; and when the examinations’ success in obtaining worthy men is discussed, none dare belittle them.

You candidates have now gained selection here and will soon compete with scholars from throughout the realm. Answering questions before the throne and entering the ranks of official service indeed begin here. How, then, will you lay the foundation for these undertakings? Surely the answer must be: do not rely solely on literary accomplishment; disciplined conduct is its defensive wall. Do not rely solely on administrative achievement; learning is its foundation. For models close at hand, there are the senior men of our own day; for models from the more distant past, there are Lords Wenxian and Zhongxiang. Ascending still higher, even Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao are my …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
儔匹爾烏可以多讓哉使畫於
一得沾沾然自喜而不知所以
求進焉則天之生賢何如國家
之取士何如乃以是而自處哉
其為科目之玷也固矣洽用是
以相告云
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正
===
何洽謹序
punctuated:
儔匹爾，烏可以多讓哉！使畫於一得，沾沾然自喜，而不知所以求進焉，則天之生賢何如？國家之取士何如？乃以是而自處哉！其為科目之玷也固矣。洽用是以相告云。
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正何洽謹序。
translation_en:
…are merely our peers; how could we concede much to them! If one confines oneself to a single attainment, complacently delights in it, and does not know how to seek further advancement, then what becomes of Heaven’s purpose in bringing forth worthy men? What becomes of the state’s purpose in selecting scholars? How could one resign oneself to such a position! Such a person would assuredly be a blemish upon the examination system. I, Qia, therefore offer these words to you all.
Preface respectfully written by He Qia, Instructor in the Confucian School of Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
皇明取士之制率三歲一舉於鄉正
德庚午適賓興之年維時廣東
藩臬重臣先事走聘才等俾司
文衡至期巡按御史王旻實監
臨之合提學副使李麟所簡士
一千五百有竒鎖院而三試焉
===
分房校藝務拔殊尤於其文之
勁徹純粹者取焉渾雄雋拔者
取焉宏博中正者取焉深茂典
雅者取焉其贍而不蕪平而不
弱豪縱而不揚簡質而有體者
亦取焉凡得士七十有五人爰
列其名第幷彙所著文爲鄉試
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

皇明取士之制，率三歲一舉於鄉。正德庚午，適賓興之年。維時廣東藩臬重臣，先事走聘才等，俾司文衡。至期，巡按御史王旻實監臨之，合提學副使李麟所簡士一千五百有竒，鎖院而三試焉。分房校藝，務拔殊尤。於其文之勁徹純粹者取焉，渾雄雋拔者取焉，宏博中正者取焉，深茂典雅者取焉。其贍而不蕪，平而不弱，豪縱而不揚，簡質而有體者，亦取焉。凡得士七十有五人，爰列其名第，幷彙所著文，爲鄉試
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Under the system for selecting men for office in our august Ming dynasty, examinations are ordinarily held in the provinces once every three years. The gengwu year of the Zhengde reign (1510) duly fell in a year for recommending worthy men. The senior officials of Guangdong’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions sent an invitation in advance to me, Cai, and my colleagues, charging us with judging the examination writings. When the appointed time arrived, Regional Inspector Wang Min served as Supervising Official. The more than fifteen hundred candidates selected by Li Lin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant, were assembled; the examination compound was sealed, and they were examined in three sessions.

Dividing the work among examination rooms, we assessed their compositions, intent on selecting those of outstanding merit. We selected writing that was vigorous, lucid, and pure; that was powerful, unified, and exceptionally distinguished; that was broad in learning, balanced, and correct; and that was profound, rich, classical, and elegant. We also selected writing that was ample without being overgrown, even without being weak, bold and unrestrained without being ostentatious, or simple and unadorned while maintaining proper form. In all, we selected seventy-five men. We then listed their names and ranks and gathered their compositions to form the Provincial Examination…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
錄以
獻甚盛典也於乎廣東逺落荒裔
而一時詞華之盛廼克間遀中
邦何哉詎非總督都御史林廷
選廓靖方維使庠序樂於敎育
歟總鎭太監潘忠提督市舶太
監畢眞總兵東寧伯焦淇崇重
===
儒紳致舒翹揚英之有加歟監
察御史郁侃劉祥江萬實鮮冕
奉公是邦風紀丕振有以起末
學之嚮往歟抑經理于內若右
參議王秩李希顏副使鄭岳僉
事江潮以及諸執事咸殫厥心
使文場筆札罔不罄其所長於
punctuated: 錄以獻，甚盛典也。於乎！廣東逺落荒裔，而一時詞華之盛，廼克間遀中邦，何哉？詎非總督都御史林廷選廓靖方維，使庠序樂於敎育歟？總鎭太監潘忠、提督市舶太監畢眞、總兵東寧伯焦淇崇重儒紳，致舒翹揚英之有加歟？監察御史郁侃、劉祥、江萬實、鮮冕奉公是邦，風紀丕振，有以起末學之嚮往歟？抑經理于內，若右參議王秩、李希顏，副使鄭岳，僉事江潮，以及諸執事，咸殫厥心，使文場筆札罔不罄其所長於
translation_en: …a record for presentation to the throne—a truly grand observance. Ah! Guangdong lies far away on the remote periphery, yet the literary brilliance of this occasion could rival that of the central regions [?]. Why was this so? Was it not because Lin Tingxuan, Governor-General and Censor-in-Chief, secured and pacified the region, allowing its schools to delight in teaching and nurturing students? Was it because Pan Zhong, the eunuch Grand Defender; Bi Zhen, the eunuch Superintendent of Maritime Trade; and Jiao Qi, Regional Commander and Earl of Dongning, honored Confucian scholars and gentry, thereby doing still more to encourage and advance outstanding talent [?]? Was it because the Investigating Censors Yu Kan, Liu Xiang, Jiang Wanshi, and Xian Mian served the public faithfully in this region, greatly strengthening discipline and inspiring the aspirations of those beginning their studies? Or was it because those managing affairs within the examination compound—Right Administration Assistants Wang Zhi and Li Xiyan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zheng Yue, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Jiang Chao, and all the other functionaries—devoted their utmost efforts, enabling every candidate writing in the examination hall to give full expression to his abilities at…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一日歟防範于外若左布政使
李思明按察使任漢左叅政羅
榮右叅政鄒虞副使詹璽左叅
議翁茂南右叅議董鉦僉事李
瑾夏璲趙繼宗譏察周詳絕乖
凌蔽欺之弊而締構靡怠心留
念歟是雖所司有輕重詳略之
===
殊其為人才之助則一爾然才
猶以為未焉粵自應聘而來度
庾關抵韶廣旁觀聳視第見奇
峯疊嶂卷阿大阜蜿蜒迤邐如
鳥獸之騰舞巉嵲孤撐蓊鬱蒼
翠若雲矗而氣浮則夫扶輿磅
礴之所鍾殆非紛葩瓌麗之物
punctuated:
一日歟？防範于外，若左布政使李思明、按察使任漢、左叅政羅榮、右叅政鄒虞、副使詹璽、左叅議翁茂南、右叅議董鉦、僉事李瑾、夏璲、趙繼宗，譏察周詳，絕乖凌蔽欺之弊，而締構靡怠，心留念歟？是雖所司有輕重詳略之殊，其為人才之助則一爾。
然才猶以為未焉。粵自應聘而來，度庾關，抵韶廣，旁觀聳視，第見奇峯疊嶂、卷阿大阜，蜿蜒迤邐，如鳥獸之騰舞；巉嵲孤撐，蓊鬱蒼翠，若雲矗而氣浮。則夫扶輿磅礴之所鍾，殆非紛葩瓌麗之物
translation_en:
…in a single day? As for precautions outside the examination compound, there were Left Administration Commissioner Li Siming, Surveillance Commissioner Ren Han, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Luo Rong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zou Yu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhan Xi, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Weng Maonan, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Dong Zheng, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Li Jin, Xia Sui, and Zhao Jizong. Did they not conduct thorough inspections, eliminate abuses involving misconduct, intimidation, concealment, and deception, and work tirelessly on the arrangements, keeping these concerns in mind [?]? Although their responsibilities differed in importance and in the degree of attention required, their contribution to nurturing talent was the same.
Yet I still consider this insufficient. Since coming in response to the invitation, I have crossed Yuguan Pass and reached Shaozhou and Guangzhou. Looking about and gazing upward, I saw extraordinary peaks and overlapping mountain ridges, winding slopes and great hills, stretching and twisting like birds and beasts leaping and dancing. Craggy heights stood alone, luxuriantly wooded and verdant, like clouds rising aloft and vapors floating. Surely the vast, pervasive energies concentrated here could not find expression merely in things of profuse splendor and extraordinary beauty…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得而獨當也其壤地之廣輪聚
落畦塍動亘數百里而浮嵐秀
水率映照上下城郭里市雖涉
喧囂而其間陂池林麓亦罔不
可亭可廬則夫玩心觀理有不
待入中條傍月泉然後得而靜
專也其川流之委會湞湟東注
===
呀呷漰湃飛湍激淙瞬息數十
里巨溟南匯波濤日夕盪汨而
魚龍神恠復隱見鯈突則又有
不待望五湖闚洛汭而後可以
發其豪懷藻思者矧荷
祖宗治化涵煦之久
今上政教漸被之深猶嘉木美箭培
punctuated: 得而獨當也。其壤地之廣輪，聚落畦塍，動亘數百里，而浮嵐秀水率映照上下。城郭里市雖涉喧囂，而其間陂池林麓亦罔不可亭可廬，則夫玩心觀理，有不待入中條、傍月泉，然後得而靜專也。其川流之委會，湞湟東注，呀呷漰湃，飛湍激淙，瞬息數十里；巨溟南匯，波濤日夕盪汨，而魚龍神恠復隱見鯈突，則又有不待望五湖、闚洛汭，而後可以發其豪懷藻思者。矧荷祖宗治化涵煦之久，今上政教漸被之深，猶嘉木美箭培
translation_en:
…could alone lay claim to it. Across the breadth and length of this land, settlements and cultivated plots with their dividing ridges often extend for hundreds of li, while floating mountain mists and lovely waters reflect one another above and below. Although its walled cities, neighborhoods, and markets are noisy, among them are ponds, woods, and wooded foothills where pavilions and dwellings might everywhere be built. Thus, to cultivate the mind and contemplate principle, one need not enter the Zhongtiao Mountains or settle beside Yuequan, the Moon Spring, before attaining tranquility and concentration.

As for the converging waterways, the Zhen and Huang rivers pour eastward, roaring and surging, their flying rapids and rushing torrents covering dozens of li in an instant. To the south, waters gather in the vast sea; its waves churn day and night, while fish, dragons, spirits, and strange creatures appear and disappear, darting suddenly about. Here too, one need not gaze upon the Five Lakes or peer at the bend of the Luo River before finding inspiration for lofty feelings and elegant literary conceptions.

Moreover, this land has long enjoyed the nurturing warmth of the imperial ancestors’ transformative rule and has been deeply permeated by the present emperor’s government and instruction, like fine trees and excellent arrow bamboo being cultivated…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
植不置枝幹固碩茂而杪末尤
曄暢敷華者嶺服之地爲然也
夫若是如之何其不郁郁乎迥
邁疇昔也哉雖然蛟龍騰翥徧
雨八荒騏驥就駕一日千里諸
士登薦鄉書部
廷之進有階而嚮用且有日顧可
===
泥尋常効圭撮而已耶大而經
世宰物康國寧民次而典司曹
局循良州邑要皆自其所以盛
者舉而措之可也是不惟上荅
聖朝作養之恩下彰主司知人之鑑
而已嶺表山川土壤亦與有光
焉若舍此而他求則非予之所
punctuated: 植不置，枝幹固碩茂，而杪末尤曄暢敷華者，嶺服之地爲然也。夫若是，如之何其不郁郁乎迥邁疇昔也哉！雖然，蛟龍騰翥，徧雨八荒；騏驥就駕，一日千里。諸士登薦鄉書，部廷之進有階，而嚮用且有日，顧可泥尋常、効圭撮而已耶？大而經世宰物，康國寧民；次而典司曹局，循良州邑。要皆自其所以盛者，舉而措之可也。是不惟上荅聖朝作養之恩，下彰主司知人之鑑而已，嶺表山川土壤亦與有光焉。若舍此而他求，則非予之所
translation_en:
…unceasingly cultivated, their branches and trunks are indeed sturdy and luxuriant, while their topmost shoots shine all the more brilliantly and unfold their blossoms: so it is with the lands of Lingnan. This being so, how could their flourishing cultural accomplishments fail to surpass those of former times by far!

Nevertheless, when dragons soar aloft, they send rain throughout the eight distant regions; when fine steeds are harnessed, they travel a thousand li in a day. You gentlemen have been entered on the provincial roll of recommended candidates. There are steps by which you may advance through the ministries and the court, and the day will come when you are entrusted with service. Can you remain confined to ordinary pursuits and render only a trifling contribution?

At the highest level, you should order the world and direct its affairs, bring well-being to the state and peace to the people; at the next, you should administer government offices and serve as conscientious and benevolent officials in prefectures and counties. In all cases, you need only take the qualities in which you excel and put them into practice. This will not merely repay the sagely dynasty’s grace in nurturing you and demonstrate the discerning judgment of the presiding examiners in recognizing worthy men: the mountains, rivers, and soil of Lingnan will share in the glory as well. If you abandon this and seek elsewhere, then that is not what I…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
生財有大道生之者衆食之者寡爲之者
疾用之者舒則財恒足矣仁者以財發
身
君子喻於義
夏曰校殷曰序周曰庠學則三代共之皆
所以明人倫也人倫明於上小民親於
下
===
易
天且弗違而況於人乎
告公從以益志也
履信思乎順又以尚賢也是以自天祐之
吉无不利也
動萬物者莫疾乎雷撓萬物者莫疾乎風
燥萬物者莫熯乎火說萬物者莫說乎
澤潤萬物者莫潤乎水終萬物始萬物
者莫盛乎艮
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

生財有大道：生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒，則財恒足矣。仁者以財發身。

君子喻於義。

夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠；學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。

易

天且弗違，而況於人乎？

告公從，以益志也。

履信，思乎順，又以尚賢也，是以自天祐之，吉无不利也。

動萬物者莫疾乎雷，撓萬物者莫疾乎風，燥萬物者莫熯乎火，說萬物者莫說乎澤，潤萬物者莫潤乎水，終萬物、始萬物者莫盛乎艮。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

There is a great way to produce wealth: let those who produce it be numerous and those who consume it few; let those who make it work swiftly and those who spend it do so slowly. Then wealth will always be sufficient. The benevolent person uses wealth to develop his character.

The gentleman understands what is right.

Under the Xia, schools were called xiao; under the Yin, xu; under the Zhou, xiang. The designation xue was shared by all three dynasties. All served to clarify human relationships. When human relationships are made clear above, the common people below live in mutual affection.

Book of Changes

Even Heaven does not oppose him; how much less would human beings?

He reports to the duke, who follows his counsel, thereby advancing his purpose.

He acts with trustworthiness, gives thought to compliance, and also honors the worthy. Therefore Heaven helps him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.

For setting the myriad things in motion, nothing is swifter than thunder; for stirring the myriad things, nothing is swifter than wind; for drying the myriad things, nothing is more parching than fire; for delighting the myriad things, nothing is more delightful than the marsh; for moistening the myriad things, nothing is more moistening than water; for bringing the myriad things to their end and initiating them anew, nothing is greater than Gen, the Mountain trigram.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
侯以明之撻以記之書用識哉欲並生哉
四海之內咸仰朕德時乃風股肱惟人良
臣惟聖
曰雨曰暘曰燠曰寒曰風曰時
其作大邑其自時配皇天毖祀于上下其
自時中乂
詩
于以盛之維筐及筥于以湘之維錡及鬵
===
南有嘉魚烝然汕汕君子有酒嘉賓式燕
以衎
江漢湯湯武夫洸洸經營四方告成于王
四方旣平王國庶定時靡有爭王心載
寧江漢之滸王命召虎式辟四方徹我
疆土匪疚匪棘王國來極于疆于理至
于南海王命召虎來旬來宣文武受命
召公維翰無曰予小子召公是似肇敏
戎公用錫爾祉釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣告
punctuated:
書

侯以明之，撻以記之，書用識哉，欲並生哉！

四海之內，咸仰朕德，時乃風。股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。

曰雨，曰暘，曰燠，曰寒，曰風，曰時。

其作大邑，其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下，其自時中乂。

詩

于以盛之？維筐及筥。于以湘之？維錡及鬵。

南有嘉魚，烝然汕汕。君子有酒，嘉賓式燕以衎。

江漢湯湯，武夫洸洸。經營四方，告成于王。四方旣平，王國庶定。時靡有爭，王心載寧。江漢之滸，王命召虎：式辟四方，徹我疆土。匪疚匪棘，王國來極。于疆于理，至于南海。王命召虎：來旬來宣。文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣，告
translation_en:
Book of Documents

Use archery targets to make their proficiency clear, beatings to impress the lesson upon them, and written records to mark their conduct. Is not the aim that all should live?

Within the Four Seas, all look up to my virtue: this is the effect of your influence. Arms and legs make a man complete; worthy ministers make a ruler a sage.

These are rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind, each arriving in its proper season.

Let him establish a great city; from here let him worthily serve August Heaven and reverently offer sacrifices to the powers above and below; from here let him govern with due balance.

Book of Odes

In what shall we put them? In square baskets and round baskets. In what shall we boil them? In tripod cauldrons and great pots.

In the south are fine fish, swimming in shoals. The lord has wine; his honored guests feast and rejoice.

The Jiang and Han rivers flow vast and strong; the warriors are fierce and valiant. They bring order to the four quarters and report their success to the king. The four quarters are now pacified; the royal realm is almost settled. There is no more strife, and the king’s heart is at peace.

On the banks of the Jiang and Han, the king commands Shao Hu: “Open up the four quarters and put our territories in order. Neither harm the people nor act with undue haste; come and take the royal realm as your standard. Mark out the boundaries and arrange the lands, as far as the southern sea.”

The king commands Shao Hu: “Go forth to inspect and proclaim my commands. When Kings Wen and Wu received Heaven’s mandate, the Duke of Shao was their supporting pillar. Do not say, ‘I am but a young man’; emulate the Duke of Shao. Begin diligently upon your great achievement, for which I bestow blessings upon you. I grant you a jade-handled libation ladle and a vessel of fragrant black-millet wine, to announce …

灌以圭璋用玉氣也
樂者爲同禮者爲異同則相親異則相敬

Music creates unity; ritual establishes distinctions. Unity brings mutual affection; distinctions bring mutual respect. title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
策五道
問自古帝王渙汗其大號所以推是心而
布之天下者也若典謨訓誥誓命之文
是已維持國脉統繫人心咸於是乎在
我
祖宗
列聖中天而興
明詔在天下固家傳而人誦矣
聖天子嗣位益隆太平之治廼今歲夏四月偶
===
因邊陲小警誕告多方海濱萬里之外
俯聽仰思知
聖天子有敬
天法
祖之心有勤民恤物之心有神武不殺之心是
心也上與
祖宗
列聖合遠與古帝王合漢去古未遠後之稱詔
者以漢爲首漢之賢君若高文景武果
punctuated:
策五道

問：自古帝王渙汗其大號，所以推是心而布之天下者也。若典、謨、訓、誥、誓、命之文是已。維持國脉，統繫人心，咸於是乎在。我祖宗列聖中天而興，明詔在天下，固家傳而人誦矣。聖天子嗣位，益隆太平之治。廼今歲夏四月，偶因邊陲小警，誕告多方。海濱萬里之外，俯聽仰思，知聖天子有敬天法祖之心，有勤民恤物之心，有神武不殺之心。是心也，上與祖宗列聖合，遠與古帝王合。漢去古未遠，後之稱詔者以漢爲首。漢之賢君，若高、文、景、武，果
translation_en:
Five Policy Questions

Question: Since antiquity, emperors and kings have issued their great proclamations as sweat flows forth from the body, thereby extending their intentions throughout the realm. Such are the canons, counsels, instructions, announcements, oaths, and commands in the Book of Documents. Sustaining the vitality of the state and binding together the hearts of the people all depend upon these. Our founding ancestors and successive sage sovereigns rose to occupy the center of Heaven; their enlightened edicts circulated throughout the realm, transmitted in every household and recited by everyone. Since succeeding to the throne, the sage Son of Heaven has further enhanced the government of the Great Peace. Now, in the fourth month of this year's summer, a minor alarm on the frontier occasioned a proclamation addressed to all regions. Here on the seacoast, more than ten thousand li away, we listen humbly and reflect reverently. We know that the sage Son of Heaven has a heart that reveres Heaven and emulates his ancestors, a heart that labors for the people and cares for all beings, and a heart possessed of divine martial prowess that does not kill. These intentions accord with those of our founding ancestors and successive sage sovereigns above, and with those of the emperors and kings of distant antiquity. The Han was not far removed from antiquity, and later generations discussing edicts have ranked those of the Han foremost. Did the worthy Han rulers, such as Gao, Wen, Jing, and Wu, indeed …

部之書而諸子百家皆列於子部豈亦
倣孟堅之體歟十家之書有鹽鐵論潛
夫論荆楚歲時記秦中歲時記昌言申
鑒中論法訓之書風俗通義群書治要
punctuated:
能有是心乎？抑能有是詔乎？其間亦有粗合夫一二者乎？諸生遭際明時，獲沾聖化久矣，有能鋪張揚厲，述此盛德，以昭示無疆者乎？華國之才，吾將爲爾薦之。

問：諸子之書，亦儒者之所嘗讀也。班固作《漢藝文志》，分爲諸子十家。然所謂十家者，有出於司徒者，有出於史官者，有出於羲和者，有出於理官者，又有出於掌禮之官、清廟之官、行人之官者，又有出於擬議之官、農稷之官、稗闔之官者，皆可得而言歟？孟堅於諸子十家之外，又刪劉歆《七略》之說而有四家。後世分四部之書，而諸子百家皆列於子部，豈亦倣孟堅之體歟？十家之書，有《鹽鐵論》、《潛夫論》、《荆楚歲時記》、《秦中歲時記》、《昌言》、《申鑒》、《中論》、《法訓》之書，《風俗通義》、《群書治要》
translation_en:
…could they possess such a heart? Or could they issue such edicts? Were there among them any who even roughly accorded with one or two of these qualities? You students have encountered an enlightened age and have long benefited from the sage ruler’s transforming influence. Can any of you expound and extol this magnificent virtue, making it manifest for all time? I shall recommend you as men whose talents bring glory to the realm.

Question: The writings of the various masters are also works that Confucian scholars have read. When Ban Gu compiled the “Treatise on Literature” in the History of the Han, he divided the masters into ten schools. Among these ten schools, some originated with the Minister of Education, some with historiographers, some with the astronomical officials Xi and He, and some with judicial officials. Others originated with officials responsible for ritual, officials of the ancestral temple, or diplomatic officials; still others with deliberative officials [?], agricultural officials, or officials called baihe [?]. Can you explain all of these origins? Beyond the ten schools of masters, Mengjian [Ban Gu’s courtesy name] also abridged Liu Xin’s Seven Summaries, producing four categories. Later generations divided books into four divisions and placed all the masters and their many schools in the Masters division. Was this also modeled on Mengjian’s arrangement? Among the books of the ten schools are Discourses on Salt and Iron (Yantie lun), Discourses of a Hidden Scholar (Qianfu lun), Record of Seasonal Observances in Jingchu (Jingchu suishi ji), Record of Seasonal Observances in Qinzhong (Qinzhong suishi ji), Forthright Words (Changyan), Extended Reflections (Shenjian), Discourses on the Mean (Zhonglun), Exemplary Instructions (Faxun), Comprehensive Account of Customs (Fengsu tongyi), and Essentials of Governance from the Collected Books (Qunshu zhiyao)…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
古今說苑管氏指要論衡說林世說類
林之集斯皆作於誰歟他如鬼谷子尉
繚子抱朴子廣成子金樓子鶡冠子鄧
析子尹文子魯連子淮南子胡非子鬻
子田子宣子陸子黔婁子之數子者抑
果何許人而其所著果為何家書歟學
者若能脩六藝之術而觀此十家之言
亦可以通萬方之略矣願詳陳之母隱
問文章可以潤身政事可以及物後世之
===
士亦各以其盛者稱鮮有能兼之者若
唐之時有韓愈宋之時有歐陽修皆以
文章名一代而論其文者乃謂奧衍閎
深佐佑六經醇深炳蔚渾然天質又謂
韓愈之才自視司馬遷楊雄歐陽修為
今之韓愈其果然歟今其遺文具在其
間議論關涉義理之大者尚可指其一
二而評之歟槩之以聖人之道亦皆有
所見歟愈為裴晉公所知然卒不能薦
punctuated:
《古今說苑》、《管氏指要》、《論衡》、《說林》、《世說》、《類林》之集，斯皆作於誰歟？他如鬼谷子、尉繚子、抱朴子、廣成子、金樓子、鶡冠子、鄧析子、尹文子、魯連子、淮南子、胡非子、鬻子、田子、宣子、陸子、黔婁子之數子者，抑果何許人，而其所著果為何家書歟？學者若能脩六藝之術，而觀此十家之言，亦可以通萬方之略矣。願詳陳之，母隱。
問：文章可以潤身，政事可以及物。後世之士，亦各以其盛者稱，鮮有能兼之者。若唐之時有韓愈，宋之時有歐陽修，皆以文章名一代。而論其文者，乃謂「奧衍閎深，佐佑六經」，「醇深炳蔚，渾然天質」；又謂韓愈之才自視司馬遷、楊雄，歐陽修為今之韓愈，其果然歟？今其遺文具在，其間議論關涉義理之大者，尚可指其一二而評之歟？槩之以聖人之道，亦皆有所見歟？愈為裴晉公所知，然卒不能薦
translation_en:
…the collections Garden of Accounts Ancient and Modern (Gujin shuoyuan), Master Guan’s Essential Points (Guanshi zhiyao), Balanced Discourses (Lunheng), Forest of Accounts (Shuolin), Accounts of the World (Shishuo), and Forest of Classified Materials (Leilin)—who wrote all these? As for such other masters as Guiguzi, Weiliaozi, Baopuzi, Guangchengzi, Jinlouzi, Heguanzi, Deng Xizi, Yin Wenzi, Lu Lianzi, Huainanzi, Hu Feizi, Yuzi, Tianzi, Xuanzi, Luzi, and Qianlouzi, just who were they, and to which schools did their writings actually belong? If scholars can cultivate the disciplines of the Six Arts and examine the teachings of these ten schools, they may also gain a comprehensive understanding of approaches to affairs in every quarter. Please explain these matters fully, withholding nothing.
Question: Literary accomplishment can adorn one’s person; the conduct of government can benefit others. Scholars of later ages have each been celebrated for the field in which they excelled, but few have been able to combine both. There were, for example, Han Yu in the Tang and Ouyang Xiu in the Song, each renowned in his age for literary writing. Those who discuss their prose describe it as “profound, expansive, broad, and deep, supporting the Six Classics,” and “rich, profound, brilliant, and luxuriant, seamlessly natural in its qualities.” They also say that Han Yu regarded his own talent as comparable to that of Sima Qian and Yang Xiong, and that Ouyang Xiu was the Han Yu of his day. Is this indeed so? Their surviving writings are now available in full. Can you identify and assess one or two passages whose arguments concern major questions of moral principle? Measured against the Way of the sages, do both writers possess genuine insight? Han Yu was appreciated by Pei, Duke of Jin, yet in the end the duke was unable to recommend him…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之於朝至韓魏公之薦修乃曰韓愈唐
之名士天下望以為相而竟不用使愈
為之未必有補於唐而談者至今以為
謗今不用修臣恐謗必及國然則使唐
誠能用愈果皆無所補歟其後修嘗為
執政矣一時建白亦有補於宋否歟抑
二子功業掩於文章而卒不可得而兼
歟請極論之以觀嚮往先哲之志
問治天下以正風俗得賢才為本然風俗
===
可易而正賢才可易而得耶其轉移化
導之機亦存乎其人耳夫輿圖之大姑
未枚舉子粤產也請以粤論粤自交州
置郡之後淳風古俗豈無可稱者歟在
漢唐宋時有質直尚信民得華風者有
習尚淳樸士多愿慤者有比郡文物不
下他州者亦可以為美矣不知其地可
乎風氣既開之後長材秀民豈無間出
者歟在漢唐宋時有累徵不起志趣高
punctuated:
之於朝。至韓魏公之薦修，乃曰：「韓愈，唐之名士，天下望以為相，而竟不用。使愈為之，未必有補於唐，而談者至今以為謗。今不用修，臣恐謗必及國。」然則使唐誠能用愈，果皆無所補歟？其後修嘗為執政矣，一時建白亦有補於宋否歟？抑二子功業掩於文章，而卒不可得而兼歟？請極論之，以觀嚮往先哲之志。

問：治天下以正風俗、得賢才為本，然風俗可易而正，賢才可易而得耶？其轉移化導之機，亦存乎其人耳。夫輿圖之大，姑未枚舉。子粤產也，請以粤論。粤自交州置郡之後，淳風古俗豈無可稱者歟？在漢唐宋時，有質直尚信、民得華風者，有習尚淳樸、士多愿慤者，有比郡文物不下他州者，亦可以為美矣。不知其地可乎？風氣既開之後，長材秀民豈無間出者歟？在漢唐宋時，有累徵不起、志趣高
translation_en:
…him for service at court. When Han, Duke of Wei, recommended Ouyang Xiu, however, he said: “Han Yu was an eminent scholar of the Tang. All under Heaven hoped he would be made chief councilor, yet in the end he was never employed in that capacity. Had Han Yu held that office, he might not necessarily have benefited the Tang; nevertheless, commentators to this day reproach the dynasty for this. If Xiu is not employed now, I fear that reproach will surely fall upon our state.” If the Tang had indeed employed Han Yu, would he really have contributed nothing? Later, Xiu did hold high executive office. Did the proposals he submitted at the time benefit the Song? Or were these two men’s achievements in government overshadowed by their literary accomplishments, so that ultimately they could not attain both? Discuss this fully, so that we may discern your aspiration to emulate the worthy men of the past.

Question: Governing all under Heaven rests upon rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent. But can customs easily be rectified, and worthy talent easily obtained? The means of transforming and guiding people lie, after all, in the person responsible. The realm is vast; let us refrain for now from enumerating its regions. You are a native of Yue; please discuss Yue. Since commanderies were established in Jiaozhou, has Yue had no wholesome traditions and ancient customs worthy of praise? During the Han, Tang, and Song, there were places where people were straightforward and valued trustworthiness, and the populace acquired the customs of Chinese civilization; places where prevailing practices were honest and simple, and scholars were mostly sincere and earnest; and places where neighboring commanderies were no less accomplished in letters and culture than other prefectures. These may indeed be considered admirable. Can you fail to know which places they were? Once the cultural climate had opened up, did people of exceptional talent and ability not emerge from time to time? During the Han, Tang, and Song, there were men who repeatedly declined imperial summons to office, whose aspirations were lofty…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
尚者有錄上金鑑坐貶荊州者有屢言
邊情三使契丹者亦可以爲賢矣不知
其人可乎
聖朝敷德海隅丕冒俗宜無不正也然未變如
信巫淫祀喪用樂之類其故何在抑可
諉諸夷否耶才固無不生也然繼出如
關敏鄧顒陳鼎之徒其行何居抑可班
諸賢否耶夫政由俗革魯多君子信乎
有開必先也閩之先有常衮蜀之先有
===
文翁吳之先有言偃楚之先有陳良固
也凡在嶺表類是而先者果何郡何人
歟亦有事類而實弗類者歟諸生以賢
才抱藝而來他日均有移風易俗之責
者盍各言之以觀厥志
問書曰民惟邦本詩曰用戒戎作則卹民
馭兵皆國之所恃以安而不可緩焉者
試以策之諸士昔人留意卹民有以減
其稅斂進戒其君者有以輕稅薄征諷
punctuated:
尚者，有錄上金鑑、坐貶荊州者，有屢言邊情、三使契丹者，亦可以爲賢矣，不知其人可乎？聖朝敷德，海隅丕冒，俗宜無不正也。然未變如信巫、淫祀、喪用樂之類，其故何在？抑可諉諸夷否耶？才固無不生也，然繼出如關敏、鄧顒、陳鼎之徒，其行何居？抑可班諸賢否耶？夫政由俗革，魯多君子，信乎有開必先也。閩之先有常衮，蜀之先有文翁，吳之先有言偃，楚之先有陳良，固也。凡在嶺表，類是而先者，果何郡何人歟？亦有事類而實弗類者歟？諸生以賢才抱藝而來，他日均有移風易俗之責者，盍各言之，以觀厥志？

問：《書》曰：「民惟邦本。」《詩》曰：「用戒戎作。」則卹民、馭兵，皆國之所恃以安而不可緩焉者。試以策之諸士：昔人留意卹民，有以減其稅斂進戒其君者，有以輕稅薄征諷
translation_en:
…lofty in their aspirations; there was one who submitted the Golden Mirror in writing and was consequently demoted to Jingzhou; and there was one who repeatedly reported on frontier conditions and went three times as an envoy to the Khitan. These, too, may be called worthy men. Is it acceptable not to know who they were?

Our sagely dynasty spreads its virtue, abundantly sheltering even the remotest coastal regions, so that all customs should surely have been rectified. Yet such practices as trusting shamans, offering improper sacrifices, and using music at funerals remain unchanged. Why is this? Can these simply be attributed to the non-Han peoples? Talent certainly arises everywhere. Yet among those who subsequently emerged, such as Guan Min, Deng Yong, and Chen Ding, how should their conduct be judged? Can they be ranked among the worthy? Government brings about changes in customs, and Lu abounded in gentlemen: surely every flowering has its pioneers. Min had Chang Gun as its pioneer; Shu had Wen Weng; Wu had Yan Yan; and Chu had Chen Liang. This is well established. Throughout Lingbiao, in which commanderies, and among which people, were there comparable pioneers? Were there also cases similar in outward circumstances but different in substance? You students have come with worthy talents and cultivated learning. In the future, each of you will bear responsibility for transforming prevailing customs. Why not each set forth your views, so that your aspirations may be seen?

Question: The Book of Documents says, “The people are the foundation of the state.” The Book of Odes says, “Thereby guard against the outbreak of armed rebellion.” Thus, caring for the people and controlling the troops are both things upon which the state depends for peace, and neither can be neglected. Let us put the following policy question to you gentlemen. Among men of former times who devoted attention to caring for the people, some admonished their rulers to reduce tax exactions; others urged lighter taxes and reduced levies in indirect remonstrances…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諫其君者又有論惜元氣在輕賦役者
立紀綱須寬民力者其人可悉數歟昔
人留意馭兵有四萬騎分屯九郡而單
于引去者有十一軍控制二邊而南詔
請還者又有監博州軍脩治器械虜人
不入者閱延州兵日夜訓練敵人相戒
者其人可歷指歟方
今堯封一統禹貢攸同萬方惟正之供軍士
樂於用戰比年以來湖湘遇歉或竭府
===
庫或停起運以賑卹之設或諸路旱澇
相仍不知若何而濟襄漢有警或調土
兵或募民兵以應援之設或他處盜賊
繼起不知若何而禦宋儒有謂斯民之
休戚係守令之賢否又有謂天下無必
勝之兵而有不可敗之將則守令將帥
任兵民之責不可以不擇也茲欲各得
其人而盡卹民馭兵之道必如之何而
後可昔人在布衣時視天下事皆爲分
punctuated: 諫其君者，又有論惜元氣在輕賦役者，立紀綱須寬民力者，其人可悉數歟？昔人留意馭兵，有四萬騎分屯九郡而單于引去者，有十一軍控制二邊而南詔請還者，又有監博州軍、脩治器械、虜人不入者，閱延州兵、日夜訓練、敵人相戒者，其人可歷指歟？方今堯封一統，禹貢攸同，萬方惟正之供，軍士樂於用戰。比年以來，湖湘遇歉，或竭府庫，或停起運，以賑卹之。設或諸路旱澇相仍，不知若何而濟？襄漢有警，或調土兵，或募民兵，以應援之。設或他處盜賊繼起，不知若何而禦？宋儒有謂斯民之休戚係守令之賢否，又有謂天下無必勝之兵而有不可敗之將，則守令將帥任兵民之責，不可以不擇也。茲欲各得其人，而盡卹民馭兵之道，必如之何而後可？昔人在布衣時，視天下事皆爲分
translation_en:
…remonstrated with their sovereign. Others argued that conserving the realm’s vital strength depended on lightening taxes and labor services, or that establishing administrative order required easing the burdens on the people’s resources. Can you name all these men? Among men of the past who gave attention to commanding troops, one stationed forty thousand cavalry in nine commanderies, whereupon the chanyu withdrew; another held two frontiers in check with eleven armies, whereupon Nanzhao requested withdrawal [?]. Another supervised the troops of Bozhou and repaired their weapons and equipment, so that the enemy did not invade; another inspected the troops of Yanzhou and trained them day and night, so that the enemy warned one another against them. Can you identify these men one by one?

Now the domain of Yao is united under one rule, and the lands described in the Tribute of Yu share that unity. All regions furnish their regular dues, and the soldiers willingly go into battle. In recent years, when the Hu-Xiang region suffered poor harvests, relief was provided either by exhausting government treasuries or by suspending fiscal shipments. But suppose droughts and floods followed one another across the various regions: how could relief be supplied? When alarms arose in the Xiang-Han region, either local troops were transferred or civilian militia recruited to provide support. But suppose bandits arose successively elsewhere: how could they be resisted? A Song Confucian scholar said that the people’s well-being or suffering depended on whether their prefects and magistrates were worthy; another said that there are no troops in the world certain to win, but there are generals who cannot be defeated. Thus prefects, magistrates, and military commanders bear responsibility for soldiers and civilians, and must be carefully selected. If we now wish to secure the right man for each post and fully realize the proper methods of caring for the people and commanding troops, what must be done to accomplish this? Men of the past, while still commoners, regarded all the affairs of the world as falling within their duty…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
內而況兵食二者尤今日之先務臣子
憂國愛民之心所不能自己者請詳言
之以觀用世之學
punctuated: 內，而況兵食二者，尤今日之先務，臣子憂國愛民之心所不能自己者。請詳言之，以觀用世之學。
translation_en: …within their own responsibility; how much more so military affairs and provisions, which are especially urgent priorities today, matters about which loyal subjects, in their concern for the state and love for the people, cannot restrain their solicitude. Please discuss these matters in detail, so that we may assess your learning as applied to public service.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人七十五名
第一名黃佐廣州府學生詩
第二名蕭汝爲潮陽縣學生書
第三名葉孟東莞縣學生禮記
第四名潘濂廣州府學附學生易
第五名李卿潮州府學生春秋
第六名彭遇廣州府學增廣生詩
第七名馮徽廣州府學附學生易
===
第八名廖任惠州府學生詩
第九名蔡士儲瓊州府學生易
第十名薛侃潮州府學附學生書
第十一名李道全四會縣學生詩
第十二名劉信新興縣學增廣生易
第十三名陳元泰河源縣學生詩
第十四名陳世美瓊州府學附學生易
第十五名盧金潤東莞縣學附學生春秋
第十六名張淮順德縣學生詩
punctuated:
中式舉人七十五名。

第一名黃佐，廣州府學生，《詩》。
第二名蕭汝爲，潮陽縣學生，《書》。
第三名葉孟，東莞縣學生，《禮記》。
第四名潘濂，廣州府學附學生，《易》。
第五名李卿，潮州府學生，《春秋》。
第六名彭遇，廣州府學增廣生，《詩》。
第七名馮徽，廣州府學附學生，《易》。
第八名廖任，惠州府學生，《詩》。
第九名蔡士儲，瓊州府學生，《易》。
第十名薛侃，潮州府學附學生，《書》。
第十一名李道全，四會縣學生，《詩》。
第十二名劉信，新興縣學增廣生，《易》。
第十三名陳元泰，河源縣學生，《詩》。
第十四名陳世美，瓊州府學附學生，《易》。
第十五名盧金潤，東莞縣學附學生，《春秋》。
第十六名張淮，順德縣學生，《詩》。
translation_en:
Seventy-five successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Huang Zuo, a student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Second: Xiao Ruwei, a student of the Chaoyang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Third: Ye Meng, a student of the Dongguan County School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.
Fourth: Pan Lian, an attached student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Fifth: Li Qing, a student of the Chaozhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
生財有大道生之者衆食之者寡爲之者
疾用之者舒則財恒足矣仁者以財發
身
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批此題舊以理財之效散財
之效對待言之殊失曾子立言之意蓋生財有道
而不自專惟仁者能之此作獨得其旨是用錄出
===
同考試官教諭江批融會傳意發揮明白如此
篇者蓋不多得
考試官學正何批詞氣雅健可嘉
考試官教授劉批大學義似此蓋穎出矣
大學旣詳言理天下之財自周於用必指言公
天下之財自得乎民甚矣財之有繫於天下也
理之固有其道而散之者豈有不得乎民哉曾
子傳大學之十章論平天下在絜矩而推廣其
意如此謂夫人君富有天下而恒慮其財之不
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
生財有大道：生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒，則財恒足矣。仁者以財發身。
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批：此題舊以理財之效、散財之效對待言之，殊失曾子立言之意。蓋生財有道，而不自專，惟仁者能之。此作獨得其旨，是用錄出。
同考試官教諭江批：融會傳意，發揮明白，如此篇者，蓋不多得。
考試官學正何批：詞氣雅健，可嘉。
考試官教授劉批：《大學》義似此，蓋穎出矣。
《大學》旣詳言理天下之財，自周於用，必指言公天下之財，自得乎民。甚矣，財之有繫於天下也！理之固有其道，而散之者豈有不得乎民哉？曾子傳《大學》之十章，論平天下在絜矩，而推廣其意如此。謂夫人君富有天下，而恒慮其財之不
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

“There is a great way to produce wealth: let those who produce it be many, those who consume it few, those who make it be swift, and those who spend it be measured; then wealth will always be sufficient. The benevolent person uses wealth to develop himself.”

Huang Zuo

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: Earlier treatments of this topic discussed the effects of managing wealth and distributing wealth as a pair of contrasting outcomes, badly missing Zengzi’s intention. There is a way to produce wealth, but only the benevolent can refrain from keeping it exclusively for themselves. This composition alone grasps that purport, and for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Essays such as this, which thoroughly comprehend the meaning of the commentary and expound it clearly, are seldom found.

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: The diction and vigor of expression are elegant and robust, deserving praise.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: An exposition of the meaning of the Great Learning such as this is truly outstanding.

Having explained in detail that managing the wealth of all under Heaven naturally makes it sufficient for use, the Great Learning must specifically explain that sharing the wealth of all under Heaven naturally wins the people’s allegiance. How profoundly wealth bears upon all under Heaven! Managing it certainly has its proper way; could those who distribute it fail to win the people’s allegiance? In the tenth chapter of his commentary on the Great Learning, Zengzi discusses how bringing peace to all under Heaven depends upon the principle of the measuring square—that is, applying to others the same measure one applies to oneself—and extends its meaning in this manner. He means that the ruler possesses all the wealth under Heaven, yet constantly worries that his wealth will not …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於財顧未得生財之大道耳其道維何蓋天下
之財以生而裕以食而耗也故必在國也農工
商賈各事其業而無游惰之民在朝也公卿大
夫皆惟其人而無幸致之位則財之生者衆而
食者寡矣天下之財爲之難成用之易竭也故
必念稼穡之艱難凡有興作而不奪其時計貨
利之出入凡有經費而不踰其節則財之爲者
疾而用者舒矣夫如是則旣務本以開財之源
而又節用以止財之流府庫充而供億之有餘
===
倉廩實而荒歉之有備何患於財之不足乎夫
生財有道如此而能公其財者誰歟蓋惟仁者
至公無我知千萬人之心卽一人之心利不獨
專也以一人之心爲千萬人之心財不私畜也
藏富於民而不急於誅求取民有制而不事於
掊克雖未嘗分我所有以與之也而民得以樂
其樂者自然愛戴歸往尊之爲天子矣雖未嘗
出吾所有以益之也而民得以利其利者自爾
忻慕感悅戴之爲元后矣何有於民之不得乎
punctuated:
於財，顧未得生財之大道耳。其道維何？蓋天下之財，以生而裕，以食而耗也。故必在國也，農工商賈各事其業，而無游惰之民；在朝也，公卿大夫皆惟其人，而無幸致之位，則財之生者衆而食者寡矣。天下之財，爲之難成，用之易竭也。故必念稼穡之艱難，凡有興作而不奪其時；計貨利之出入，凡有經費而不踰其節，則財之爲者疾而用者舒矣。夫如是，則旣務本以開財之源，而又節用以止財之流，府庫充而供億之有餘，倉廩實而荒歉之有備，何患於財之不足乎？

夫生財有道如此，而能公其財者誰歟？蓋惟仁者至公無我，知千萬人之心卽一人之心，利不獨專也；以一人之心爲千萬人之心，財不私畜也。藏富於民而不急於誅求，取民有制而不事於掊克。雖未嘗分我所有以與之也，而民得以樂其樂者，自然愛戴歸往，尊之爲天子矣。雖未嘗出吾所有以益之也，而民得以利其利者，自爾忻慕感悅，戴之爲元后矣。何有於民之不得乎？
translation_en:
… with regard to wealth [?], it is simply that he has not grasped the great way of producing wealth. What is that way? The wealth of the realm grows abundant through production and is depleted through consumption. Thus, throughout the state, farmers, artisans, merchants, and traders must each pursue their occupations, with no idle people; at court, dukes, ministers, and grand masters must all be suitable men, with no posts obtained through undeserved favor. Then those who produce wealth will be many, and those who consume it few. The realm’s wealth is difficult to produce and accumulate, but easily exhausted in use. One must therefore bear in mind the hardships of sowing and harvesting, ensuring that no undertaking takes away the people’s time for farming; one must reckon the inflow and outflow of goods and revenues, ensuring that no regular expenditure exceeds its proper limits. Then wealth will be produced rapidly and consumed slowly. In this way, by attending to the root—agriculture—one opens the source of wealth, while by economizing one checks its outflow. Treasuries will be full, with more than enough to meet demands for supplies; granaries will be well stocked, with reserves against crop failure and famine. Why worry that wealth will be insufficient?

Such is the way to produce wealth; but who can make his wealth serve the common good? Only the benevolent man is utterly impartial and without selfishness. He knows that the desires of the myriad people are the same as those of one man, and so does not monopolize profit; he makes his own heart the heart of the myriad people, and so does not hoard wealth for himself. He stores wealth among the people and does not press them with exacting demands; he observes limits in taking from them and does not engage in oppressive extraction. Although he has never divided up his own possessions to give to them, the people, enabled to delight in what delights them, naturally love him, give him their allegiance, and honor him as the Son of Heaven. Although he has never disbursed his own possessions to enrich them, the people, enabled to benefit from what benefits them, naturally admire him with joy, respond with gratitude and pleasure, and uphold him as their sovereign. How could he fail to win the people’s allegiance?

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
然則爲治者可不知所以足國之道而顧以專
利爲哉大抵財用國家所急而不可一日缺者
也然或斂之無道而徒朘削於民未有不失民
之心者故曾子於此論足國之道而必歸之仁
人豈非萬世君天下者之明法歟他日孟軻氏
有曰無政事則財用不足又曰王如好貨與百
姓同之於王何有其亦曾子之意歟
君子喻於義
薛侃
===
同考試官教諭顧 批喻義分明孰知上說諸士子多於
行義上敷演殊戾本旨此作卓有所見而詞亦雅贍錄之
同考試官教諭閔 批說理文字不冗則晦求其體認
親切而善於措辭者無踰此篇
考試官學正何 批整潔可誦
考試官教授劉 批文有理致
聖人論有德者深知夫天理之所宜也蓋君子
之心一於理而已則其所喻者豈有外於理之
所宜哉聖人論君子之異於小人者如此謂夫
punctuated:
然則爲治者可不知所以足國之道，而顧以專利爲哉？大抵財用，國家所急而不可一日缺者也。然或斂之無道，而徒朘削於民，未有不失民之心者。故曾子於此論足國之道，而必歸之仁人，豈非萬世君天下者之明法歟？他日孟軻氏有曰：「無政事則財用不足。」又曰：「王如好貨，與百姓同之，於王何有？」其亦曾子之意歟？

君子喻於義
薛侃

同考試官教諭顧批：「喻義分明，孰知上說。諸士子多於行義上敷演，殊戾本旨。此作卓有所見，而詞亦雅贍，錄之。」
同考試官教諭閔批：「說理文字，不冗則晦。求其體認親切而善於措辭者，無踰此篇。」
考試官學正何批：「整潔可誦。」
考試官教授劉批：「文有理致。」

聖人論有德者深知夫天理之所宜也。蓋君子之心一於理而已，則其所喻者，豈有外於理之所宜哉？聖人論君子之異於小人者如此，謂夫
translation_en:
Then can those who govern fail to understand the way to make the state’s resources sufficient, and instead pursue the monopolization of profit? Financial resources are, generally speaking, an urgent necessity for the state, something it cannot lack for even a single day. Yet whenever they are collected without proper principles, merely stripping resources from the people, the people’s allegiance is invariably lost. Thus, when Master Zeng discusses here the way to secure sufficient resources for the state, he necessarily attributes it to the benevolent person. Is this not a clear rule for all who rule the world in succeeding ages? Later, Meng Ke said, “Without the conduct of government, financial resources will be insufficient.” He also said, “If Your Majesty loves wealth, share it with the common people. What difficulty would there be in becoming a true king?” Was this not also Master Zeng’s meaning?

“The Gentleman Understands Righteousness”
By Xue Kan

Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: “The understanding of righteousness is clearly distinguished, and the discussion proceeds in terms of knowing [?]. Most candidates elaborate on the practice of righteousness, departing considerably from the original purport. This composition displays outstanding insight, and its language is also elegant and ample. I select it for inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Min, Instructor, comments: “Writing that expounds principles tends to be either prolix or obscure. For intimate comprehension and skill in expression, no essay surpasses this one.”
Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: “Orderly, cleanly written, and worthy of recitation.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “The composition conveys principled insight.”

The Sage speaks of how those possessed of virtue deeply understand what accords with Heavenly principle. The gentleman’s mind is wholly devoted to principle; could what he understands therefore lie outside what accords with that principle? Such is the Sage’s account of how the gentleman differs from the petty man. He means that…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人品不同則其所喻亦異惟所謂君子者氣質
清明而其所造詣者蓋極其深德性渾全而其
所識見者一出於正天下之事開闔常變莫不
各有當然之則君子則不昧於所從焉天下之
物大小精粗莫不各有自然之理君子則能審
其所向焉無適無莫於凡義之所比者知之極
其精而他岐不足以惑之不信不果於凡義之
所在者見之極其明而外物不得以蔽之大而
一身之進退小而一物之取予在我之權度精
===
切而所以處之者確乎不差奚翅龜卜而蓍筮
邪大而死生之故小而食息之微在我之方寸
虛明而所以辨之者的然不惑奚翅燭照而數
計邪吁君子之喻於義者如此若夫小人則反
是矣學者其可不知所以擇之乎大抵天下之
道二義與利耳出乎此則入乎彼幾微之際蓋
有未易辨者尚父之戒武王而曰義勝欲者從
欲勝義者凶孟子亦曰舜與蹠之分善與利之
間而已毫釐之不審天淵之懸隔聖賢每於是
punctuated: 人品不同，則其所喻亦異。惟所謂君子者，氣質清明，而其所造詣者蓋極其深；德性渾全，而其所識見者一出於正。天下之事，開闔常變，莫不各有當然之則，君子則不昧於所從焉；天下之物，大小精粗，莫不各有自然之理，君子則能審其所向焉。無適無莫，於凡義之所比者，知之極其精，而他岐不足以惑之；不信不果，於凡義之所在者，見之極其明，而外物不得以蔽之。大而一身之進退，小而一物之取予，在我之權度精切，而所以處之者確乎不差，奚翅龜卜而蓍筮邪？大而死生之故，小而食息之微，在我之方寸虛明，而所以辨之者的然不惑，奚翅燭照而數計邪？吁！君子之喻於義者如此，若夫小人則反是矣。學者其可不知所以擇之乎？大抵天下之道二，義與利耳。出乎此，則入乎彼，幾微之際，蓋有未易辨者。尚父之戒武王而曰：「義勝欲者從，欲勝義者凶。」孟子亦曰：「舜與蹠之分，善與利之間而已。」毫釐之不審，天淵之懸隔，聖賢每於是
translation_en: …People differ in character, and so what they understand also differs. Those called gentlemen possess a clear and lucid physical endowment, and their attainments are exceedingly profound; their moral nature is whole and complete, and their understanding proceeds entirely from what is right. All the affairs of the world, in their unfolding and closing, their constancy and change, have their proper standards, and the gentleman is never ignorant of what to follow. All things in the world, great or small, subtle or coarse, have their inherent principles, and the gentleman can discern where to direct himself. With neither fixed preferences nor fixed aversions, he understands with utmost precision whatever accords with righteousness, and divergent paths cannot confuse him. Without insisting rigidly on keeping his word or carrying an action through, he sees with utmost clarity wherever righteousness lies, and external things cannot obscure his understanding. In matters as great as his own advancement or withdrawal, or as small as accepting or giving a single object, his inner measures are precise, and his handling of them is assuredly without error. How could this be merely comparable to divination by tortoise shell or milfoil stalks? In matters as great as life and death, or as slight as eating and resting, his heart is unclouded and clear, and his discernment is certain and free from confusion. How could this be merely comparable to illumination by a lamp or reckoning by numbers? Ah! Such is the gentleman’s understanding of righteousness; the petty man is the opposite. Can students fail to understand how to choose between them? Broadly speaking, there are only two paths in the world: righteousness and profit. To leave one is to enter the other, and at the subtlest point of divergence they may not be easy to distinguish. Shangfu admonished King Wu, saying: “When righteousness overcomes desire, things go favorably [?]; when desire overcomes righteousness, misfortune follows.” Mengzi also said: “The distinction between Shun and Zhi lies simply in the difference between goodness and profit.” Failure to discern a hair’s breadth of difference results in a gulf as vast as that between heaven and the depths. The sages and worthies invariably, with regard to these…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
二者對舉而互言之其垂訓之意至矣厥後宋
儒張子有曰無所為而為之者義也有所為而
為之者利也朱子謂其擴前聖所未發是又後
學之所當知
夏曰校殷曰序周曰庠學則三代共之皆
所以明人倫也人倫明於上小民親於
下
陳世美
同考試官訓導陳批三代立學教民成俗之意具
===
於此數語而能鋪叙有法僅見此篇
同考試官訓導楊批平平說去而步驟自然中節
蓋必養之有素者
考試官學正何批文字有機軸
考試官教授劉批講語精確
大賢詳舉三代之學必指其教之所以立而及
其化之所由成也蓋人倫者立教之本也三代
以是教民而民豈有不化者哉昔孟子答滕文
公為國之問及此若曰政莫要於教民法莫善
punctuated:
二者對舉而互言之，其垂訓之意至矣。厥後宋儒張子有曰：「無所為而為之者，義也；有所為而為之者，利也。」朱子謂其擴前聖所未發，是又後學之所當知。

夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠，學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。

陳世美

同考試官訓導陳批：三代立學、教民、成俗之意，具於此數語，而能鋪叙有法，僅見此篇。

同考試官訓導楊批：平平說去，而步驟自然中節，蓋必養之有素者。

考試官學正何批：文字有機軸。

考試官教授劉批：講語精確。

大賢詳舉三代之學，必指其教之所以立，而及其化之所由成也。蓋人倫者，立教之本也。三代以是教民，而民豈有不化者哉？昔孟子答滕文公為國之問，及此，若曰：「政莫要於教民，法莫善
translation_en:
…these two were set against one another and discussed in relation to each other: the intention of the sages in transmitting their instruction was most profound. Later, the Song scholar Master Zhang said: “To act without an ulterior purpose is righteousness; to act with an ulterior purpose is profit-seeking.” Master Zhu said that this extended what earlier sages had left unexpressed. This, too, is something later students should understand.

“In the Xia they were called xiao, in the Yin xu, and in the Zhou xiang; as for xue, all three dynasties shared that designation. All served to clarify human relationships. When human relationships are made clear above, the common people below live in affection with one another.”

Chen Shimei

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: The intentions behind the Three Dynasties’ establishment of schools, instruction of the people, and formation of customs are all contained in these few words. Yet this is the only essay I have seen that develops them in an orderly manner.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: The exposition proceeds in a plain, unforced manner, yet its progression naturally accords with the proper measure. This must surely be the work of someone who has long cultivated his abilities.

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: The writing has an organizing conception.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: The explanation is precise.
