When the great worthy enumerates in detail the schools of the Three Dynasties, he necessarily identifies the basis on which their teaching was established and goes on to explain how its transforming influence was achieved. Human relationships are the foundation of instruction. The Three Dynasties taught the people through these relationships: how could any of the people have failed to be transformed? Formerly, when Mencius answered Duke Wen of Teng’s question about governing a state, he touched on this point, as though saying: “In government, nothing is more essential than teaching the people; no models are better …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於三代彼其都鄙鄉遂之地必有鄉學夏之鄉
學則取教民之義名之曰校殷之鄉學則取習
射之義名之曰序周之鄉學則謂之庠蓋有取
於養老之義焉是皆所謂小學也至於王畿首
善之地必有國學則殷因於夏而稱之無異名
周因於殷而名之無異義是則所謂大學也夫
以庠序學校之設如此而其所以爲教者夫豈
求之民性之外哉蓋以父子之親君臣之義人
之大倫也然或奪於情而牽於愛則日就晦蝕
===
矣必於學而講明之夫婦之別長幼之序朋友
之信亦人之大倫也然或溺於私而流於俗則
日就昏昧矣必於學而開發之本之於躬行心
得之餘加之以鼓舞作興之道親義之倫明於
上而天下之爲父子君臣者各得其分翕然相
敬而相愛雍穆之化行矣序別信之倫明於上
而天下之爲夫婦長幼朋友者各止其所怡然
相信而相悅和順之俗作矣化行於上俗美於
下三代教民之善如此文公爲國舍是將誰法
punctuated: 於三代。彼其都鄙鄉遂之地，必有鄉學。夏之鄉學，則取教民之義，名之曰校；殷之鄉學，則取習射之義，名之曰序；周之鄉學，則謂之庠，蓋有取於養老之義焉。是皆所謂小學也。至於王畿首善之地，必有國學，則殷因於夏而稱之無異名，周因於殷而名之無異義，是則所謂大學也。夫以庠序學校之設如此，而其所以爲教者，夫豈求之民性之外哉？蓋以父子之親、君臣之義，人之大倫也，然或奪於情而牽於愛，則日就晦蝕矣，必於學而講明之。夫婦之別、長幼之序、朋友之信，亦人之大倫也，然或溺於私而流於俗，則日就昏昧矣，必於學而開發之。本之於躬行心得之餘，加之以鼓舞作興之道。親義之倫明於上，而天下之爲父子君臣者各得其分，翕然相敬而相愛，雍穆之化行矣；序別信之倫明於上，而天下之爲夫婦長幼朋友者各止其所，怡然相信而相悅，和順之俗作矣。化行於上，俗美於下，三代教民之善如此，文公爲國，舍是將誰法
translation_en: …than those of the Three Dynasties. In their cities and outlying settlements, their inner and outer rural districts, there were invariably local schools. The local schools of the Xia were named xiao, taking their meaning from teaching the people; those of the Yin were named xu, taking their meaning from practicing archery; those of the Zhou were called xiang, taking their meaning from nurturing the aged. These were all what are called elementary schools. In the royal domain, the place foremost in moral excellence, there was invariably a state school. The Yin followed the Xia without changing its designation, and the Zhou followed the Yin without changing the meaning of its name. This was what is called the great school. With schools of these various kinds thus established, could the teaching they provided possibly have been sought outside the people's own nature? Affection between father and son and righteousness between ruler and minister are fundamental human relationships. Yet when people are overcome by emotion and swayed by attachment, these become increasingly obscured and impaired. They must therefore be expounded and clarified in the schools. Distinction between husband and wife, precedence between elder and younger, and trust between friends are also fundamental human relationships. Yet when people sink into selfishness and drift with prevailing customs, these become increasingly obscure. They must therefore be elucidated and brought to light in the schools. Having grounded this teaching in personal practice and understanding attained in the heart, one must further employ ways of inspiring and rousing people. When the relationships of affection and righteousness are made clear above, fathers and sons, rulers and ministers throughout the realm each fulfill their proper roles, united in mutual respect and affection, and the transforming influence of harmony and reverence spreads. When the relationships of precedence, distinction, and trust are made clear above, husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends throughout the realm each abide in their proper places, gladly trusting and delighting in one another, and customs of harmony and concord arise. Transforming influence proceeds from above, and customs become fine below. Such was the excellence with which the Three Dynasties taught the people. If Duke Wen, in governing his state, were to abandon this, whom would he take as his model…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉抑論戰國之時三代之教盡廢區區小國之
君如滕文者尚何望其能興三代之治然而孟
子拳拳以是告之亦獨何哉蓋聖賢之所學者
三代之法也齊梁之君地大民眾足以有爲既
嘗以是語之而卒不見用滕文有志則亦安得
不爲之告邪嗚呼於此可見聖賢之用心矣
易
天且弗違而況於人乎
潘濂
===
同考試官訓導陳批作者多將天且弗違兼後天
說況於人乎作利見說惟此篇於天人處體認真切錄之
同考試官訓導楊批題本明白學者多體認不真
此篇理順詞暢是用錄之爲治易者式
考試官學正何批詞理俱到
考試官教授劉批得本義旨
道所由出者既從乎大人道所同具者必從乎
大人夫道出於天而具於人也大人所爲皆道
天既從之矣人豈有不從者哉文言釋乾九五
punctuated:
哉？抑論戰國之時，三代之教盡廢，區區小國之君如滕文者，尚何望其能興三代之治？然而孟子拳拳以是告之，亦獨何哉？蓋聖賢之所學者，三代之法也。齊梁之君，地大民眾，足以有爲，既嘗以是語之，而卒不見用。滕文有志，則亦安得不爲之告邪？嗚呼！於此可見聖賢之用心矣。

易
天且弗違，而況於人乎？
潘濂

同考試官訓導陳批：作者多將「天且弗違」兼「後天」說，「況於人乎」作「利見」說。惟此篇於天人處體認真切，錄之。
同考試官訓導楊批：題本明白，學者多體認不真。此篇理順詞暢，是用錄之，爲治易者式。
考試官學正何批：詞理俱到。
考試官教授劉批：得本義旨。

道所由出者既從乎大人，道所同具者必從乎大人。夫道出於天而具於人也，大人所爲皆道。天既從之矣，人豈有不從者哉？文言釋乾九五
translation_en:
…? Yet consider the Warring States period: the teachings of the Three Dynasties had been entirely abandoned. What hope could there have been that the ruler of a mere small state, such as Duke Wen of Teng, could revive the governance of the Three Dynasties? Why, then, did Mengzi so earnestly instruct him in this? It was because the sages and worthies studied the methods of the Three Dynasties. The rulers of Qi and Liang had extensive territories and large populations, sufficient to accomplish something. Mengzi had already spoken to them of these methods, but in the end his counsel was not adopted. Since Duke Wen of Teng had the aspiration, how could Mengzi refrain from instructing him? Ah! Here we can see the intentions of the sages and worthies.

Book of Changes
“Even Heaven does not oppose him; how much less will men?”
Pan Lian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: Most writers interpret “Even Heaven does not oppose him” as also encompassing “acting after Heaven,” and explain “how much less will men?” in terms of “it is beneficial to see [the great man].” This essay alone shows a precise and genuine understanding of Heaven and humanity in this passage. I have selected it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: The topic is inherently clear, but students often fail to grasp it truly. This essay has coherent reasoning and fluent expression. I have therefore selected it as a model for those studying the Book of Changes.

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: It captures the purport of the Original Meaning of the Book of Changes.

Since that from which the Way issues follows the great man, those who alike possess the Way must follow the great man. The Way issues from Heaven and is present in human beings. Everything the great man does accords with the Way. Since Heaven follows him, how could human beings fail to follow him? The Commentary on the Words of the Text, explaining the fifth, yang line of Qian …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爻義至此謂夫九五大人至公无私以道爲體
是以天理民彝天固不能无賴於大人也彼則
聰明以開其先凡心之所經畫者即天之所默
成天且從之而不違民生日用天固不能无望
於大人也彼則沉幾以創其始凡意之所建立
者即天之所默定天且順之而不拂觀其通變
神化也則祐之以吉无不利裁成輔相也則因
之而无過不及天豈能違之哉天且弗違如此
況人之生也藐然有身其心即天之心也於大
===
人所經畫者必遵之以寡過混然中處其道即
天之道也於大人所建立者必宜之而不倦在
當世則曰立我烝民莫匪爾極出入惟順帝之
則而已求其自用自專者何有在後世則曰佑
啓後人以正罔缺日用惟遵王之道而已求其
不信不從者蔑如人又豈能違之哉吁大人所
爲建之於天而天不悖徵之於人而人必從如
此是其道德之純絕无有我之私允爲人類之
首而爲人所利見也歟雖然分而二之天之弗
punctuated: 爻義至此，謂夫九五大人至公无私，以道爲體。是以天理民彝，天固不能无賴於大人也。彼則聰明以開其先，凡心之所經畫者，即天之所默成，天且從之而不違。民生日用，天固不能无望於大人也。彼則沉幾以創其始，凡意之所建立者，即天之所默定，天且順之而不拂。觀其通變神化也，則祐之以吉，无不利；裁成輔相也，則因之而无過不及。天豈能違之哉？天且弗違如此，況人之生也，藐然有身，其心即天之心也，於大人所經畫者，必遵之以寡過；混然中處，其道即天之道也，於大人所建立者，必宜之而不倦。在當世則曰：「立我烝民，莫匪爾極。」出入惟順帝之則而已，求其自用自專者何有？在後世則曰：「佑啓後人，以正罔缺。」日用惟遵王之道而已，求其不信不從者蔑如。人又豈能違之哉？吁！大人所爲，建之於天而天不悖，徵之於人而人必從，如此，是其道德之純，絕无有我之私，允爲人類之首，而爲人所利見也歟！雖然，分而二之，天之弗
translation_en:
…the meaning of the line, reaching this point, is that the great man of the nine in the fifth place is utterly impartial and without selfishness, taking the Way as his substance. Thus, in matters of Heaven’s principle and the constant norms of human conduct, Heaven itself must rely upon the great man. Through his perceptiveness he opens the way: whatever his mind plans is precisely what Heaven silently accomplishes. Even Heaven follows him without departing from him. In matters of the people’s livelihood and daily needs, Heaven itself must place its hopes in the great man. Through profound discernment of incipient developments he initiates things: whatever his intention establishes is precisely what Heaven silently determines. Even Heaven accords with him without opposing him. Consider how he comprehends change and brings about wondrous transformation: Heaven blesses him with good fortune, with nothing that is not beneficial. Consider how he regulates and completes, assists and supports: Heaven follows his work, so that there is neither excess nor deficiency. How could Heaven depart from him?

If even Heaven does not depart from him in this way, how much more must this hold for human beings! Born with their small and insignificant bodies, their minds are nevertheless Heaven’s mind. They must follow what the great man plans, so as to lessen their faults. Dwelling amid the undivided whole [?], their Way is Heaven’s Way. They must fit themselves to what the great man establishes, without growing weary. Of his own age it is said: “You establish our teeming people; none fails to take you as the standard.” In all their movements they simply follow the Supreme Lord’s rule. Where could one find anyone acting solely on personal judgment or asserting independent authority? Of later ages it is said: “Aid and enlighten those who come after, through rectitude without deficiency.” In daily life they simply follow the king’s Way. Those who neither trust nor follow him are nowhere to be found. How, then, could human beings depart from him?

Ah! What the great man does is set before Heaven, and Heaven does not contradict it; it is tested against human beings, and they invariably follow it. Such is the purity of his Way and virtue, entirely free of selfish concern for himself. Surely he is worthy to stand at the head of humankind and to be one whom it benefits people to see! Nevertheless, if we distinguish the two, Heaven’s not departing…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
違人必不違也合而一之則天之視聽皆在於
人人之從違即天之從違也是故觀天命者每
卜諸人心善言天者必有驗於人外乎人以求
天不可也噫安得學貫天人者而與之言易哉
履信思乎順又以尚賢也是以自天祐之
吉无不利也
蔡士儲
同考試官訓導陳批說出大有上九滿而不溢
明白簡當較之衆作自別本房殆無出其右者
===
同考試官訓導楊批此題卦爻本義明白作者
多無根據晚得此卷讀之令人嘆賞
考試官學正何批得潔淨精微之旨
考試官教授劉批理明詞到
能盡處有之道斯享所有之福聖人釋大有爻
義然也夫有大者不可以盈也上九處之盡其
道則其獲天之祐不亦宜乎大傳釋大有上九
爻辭如此意謂上九所以自天祐之吉無不利
者何哉蓋其大有之世以剛居上而能下從六
punctuated:
違，人必不違也；合而一之，則天之視聽皆在於人，人之從違即天之從違也。是故觀天命者，每卜諸人心；善言天者，必有驗於人。外乎人以求天，不可也。噫！安得學貫天人者，而與之言易哉！
「履信思乎順，又以尚賢也，是以自天祐之，吉无不利也。」
蔡士儲
同考試官訓導陳批：說出大有上九滿而不溢，明白簡當，較之衆作自別，本房殆無出其右者。
同考試官訓導楊批：此題卦爻本義明白，作者多無根據。晚得此卷，讀之令人嘆賞。
考試官學正何批：得潔淨精微之旨。
考試官教授劉批：理明詞到。
能盡處有之道，斯享所有之福，聖人釋大有爻義然也。夫有大者，不可以盈也。上九處之盡其道，則其獲天之祐，不亦宜乎？大傳釋大有上九爻辭如此，意謂上九所以自天祐之、吉無不利者，何哉？蓋其大有之世，以剛居上，而能下從六
translation_en:
…does not oppose, people will certainly not oppose either. If the two are considered as one, Heaven’s seeing and hearing reside entirely in the people: the people’s assent or opposition is precisely Heaven’s assent or opposition. Thus, those who observe Heaven’s mandate always seek its indications in the hearts of the people; those who speak well of Heaven must have their words verified among the people. To seek Heaven apart from the people is impossible. Ah! Where might one find someone whose learning comprehends both Heaven and humanity, with whom to discuss the Book of Changes?
“He practices trustworthiness and gives thought to compliance, and furthermore honors the worthy. Therefore Heaven itself aids him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.”
Cai Shichu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: The essay explains how the top nine of Great Possession is full without overflowing. Clear, concise, and apt, it stands apart from the other compositions. Among the papers in this examining section, scarcely any surpass it.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: The original meaning of the hexagram and line relevant to this topic is clear, yet most writers offer arguments without foundation. I received this paper late; reading it inspires admiration.
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: It grasps the purport of purity, refinement, and subtlety.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: Its principles are clear, and its wording fully expresses them.
Only by fully realizing the Way of living amid possessions can one enjoy the blessings of what one possesses: such is the sage’s explanation of the meaning of the line in Great Possession. One whose possessions are great must not become self-satisfied. Since the top nine fully realizes the proper Way in this situation, is it not fitting that it receives Heaven’s aid? Such is the Great Commentary’s explanation of the line statement for the top nine of Great Possession. Its meaning is this: why does the top nine receive aid from Heaven itself, with good fortune and nothing unfavorable? It is because, in the time of Great Possession, it occupies the highest position with firmness, yet can follow the six below …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
五則是五之虛中有信之德也彼則能履其信
凡措諸躬行者信以發志未嘗恃有而放誕五
之柔巽有順之德也彼則能思其順凡存諸念
慮者卑以自牧未嘗挾有而驕矜匪惟履信而
已又能降志以尊尚乎六五之賢不自作其聰
明焉匪惟思順而已又能致恭以崇重乎六五
之德不自用其賢智焉夫上九能盡處有之道
如此將見天眷來於信順之餘而所以祐之者
有隆而無替帝心簡於尚賢之後而所以福之
===
者方進而未已滿而不溢位之受於先者猶鞏
用黃牛之革吉於我乎得矣何所往而不利哉
大而不盈禄之得於舊者有繫于苞桑之固吉
於我乎獲矣何所適而不宜哉吁盡道於已獲
福於天上九其善於處有歟嗟夫謙則受益滿
則招損大有上九所有既極使非持盈守滿之
有道則如乾上九亢龍之悔旅上九喪牛之凶
將不免矣尚望其吉無不利而保所有於終哉
噫有大能謙必豫窮大者必失其居孔子之意
punctuated: 五，則是五之虛中有信之德也，彼則能履其信。凡措諸躬行者，信以發志，未嘗恃有而放誕。五之柔巽有順之德也，彼則能思其順。凡存諸念慮者，卑以自牧，未嘗挾有而驕矜。匪惟履信而已，又能降志以尊尚乎六五之賢，不自作其聰明焉；匪惟思順而已，又能致恭以崇重乎六五之德，不自用其賢智焉。夫上九能盡處有之道如此，將見天眷來於信順之餘，而所以祐之者有隆而無替；帝心簡於尚賢之後，而所以福之者方進而未已。滿而不溢，位之受於先者，猶鞏用黃牛之革，吉於我乎得矣，何所往而不利哉？大而不盈，禄之得於舊者，有繫于苞桑之固，吉於我乎獲矣，何所適而不宜哉？吁！盡道於已，獲福於天，上九其善於處有歟！嗟夫！謙則受益，滿則招損。大有上九，所有既極，使非持盈守滿之有道，則如乾上九亢龍之悔、旅上九喪牛之凶，將不免矣，尚望其吉無不利而保所有於終哉？噫！有大能謙必豫，窮大者必失其居，孔子之意
translation_en:
…the fifth line: since the fifth line’s inner emptiness embodies the virtue of trustworthiness, the top nine can put that trustworthiness into practice. In all his personal conduct, he expresses his intentions through good faith, never relying on his possessions to act without restraint. Since the fifth line’s yielding gentleness embodies the virtue of compliance, he can keep that compliance in mind. In all his thoughts and deliberations, he cultivates himself through humility, never using his possessions as grounds for arrogance. Not only does he practice good faith; he also humbles his will to honor the worthiness of the six in the fifth place, rather than setting up his own discernment as authoritative. Not only does he reflect on compliance; he also shows reverence to honor the virtue of the six in the fifth place, rather than relying exclusively on his own worthiness and wisdom.

Since the top nine so fully realizes the proper way of possessing abundance, Heaven’s favor will follow upon his good faith and compliance, and its protection will increase without declining. After he has honored the worthy, he will be singled out in the heart of the Supreme Lord, whose blessings will continue to advance without cease. Full but not overflowing, he will hold the position received earlier as securely as if bound with the hide of a yellow ox. Good fortune is thus mine: wherever I go, what could fail to be beneficial? Great but not overfull, he will retain the emoluments formerly acquired as firmly as if tied to a clump of mulberry trees. Good fortune is thus mine: wherever I turn, what could fail to be fitting? Ah! Fully realizing the Way in oneself and receiving blessings from Heaven—how well the top nine handles abundance!

Alas! Humility brings benefit; fullness invites loss. At the top nine of Great Possession, one’s possessions have reached their utmost extent. Without a proper way to sustain and preserve such fullness, one could not escape the regret of the ‘overreaching dragon’ at the top nine of The Creative, or the misfortune of ‘losing the ox’ at the top nine of The Wanderer. Could one still hope for ‘good fortune, with nothing unfavorable,’ and preserve one’s possessions to the end? Ah! One who possesses greatness yet remains humble will surely find contentment; one who pushes greatness to its limit will surely lose his dwelling. This meaning of Confucius …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
又於序卦發之合而觀之則保有之道可得矣
書
侯以明之撻以記之書用識哉欲並生哉
蕭汝爲
同考試官教諭顧批題本不難解而作者鋪叙
多至晦澁詞不費而意自到無喻此篇
同考試官教諭閔批圓轉條暢經義似此者絕少
考試官學正何批意思周匝
考試官教授劉批說出有虞不輕棄人處宛
然在目
===
聖世於未化之人詳有以教之者欲有以全之
也甚矣聖世不輕於棄人也則於侯明撻記而
書識之者豈非欲化其善而全其生也哉昔帝
舜告禹之意若曰臣鄰之責在汝無負固可以
爲忠直之勸矣然一有頑愚讒說出於其間則
爲盛治之累矣可無道以處之乎是故射所以
觀德也於是取彼射侯試以射藝若使容體不
比於禮而其發也或不能中節奏不比於樂而
punctuated:
又於《序卦》發之。合而觀之，則保有之道可得矣。

書
「侯以明之，撻以記之，書用識哉！欲並生哉！」
蕭汝爲

同考試官教諭顧批：「題本不難解，而作者鋪叙多至晦澁。詞不費而意自到，無喻此篇。」
同考試官教諭閔批：「圓轉條暢，經義似此者絕少。」
考試官學正何批：「意思周匝。」
考試官教授劉批：「說出有虞不輕棄人處，宛然在目。」

聖世於未化之人，詳有以教之者，欲有以全之也。甚矣，聖世不輕於棄人也！則於侯明、撻記而書識之者，豈非欲化其善而全其生也哉？昔帝舜告禹之意若曰：「臣鄰之責，在汝無負，固可以爲忠直之勸矣。然一有頑愚讒說出於其間，則爲盛治之累矣，可無道以處之乎？是故射所以觀德也，於是取彼射侯，試以射藝。若使容體不比於禮，而其發也或不能中；節奏不比於樂，而」
translation_en:
…He also expounded this in the Sequence of the Hexagrams. Considered together, these passages reveal the way to preserve what one possesses.

Book of Documents
“Use the archery target to make their character clear; use flogging to impress it upon their memory; use written records to mark their faults! The wish is that all should live!”
By Xiao Ruwei.

Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is not difficult to understand, yet writers often elaborate it to the point of obscurity. For economical wording that fully conveys the meaning, nothing surpasses this piece [?].”
Associate Examiner Min, Instructor, comments: “Smoothly flowing and lucidly ordered. Expositions of the Classics like this are exceedingly rare.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The ideas are comprehensive and thorough.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “It brings vividly before our eyes the way the ruler of Youyu did not lightly abandon people.”

In a sage-governed age, the careful provision made to teach those who have not yet been transformed is intended to preserve them. How very reluctant such an age is to abandon people! Thus, when their character is revealed through the target, correction impressed upon them through flogging, and their faults noted in writing, is this not intended to transform them toward goodness and preserve their lives?

The meaning of Emperor Shun’s words to Yu in former times was as though he said: “The responsibilities of a minister who stands close to his ruler rest upon you: do not fail them. This can certainly encourage loyalty and uprightness. Yet if even one stubborn fool or slanderer appears among them, he will burden this flourishing government. Can there be no way to deal with him? Thus archery is a means of observing virtue. Take the archery target and test him in the art of shooting. If his bearing and posture do not accord with ritual, his shots may fail to hit; if his rhythm does not accord with the music, and…”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其中也亦不能多則其心之不正而爲頑愚讒
說也無疑矣然於此而遂釋之不可也故必施
夫夏楚而治之以學校之刑使其備嘗折辱於
膚體之間庶幾記憶於心不至於或忘焉於此
而遂置之不可也又必錄其過惡而揭之於簡
冊之書于以暴著事迹於耳目之表庶幾愧念
於心不能以自己焉然其所以教之之詳如此
者果何意哉蓋以頑愚不改勢不免於刑誅矣
所以侯明而撻記之者非忍外之也蓋欲啓其
===
憤發其悱變頑愚而爲忠直而與濟濟臣工並
生於天地之間不爲盛世之棄人矣讒說不悛
勢必至於滅絕矣所以撻記而書識之者非故
薄之也蓋欲改其惡遷於善變讒說而爲臣鄰
而與烝烝士庶並生於覆載之內不爲太平之
棄物矣吁教之詳可以見聖人之義待之至可
以見聖人之仁宜乎史臣詳載之於書也抑觀
有虞之世萬邦咸寧可謂盛矣近而九德咸事
遠而黎獻共臣尚何庶頑讒說之足慮哉觀舜
punctuated: 其中也亦不能多，則其心之不正而爲頑愚讒說也無疑矣。然於此而遂釋之，不可也。故必施夫夏楚，而治之以學校之刑，使其備嘗折辱於膚體之間，庶幾記憶於心，不至於或忘焉。於此而遂置之，不可也。又必錄其過惡，而揭之於簡冊之書，于以暴著事迹於耳目之表，庶幾愧念於心，不能以自己焉。然其所以教之之詳如此者，果何意哉？蓋以頑愚不改，勢不免於刑誅矣。所以侯明而撻記之者，非忍外之也，蓋欲啓其憤，發其悱，變頑愚而爲忠直，而與濟濟臣工並生於天地之間，不爲盛世之棄人矣。讒說不悛，勢必至於滅絕矣。所以撻記而書識之者，非故薄之也，蓋欲改其惡，遷於善，變讒說而爲臣鄰，而與烝烝士庶並生於覆載之內，不爲太平之棄物矣。吁！教之詳，可以見聖人之義；待之至，可以見聖人之仁。宜乎史臣詳載之於書也！抑觀有虞之世，萬邦咸寧，可謂盛矣。近而九德咸事，遠而黎獻共臣，尚何庶頑讒說之足慮哉？觀舜
translation_en:
…and his hits are also few, then there can be no doubt that his heart is not upright and that he is obstinate, foolish, and given to slander. Yet simply to let him go at this point would be unacceptable. Thus the disciplinary rods must be applied, subjecting him to the punishments of the schools and making him experience humiliation and pain in his own flesh, in the hope that he will remember it in his heart and never forget. Nor would it be acceptable simply to leave him alone thereafter. His faults and misdeeds must also be recorded and displayed in written registers, making his deeds publicly visible and known, in the hope that shame and reflection will arise in his heart and that he will be unable to stop them.

But what, indeed, is the purpose of instructing him so thoroughly? If obstinacy and foolishness remain uncorrected, punishment and execution will inevitably follow. The purpose of using the archery target to reveal his character and flogging to impress the lesson upon him is not to cast him out without pity. Rather, it is to awaken his striving to understand and help him express what he struggles to articulate, transforming obstinacy and foolishness into loyalty and uprightness. He may then live between Heaven and Earth alongside the assembled officials, without becoming an outcast of a flourishing age. If slanderous conduct remains unrepented, it must inevitably lead to destruction. The purpose of flogging to impress the lesson upon him and writing it down as a lasting record is not deliberately to slight him. Rather, it is to make him reform his evil ways and turn toward goodness, changing him from a slanderer into a minister and close supporter of the ruler. He may then live beneath Heaven’s canopy and upon Earth’s sustaining ground alongside the multitudes of gentlemen and commoners, without becoming a castoff of an age of peace.

Ah! In the thoroughness of this instruction we can see the sage’s righteousness; in the utmost care of this treatment we can see the sage’s benevolence. It is fitting that the court historians recorded it in detail in the Documents! Now consider the age of Youyu: the myriad states were all at peace, and it could indeed be called flourishing. Near at hand, those possessing the nine virtues all served in office; far away, the worthy among the people all served as subjects. What cause for concern could there still have been in the obstinate and slanderous? Consider Shun…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之命龍而欲審於出納防其漸也至此復以命
禹而欲詳於教導化其惡也蓋深慮讒邪之害
治而欲謹之於微焉夫子告顏淵之為邦而曰
遠佞人其意不猶是歟
其作大邑其自時配皇天毖祀于上下其
自時中乂
蘇信
同考試官教諭顧批講王者宅洛事辭意嚴整
蓋精於經學者宜錄以為式
===
同考試官教諭閔批詞簡而意自見可以矯經
生浮冗支離之習矣
考試官學正何批不蔓不腐自是作手
考試官教授劉批講語精切
建天下之大業以行天下之大事大臣言作洛
之意也蓋建都王業之大也奉天祀神治民之
事咸於是乎行焉夫豈徒建也哉昔召公告成
王宅洛而舉周公之言如此其意蓋曰不言王
者居洛之事不知王者作洛之意彼擇地以卜
punctuated:
之命龍而欲審於出納，防其漸也。至此復以命禹而欲詳於教導，化其惡也。蓋深慮讒邪之害治，而欲謹之於微焉。夫子告顏淵之為邦而曰：「遠佞人。」其意不猶是歟？
其作大邑，其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下，其自時中乂。
蘇信
同考試官教諭顧批：講王者宅洛事，辭意嚴整，蓋精於經學者，宜錄以為式。
同考試官教諭閔批：詞簡而意自見，可以矯經生浮冗支離之習矣。
考試官學正何批：不蔓不腐，自是作手。
考試官教授劉批：講語精切。
建天下之大業，以行天下之大事，大臣言作洛之意也。蓋建都，王業之大也；奉天、祀神、治民之事，咸於是乎行焉，夫豈徒建也哉！昔召公告成王宅洛，而舉周公之言如此。其意蓋曰：不言王者居洛之事，不知王者作洛之意。彼擇地以卜
translation_en:
…when Shun charged Long to scrutinize what was communicated to the ruler and what was issued from him, he was guarding against the beginnings of this danger. Here he again charged Yu to provide thorough instruction and guidance, to transform their wickedness. Deeply concerned that slander and depravity would harm good government, he wished to take precautions while their manifestations were still slight. When the Master spoke to Yan Yuan about governing a state, he said, “Keep glib flatterers at a distance.” Was his intention not the same?
“Let him build the great city; from here let him match August Heaven in virtue and carefully offer sacrifices to the powers above and below; from here let him govern from the center.”
Su Xin
Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: “The discussion of the king’s taking up residence at Luo is rigorous and orderly in both expression and meaning. Its author is evidently proficient in classical learning; it should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Min, Instructor: “The language is concise, yet the meaning emerges clearly. It can correct the superficiality, verbosity, and fragmentation habitual among students of the Classics.”
Comment by Examiner He, School Director: “Neither rambling nor stale: clearly an accomplished writer.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “The exposition is precise and pertinent.”
To establish the great enterprise of All-under-Heaven so as to carry out the great affairs of All-under-Heaven: this was what the great minister meant in speaking of the founding of Luo. Establishing a capital is a great undertaking of kingship. The duties of serving Heaven, sacrificing to the spirits, and governing the people are all carried out there. Could its purpose be merely to build? Formerly, when the Duke of Shao addressed King Cheng about taking up residence at Luo, he cited these words of the Duke of Zhou. His meaning was this: unless one explains what the king is to do while residing at Luo, one cannot understand the king’s intention in founding Luo. In selecting the site and consulting the oracle …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
基之定之王城中建足以來百辟之朝會體勢
何尊嚴也趨事以民經之營之下都外拓足以
奠四民之居止規模何宏遠也是豈麗宮室而
事游幸哉亦豈輕改作而圖壯觀哉蓋皇矣上
帝天子配之自是可以體元居正臨萬國於覆
幬之下天維顯思仰之不愧也天神地祇天子
祭之自是可以執圭奉幣舉大禮於郊社之時
神之格思祭之不黷也至若和恒居師天子主
之自是可以中天下而立謹身率物惟誠和之
===
治是圖焉定四海之民敬德祈天惟撫綏之政
是修焉吁洛邑之不徒作也如此人君於洛其
可以易而為之哉周公之意深矣抑洛邑之作
豈真舍鎬京之舊而慕新造之樂耶蓋將有所
事也是意也周公知之召公知之恐成王之不
盡知也故周有中乂之言召復繼以自服土中
焉召肯以周固言之乃更其說以自異耶故周
公曰襄我二人汝有合哉噫此二公之所以同
心輔政也
punctuated: 基之，定之，王城中建，足以來百辟之朝會，體勢何尊嚴也！趨事以民，經之，營之，下都外拓，足以奠四民之居止，規模何宏遠也！是豈麗宮室而事游幸哉？亦豈輕改作而圖壯觀哉？蓋皇矣上帝，天子配之，自是可以體元居正，臨萬國於覆幬之下，天維顯思，仰之不愧也。天神地祇，天子祭之，自是可以執圭奉幣，舉大禮於郊社之時，神之格思，祭之不黷也。至若和恒居師，天子主之，自是可以中天下而立，謹身率物，惟誠和之治是圖焉；定四海之民，敬德祈天，惟撫綏之政是修焉。吁！洛邑之不徒作也如此，人君於洛，其可以易而為之哉？周公之意深矣！抑洛邑之作，豈真舍鎬京之舊而慕新造之樂耶？蓋將有所事也。是意也，周公知之，召公知之，恐成王之不盡知也。故周有中乂之言，召復繼以自服土中焉。召肯以周固言之，乃更其說以自異耶？故周公曰：「襄我二人，汝有合哉！」噫！此二公之所以同心輔政也。
translation_en:
…laying its foundations and establishing it, they built the royal city at the center, sufficient to draw the many lords to court assemblies. How imposing and venerable its configuration! Employing the people to carry out the work, they planned and constructed it, extending the lower city outward [?], sufficient to provide settled dwellings for the four classes of people. How grand and far-reaching its design! Could this have been merely to adorn palaces and indulge in imperial excursions? Could it have been to undertake alterations lightly and seek a magnificent spectacle?

For august is the Lord on High, and the Son of Heaven serves as his counterpart. From here he could embody the primal principle and occupy his rightful position, presiding over the myriad states beneath Heaven’s sheltering canopy. “Heaven is indeed manifest”: he could look up to it without shame. The Son of Heaven sacrifices to the celestial and terrestrial spirits. From here he could hold the jade tablet and present offerings of silk, performing the great rites at the suburban sacrifices and the altars of soil. “The spirits come”: he could sacrifice to them without irreverence. As for maintaining harmony and constancy and settling the multitude [?], the Son of Heaven takes charge of these. From here he could stand at the center of All-under-Heaven, conduct himself carefully, and lead others by example, seeking only government founded on sincerity and harmony. He could settle the people within the Four Seas, revere virtue and seek Heaven’s favor, practicing only policies that comfort and pacify them.

Ah! Such were the purposes for which Luoyi was built; it was no idle undertaking. Could a ruler treat his responsibilities at Luo lightly? Profound indeed was the Duke of Zhou’s intention! Moreover, was the construction of Luoyi truly a matter of abandoning the old capital at Haojing out of a desire for the pleasures of building anew? Rather, there were duties to be performed there. The Duke of Zhou understood this intention, and the Duke of Shao understood it, but they feared that King Cheng did not fully understand it. Thus the Duke of Zhou spoke of governing from the center, and the Duke of Shao followed this by speaking of personally carrying out his duties at the center of the land. Would the Duke of Shao, merely because the Duke of Zhou had already said it, have changed his account to distinguish himself? Thus the Duke of Zhou said: “Assist us two; may you be in accord!” Ah! This is how the two dukes aided the government with one heart.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詩
江漢湯湯武夫洸洸經營四方告成于王
四方旣平王國庶定時靡有爭王心載
寧江漢之滸王命召虎式辟四方徹我
疆土匪疚匪棘王國來極于疆于理至
于南海王命召虎來旬來宣文武受命
召公維翰無曰予小子召公是似肇敏
戎公用錫爾祉釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣告
于文人錫山土田于周受命自召祖命
===
彭遇
同考試官教諭莊 批長題難於包括此作明白
整齊且深得詩人稱美召穆公之旨佳士也健
羨健羨
同考試官教諭江 批大雅題塲中作者多體認
失真僅得此篇理明辭暢其葩經中之傑然者是
用錄出
考試官學正何 批分截明白詞語平正戛異諸作
考試官教授劉 批不枯不腴雅義正如此
punctuated:
詩

江漢湯湯，武夫洸洸。經營四方，告成于王。四方旣平，王國庶定。時靡有爭，王心載寧。江漢之滸，王命召虎：「式辟四方，徹我疆土。匪疚匪棘，王國來極。于疆于理，至于南海。」王命召虎：「來旬來宣。文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣。告于文人，錫山土田。于周受命，自召祖命。」

彭遇

同考試官教諭莊批：「長題難於包括，此作明白整齊，且深得詩人稱美召穆公之旨。佳士也！健羨健羨！」

同考試官教諭江批：「大雅題，塲中作者多體認失真，僅得此篇理明辭暢，其葩經中之傑然者，是用錄出。」

考試官學正何批：「分截明白，詞語平正，戛異諸作。」

考試官教授劉批：「不枯不腴，雅義正如此。」
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Vast flow the Jiang and Han rivers; valiant are the warriors. They bring order to the four quarters and report success to the king. The four quarters now pacified, the royal realm may be secure. There is no more contention, and the king’s heart is at peace.

On the banks of the Jiang and Han, the king commands Shao Hu: ‘Open up the four quarters and set in order our territory. Neither cause distress nor act with haste; come and take the royal realm as your standard. Define the boundaries and put the lands in order, reaching as far as the southern sea.’

The king commands Shao Hu: ‘Come, make your rounds; come, proclaim my commands. Wen and Wu received the Mandate, and the Duke of Shao was their mainstay. Do not say, “I am but a young man”; emulate the Duke of Shao. Begin diligently upon your great service, and I shall bestow blessings upon you. I grant you a jade-handled libation ladle and a vessel of black-millet sacrificial wine. Report this to your cultured ancestor. I grant you mountains and fields. Receive your charge at Zhou, following the charge given to your ancestor, the Duke of Shao.’”

Peng Yu

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: “A long examination topic is difficult to cover comprehensively. This composition is clear and orderly, and it also grasps profoundly the poet’s intention in praising Duke Mu of Shao. A fine scholar! Admirable indeed, admirable indeed! [?]”

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “For topics from the Greater Odes, most candidates in the examination hall misconstrue the true meaning. This was the one essay we found with clear reasoning and fluent expression. It is an outstanding piece among those on the Book of Odes, and for this reason we have selected it for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor (xuezheng): “The divisions are clear, and the language is balanced and correct. It stands distinctly apart from the other compositions.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “Neither dry nor overrich: this is precisely how the meaning of the Odes should be expressed.”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詩人美世臣歷建其功必詳述王者命之切而
報之厚也蓋建功者臣之職報功者君之禮也
君臣兩盡其道非盛世其能然哉昔宣王命召
穆公平淮南之夷詩人美之意謂惟我召虎受
命南征瞻彼江漢之水湯湯然而深廣率此武
夫之眾洸洸然而奮揚來求來鋪于以經營乎
四方不矜不伐將以告成于天子當是時王國
靡定以四方之未平也今既平矣王國於是而
大定焉王心匪寧以天下之有爭也今靡爭矣
===
王心於是而載寧焉若此者皆召虎之功也江
漢既平王又命召虎視四方之侵地未闢要皆
闢之以復其舊按疆土之徹法弗行要皆徹之
以行其法固非病彼之民亦非急我之欲也但
使其來取正於王國合人心於一統耳於是遂
疆之而至於南海則大界之定截然矣理之而
止於海邦則溝塗之分井然矣若此者亦召虎
之功也然豈無所激勸哉蓋王初命召虎來此
江漢之滸國事則徧治也王命則宣布也乃謂
punctuated:
詩人美世臣歷建其功，必詳述王者命之切而報之厚也。蓋建功者臣之職，報功者君之禮也。君臣兩盡其道，非盛世其能然哉？昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之夷，詩人美之，意謂惟我召虎受命南征，瞻彼江漢之水，湯湯然而深廣；率此武夫之眾，洸洸然而奮揚。來求來鋪，于以經營乎四方；不矜不伐，將以告成于天子。當是時，王國靡定，以四方之未平也；今既平矣，王國於是而大定焉。王心匪寧，以天下之有爭也；今靡爭矣，王心於是而載寧焉。若此者，皆召虎之功也。

江漢既平，王又命召虎，視四方之侵地未闢，要皆闢之，以復其舊；按疆土之徹法弗行，要皆徹之，以行其法。固非病彼之民，亦非急我之欲也，但使其來取正於王國，合人心於一統耳。於是遂疆之而至於南海，則大界之定截然矣；理之而止於海邦，則溝塗之分井然矣。若此者，亦召虎之功也。

然豈無所激勸哉？蓋王初命召虎來此江漢之滸，國事則徧治也，王命則宣布也，乃謂：
translation_en:
When the poet praises the successive achievements of a hereditary servant of the state, he necessarily recounts in detail how earnestly the king charged him with his task and how generously he rewarded him. For achieving merit is the minister’s duty, and rewarding merit is the ruler’s ritual obligation. Could ruler and minister both fully discharge their proper roles except in an age of flourishing government? Formerly, King Xuan ordered Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the Yi peoples south of the Huai River, and the poet praised him. The sense is this: our Shao Hu received orders to campaign in the south. He beheld the waters of the Jiang and Han, surging, deep, and broad, and led his host of warriors, martial and spirited. He came to seek out and deploy [?], thereby bringing order to the four quarters. Neither vaunting himself nor boasting of his deeds, he would report his success to the Son of Heaven. At that time, the royal realm was unsettled because the four quarters had not been pacified. Now that they were pacified, the royal realm became firmly settled. The king’s heart was uneasy because there was strife under Heaven. Now that strife had ceased, the king’s heart at last found peace. All these were Shao Hu’s achievements.

Once the Jiang and Han regions had been pacified, the king again commanded Shao Hu to inspect lands in the four quarters that had been encroached upon and not yet recovered: he was to recover them all and restore their former extent. He was also to examine where the che system of land taxation was not being implemented throughout the territory: he was to apply it everywhere, putting its regulations into effect. This was certainly not to afflict those people, nor to press for the satisfaction of his own desires. It was simply to have them take their standards from the royal realm and unite the people’s hearts under a single rule. Thus Shao Hu established boundaries as far as the Southern Sea, clearly fixing the realm’s outer limits. He ordered the land as far as the coastal states, arranging its ditches and roads in orderly divisions. These too were Shao Hu’s achievements.

Yet could he have lacked encouragement and incentive? When the king first commanded Shao Hu to come to these banks of the Jiang and Han, he charged him to attend comprehensively to affairs of state and to proclaim the royal commands. He then said: …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昔我祖文武受命于天惟汝祖召公爲周之翰
今汝勿曰予小子故也但當似汝召公可焉汝
能開敏其功果無愧於召公之維翰則我當錫
汝以福必不靳於文武之褒崇然豈徒空言爲
哉今王賜以策命念其祀先恩薄也則釐爾圭
瓚秬鬯一卣使得以祀其先祖知其封邑未廣
也則告于文人錫山土田使得以廣其封邑然
命不苟受必使往岐周興王之地而受之往不
徒行必從祖康公受命之所以寵之一以昭報
===
貺之厚恩非出於今也一以表世臣之賢功無
替於先也吁臣有功而不負君之命君有賜而
不負臣之功此有周之所以中興也歟嗟夫君
臣相遇自古爲難周至宣王內脩外攘志在恢
復誠可謂有道之賢君矣時則有若吉甫方叔
召穆公者出南征北伐各獻其功亦皆名世之
賢佐也噫雲龍相從風虎相就中興之盛是豈
偶然者哉
載戢干戈載櫜弓矢
punctuated:
「昔我祖文武受命于天，惟汝祖召公爲周之翰。今汝勿曰予小子故也，但當似汝召公可焉。汝能開敏其功，果無愧於召公之維翰，則我當錫汝以福，必不靳於文武之褒崇。」然豈徒空言爲哉？今王賜以策命，念其祀先恩薄也，則釐爾圭瓚、秬鬯一卣，使得以祀其先祖；知其封邑未廣也，則告于文人，錫山土田，使得以廣其封邑。然命不苟受，必使往岐周興王之地而受之；往不徒行，必從祖康公受命之。所以寵之，一以昭報貺之厚恩非出於今也，一以表世臣之賢功無替於先也。吁！臣有功而不負君之命，君有賜而不負臣之功，此有周之所以中興也歟！嗟夫！君臣相遇，自古爲難。周至宣王，內脩外攘，志在恢復，誠可謂有道之賢君矣。時則有若吉甫、方叔、召穆公者出，南征北伐，各獻其功，亦皆名世之賢佐也。噫！雲龍相從，風虎相就，中興之盛，是豈偶然者哉！

載戢干戈，載櫜弓矢。
translation_en:
…“In former times, my ancestors Wen and Wu received Heaven’s mandate, and your ancestor, the Duke of Shao, was a pillar of Zhou. Now do not plead that you are merely a young man; you need only emulate your Duke of Shao. If you can advance your achievements with diligence [?], truly proving worthy of the Duke of Shao’s service as a pillar, I shall bestow blessings upon you, assuredly no less generously than Wen and Wu bestowed praise and honor.” Yet how could these be merely empty words? Now the king grants him a written investiture. Mindful that the favors enabling him to sacrifice to his ancestors have been scant, he says, “I grant you a jade-handled libation ladle and one vessel of fragrant black-millet wine,” enabling him to sacrifice to his forebears. Knowing that his fief is not yet extensive, he announces the grant to his cultivated ancestor and bestows mountains and farmland, enabling him to enlarge his fief. Yet the investiture is not to be received casually: he must go to Qizhou, the place where the royal house arose, to receive it. Nor is the journey undertaken without purpose: he must receive the investiture in the presence of his ancestor, Duke Kang. The honors bestowed upon him both manifest the abundant favor of these rewards, which did not originate only in the present reign, and show that the worthy achievements of a hereditary servant have not fallen below those of his forebears. Ah! The servant achieves merit and does not fail his lord’s charge; the lord bestows rewards and does not fail his servant’s merit. Was this not how Zhou achieved its restoration? Alas! Since antiquity, a fitting encounter between lord and servant has been difficult to attain. When Zhou reached the reign of King Xuan, he strengthened affairs within and repelled threats from without, setting his will upon restoration. He may truly be called a worthy ruler who possessed the Way. At that time men such as Jifu, Fang Shu, and Duke Mu of Shao came forth, campaigning south and north, each contributing his achievements. They too were all worthy assistants renowned in their age. Ah! Clouds and dragons follow one another; winds and tigers come together. Could the splendor of this restoration have been merely accidental?

Then they laid away their shields and dagger-axes; then they sheathed their bows and arrows.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批寫出武王偃武之意宛
在目宜錄之以式學者
同考試官教諭江批作此題者多不就巡狩上
說且綴緝陳語可厭晚得此篇形容武王巡狩偃武
之意親切可愛宜冠本房
考試官學正何批詞贍氣充必有學之士也允
宜高薦
考試官教授劉批得頌體
===
王者巡狩而藏乎武備正欲以偃乎武事也蓋
用武非聖人之得已也周王巡狩而欲偃武焉
武備安得而不藏之哉此巡狩而朝會祭告之
樂歌也其意若謂非武無以定天下徒武無以
致太平彼當陳師牧野之時固嘗稱干而比戈
矣今朝會一行而諸侯聽命干戈其可以弗戢
乎會兵孟津之日固嘗張弓而挾矢矣今祭告
一舉而百神受職弓矢其可以弗櫜乎於是大
開明堂渙頒號令意以干戈雖堅且利也自今
punctuated:
黃佐

同考試官教諭莊批：「寫出武王偃武之意，宛在目，宜錄之以式學者。」

同考試官教諭江批：「作此題者，多不就巡狩上說，且綴緝陳語，可厭。晚得此篇，形容武王巡狩偃武之意，親切可愛，宜冠本房。」

考試官學正何批：「詞贍氣充，必有學之士也，允宜高薦。」

考試官教授劉批：「得頌體。」

王者巡狩而藏乎武備，正欲以偃乎武事也。蓋用武非聖人之得已也。周王巡狩而欲偃武焉，武備安得而不藏之哉？此巡狩而朝會祭告之樂歌也。其意若謂：非武無以定天下，徒武無以致太平。彼當陳師牧野之時，固嘗稱干而比戈矣。今朝會一行，而諸侯聽命，干戈其可以弗戢乎？會兵孟津之日，固嘗張弓而挾矢矣。今祭告一舉，而百神受職，弓矢其可以弗櫜乎？於是大開明堂，渙頒號令，意以干戈雖堅且利也，自今
translation_en:
Huang Zuo 黃佐

Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor, comments: “It brings King Wu’s intention to lay aside warfare vividly before our eyes. It should be included as a model for students.”

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Most who wrote on this topic did not explain it in terms of the royal inspection tour. Moreover, they stitched together stale phrases, which was tiresome. At last I came upon this essay: its portrayal of King Wu’s intention to lay aside warfare during his inspection tour is apt and pleasing. It deserves first place among the papers in this examining room.”

Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: “Its language is ample and its spirit full. The author must be a man of learning and certainly deserves a high recommendation.”

Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “It captures the form of the hymn.”

When a king makes an inspection tour and stores away his military equipment, his very purpose is to bring warfare to an end. For the sage resorts to arms only when he has no alternative. Since the king of Zhou wished to lay aside warfare on his inspection tour, how could he fail to store away his military equipment? This is the ritual song for the court assemblies and sacrificial announcements held during that tour. Its meaning seems to be this: without military force, the realm cannot be pacified; through military force alone, supreme peace cannot be achieved. When he arrayed his army at Muye, he had indeed raised shields and aligned dagger-axes. Now, with a court assembly held and the feudal lords obeying his commands, could the shields and dagger-axes remain unstored? On the day he assembled his troops at Mengjin, he had indeed drawn bows and grasped arrows. Now, with the sacrificial announcements performed and the hundred spirits receiving their appointed duties, could the bows and arrows remain unbagged? Thereupon he opened wide the Hall of Enlightenment and issued commands far and wide, conveying this intention: although shields and dagger-axes are sturdy and sharp, from now on…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以始藏諸府庫毋復稱之比之以擾吾民弓矢
雖強且鈞也自是而後抗諸鞬服勿復張焉挾
焉以方吾命干戈戢之非於鑠之師終於弛而
弗張誠以大統旣集尚文不尚武也於此不戢
則武流於黷矣何以慰商民之宿望哉弓矢櫜
之非虎賁之士恃其安而忘危誠以四海旣清
耀德不耀兵也於此不櫜則兵幾於窮矣何以
昭我周之新命哉吁用武於天下未平之初固
王者之大義偃武於天下旣平之後尤王者之
===
至仁仁義並行文教斯舉此武王所以為受命
之聖君也天其不子之乎大抵事有定理兵無
常形時乎用則用時乎藏則藏聖人何容心於
其間哉一於用秦皇之黷武也一於藏晉武之
銷兵也之二君者胥失之矣乃若唐之太宗比
迹湯武其庶幾乎惜夫殿廷非習射之所也噫
武王其盡美者耶
春秋
荆人來聘莊公二十三年
punctuated:
以始，藏諸府庫，毋復稱之比之，以擾吾民。弓矢雖強且鈞也，自是而後，抗諸鞬服，勿復張焉挾焉，以方吾命。干戈戢之，非於鑠之師終於弛而弗張，誠以大統旣集，尚文不尚武也。於此不戢，則武流於黷矣，何以慰商民之宿望哉？弓矢櫜之，非虎賁之士恃其安而忘危，誠以四海旣清，耀德不耀兵也。於此不櫜，則兵幾於窮矣，何以昭我周之新命哉？吁！用武於天下未平之初，固王者之大義；偃武於天下旣平之後，尤王者之至仁。仁義並行，文教斯舉，此武王所以為受命之聖君也。天其不子之乎？大抵事有定理，兵無常形。時乎用則用，時乎藏則藏，聖人何容心於其間哉？一於用，秦皇之黷武也；一於藏，晉武之銷兵也。之二君者，胥失之矣。乃若唐之太宗，比迹湯武，其庶幾乎？惜夫！殿廷非習射之所也。噫！武王其盡美者耶？

春秋

荆人來聘。莊公二十三年。
translation_en:
…from this time onward, store them in the government treasuries and arsenals. No longer raise the shields or array the spears to disturb my people. Though the bows and arrows are strong and well matched, henceforth put them away in their cases and quivers; no longer draw the bows or carry the arrows in defiance of my command.

Putting away shields and spears does not mean that the glorious army is ultimately to become slack and never again be marshalled. Rather, now that the great succession to rule has been secured, civil culture is to be esteemed above military force. If weapons are not put away at this point, warfare will degenerate into wanton aggression. How could this satisfy the longstanding hopes of the people of Shang? Encasing bows and arrows does not mean that the brave warriors rely on their security and forget danger. Rather, now that all within the Four Seas is pacified, virtue is to be displayed, rather than arms. If weapons are not encased at this point, military force will verge on reckless overuse. How could this make manifest the new mandate of our Zhou?

Ah! To employ military force at the outset, when the realm is not yet pacified, is indeed the great righteousness of a true king; to lay down arms afterward, when the realm has been pacified, is especially the consummate benevolence of a true king. With benevolence and righteousness proceeding together, civil instruction flourishes. This is why King Wu was a sage ruler who received Heaven’s mandate. Would Heaven not cherish him as its son?

Generally speaking, affairs have fixed principles, but warfare has no constant configuration. When the time calls for employing arms, employ them; when it calls for storing them away, store them away. How could the sage interpose his own preconceptions? To insist solely on employing arms is the First Emperor of Qin’s wanton militarism; to insist solely on storing them away is Emperor Wu of Jin’s abolition of arms. Both these rulers erred. As for Emperor Taizong of Tang, whose deeds bear comparison with those of Tang and Wu, did he not come close? What a pity that the palace court was no place to practise archery! Ah! Was King Wu not perfect in every respect?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“A man of Jing came on a diplomatic visit.” The twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
盧金潤
考試官學正何批春秋義謹嚴如此作者絕少
考試官教授劉批題本胡傳作者體認欠真下筆多牽滯此作明白簡瑩是用錄出
春秋於外交內而進之嘉其事之善而原其類
之善也此荆之聘魯遂以人稱聖人樂與人為
善而重絕人之意寓焉且荆楚嘗僭號不臣矣
又嘗猾夏不恭矣春秋狄之宜也今而遣使聘
魯遂以人稱所謂謹華夷之辨內夏外夷義安
===
在乎蓋中國諸侯之事朝聘之禮為重也荆楚
一旦革其固陋求以自通駟牡之駕不遠千里
玉帛之將恭奠兩觀禽父之澤慰於仰止者不
少禮樂之化得於觀感者必多非如入蔡伐鄭
狼貪蠶食亂我中華之無厭也借曰假禮行詐
不可測焉聖人樂與人為善不追其既往不逆
其將來與其潔而與其進以是心至斯受之矣
况先王封建之國聖賢之後不遺也荆楚上世
祝融垂裕熊繹襲封苗裔之昌延於百世茅土
punctuated:
盧金潤

考試官學正何批：春秋義謹嚴如此，作者絕少。

考試官教授劉批：題本胡傳，作者體認欠真，下筆多牽滯。此作明白簡瑩，是用錄出。

春秋於外交內而進之，嘉其事之善，而原其類之善也。此荆之聘魯，遂以人稱，聖人樂與人為善而重絕人之意寓焉。且荆楚嘗僭號不臣矣，又嘗猾夏不恭矣，春秋狄之宜也。今而遣使聘魯，遂以人稱，所謂謹華夷之辨，內夏外夷，義安在乎？蓋中國諸侯之事，朝聘之禮為重也。荆楚一旦革其固陋，求以自通，駟牡之駕不遠千里，玉帛之將恭奠兩觀，禽父之澤慰於仰止者不少，禮樂之化得於觀感者必多，非如入蔡伐鄭，狼貪蠶食，亂我中華之無厭也。借曰假禮行詐，不可測焉，聖人樂與人為善，不追其既往，不逆其將來，與其潔而與其進，以是心至，斯受之矣。况先王封建之國，聖賢之後不遺也。荆楚上世，祝融垂裕，熊繹襲封，苗裔之昌延於百世，茅土
translation_en:
Lu Jinrun

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: Essays on the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals as scrupulous and rigorous as this are exceedingly rare.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Prefectural School Professor: The topic is based on Hu’s Commentary. Writers often fail to grasp its meaning accurately, and their writing becomes strained and impeded. This essay is clear, concise, and polished; hence its selection for inclusion.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals admits an outside state into the inner circle and advances its standing, it commends the goodness of its actions and traces the goodness of its lineage. Here, when Jing paid a diplomatic visit to Lu, it was accordingly designated by the term “men.” This embodies the Sage’s willingness to help others do good and his reluctance to cut them off. Now Jing-Chu had previously usurped a royal title and refused allegiance; it had also disturbed the Xia states and behaved disrespectfully. It was fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should treat it as barbarian. Yet now, upon its sending an envoy to visit Lu, it was designated by the term “men.” Where, then, is the principle of carefully distinguishing Hua from Yi, treating the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders?

Among the affairs of the feudal lords of the central states, the rites of court attendance and diplomatic visits carry great weight. Once Jing-Chu reformed its entrenched ignorance and sought to establish relations, its carriages drawn by teams of four stallions did not shrink from traveling a thousand li. Its offerings of jade and silk were respectfully presented at the two gate towers. Not a few who looked up in reverence found solace in the enduring beneficence of Qinfu; surely many gained something of the transforming influence of rites and music through observing them and being moved by them. This was unlike entering Cai and attacking Zheng, ravenously seizing and steadily encroaching, insatiably bringing disorder to our central states.

Suppose it were said that Jing-Chu was using ritual as a pretext for deceit, and that its intentions could not be fathomed. The Sage delights in helping others do good. He does not pursue their past faults or anticipate their future conduct. He approves their purification and their advancement: if they come with this intention, he receives them.

Moreover, among the states enfeoffed by the former kings, the descendants of sages and worthies were not left out. Among the remote ancestors of Jing-Chu, Zhurong bequeathed blessings to posterity, and Xiong Yi inherited an enfeoffment. Their descendants flourished through a hundred generations; the thatch and earth of enfeoffment…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之承列於五等元德顯功通于周室者未泯衣
裳冠帶視之百辟也何殊豈若西戎北狄狼子
野心非我族類之可比也借曰以夷變夏方且
膺之然聖人猶不欲絕其類不使與中國同不
使與夷狄均推可遠而引可來苟可善焉斯進
之矣故特書曰荆人來聘傳曰嘉其慕義自通
故進之也又曰諸夏之變於夷者故書法如此
聖人宅心忠恕於茲不具見乎雖然聖人宅心
雖恕而立法則嚴後世之君能以聖人之心為
===
心則與天地相似凡變於夷者叛則懲其不恪
而威之以刑來則嘉其慕義而接之以禮邇人
安遠者服矣噫春秋所以為天子之事百王之
法度萬世之準繩也歟
盟于召陵僖公四年公會齊侯宋公陳侯衞
侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城 諸侯遂救許僖
公六年
李卿
考試官學正何 批體貼傳意辭不費而意自
punctuated:
之承，列於五等；元德顯功通于周室者未泯。衣裳冠帶，視之百辟也何殊？豈若西戎北狄，狼子野心，非我族類之可比也？借曰以夷變夏，方且膺之，然聖人猶不欲絕其類，不使與中國同，不使與夷狄均。推可遠而引可來，苟可善焉，斯進之矣。故特書曰：「荆人來聘。」傳曰：「嘉其慕義自通，故進之也。」又曰：「諸夏之變於夷者。」故書法如此。聖人宅心忠恕，於茲不具見乎？雖然，聖人宅心雖恕，而立法則嚴。後世之君能以聖人之心為心，則與天地相似。凡變於夷者，叛則懲其不恪，而威之以刑；來則嘉其慕義，而接之以禮。邇人安，遠者服矣。噫！《春秋》所以為天子之事，百王之法度，萬世之準繩也歟！

盟于召陵，僖公四年。公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衞侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。諸侯遂救許，僖公六年。

李卿

考試官學正何批：體貼傳意，辭不費而意自
translation_en:
…their succession to the enfeoffment placed them among the five ranks of nobility; the great virtue and illustrious achievements that linked them to the royal house of Zhou had not been forgotten. In their robes, caps, and girdles, how did they differ from the other lords? How could they be compared with the Western Rong and Northern Di, whose hearts were wild as wolf cubs and who were not of our kind? Granted that they had transformed Xia ways into those of the barbarians and were therefore to be resisted, the Sage still did not wish to cut off their kind. He neither accorded them the same standing as the central states nor ranked them equally with the barbarians. They could be pushed away or drawn near; if they could become good, he would advance them.

Thus he specifically wrote: “A man of Jing came on a diplomatic visit.” The Commentary says: “He commended their admiration for righteousness and their initiative in establishing relations, and therefore advanced them.” It also says: “Those among the Xia states who had changed to barbarian ways.” Hence this manner of recording the event. Is the Sage’s disposition of conscientiousness and sympathetic understanding not fully apparent here? Nevertheless, although the Sage was sympathetic in his heart, he was strict in establishing standards. If rulers of later ages could make the Sage’s heart their own, they would resemble Heaven and Earth. Whenever those who had adopted barbarian ways rebelled, they would punish their irreverence and overawe them with penalties; when they came, they would commend their admiration for righteousness and receive them with ritual propriety. Those nearby would be secure, and those far away would submit. Ah! Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals constitutes the business of the Son of Heaven, the standard for all kings, and the measure for all ages?

“They made a covenant at Shaoling.” Fourth year of Duke Xi. “The Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng and besieging Xincheng.” “The feudal lords then went to the aid of Xu.” Sixth year of Duke Xi.

Li Qing.

Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: “It closely captures the meaning of the Commentary; the wording is economical, while the meaning itself…”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
足蓋甞精於是經者
考試官敎授劉批說出聖人與桓之意整嚴
可觀讀之令人起敬
春秋旣予伯主得用師待敵之道尤予伯主得
討罪恤患之義此見齊桓召陵之師討鄭救許
之事所以爲善也且夫盟者諸侯之所不得爲
也春秋於齊桓召陵之盟何以予之耶蓋自荆
楚伐鄭其勢浸强于時齊桓主伯志在攘夷八
國南征楚人畏懾若可乘勝一鼓而直搗其墟
===
矣桓則以爲大兵之後狃於一勝而不知止如
萬全之道何楚人悔禍屈完請成若可以俘執
軍門而釁之鼓矣桓則以爲敵旣來歸不招之
以禮而一其心如柔遠之道何於是載戢干戈
而退舍召陵之地載敦玉帛而徼惠屈完之盟
於此見師雖强桓公能以律用之而不暴楚已
服桓公能以禮下之而不驕庶幾王者之師矣
春秋書盟于召陵于次陘之下傳曰序桓績也
聖人予桓之意明矣至若兵者聖人之所甚重
punctuated:
足，蓋甞精於是經者。
考試官敎授劉批：說出聖人與桓之意，整嚴可觀，讀之令人起敬。
春秋旣予伯主得用師待敵之道，尤予伯主得討罪恤患之義。此見齊桓召陵之師、討鄭救許之事所以爲善也。且夫盟者，諸侯之所不得爲也。春秋於齊桓召陵之盟，何以予之耶？蓋自荆楚伐鄭，其勢浸强。于時齊桓主伯，志在攘夷，八國南征，楚人畏懾，若可乘勝一鼓而直搗其墟矣。桓則以爲，大兵之後，狃於一勝而不知止，如萬全之道何？楚人悔禍，屈完請成，若可以俘執軍門而釁之鼓矣。桓則以爲，敵旣來歸，不招之以禮而一其心，如柔遠之道何？於是載戢干戈，而退舍召陵之地；載敦玉帛，而徼惠屈完之盟。於此見師雖强，桓公能以律用之而不暴；楚已服，桓公能以禮下之而不驕，庶幾王者之師矣。春秋書盟于召陵于次陘之下，傳曰：「序桓績也。」聖人予桓之意明矣。至若兵者，聖人之所甚重
translation_en:
…complete in meaning; surely he has studied this Classic deeply.
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It brings out the Sage’s intention in approving Duke Huan. Orderly and rigorous, it merits admiration; reading it inspires respect.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals approves the hegemon’s grasp of the proper way to employ armies and deal with enemies, and especially approves his understanding of the righteousness of punishing wrongdoing and relieving distress. This shows why Duke Huan of Qi’s expedition to Shaoling and his actions in attacking Zheng and rescuing Xu were good. Now, making covenants was something the feudal lords were not entitled to do. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve Duke Huan of Qi’s covenant at Shaoling? Since Jing-Chu had attacked Zheng, its power had gradually grown. At that time Duke Huan of Qi held the hegemony and aimed to repel the barbarians. The forces of eight states marched south, and the people of Chu were terrified. It seemed that he could exploit his advantage, advance at a single beating of the drums, and strike directly at their capital. Yet Huan reasoned: after a great military expedition, if one grew complacent over a single victory and did not know when to stop, what would become of the principle of ensuring complete security? The people of Chu regretted having brought calamity upon themselves, and Qu Wan requested peace. It seemed that Huan could seize him at the army’s gate and smear his blood upon the drums. Yet Huan reasoned: when an enemy has come to submit, if one does not receive him with ritual propriety and thereby secure his wholehearted allegiance, what would become of the way of conciliating distant peoples? Thus he put away his weapons and withdrew to encamp at Shaoling; he made generous offerings of jade and silk and sought the favor of a covenant with Qu Wan. Here we see that, although his army was strong, Duke Huan could employ it with discipline and without brutality; although Chu had submitted, he could treat it with ritual humility and without arrogance. His army thus came close to being that of a true king. The Spring and Autumn Annals records “made a covenant at Shaoling” after “encamped at Xing.” The Commentary says: “This sets forth Huan’s achievements.” The Sage’s intention in approving Huan is clear. As for warfare, it is something to which the Sage attached the utmost importance…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也春秋於齊桓伐鄭救許之師何以予之耶蓋
自鄭與楚合首止逃盟是時齊桓憂之急於討
貳兵連六國執詞伐鄭宜若振槁然桓則以為
好攻樂殺於罪為大是可忍心為之哉許受楚
攻朝不保暮宜若倒懸然桓則以為救患分災
於禮為急是可坐視不為哉於是寧遺力而不
逞新城之下即解兵而遠赴許人之圍於此見
鄭可討桓公以義討之而不暴許可救桓公以
義救之而不緩庶幾君子之道矣春秋書救許
===
於伐鄭圍新城之下傳曰善之尤也聖人予桓
之心亦著矣吁盟非美事而召陵之盟在春秋
所宜有兵本凶器而伐鄭救許之兵在春秋不
可無然則聖人之予之豈得已耶大抵伯者莫
難於立功功既成則其志驕志驕則其行荒行
荒則其業怠故陽穀之會于卞之會肆於寵樂
緣陵之城于匡之次楚之伐黃狄之侵衛忽於
簡書而視召陵之盟救許之兵不可同日語矣
先儒謂其量淺而器不宏又曰假之不久而遽
punctuated:
也。春秋於齊桓伐鄭救許之師，何以予之耶？蓋自鄭與楚合，首止逃盟，是時齊桓憂之，急於討貳，兵連六國，執詞伐鄭，宜若振槁。然桓則以為好攻樂殺，於罪為大，是可忍心為之哉？許受楚攻，朝不保暮，宜若倒懸。然桓則以為救患分災，於禮為急，是可坐視不為哉？於是寧遺力而不逞新城之下，即解兵而遠赴許人之圍。於此見鄭可討，桓公以義討之而不暴；許可救，桓公以義救之而不緩，庶幾君子之道矣。春秋書救許於伐鄭圍新城之下，傳曰：「善之尤也。」聖人予桓之心亦著矣。
吁！盟非美事，而召陵之盟在春秋所宜有；兵本凶器，而伐鄭救許之兵在春秋不可無。然則聖人之予之，豈得已耶？大抵伯者莫難於立功，功既成則其志驕，志驕則其行荒，行荒則其業怠。故陽穀之會、于卞之會，肆於寵樂；緣陵之城、于匡之次、楚之伐黃、狄之侵衛，忽於簡書，而視召陵之盟、救許之兵，不可同日語矣。先儒謂其量淺而器不宏，又曰：「假之不久而遽
translation_en:
… Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve of Duke Huan of Qi’s campaign against Zheng and his relief of Xu? After Zheng allied itself with Chu and evaded the covenant at Shouzhi, Duke Huan of Qi became troubled and urgently sought to punish its disloyalty. Joining the forces of six states, he advanced against Zheng with declared grounds for punishment; victory should have been as easy as shaking down withered leaves. Yet Duke Huan considered delight in aggression and killing to be among the gravest offenses: could he harden his heart and do such a thing? Under attack from Chu, Xu could not be certain in the morning of surviving until evening; its plight was like that of someone hanging upside down. Yet Duke Huan considered rescuing those in distress and sharing the burden of calamity to be urgent obligations of ritual propriety: could he sit by and do nothing? Thus he preferred to leave his strength unspent rather than press his advantage beneath the walls of Xincheng. He immediately lifted the siege and marched far away to relieve the people of Xu. Here we see that, when Zheng deserved punishment, Duke Huan punished it in accordance with righteousness, without brutality; when Xu deserved rescue, he rescued it in accordance with righteousness, without delay. He came close to the way of the gentleman. The Spring and Autumn Annals records the relief of Xu after the attack on Zheng and the siege of Xincheng. The commentary says: “This was an especially commendable deed.” The sage’s intention to approve of Duke Huan is thus also manifest.
Ah! Covenant-making is no fine thing, yet the covenant at Shaoling was fitting in the circumstances of the Spring and Autumn period. Weapons are inherently instruments of ill omen, yet the campaign against Zheng and the relief of Xu were indispensable in that age. Could the sage, then, have withheld his approval? Generally, nothing is harder for a hegemon than establishing achievements. Once his achievements are secured, his resolve grows arrogant; arrogance leads to dissolute conduct, and dissolute conduct leads to neglect of his undertaking. Thus, at the meetings at Yanggu and Bian, he indulged in favored companions and pleasures; in the walling of Yuanling, the encampment at Kuang, Chu’s attack on Huang, and the Di invasion of Wei, he neglected the obligations conveyed by written summons. These deeds cannot be spoken of in the same breath as the covenant at Shaoling and the relief of Xu. Earlier Confucian scholars said that his capacity was shallow and his caliber limited. They also said: “He borrowed it only briefly, and then abruptly …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
歸是足以槩桓之顛末矣使其慎終如始而敦
不息之誠則進於王德而不爲聖門之所不道
也
禮記
樂者爲同禮者爲異同則相親異則相敬
樂勝則流禮勝則離合情飾貌者禮樂
之事也禮義立則貴賤等矣樂文同則
上下和矣好惡著則賢不肖别矣刑禁
暴爵舉賢則政均矣仁以愛之義以正
===
之如此則民治行矣
葉孟
同考試官教諭林批說先王用禮樂治民情及民
治行處前後照應明白是宜錄之以式學者
考試官學正何批理明詞順
考試官教授劉批得旨
禮樂異其用而民心所由感禮樂濟其偏而民
化所由成夫禮樂之足以感民也尚矣但不能
無偏勝之弊耳偏而能濟化豈有不成哉且先
punctuated:
歸，是足以槩桓之顛末矣。使其慎終如始，而敦不息之誠，則進於王德，而不爲聖門之所不道也。

禮記
樂者爲同，禮者爲異。同則相親，異則相敬。樂勝則流，禮勝則離。合情飾貌者，禮樂之事也。禮義立，則貴賤等矣；樂文同，則上下和矣；好惡著，則賢不肖别矣；刑禁暴，爵舉賢，則政均矣。仁以愛之，義以正之，如此則民治行矣。

葉孟

同考試官教諭林批：說先王用禮樂治民情及民治行處，前後照應明白，是宜錄之以式學者。
考試官學正何批：理明詞順。
考試官教授劉批：得旨。

禮樂異其用，而民心所由感；禮樂濟其偏，而民化所由成。夫禮樂之足以感民也尚矣，但不能無偏勝之弊耳。偏而能濟，化豈有不成哉？且先
translation_en:
…returned it. This suffices to sum up the course of Duke Huan’s career from beginning to end. Had he been as careful at the end as at the beginning, and cultivated unceasing sincerity, he would have advanced toward kingly virtue and would not have been someone whom the followers of the Sage declined to discuss.

Book of Rites
“Music creates unity; ritual establishes distinctions. Unity brings mutual affection; distinctions bring mutual respect. When music predominates, there is dissoluteness; when ritual predominates, there is estrangement. Harmonizing feelings and refining outward demeanor are the work of ritual and music. When the principles of ritual are established, the noble and the lowly have their proper ranks. When musical forms are shared, superiors and inferiors are in harmony. When approval and disapproval are made clear, the worthy are distinguished from the unworthy. When punishments restrain violence and ranks elevate the worthy, government is equitable. Love them through benevolence and set them right through righteousness: in this way, the ordering of the people is accomplished.”

Ye Meng 葉孟

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The discussion of how the former kings used ritual and music to regulate the people’s feelings clearly corresponds, from beginning to end, with the passage on accomplishing the ordering of the people. This deserves to be recorded as a model for students.”
Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: “Clear reasoning and fluent expression.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “Grasps the purport.”

Ritual and music differ in their functions, yet through them the people’s hearts are moved; ritual and music remedy each other’s imbalances, and through them the transformation of the people is accomplished. The power of ritual and music to move the people has long been recognized. Yet they cannot be free of the harm caused by the predominance of one over the other. If such imbalance can be remedied, how could the people’s transformation fail to be accomplished? Moreover, the former…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王因人情而作禮樂慮其乖而不同也則導以
樂之和而凡聲容節奏之翕然者皆所以統同
也慮其混而無異也則導以禮之序而凡儀文
度數之截然者皆所以辨異也唯統同則情敦
而雍睦之風作矣民不由之而相親乎唯辨異
則分定而侵陵之患息矣民不由之而相敬乎
夫禮樂之有以感民也固如此使樂過於同禮
過於異則偏勝而有流離之弊矣於此將何以
救之亦唯合情於內而救其離之失此樂以和
===
禮之事也飾貌於外而救其流之失此禮以節
樂之事也禮以節樂而禮之義以立則貴賤秩
然其有等矣樂以和禮而樂之文以同則上下
藹然其恊和矣賢否無別非所以輔禮樂也賢
者從而好之不肖者從而惡之而賢否曾有不
別乎政事不均非所以輔禮樂也暴者刑禁之
必及賢者爵舉之無遺而政事曾有不均乎然
猶未也仁以愛之使辨異之中一吾心之至誠
惻怛者存義以正之使統同之中一吾心之裁
punctuated: 王因人情而作禮樂，慮其乖而不同也，則導以樂之和，而凡聲容節奏之翕然者，皆所以統同也；慮其混而無異也，則導以禮之序，而凡儀文度數之截然者，皆所以辨異也。唯統同，則情敦而雍睦之風作矣，民不由之而相親乎？唯辨異，則分定而侵陵之患息矣，民不由之而相敬乎？夫禮樂之有以感民也，固如此。使樂過於同，禮過於異，則偏勝而有流離之弊矣。於此將何以救之？亦唯合情於內，而救其離之失，此樂以和禮之事也；飾貌於外，而救其流之失，此禮以節樂之事也。禮以節樂，而禮之義以立，則貴賤秩然其有等矣；樂以和禮，而樂之文以同，則上下藹然其恊和矣。賢否無別，非所以輔禮樂也；賢者從而好之，不肖者從而惡之，而賢否曾有不別乎？政事不均，非所以輔禮樂也；暴者刑禁之必及，賢者爵舉之無遺，而政事曾有不均乎？然猶未也。仁以愛之，使辨異之中一吾心之至誠惻怛者存；義以正之，使統同之中一吾心之裁
translation_en:
…the former kings created rites and music in accordance with human feelings. Concerned that people might diverge and lack unity, they guided them through the harmony of music: its blended sounds, movements, rhythms, and cadences all served to bring them into unity. Concerned that people might mingle without distinctions, they guided them through the ordering of rites: their clearly delineated ceremonial forms, measures, and regulations all served to distinguish differences. Through unity, feelings grow sincere and a spirit of concord arises. Would the people not thereby become affectionate toward one another? Through distinctions, social stations become settled and the trouble caused by encroachment and oppression ceases. Would the people not thereby respect one another?

Such indeed is the power of rites and music to move the people. Yet if music goes too far toward sameness, and rites too far toward differentiation, one prevails excessively, producing the faults of unrestrained indulgence and estrangement. How, then, can these be remedied? Simply by uniting feelings within and correcting estrangement: this is music's work of harmonizing rites. By giving outward bearing its proper form and correcting unrestrained indulgence: this is the work of rites in regulating music. When rites regulate music and the proper principles of rites are established, the noble and the lowly are orderly in their respective ranks. When music harmonizes rites and its patterned expression brings unity, superiors and inferiors are warmly concordant.

Failing to distinguish the worthy from the unworthy does nothing to support rites and music. If one accordingly cherishes the worthy and abhors the unworthy, how could worthiness and unworthiness remain undistinguished? Inequitable government likewise does nothing to support rites and music. If punishments and prohibitions unfailingly reach the violent, and none of the worthy is overlooked in the bestowal of rank and advancement, how could government be inequitable? Yet this is still not enough. Love them through benevolence, so that, amid the distinguishing of differences, the wholehearted sincerity and compassion of one's heart remain present; set them right through righteousness, so that, amid the bringing of unity, one's heart's capacity to judge…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
割斷制者在此又以仁義爲禮樂之輔也夫然
則所以救其偏弊者亦無不至矣自是民之漸
被於禮樂者同焉能異自相親而不至於流異
焉能同自相敬而不至於離民治豈有不行哉
至是則化成矣抑先王之作禮樂也效法天地
而又有和敬之德以爲之本故推之於治宜乎
民無不化矣豈唯民化而已哉位天地育萬物
要皆此禮樂之所爲也後世人君不務出此往
往因陋就簡以圖一時之近功耳宋儒歐陽氏
===
有曰三代而上治出於一而禮樂達于天下三
代而下治出於二而禮樂爲虛名者此之謂也
爲治者盍亦知所務哉
故君子與其使食浮於人也寧使人浮於
食
葉孟
同考試官教諭林批寫出君子耻食浮之意儘
是親切他日見用殆非竊禄者矣
考試官學正何批明鬯
punctuated:
割斷制者在，此又以仁義爲禮樂之輔也。夫然，則所以救其偏弊者亦無不至矣。自是民之漸被於禮樂者，同焉能異，自相親而不至於流；異焉能同，自相敬而不至於離。民治豈有不行哉？至是則化成矣。抑先王之作禮樂也，效法天地，而又有和敬之德以爲之本，故推之於治，宜乎民無不化矣。豈唯民化而已哉？位天地，育萬物，要皆此禮樂之所爲也。後世人君不務出此，往往因陋就簡，以圖一時之近功耳。宋儒歐陽氏有曰：「三代而上，治出於一，而禮樂達于天下；三代而下，治出於二，而禮樂爲虛名。」者，此之謂也。爲治者盍亦知所務哉？

故君子與其使食浮於人也，寧使人浮於食。

葉孟

同考試官教諭林批：寫出君子耻食浮之意，儘是親切。他日見用，殆非竊禄者矣。

考試官學正何批：明鬯。
translation_en:
…the capacity of my heart to discriminate and decide remains present. This, too, is to use benevolence and righteousness to support rites and music. Thus every means of remedying their one-sided tendencies and attendant failings is fully employed. Henceforth, as the people gradually come under the influence of rites and music, they can retain distinctions within their unity: they naturally feel affection for one another without lapsing into excess. They can maintain unity within their distinctions: they naturally respect one another without becoming estranged. How could good government of the people fail to take effect? At this point, their moral transformation is complete. Moreover, in creating rites and music, the former kings took Heaven and Earth as their models and grounded their work in the virtues of harmony and reverence. When these were extended to government, it was fitting that no one among the people should remain untransformed. Yet was this merely a matter of transforming the people? Giving Heaven and Earth their proper places and nourishing the myriad things are, in essence, all accomplished through these rites and music. Rulers of later ages have not endeavored to follow this course. They have often made do with crude and inadequate arrangements, seeking only immediate results for the moment. The Song Confucian scholar Ouyang said: “During the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm; after the Three Dynasties, government issued from two sources, and rites and music became empty names.” This is what he meant. Should those who govern not also understand where to direct their efforts?

“Thus, rather than allow his emoluments to exceed his worth, the gentleman prefers that his worth exceed his emoluments.”

Ye Meng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “He expresses the gentleman’s sense of shame at receiving emoluments beyond his worth, and does so with great aptness and immediacy. If appointed to office in the future, he will surely not be one who draws a salary without earning it.”

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “Clear and lucid.”

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授劉批文理通暢
君子之仕也不欲厚其所受於君者唯欲厚其
所事於君者夫事君之才德薄而受祿厚則其
仕也苟祿耳曾謂君子而肯爲此哉夫子之言
如此其意謂夫古之君子未嘗不欲仕而其仕
也亦曷嘗以苟祿爲哉彼如才僅可以爲士而
君以大夫之祿予之德僅可以爲大夫而君以
公卿之祿予之則食浮於人矣人情於此孰不
利之君子必曰君之所以祿我者如此固足以
===
自富矣報踰其分獨不有負於君乎賞過其功
獨不有愧於己乎與其受之而使食浮於人不
若辭之而使人浮於食也如德可以爲公卿而
但受大夫之祿德可以爲大夫而但受士之祿
則人浮於食矣人情於此雖若不堪君子必曰
君之所以祿我者如此亦足以代耕矣吾唯盡
其職耳位不滿其德何計哉吾唯敬其事耳祿
不稱其功何恤哉君子之仕如此則其受於君
者薄而事於君者厚所謂辭貴不辭賤辭富不
punctuated:
考試官教授劉批：文理通暢。

君子之仕也，不欲厚其所受於君者，唯欲厚其所事於君者。夫事君之才德薄而受祿厚，則其仕也苟祿耳，曾謂君子而肯爲此哉？夫子之言如此，其意謂夫古之君子未嘗不欲仕，而其仕也亦曷嘗以苟祿爲哉？彼如才僅可以爲士，而君以大夫之祿予之；德僅可以爲大夫，而君以公卿之祿予之，則食浮於人矣。人情於此，孰不利之？君子必曰：「君之所以祿我者如此，固足以自富矣。報踰其分，獨不有負於君乎？賞過其功，獨不有愧於己乎？」與其受之而使食浮於人，不若辭之而使人浮於食也。如德可以爲公卿，而但受大夫之祿；德可以爲大夫，而但受士之祿，則人浮於食矣。人情於此，雖若不堪，君子必曰：「君之所以祿我者如此，亦足以代耕矣。吾唯盡其職耳，位不滿其德，何計哉？吾唯敬其事耳，祿不稱其功，何恤哉？」君子之仕如此，則其受於君者薄，而事於君者厚。所謂辭貴不辭賤，辭富不
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The writing and reasoning are coherent and fluent.

When a gentleman serves in office, he does not seek abundant rewards from his ruler; he seeks only to render abundant service to him. If his ability and virtue in serving the ruler are meager, yet his emolument is generous, his holding office amounts merely to drawing an unearned stipend. Could anyone called a gentleman consent to this? Such are the Master's words. Their meaning is that gentlemen of antiquity certainly wished to hold office, but when did they ever do so merely to draw an unearned stipend? If a man's ability qualifies him only to be a serviceman, yet the ruler grants him the emolument of a grand master, or his virtue qualifies him only to be a grand master, yet the ruler grants him the emolument of a duke or minister, then his emolument exceeds his worth. Who, following ordinary human inclinations, would not regard this as advantageous? The gentleman, however, will surely say: “The emolument my ruler grants me is certainly sufficient to enrich me. But if my recompense exceeds my due, would I not be failing my ruler? If my reward exceeds my achievement, would I not feel ashamed before myself?” Rather than accept it and let his emolument exceed his worth, he would decline it and let his worth exceed his emolument. If his virtue qualifies him to be a duke or minister, yet he receives only a grand master's emolument, or his virtue qualifies him to be a grand master, yet he receives only a serviceman's emolument, then his worth exceeds his emolument. Although ordinary human feelings might find this intolerable, the gentleman will surely say: “The emolument my ruler grants me is still sufficient to provide a livelihood in place of farming. I seek only to discharge my duties. Why concern myself if my rank falls short of my virtue? I seek only to attend respectfully to my work. Why worry if my emolument does not match my achievement?” When a gentleman serves in this way, what he receives from his ruler is meager, while the service he renders is abundant. This is what is meant by declining high station but not low station, declining wealth but not…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
辭貧者在是矣政事豈有不脩而風俗豈有不
美哉大抵三代以前君之爵人也唯恐不得其
人臣之受命也唯恐不稱其職故有虞咨岳命
官當時在廷之臣類皆推賢讓能而不敢直以
爲已任也世降春秋儋爵食祿者不過藉此以
媒富貴耳辭富貴而寧處貧賤者幾何此所以
爭奪之禍作矣噫夫子言此其亦有所感也夫
第貳場
論
===
聖人之道猶天然
馮徽
同考試官訓導陳批論題正大士子類能道之
但多模擬形似而無親切意味令人厭觀晚得此
篇議論平妥而理致明白决非疎淺之學所能到
也是用錄出
同考試官訓導楊批議論層出而抑揚中度非
老於文學者不能爲也健羨健羨
考試官學正何批文思清潤而氣象悠揚若
punctuated:
辭貧者在是矣。政事豈有不脩，而風俗豈有不美哉？大抵三代以前，君之爵人也，唯恐不得其人；臣之受命也，唯恐不稱其職。故有虞咨岳命官，當時在廷之臣，類皆推賢讓能，而不敢直以爲已任也。世降春秋，儋爵食祿者，不過藉此以媒富貴耳。辭富貴而寧處貧賤者幾何？此所以爭奪之禍作矣。噫！夫子言此，其亦有所感也夫！

第貳場
論

聖人之道猶天然
馮徽

同考試官訓導陳批：論題正大，士子類能道之，但多模擬形似，而無親切意味，令人厭觀。晚得此篇，議論平妥，而理致明白，决非疎淺之學所能到也，是用錄出。

同考試官訓導楊批：議論層出，而抑揚中度，非老於文學者不能爲也。健羨！健羨！

考試官學正何批：文思清潤，而氣象悠揚，若
translation_en:
…declining poverty: herein lies the principle. How could government affairs fail to be well ordered, or customs fail to improve? Generally, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, when rulers conferred rank, their sole fear was that they might not find the right men; when ministers accepted appointments, their sole fear was that they might not be equal to their duties. Thus, when the ruler of Yu consulted the Four Mountains and appointed officials, the ministers then at court generally recommended the worthy and deferred to the capable, not daring simply to regard the responsibility as their own. As the ages declined into the Spring and Autumn period, those who held rank and drew stipends merely used these to procure wealth and eminence. How many declined wealth and eminence and preferred to remain poor and lowly? This is why the calamities of contention and rivalry arose. Alas! When the Master said this, he surely had something that moved him to speak!

Second Session
Discourse

The Way of the Sage Is Like Heaven
Feng Hui

Yet most merely imitate its outward form, without any meaning grounded in intimate understanding, making their essays tiresome to read. Late in the process I obtained this piece. Its arguments are balanced and appropriate, and its reasoning is lucid—certainly beyond the reach of superficial learning. I have therefore selected it for inclusion.
