title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不竟其說者可以占其中之所存矣
考試官教授劉批〔詞有根據作性理論當如是〕
道至聖人而止也論聖道而必擬諸天其善於
立言者矣何也道莫全於聖人也道以聖人而
全亦以聖人而止窮天下後世無以復加者也
自其跡觀之聖人亦天地間一人耳自其道論
之則聖人未始不爲天而天未始不爲聖人也
夫豈可以差殊觀之哉程子曰聖人之道猶天
然門弟子親炙而冀及之然後知其高且遠也
===
味斯言也程子不惟知聖人亦知天矣其善於
立言者歟且聖人之道何道也中庸率性之謂
也原於天命之正具於人心之微其體則仁義
禮智其用則喜怒哀樂其倫則父子君臣夫婦
長幼朋友其法則禮樂刑政其文則詩書易春
秋其爲道易明而其爲教易行也是道也人皆
有之而獨以聖人爲言者何哉蓋道之得於天
者雖同而其成於人者自異衆人有之而不知
賢者踐之而未盡聖人獨能盡之而無餘故舉
punctuated:
不竟其說者，可以占其中之所存矣。

考試官教授劉批〔詞有根據，作性理論當如是。〕

道至聖人而止也，論聖道而必擬諸天，其善於立言者矣。何也？道莫全於聖人也。道以聖人而全，亦以聖人而止，窮天下後世無以復加者也。自其跡觀之，聖人亦天地間一人耳；自其道論之，則聖人未始不爲天，而天未始不爲聖人也。夫豈可以差殊觀之哉？程子曰：「聖人之道猶天然，門弟子親炙而冀及之，然後知其高且遠也。」味斯言也，程子不惟知聖人，亦知天矣，其善於立言者歟！且聖人之道何道也？《中庸》率性之謂也。原於天命之正，具於人心之微，其體則仁義禮智，其用則喜怒哀樂，其倫則父子、君臣、夫婦、長幼、朋友，其法則禮樂刑政，其文則《詩》《書》《易》《春秋》，其爲道易明，而其爲教易行也。是道也，人皆有之，而獨以聖人爲言者何哉？蓋道之得於天者雖同，而其成於人者自異。衆人有之而不知，賢者踐之而未盡，聖人獨能盡之而無餘，故舉
translation_en:
…not exhausting what he has to say; from this one may discern what he holds within.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: 〔The wording has a firm basis. A discourse on human nature and principle should be written like this.〕

The Way reaches its culmination in the sage. To discuss the sagely Way and invariably compare it to Heaven is indeed to be skilled in formulating one's words. Why is this? Nowhere is the Way more complete than in the sage. Through the sage the Way attains completeness, and in the sage it also reaches its culmination: throughout the world and all subsequent ages, nothing can be added to it. Viewed through his outward deeds, the sage is merely one person between Heaven and Earth. Yet considered in terms of his Way, the sage has never been other than Heaven, nor has Heaven ever been other than the sage. How could they be regarded as different? Master Cheng said: “The Way of the sage is like Heaven. His disciples personally received his teaching and hoped to attain it; only then did they understand its height and remoteness.” Pondering these words, we see that Master Cheng understood not only the sage but Heaven as well. Was he not skilled in formulating his words!

Moreover, what Way is the Way of the sage? It is what the Doctrine of the Mean calls following one's nature. It originates in the rectitude of Heaven's mandate and is fully present in the subtle depths of the human mind. Its substance is benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom; its functioning is joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure. Its relationships are those between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends. Its institutions are ritual, music, punishments, and government. Its writings are the Book of Odes, Book of Documents, Book of Changes, and Spring and Autumn Annals. As a Way it is easy to understand, and as a teaching it is easy to put into practice. Everyone possesses this Way; why, then, speak of it only in terms of the sage? Although the Way received from Heaven is the same, its realization in human beings naturally differs. Ordinary people possess it but do not understand it; the worthy practice it but do not realize it fully. Only the sage can realize it completely, leaving nothing unfulfilled. Hence it is taken in its entirety…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而歸諸聖人也然聖人之道亦不過循其性之
自然盡其理之當然初非外此而別有所增益
也論聖道而必以天為言者何哉蓋天之所賦
於我者本如是其渾全也吾於是而偏曲之則
人矣而非天也本如是其博大也吾於是而狹
小之則人矣而非天也本如是其精純粹美也
吾於是而矯揉駁雜之則人矣而非天也聖人
於其所謂渾全者而渾全之博大者而博大之
精純粹美者而精純粹美之不偏曲也不狹小
===
也不矯揉駁雜也一全其天之本體而無虧焉
則善繼善述而克肖乎天矣克肖乎天者天固
天也聖人亦天也其道不亦高矣乎不亦遠矣
乎聖人之心亦非故欲為此高遠以絕人也蓋
其生也聖由天縱性本天成氣極其清質極其
粹所謂渾全者博大者純粹精美者自然凝聚
厥躬無少疵類無少間斷仁義禮智以立其體
喜怒哀樂以達其用父子君臣夫婦長幼朋友
以敦其倫禮樂刑政以立其法詩書易春秋以
punctuated: 而歸諸聖人也。然聖人之道，亦不過循其性之自然，盡其理之當然，初非外此而別有所增益也。論聖道而必以天為言者，何哉？蓋天之所賦於我者，本如是其渾全也，吾於是而偏曲之，則人矣，而非天也；本如是其博大也，吾於是而狹小之，則人矣，而非天也；本如是其精純粹美也，吾於是而矯揉駁雜之，則人矣，而非天也。聖人於其所謂渾全者而渾全之，博大者而博大之，精純粹美者而精純粹美之，不偏曲也，不狹小也，不矯揉駁雜也。一全其天之本體而無虧焉，則善繼善述而克肖乎天矣。克肖乎天者，天固天也，聖人亦天也。其道不亦高矣乎？不亦遠矣乎？聖人之心，亦非故欲為此高遠以絕人也。蓋其生也，聖由天縱，性本天成，氣極其清，質極其粹，所謂渾全者、博大者、純粹精美者，自然凝聚厥躬，無少疵類，無少間斷。仁義禮智以立其體，喜怒哀樂以達其用，父子君臣夫婦長幼朋友以敦其倫，禮樂刑政以立其法，詩書易春秋以
translation_en: …and attribute it to the sages. Yet the Way of the sages does no more than follow what is spontaneous in their nature and fully realize what its principles require; nothing additional is supplied from outside this. Why must discussion of the sages’ Way always invoke Heaven? What Heaven has endowed in us is originally so complete and undivided. If we make it partial and distorted, that is human doing, not Heaven. It is originally so broad and vast. If we narrow and diminish it, that is human doing, not Heaven. It is originally so refined, pure, and beautiful. If we force and adulterate it, that is human doing, not Heaven. The sages preserve the completeness of what is complete, the breadth of what is broad, and the refinement, purity, and beauty of what is refined, pure, and beautiful. They neither distort nor narrow it, nor force or adulterate it. By preserving wholly and without impairment the original substance bestowed by Heaven, they aptly carry it forward and perpetuate it, and thus fully resemble Heaven. When they fully resemble Heaven, Heaven is of course Heaven, but the sages too are Heaven. Is their Way not lofty? Is it not far-reaching? Nor do the sages deliberately seek such loftiness and remoteness in order to place themselves beyond other people’s reach. From birth, their sageliness is Heaven’s gift, their nature is formed by Heaven, their vital energy is supremely clear, and their constitution supremely pure. What is complete, broad, pure, refined, and beautiful naturally gathers within their persons, without the slightest blemish [?] or interruption. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom establish the substance of their Way; joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure give expression to its functioning. The relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends strengthen its human bonds. Rites, music, punishments, and governance establish its standards. The Odes, the Documents, the Changes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals serve to…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聞其文至於動靜語默之間食息起居之際無
一事而非道也無一事而非道則無一事而非
天矣故淪於卑者自見其道之高不可及也狃
於近者自見其道之遠不可卽也吾嘗合天與
聖人而觀之聖道之所謂一本者卽維天之命
於穆不已也聖道之所謂萬殊者卽乾道變化
各正性命也意必固我之絕無其太虛之明淨
乎仕止久速之適可其四時之錯行乎老者安
而少者懷一物各付物之妙也用則行而舍則
===
藏一盈虛消息之理也聖人之所以爲聖人者
如此是蓋靜與天游也動與天俱也易曰先天
而天弗違後天而奉天時朱子曰孔子其太極
邵子曰聖人與昊天爲一道皆此意也程子之
言其弗信矣乎抑非程子之言也夫子之不可
及也猶天之不可階而升也子貢嘗有是言矣
天何言哉四時行焉百物生焉吾夫子亦嘗以
天自謂矣惜乎當時門人默契此道者僅見顏
曾二子而已其他如子貢者無言之敎猶不能
punctuated:
聞其文。至於動靜語默之間，食息起居之際，無一事而非道也。無一事而非道，則無一事而非天矣。故淪於卑者，自見其道之高不可及也；狃於近者，自見其道之遠不可卽也。吾嘗合天與聖人而觀之：聖道之所謂一本者，卽維天之命，於穆不已也；聖道之所謂萬殊者，卽乾道變化，各正性命也。意必固我之絕無，其太虛之明淨乎？仕止久速之適可，其四時之錯行乎？老者安而少者懷，一物各付物之妙也；用則行而舍則藏，一盈虛消息之理也。聖人之所以爲聖人者如此，是蓋靜與天游也，動與天俱也。《易》曰：「先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。」朱子曰：「孔子其太極。」邵子曰：「聖人與昊天爲一道。」皆此意也。程子之言，其弗信矣乎？

抑非程子之言也。「夫子之不可及也，猶天之不可階而升也。」子貢嘗有是言矣。「天何言哉？四時行焉，百物生焉。」吾夫子亦嘗以天自謂矣。惜乎當時門人默契此道者，僅見顏、曾二子而已。其他如子貢者，無言之敎猶不能
translation_en:
…make his cultural refinement known [?]. In movement and stillness, speech and silence, eating and resting, rising and retiring, there is nothing that is not the Way. If nothing is other than the Way, then nothing is other than Heaven. Thus those sunk in lowliness themselves perceive the height of his Way as beyond their reach; those accustomed to what is near themselves perceive its remoteness as beyond their approach. I have considered Heaven and the sage together. What is called the single root of the sage’s Way is precisely this: “The mandate of Heaven—how profound and unceasing!” What are called its myriad differentiations are precisely this: “The Way of Qian transforms and changes, and each thing attains its proper nature and allotted existence.” His utter freedom from conjecture, insistence, obstinacy, and self-centeredness—is this not the clarity and purity of the Great Void? His perfect appropriateness in taking office or withdrawing, remaining long or departing promptly—is this not like the alternating course of the four seasons? Giving the old repose and cherishing the young embodies the same subtle working by which each thing is entrusted to itself. Acting when employed and withdrawing when set aside embodies the same principle of fullness and emptiness, waning and waxing. Such is what makes the sage a sage: in stillness he wanders with Heaven; in movement he accompanies Heaven. The Book of Changes says: “When he precedes Heaven, Heaven does not oppose him; when he follows Heaven, he accords with Heaven’s seasons.” Master Zhu said: “Confucius is surely the Supreme Ultimate.” Master Shao said: “The sage and August Heaven constitute a single Way.” All express this meaning. Can Master Cheng’s words, then, be disbelieved?

Yet these are not solely Master Cheng’s words. “The Master cannot be equaled, just as Heaven cannot be ascended by a stairway.” Zigong once said this. “What does Heaven say? The four seasons proceed, and the myriad things come into being.” Our Master, too, once spoke of himself by comparison with Heaven. Alas, among his disciples at that time, only Yan Hui and Zeng Shen appear to have tacitly grasped this Way. Others, such as Zigong, were still unable to comprehend the teaching without words …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
喻况其下者乎有隱之疑宜乎諸弟子所不能
免矣於戲聖人作止語默無非教也亦猶天之
四時行百物生無非天理發見流行之實也曾
何有隱而亦何待於言哉學者果能悟夫子無
隱之言力求其實而因以得其無言之妙則高
者可及而遠者可即矣此固程子之意也
表
擬宋以孔宜襲封文宣公謝表太平興國三年
黃佐
===
同考試官教諭莊批表體駢儷學者類能為之
求其意婉而厚語贍而莊寓忠愛於稱謝間者僅見此篇
同考試官教諭江批文辭典則氣象渾厚寫出崇
德象賢之意可佳
考試官學正何批四六中用事切當錄之
考試官教授劉批溫純整潔可誦
臣宜言今月某日某官某奉宣
詔旨以臣宜為右贊善大夫襲封文宣公者臣
誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言
punctuated:
喻，况其下者乎？有隱之疑，宜乎諸弟子所不能免矣。於戲！聖人作止語默，無非教也；亦猶天之四時行、百物生，無非天理發見流行之實也。曾何有隱，而亦何待於言哉？學者果能悟夫子無隱之言，力求其實，而因以得其無言之妙，則高者可及，而遠者可即矣。此固程子之意也。

表
擬宋以孔宜襲封文宣公謝表，太平興國三年。
黃佐

同考試官教諭莊批：表體駢儷，學者類能為之。求其意婉而厚，語贍而莊，寓忠愛於稱謝間者，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭江批：文辭典則，氣象渾厚，寫出崇德象賢之意，可佳。
考試官學正何批：四六中用事切當，錄之。
考試官教授劉批：溫純整潔，可誦。

臣宜言：今月某日，某官某奉宣詔旨，以臣宜為右贊善大夫，襲封文宣公者。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：
translation_en:
…understand it; how much less could those below him? It was natural that the disciples could not escape the suspicion that something was being concealed from them. Alas! The sage’s activity and repose, speech and silence, are all instruction. They resemble Heaven’s succession of the four seasons and generation of the myriad things: all are actual manifestations and workings of heavenly principle. What, then, is concealed, and what need is there for words? If students can truly grasp the Master’s statement that he conceals nothing, earnestly seek its substance, and thereby apprehend the subtlety of his wordless teaching, then what is lofty can be attained and what is distant can be approached. This, indeed, is Master Cheng’s meaning.

Memorial
A simulated memorial of thanks on the Song dynasty’s granting Kong Yi succession to the title Duke of Literary Proclamation (Wenxuan), in the third year of Taiping Xingguo [978].
By Huang Zuo.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: Students can generally compose the paired and parallel phrases characteristic of memorials. But seeking one whose meaning is tactful yet substantial, whose language is ample yet dignified, and which conveys loyalty and affection through its expressions of thanks, I have found only this piece.
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Its diction is classical and correct, its overall bearing full and substantial. It expresses the intention of honoring virtue and taking worthy ancestors as models. Commendable.
Comment by Examiner He, School Instructor: The allusions within its four- and six-character parallel prose are aptly employed. Include it.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: Gentle, pure, orderly, and polished; worthy of recitation.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝德重華開萬世文明之象儒門有慶荷
九天錫命之光道尊素王恩及苗裔建官作
一人之輔列爵居五等之先家學淵源世遠敢
忘似續
皇仁浩博才微幸獲涵容
綸綍下頒箕裘內愧兹蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
沉幾先物
英斷合天河洛圖書夙嘗授之
===
宣廟範疇福德蚤巳占之
藝皇四海
帝臣龍行雲擁萬方王會虎步風生閔農事戒
田荒心欲所其無逸抑禎符絕遠物治必
保其有終大哉
中國聖人允矣
太平天子明昭定烈不一再朞崇德象賢越四
十世上爵賜繇隋帝嘉名制自唐宗監彼
儀文畀兹朽質重輔導俾兼其職輕征徭
punctuated: 帝德重華，開萬世文明之象；儒門有慶，荷九天錫命之光。道尊素王，恩及苗裔。建官作一人之輔，列爵居五等之先。家學淵源，世遠敢忘似續；皇仁浩博，才微幸獲涵容。綸綍下頒，箕裘內愧。兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，沉幾先物，英斷合天。河洛圖書，夙嘗授之宣廟；範疇福德，蚤巳占之藝皇。四海帝臣，龍行雲擁；萬方王會，虎步風生。閔農事，戒田荒，心欲所其無逸；抑禎符，絕遠物，治必保其有終。大哉，中國聖人！允矣，太平天子！明昭定烈，不一再朞；崇德象賢，越四十世。上爵賜繇隋帝，嘉名制自唐宗。監彼儀文，畀兹朽質。重輔導，俾兼其職；輕征徭，
translation_en:
Imperial virtue renews the brilliance of Shun, revealing the promise of civilization for ten thousand generations; the Confucian lineage has cause for celebration, receiving the radiant favor of an imperial appointment from the Ninth Heaven. The Way brings honor to the Uncrowned King, and imperial grace reaches his descendants. An office is established to assist the One Man; a noble rank is conferred that stands foremost among the five grades. Our family learning has a profound source: though generations have passed, how could I dare forget to carry it on? Imperial benevolence is vast: though my talents are slight, I have fortunately received its generous indulgence. As the imperial decree is bestowed from above, I inwardly feel ashamed of my inadequacy to carry on my ancestral calling.
This is because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, 〇〇〇〇 [text unclear], whose profound discernment anticipates events and whose brilliant decisions accord with Heaven. The River Chart and Luo Writing had long ago been bestowed upon the Xuan ancestral temple [?]; the categories of the Great Plan, with their blessings and virtues, had already furnished auspicious signs for Emperor Yi [?]. Throughout the Four Seas, the emperor’s servants advance like dragons, with clouds gathering around them; from every quarter, those attending the royal assembly stride like tigers, raising the wind. You care for agricultural affairs and guard against fields falling waste, your heart intent upon abiding in freedom from idleness [?]. You restrain the presentation of auspicious portents and reject exotic goods from distant lands, ensuring that your government will reach a worthy conclusion. Great indeed is the sage of the Central Kingdom! Truly you are the Son of Heaven of Great Peace! Your luminous achievements have been established in scarcely one or two years; in honoring virtue and recognizing ancestral worth in descendants, your favor spans more than forty generations. The exalted noble rank was bestowed by a Sui emperor; the honored title was instituted by a Tang emperor. Following those ceremonial precedents, you have conferred them upon this decrepit person. Esteeming the work of guidance, you have ordered me concurrently to hold that office; lightening taxes and labor services, …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
用復其家岱嶽滄溟高揭仲尼日月魯邦
兗土弘開夫子宮墻延賞無窮
君恩已極受爵不讓臣罪何辭竊念臣宜下第
乾德之初征商星子之鎮遠違廊廟久涉
江湖詣
闕上書迹頗似於韓愈還
朝獻賦文不類於相如詎意菲葑謬登鼎俎
仰天有愧俯地何從敢不砥礪亷隅期無
負於
===
明詔纘承統緒求不忝於前人啓沃之心尚
圖夙夜將順之美莫補涓埃三祝華封
堯仁曷能想像載歌天保
周德難以形容伏願五星永聚奎躔人文與
天文並耀六籍大明
聖世
國統與道統同尊臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
punctuated: 用復其家。岱嶽滄溟，高揭仲尼日月；魯邦兗土，弘開夫子宮墻。延賞無窮，君恩已極；受爵不讓，臣罪何辭？竊念臣宜下第乾德之初，征商星子之鎮，遠違廊廟，久涉江湖。詣闕上書，迹頗似於韓愈；還朝獻賦，文不類於相如。詎意菲葑，謬登鼎俎？仰天有愧，俯地何從？敢不砥礪亷隅，期無負於明詔；纘承統緒，求不忝於前人。啓沃之心，尚圖夙夜；將順之美，莫補涓埃。三祝華封，堯仁曷能想像？載歌天保，周德難以形容。伏願五星永聚奎躔，人文與天文並耀；六籍大明聖世，國統與道統同尊。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉
translation_en:
…thereby exempting my household from service. As lofty as Mount Dai and as vast as the blue sea, you raise high the sun and moon of Zhongni; in the land of Lu and the territory of Yan, you greatly enlarge the Master's palace walls. Your rewards extend without end; your sovereign kindness has reached its utmost. Having accepted the title without declining it, how can your servant excuse his fault?

I reflect that I, your servant Yi [?], failed the examination at the beginning of the Qiande era and collected commercial taxes in the town of Xingzi. Far removed from the imperial court, I long sojourned among rivers and lakes. In approaching the palace to submit a letter, my conduct somewhat resembled Han Yu's; in returning to court to present a rhapsody, my writing bore no comparison to Sima Xiangru's. How could I have imagined that such humble greens as I would mistakenly find a place among the sacrificial vessels? Looking up to Heaven, I feel shame; looking down to earth, where can I turn?

How dare I fail to temper my integrity, hoping not to disappoint your enlightened edict, and to carry forward the ancestral succession, seeking not to disgrace my forebears? With a heart devoted to enlightening and nourishing the sovereign's understanding, I still intend to exert myself morning and night; yet in supporting and furthering your virtues, I cannot contribute even a drop or a speck. Even the three blessings offered by the border warden of Hua could scarcely convey your benevolence, equal to Yao's. Singing anew the ode Heaven Protects You, I could hardly describe your virtue, equal to that of Zhou.

I humbly wish that the five planets may forever gather in the celestial lodge Kui, so that human culture and Heaven's patterns shine together; and that the Six Classics may shine brightly in this sage-governed age, with the imperial succession and the succession of the Way equally revered. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to the sage sovereign, cannot contain his intense emotion and utmost reverent trepidation. I respectfully present…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
表稱
謝以
聞
第參場
策五道
第一問
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批
朝廷盛德大業默寓
===
詔旨此策發揚殆盡末復以古人自期遠大之到吾切有望於子
同考試官教諭江批能鋪張我
聖天子至仁盛德之實誦之不覺嘆賞至再况五策翩翩氣充詞贍吾
意此子殆不止魁一省而已健羨健羨
考試官學正何批我
朝詔令如天難名子能詳悉無遺則才之宏博有可占矣華國之薦
舍子其誰
考試官教授劉批此策議論閎闊揄揚得體
有士如此真足以薦
punctuated:
表稱謝以聞。

第參場。策五道。第一問。黃佐。

同考試官教諭莊批：朝廷盛德大業，默寓詔旨。此策發揚殆盡，末復以古人自期，遠大之到，吾切有望於子。

同考試官教諭江批：能鋪張我聖天子至仁盛德之實，誦之不覺嘆賞至再。况五策翩翩，氣充詞贍，吾意此子殆不止魁一省而已。健羨！健羨！

考試官學正何批：我朝詔令，如天難名。子能詳悉無遺，則才之宏博有可占矣。華國之薦，舍子其誰？

考試官教授劉批：此策議論閎闊，揄揚得體。有士如此，真足以薦
translation_en:
…this memorial expressing thanks, submitted for imperial hearing.

Third Session. Five Policy Questions. First Question. Huang Zuo 黃佐.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor: The court’s abundant virtue and great achievements are implicitly embodied in the imperial edict. This policy essay brings them out almost exhaustively. At the end, you further take the ancients as the standard you aspire to attain. Such far-reaching attainment [?] gives me earnest hopes for you.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: You amply expound the substance of our sagely Son of Heaven’s utmost benevolence and abundant virtue. Reading this aloud, I could not help repeatedly sighing in admiration. Moreover, all five policy essays flow gracefully, full of vigor and rich in expression. I think this young man will surely do more than merely rank first in a single province. How enviable! How enviable!

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor (xuezheng): Our dynasty’s edicts and commands, like Heaven itself, are difficult to describe adequately. Your ability to explain them thoroughly, omitting nothing, reveals the breadth and comprehensiveness of your talent. Whom but you should we recommend to bring glory to the realm?

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: This policy essay is broad in its argument and fitting in its praise. A scholar such as this truly deserves to be recommended…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
上矣
聖人之感人心也有所以立天下之本有
所以示天下之機有其本則允德協下而
感之也深有其機則嘉言孔彰而應之也
速是故問其德曰天下之大本也問其言
曰天下之大機也聖人者作操其本握其
機言出而天下從之夫天下豈可以空言
感動之哉愚因反覆明問而有以知
聖世
===
皇言之大足以配帝王而陋西漢矣敬陳其槩
粤自戊申春正月我
太祖高皇帝首以
卽位詔天下則
上帝
祖考之靈建元定號之正續中國帝王之統開
億萬載無疆之休其精神命脉固已潛孚
於天下矣乃若求遺書定律令定文武科
取士之法出師以定中原馳檄以諭齊魯
punctuated:
上矣。
聖人之感人心也，有所以立天下之本，有所以示天下之機。有其本，則允德協下而感之也深；有其機，則嘉言孔彰而應之也速。是故問其德，曰天下之大本也；問其言，曰天下之大機也。聖人者作，操其本，握其機，言出而天下從之。夫天下豈可以空言感動之哉？愚因反覆明問，而有以知聖世皇言之大，足以配帝王而陋西漢矣。敬陳其槩。
粤自戊申春正月，我太祖高皇帝首以卽位詔天下，則上帝祖考之靈、建元定號之正，續中國帝王之統，開億萬載無疆之休，其精神命脉固已潛孚於天下矣。乃若求遺書、定律令、定文武科取士之法、出師以定中原、馳檄以諭齊魯
translation_en:
…to the throne!
When a sage moves people’s hearts, he has the means to establish the foundation of all under Heaven and to reveal the mainspring of action throughout the realm. With that foundation, his truly trustworthy virtue brings those below into harmony, and his influence reaches deep; with that mainspring, his excellent words shine forth, and the response comes swiftly. Thus, if asked about his virtue, one says that it is the great foundation of all under Heaven; if asked about his words, one says that they are the great mainspring of all under Heaven. When a sage arises, he holds that foundation and controls that mainspring: his words go forth, and all under Heaven follow him. How could empty words move the realm? Through repeatedly considering your illuminating question, I have come to understand that the greatness of imperial pronouncements in this sagely age is sufficient to match those of the ancient emperors and kings and to make those of the Western Han seem paltry. I respectfully present their general outline.
Beginning in the first month of spring in the wushen year, our Emperor Taizu Gao first proclaimed his accession to all under Heaven. His proclamation set forth [?] the numinous aid of the Lord on High and his ancestors, and the legitimacy of establishing an era and fixing the dynastic designation, continuing the succession of China’s emperors and kings and inaugurating boundless blessings for countless ages. Its vital spirit had already silently won the confidence of the realm. Then there were the search for surviving books, the establishment of statutes and ordinances, the determination of methods for recruiting men through the civil and military examinations, the dispatch of armies to pacify the Central Plain, and the swift circulation of proclamations to instruct the people of Qi and Lu…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
河洛燕薊秦晉之人此
令行於立國之初者也先之以農桑學校繼
之以求言又繼之以赦宥存恤免姑孰金
陵免唐鄧秦隴等處田租諭山東山西省
臣諭元舊相諭高麗安南日本諸國此
詔頒於一統之後者也嗣是而
太宗之入正大統
仁宗
宣宗之纘緒
===
英宗之復辟
憲宗
孝宗之繼體守文莫不有
詔惟繼天立極之德無一而不備故經天緯
地之文無一而不周萬世遵之萬世之治
也迺今庚午夏四月
聖天子特下
明詔命討寧夏之罪首舉法天立政卽堯之
欽若昊天湯之祗承上帝而敬
punctuated:
河洛燕薊秦晉之人，此令行於立國之初者也。先之以農桑學校，繼之以求言，又繼之以赦宥存恤，免姑孰金陵、免唐鄧秦隴等處田租，諭山東山西省臣，諭元舊相，諭高麗安南日本諸國，此詔頒於一統之後者也。嗣是而太宗之入正大統，仁宗、宣宗之纘緒，英宗之復辟，憲宗、孝宗之繼體守文，莫不有詔。惟繼天立極之德無一而不備，故經天緯地之文無一而不周。萬世遵之，萬世之治也。
迺今庚午夏四月，聖天子特下明詔，命討寧夏之罪，首舉法天立政，卽堯之欽若昊天、湯之祗承上帝，而敬
translation_en:
…the people of Heluo, Yan, Ji, Qin, and Jin: these commands were put into effect at the founding of the state. First came measures concerning agriculture, sericulture, and schools; next came the solicitation of counsel; then pardons, relief, and care for those in need. Land taxes were remitted in Gushu and Jinling, and in Tang, Deng, Qin, Long, and other places. Instructions were issued to the provincial officials of Shandong and Shanxi, to former chief councilors of the Yuan, and to the kingdoms of Gaoli, Annan, Japan, and others. These edicts were promulgated after unification. Thereafter, when Taizong assumed the imperial succession, when Renzong and Xuanzong carried on the imperial line, when Yingzong was restored to the throne, and when Xianzong and Xiaozong inherited the throne and upheld established institutions, each issued edicts. Because their virtue in succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard lacked nothing, their writings, which ordered Heaven and Earth, likewise left nothing unaddressed. If followed for ten thousand generations, they would secure orderly government for ten thousand generations.
Now, in the fourth month of summer in the gengwu year [1510], the sagely Son of Heaven has specially issued an illustrious edict commanding a punitive expedition against the wrongdoing in Ningxia. It opens by invoking the principle of modeling government on Heaven, just as Yao reverently followed August Heaven and Tang respectfully served the Lord on High; and his reverence…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天之心何至也上念
祖宗付託即高宗之監于成憲成王之對揚耿
光而法
祖之心何至也以同仁之政布天下即堯之協
和萬邦湯之輯寧邦家也而勤民恤物之
心至矣以問罪之師告天下即舜之徂征
有苗啓之用勦有扈也而神武不殺之心
至矣回視漢之高祖約法三章似得文王
慎罰之意也文帝田租賜半似得大禹養
===
民之意也宣帝之戒脩職似得成王訓官
之意也武帝之罷輪臺似得太甲悔過之
意也然究其本則漢之君無精一執中之
傳而漢之詔豈復有虞夏商周四代之書
之氣象耶我
聖天子有
祖宗
列聖之德發而為
祖宗
punctuated: 天之心何至也！上念祖宗付託，即高宗之監于成憲、成王之對揚耿光，而法祖之心何至也！以同仁之政布天下，即堯之協和萬邦、湯之輯寧邦家也，而勤民恤物之心至矣！以問罪之師告天下，即舜之徂征有苗、啓之用勦有扈也，而神武不殺之心至矣！回視漢之高祖約法三章，似得文王慎罰之意也；文帝田租賜半，似得大禹養民之意也；宣帝之戒脩職，似得成王訓官之意也；武帝之罷輪臺，似得太甲悔過之意也。然究其本，則漢之君無精一執中之傳，而漢之詔豈復有虞夏商周四代之書之氣象耶？我聖天子有祖宗列聖之德，發而為祖宗
translation_en:
…how consummate is his reverence for Heaven! His Majesty bears in mind the charge entrusted to him by his ancestors, just as Gaozong looked to established statutes and King Cheng acknowledged and extolled his predecessor’s brilliant virtue. How consummate is his resolve to emulate his ancestors! He proclaims throughout the realm a government of impartial benevolence, just as Yao brought the myriad states into harmony and Tang secured peace for his dominions. His concern for the people and care for all beings are indeed consummate! He announces to the realm an army dispatched to punish wrongdoing, just as Shun marched against the Youmiao and Qi used force to destroy the Youhu. His resolve to exercise divine martial power without killing is indeed consummate!

Looking back at the Han, Gaozu’s reduction of the laws to three articles seems to have grasped King Wen’s intention of exercising caution in punishment. Emperor Wen’s remission of half the land tax seems to have grasped Yu the Great’s intention of nourishing the people. Emperor Xuan’s admonition that officials attend to their duties seems to have grasped King Cheng’s intention in instructing his officers. Emperor Wu’s abandonment of the Luntai undertaking seems to have grasped Tai Jia’s intention in repenting his faults. Yet, examining their foundations, the Han rulers lacked the transmitted teaching of refinement and single-mindedness in holding fast to the mean. How, then, could Han edicts possess the spirit of the documents of the four ages of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou?

Our sagely Son of Heaven possesses the virtue of his ancestors, the successive sage emperors, and gives it expression as his ancestors’…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列聖之言有二帝三王之德發而爲典謨訓誥
誓命之文故曰聖人之心見於書猶化工
之妙著於物非精深不能識也天下之人
沐其德而莫知其本誦其言而莫測其機
草茅何足以形容之然愚於漢而有感焉
趙佗嘗帝越矣尺書南下佗卽稱臣奉貢
而何感之易耶漢文恭儉之風卑遜謙抑
之語海濱父老至于今猶能道之漢詔之
感人蓋不止於山東之民扶杖而往聽也
===
而况我
聖天子之詔乎愚生也晚當鼓舞振作之下而
誦習久矣茲欲鋪張揚厲以昭
聖德神功於罔極則自有燕許大筆在而愚愧
非其人也惟進教之幸甚
第二問
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批
策問諸子之書場中善對者
少惟此一卷考據精詳評論切當且以六經折衷其說
punctuated:
列聖之言，有二帝三王之德，發而爲典謨訓誥誓命之文。故曰：「聖人之心見於書，猶化工之妙著於物，非精深不能識也。」天下之人沐其德而莫知其本，誦其言而莫測其機，草茅何足以形容之？然愚於漢而有感焉。趙佗嘗帝越矣，尺書南下，佗卽稱臣奉貢，而何感之易耶？漢文恭儉之風，卑遜謙抑之語，海濱父老至于今猶能道之。漢詔之感人，蓋不止於山東之民扶杖而往聽也。而况我聖天子之詔乎？愚生也晚，當鼓舞振作之下，而誦習久矣。茲欲鋪張揚厲，以昭聖德神功於罔極，則自有燕許大筆在，而愚愧非其人也。惟進教之，幸甚！
第二問
黃佐
同考試官教諭莊批：
策問諸子之書，場中善對者少，惟此一卷，考據精詳，評論切當，且以六經折衷其說。
translation_en:
…the words of the successive sage emperors. He possesses the virtue of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, which finds expression in writings such as the canons, counsels, instructions, announcements, oaths, and commands. Thus it is said: “The sage’s mind is revealed in his writings, just as the wondrous workings of creation are manifest in things; without profound discernment, one cannot comprehend it.” All under Heaven enjoy his virtue without knowing its source and recite his words without fathoming their workings. How could a humble scholar outside official service adequately describe these things? Yet the Han dynasty gives me cause for reflection. Zhao Tuo once proclaimed himself emperor in Yue. When a brief letter went south, Tuo immediately acknowledged himself a subject and presented tribute. Why was he so readily moved? Even today, elders along the coast can still recount Emperor Wen of Han’s manner of reverence and frugality and his humble, deferential words. The power of Han edicts to move people surely extended beyond the inhabitants east of the mountains who went, leaning on their staffs, to hear them. How much more powerful, then, are the edicts of our sage Son of Heaven!
Born in this later age, I have long recited and studied these edicts under their inspiring and invigorating influence. If their grandeur is now to be fully expounded, making manifest the boundless virtue of the sage and his divine achievements, there are already great pens such as those of the Dukes of Yan and Xu to undertake it. I am ashamed that I am not such a man. I would be most fortunate if you would impart your instruction to me.
Second Policy Question
Huang Zuo
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor:
The policy question concerns the writings of the various philosophical masters. Few candidates in the examination hall answered it well. This essay alone is meticulous and thorough in its examination of evidence, apt in its judgments, and moreover uses the Six Classics as the standard for weighing their doctrines…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得士如此亦可以自慶矣
同考試官教諭江批晚得此策獨能於周秦漢
唐上下千餘年間所紀之書所作之人歷歷陳說無
遺披閱之次不覺為之歛衽
考試官學正何批條答有據而文亦清致其
空谷之足音歟
考試官教授劉批考究旣詳折衷允當蓋學
之博而知其要者也
對欲博極夫諸子之書必折衷以六經之
===
旨蓋諸子之書各以所見為說駁而不醇
雜而無統其於聖人之道背馳焉者多矣
茲欲遍考其書而不以六經之旨折衷其
說則其為道之蔽也豈淺淺哉故曰眾言
殽亂折諸聖其是之謂乎先儒有言不觀
非聖之書又曰學不博則不能約則夫諸
子之書固儒者之所當知請因明問而歷
陳之可乎聖人之道載在六經如日月之
中天萬古常明六經之外而有諸子諸子
punctuated:
得士如此，亦可以自慶矣。

同考試官教諭江批：晚得此策，獨能於周秦漢唐上下千餘年間所紀之書、所作之人，歷歷陳說無遺。披閱之次，不覺為之歛衽。

考試官學正何批：條答有據，而文亦清致，其空谷之足音歟？

考試官教授劉批：考究旣詳，折衷允當，蓋學之博而知其要者也。

對：欲博極夫諸子之書，必折衷以六經之旨。蓋諸子之書，各以所見為說，駁而不醇，雜而無統，其於聖人之道背馳焉者多矣。茲欲遍考其書，而不以六經之旨折衷其說，則其為道之蔽也，豈淺淺哉？故曰：「眾言殽亂，折諸聖。」其是之謂乎？先儒有言：「不觀非聖之書。」又曰：「學不博則不能約。」則夫諸子之書，固儒者之所當知。請因明問而歷陳之，可乎？聖人之道載在六經，如日月之中天，萬古常明。六經之外而有諸子，諸子
translation_en:
…To obtain a scholar like this is indeed cause for congratulating ourselves.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: I obtained this policy essay late in the proceedings. It alone can clearly set forth, without omission, the books recorded and their authors over the thousand and more years spanning the Zhou, Qin, Han, and Tang. As I read it, I could not help straightening my robes in respect.

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: His answers to the individual points have supporting evidence, and his writing is lucid and elegant. Is this not the sound of footsteps in an empty valley—a rare and welcome discovery?

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: His investigation is thorough, and his critical judgments are sound. Here is someone whose learning is broad and who understands its essentials.

Response: To attain comprehensive knowledge of the writings of the various masters, one must judge them by the purport of the Six Classics. For the writings of the various masters each advance doctrines based on their own particular insights: they are mixed rather than pure, miscellaneous and without a unifying principle. Much in them runs counter to the Way of the sages. If one now wishes to examine all their books without judging their doctrines by the purport of the Six Classics, could the resulting obscuration of the Way possibly be slight? Thus it is said: “When the many teachings are confused, judge them by the sages.” Does this not express precisely that point? An earlier Confucian scholar said, “Do not read books that are not those of the sages.” Yet it is also said, “Unless one’s learning is broad, one cannot grasp its essentials.” The writings of the various masters are therefore certainly something Confucian scholars ought to know. May I respond to your illuminating question by setting them forth in order? The Way of the sages is recorded in the Six Classics, like the sun and moon in mid-heaven, shining perpetually through the ages. Beyond the Six Classics there are the writings of the various masters. The Zhuzi [Masters; a book title?]…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
作於李綽昌言則作於仲長統申鑒則作
於荀悅氏中論作於魏之徐幹法訓作於
蜀之譙周應劭有風俗通義之書魏證有
群書治要之典李吉甫則有古今說苑杜
佑則有管氏指要論衡說林非作於王充
孔衍乎世說類林非作於義慶子野乎他
如鬼谷子則周世之隱士尉繚子則六國
之時人抱朴子則爲葛洪金樓子則爲梁
元廣成子則爲商路公鶡冠子則爲齊隱
===
士鄧析子則鄭人與子產同時者尹文子
則宋人與宋鈃同遊者魯連子則六國之
仲連淮南子則劉漢之王安胡非子非墨
翟之弟子乎黔婁子非齊國之隱士乎鬻
子則爲鬻熊田子則爲田駢宣子則爲宣
聘陸子則爲陸雲論其人之所產不過秦
漢上下之人論其所著之書不出藝文十
家之外然皆起于王道旣衰聖人旣沒之
後時君世主好尚殊方是以十家之術蠭
punctuated:
作於李綽，《昌言》則作於仲長統，《申鑒》則作於荀悅氏，《中論》作於魏之徐幹，《法訓》作於蜀之譙周。應劭有《風俗通義》之書，魏證有《群書治要》之典，李吉甫則有《古今說苑》，杜佑則有《管氏指要》。《論衡》《說林》非作於王充、孔衍乎？《世說》《類林》非作於義慶、子野乎？他如《鬼谷子》，則周世之隱士；《尉繚子》，則六國之時人；《抱朴子》，則爲葛洪；《金樓子》，則爲梁元；《廣成子》，則爲商路公；《鶡冠子》，則爲齊隱士；《鄧析子》，則鄭人與子產同時者；《尹文子》，則宋人與宋鈃同遊者；《魯連子》，則六國之仲連；《淮南子》，則劉漢之王安。《胡非子》非墨翟之弟子乎？《黔婁子》非齊國之隱士乎？《鬻子》則爲鬻熊，《田子》則爲田駢，《宣子》則爲宣聘，《陸子》則爲陸雲。
論其人之所產，不過秦漢上下之人；論其所著之書，不出藝文十家之外。然皆起于王道旣衰、聖人旣沒之後，時君世主好尚殊方，是以十家之術蠭
translation_en:
…was written by Li Chuo; Forthright Words (Changyan) by Zhongchang Tong; Extended Reflections (Shenjian) by Xun Yue; Central Discourses (Zhonglun) by Xu Gan of Wei; and Model Instructions (Faxun) by Qiao Zhou of Shu. Ying Shao wrote Comprehensive Explanations of Customs (Fengsu tongyi), and Wei Zheng compiled Essentials of Government from Collected Books (Qunshu zhiyao). Li Jifu had his Garden of Sayings Ancient and Modern (Gujin shuoyuan) [?], and Du You his Essential Teachings of Master Guan (Guanshi zhiyao) [?]. Were Balanced Discourses (Lunheng) and Forest of Sayings (Shuolin) not written by Wang Chong and Kong Yan respectively? Were Accounts of the World (Shishuo) and Forest of Classified Matters (Leilin) not written by Yiqing and Ziye respectively?
Among other works, Master of Ghost Valley (Guiguzi) was by a recluse of the Zhou age; Master Wei Liao (Weiliaozi) by a man of the Six States period; Master Who Embraces Simplicity (Baopuzi) by Ge Hong; and Master of the Golden Tower (Jinlouzi) by Emperor Yuan of Liang. Master Guangcheng (Guangchengzi) was by Lord Lu of Shang [?]; Pheasant-Cap Master (Heguanzi) by a recluse of Qi; Master Deng Xi (Dengxizi) by a man of Zheng who lived at the same time as Zichan; and Master Yin Wen (Yinwenzi) by a man of Song who associated with Song Xing. Master Lu Lian (Lulianzi) was by Zhonglian of the Six States period, and Master of Huainan (Huainanzi) by Prince An of the Liu family's Han dynasty. Was Master Hu Fei (Hufeizi) not by a disciple of Mo Di? Was Master Qian Lou (Qianlouzi) not by a recluse of Qi? Master Yu (Yuzi) was by Yu Xiong; Master Tian (Tianzi) by Tian Pian; Master Xuan (Xuanzi) by Xuan Pin [?]; and Master Lu (Luzi) by Lu Yun [?].
As for the times in which these men lived, they fall within the Qin and Han periods and the ages immediately before and after them. As for their writings, these fall within the ten bibliographical schools. Yet all arose after the Way of the Kings had declined and the sages had passed away. The rulers of their times differed in their preferences, and thus the teachings of the ten schools swarmed…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
然並作各持其說取合諸侯論其書雖有
蔽短之不同要其歸豈無梗槩之可取使
其人遭際明時設學校而陶鎔之以道德
而衷正之會其同而變其異取其純而去
其謬則皆可爲六經之羽翼矣學者苟能
脩六藝之術以觀此諸家之書又豈不能
通萬方之略而爲游藝之一助乎愚也無
高睨千古之見乏貫串百家之學孤陋寡
聞對揚明問固不能免夫掛一漏萬之誚
===
矣
第三問
廖任
同考試官教諭莊批評二公文章政事以道爲主
而折以程朱之論可謂有見且先後布置俱合法程
盖嶺南之佳士也
同考試官教諭江批閱此一策考據詳明斷制精
確豈嘗熟讀二公之文而尚論其世者歟
考試官學正何批此策於韓歐二公文章事業
punctuated:
然並作，各持其說，取合諸侯。論其書，雖有蔽短之不同，要其歸，豈無梗槩之可取？使其人遭際明時，設學校而陶鎔之，以道德而衷正之，會其同而變其異，取其純而去其謬，則皆可爲六經之羽翼矣。學者苟能脩六藝之術，以觀此諸家之書，又豈不能通萬方之略，而爲游藝之一助乎？愚也，無高睨千古之見，乏貫串百家之學，孤陋寡聞，對揚明問，固不能免夫掛一漏萬之誚矣。

第三問
廖任

同考試官教諭莊批：評二公文章政事，以道爲主，而折以程朱之論，可謂有見。且先後布置，俱合法程，盖嶺南之佳士也。

同考試官教諭江批：閱此一策，考據詳明，斷制精確，豈嘗熟讀二公之文，而尚論其世者歟？

考試官學正何批：此策於韓歐二公文章事業
translation_en:
…arose together, each maintaining its own doctrines and seeking the approval of the feudal lords. Although their books differ in their limitations and shortcomings, if we examine their ultimate purport, surely there are broad outlines worth adopting? Had these men lived in an enlightened age, with schools established to cultivate them and the Way and moral virtue employed to set them right—reconciling their agreements and transforming their differences, retaining what was pure and removing what was erroneous—they could all have served as auxiliaries to the Six Classics. If scholars cultivate the arts of the Six Classics and use them to examine the writings of these various schools, could they not comprehend the essentials of myriad approaches and thereby gain another aid to taking their pleasure in the arts? I, in my ignorance, lack both the vision to survey the ages from on high and the learning to connect the teachings of the hundred schools. With my limited learning and scant knowledge, in respectfully answering your illuminating question I certainly cannot escape the reproach of mentioning one thing while omitting ten thousand.

Third Policy Question
Liao Ren

Associate Examiner Zhuang, Instructor, comments: In assessing the literary writings and governmental accomplishments of the two masters, he takes the Way as his guiding principle and judges them by the arguments of Cheng and Zhu. This may truly be called discernment. Moreover, the arrangement throughout conforms to the proper standards. He is indeed an outstanding scholar of Lingnan.

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: Reading this policy essay, I find its examination of evidence detailed and clear, and its judgments precise. Could he be someone who has read the two masters’ writings thoroughly and sought to understand the age in which they lived?

Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: This policy essay, concerning the literary writings and achievements of the two masters Han and Ou…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
評品停當足見學識
考試官教授劉批詞氣舂容而議論切實當
是策手
對文章政事出於道則隨所用而咸備文
章政事離於道則隨所就而難兼蓋文章
不可徒為政事不可徒施要必有道以為
之本本有未至隨其才力之所就則優於
此者未必能兼於彼而文章政事始岐而
為二矣請因明問而陳其槩易曰言之無
===
文行之不遠則文章固足以潤身書曰道
洽政治澤潤生民則政事固足以及物然
自三代而上士以脩身體道為本文章乃
其餘事學以窮理盡性為先政事乃其末
節伊尹之德協于克一而伐夏救民之功
伊訓太甲之書後世未有能及之者尹吉
甫之德萬邦為憲而攘夷安夏之功崧高
烝民之什後世未有能過之者世變日下
道學不明則所謂文章者藝焉而已而非
punctuated:
評品停當，足見學識。
考試官教授劉批：詞氣舂容，而議論切實，當是策手。
對：文章政事出於道，則隨所用而咸備；文章政事離於道，則隨所就而難兼。蓋文章不可徒為，政事不可徒施，要必有道以為之本。本有未至，隨其才力之所就，則優於此者未必能兼於彼，而文章政事始岐而為二矣。請因明問而陳其槩。《易》曰：「言之無文，行之不遠。」則文章固足以潤身。《書》曰：「道洽政治，澤潤生民。」則政事固足以及物。然自三代而上，士以脩身體道為本，文章乃其餘事；學以窮理盡性為先，政事乃其末節。伊尹之德，協于克一，而伐夏救民之功，《伊訓》《太甲》之書，後世未有能及之者。尹吉甫之德，萬邦為憲，而攘夷安夏之功，《崧高》《烝民》之什，後世未有能過之者。世變日下，道學不明，則所謂文章者，藝焉而已，而非
translation_en:
…The assessments are well judged, amply demonstrating learning and discernment.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The language and tenor are measured and expansive, while the arguments are pertinent and substantial. He must be an accomplished writer of policy essays.

Reply: When literary composition and government affairs proceed from the Way, both are fully provided for, whatever the application. When they depart from the Way, accomplishment in one makes it difficult to encompass the other. Literary compositions must not be written merely for their own sake, nor government measures undertaken merely for the sake of acting: both must have the Way as their foundation. If that foundation is imperfect, each person follows where his talents and abilities lead; someone who excels in one field may not also encompass the other. Thus literary composition and government affairs begin to diverge into two separate pursuits. Allow me to respond to your illuminating question by setting out the broad outline.

The Book of Changes says, “Words without refinement will not travel far.” Thus literary composition assuredly can adorn one's person. The Book of Documents says, “The Way prevailed and government was well ordered; beneficence nourished the people.” Thus government affairs assuredly can benefit others. Yet in the Three Dynasties and earlier, scholars took cultivating themselves and embodying the Way as their foundation; literary composition was merely a subsidiary undertaking. Learning gave priority to fathoming principle and fully realizing one's nature; government affairs were merely its secondary particulars.

Yi Yin's virtue accorded with the attainment of unity. His achievements in overthrowing the Xia and rescuing the people, and the texts “Instructions of Yi” and “Tai Jia,” have never been equaled by anyone in later ages. Yin Jifu's virtue served as a model for the myriad states. His achievements in repelling the foreign peoples and securing the central states, and the odes “Lofty Mountains” and “The Multitude of the People,” have never been surpassed by anyone in later ages.

As the world changed and declined day by day, learning devoted to the Way became obscured. What was called literary composition then became merely a craft, rather than…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
載道之具所謂政事者法焉而已而非正
已之推才性有通塞功力有疎密優於此
者或劣於彼求其能兼之者實難其人試
以韓歐二子論之唐之文章承八代之後
專以雕琢綺麗爲工而氣象萎薾陳子昂
嘗欲變之矣而力弗逮至元和間韓愈者
出力去陳言務追古作宋庠謂其奧衍閎
深佐佑六經史臣謂愈之才自視司馬遷
楊雄殆非虛語矣然遷於愈固相上下雄
===
之命意措詞短局滯澁不若愈之肆意有
作不煩繩削則愈於雄似爲過之也宋之
文章承五代之後專以聲律對偶爲事而
文體卑弱穆修嘗欲變之矣而才不乃及至
景祐間歐陽修者出深黜險譎務趨平淡
曾鞏謂其醇深炳鬱渾然天質蘇軾謂修
爲今之韓子亦非過論也然修初得韓文
於故壁破簏之中披閱校讎至老不懈雖
未嘗規規追躡其故步而體裁矩矱自成
punctuated:
載道之具，所謂政事者，法焉而已，而非正已之推。才性有通塞，功力有疎密，優於此者或劣於彼，求其能兼之者，實難其人。試以韓歐二子論之：唐之文章承八代之後，專以雕琢綺麗爲工，而氣象萎薾。陳子昂嘗欲變之矣，而力弗逮。至元和間，韓愈者出，力去陳言，務追古作。宋庠謂其奧衍閎深，佐佑六經；史臣謂愈之才自視司馬遷、楊雄，殆非虛語矣。然遷於愈固相上下，雄之命意措詞，短局滯澁，不若愈之肆意有作，不煩繩削，則愈於雄似爲過之也。
宋之文章承五代之後，專以聲律對偶爲事，而文體卑弱。穆修嘗欲變之矣，而才不乃及。至景祐間，歐陽修者出，深黜險譎，務趨平淡。曾鞏謂其醇深炳鬱，渾然天質；蘇軾謂修爲今之韓子，亦非過論也。然修初得韓文於故壁破簏之中，披閱校讎，至老不懈。雖未嘗規規追躡其故步，而體裁矩矱自成
translation_en:
…a vehicle for conveying the Way; what is called governance amounts merely to rules, rather than an extension of setting oneself right. Natural abilities may be receptive or obstructed, and application may be lax or thorough. Those who excel in one sphere may fall short in another; it is truly difficult to find someone who combines excellence in both. Let us consider Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu. Tang writing inherited the legacy of eight preceding dynasties, taking elaborate ornament and gorgeous diction as its sole standard of accomplishment, while its spirit had grown feeble. Chen Zi’ang once sought to change this, but his powers proved insufficient. During the Yuanhe reign period, Han Yu emerged, vigorously rejecting stale expressions and striving to emulate ancient compositions. Song Xiang described his writing as profound, expansive, grand, and deep, supporting and assisting the Six Classics. The official historian stated that Han Yu considered his own talent comparable to that of Sima Qian and Yang Xiong. These were surely no empty words. Yet while Sima Qian and Han Yu were indeed on a comparable level, Yang Xiong’s conception and phrasing were cramped, constrained, sluggish, and obscure. They did not match Han Yu’s freedom of composition, which required no laborious trimming to prescribed rules. Han Yu thus seems to have surpassed Yang Xiong.
Song writing inherited the legacy of the Five Dynasties, concerning itself exclusively with tonal patterns and parallel phrasing, while its literary style was low and weak. Mu Xiu once sought to change this, but his talent proved insufficient [?]. During the Jingyou reign period, Ouyang Xiu emerged, firmly rejecting strained and eccentric expression and striving for plainness and simplicity. Zeng Gong described his writing as pure and deep, brilliant and richly textured, an integral expression of natural gifts. Su Shi called Ouyang Xiu the Master Han of his own day; this too was no exaggerated judgment. Yet Ouyang Xiu first obtained Han Yu’s writings from a broken bamboo chest by an old wall. He read and collated them, never slackening even in old age. Although he never scrupulously retraced his predecessor’s steps, in literary form and standards he independently established…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一家則修於愈庶乎及之矣今考其遺文
愈之原道原性師說等篇發明天地人物
之理往往有前人所未發者程子所謂不
可漫觀者是已惜其因文見道而無格致
之學故以博愛爲仁則語用而遺體性有
三品則泝流而失源揆之以聖人之道不
能無牴牾焉修之本論易童子問詩本義
諸作發明古今名物之理往往有經傳所
未及者朱文公所謂平易說理者是已惜
===
其專意業文而無濂洛之學故以繫辭非
孔子之經周禮非周公所作揆之於聖人
之道不能無枘鑿焉愈性鯁直李逢吉皇
甫鎛輩深忌之晚爲裴度所知然卒不能
薦之於朝議者深爲之惜然觀其始論宮
市繼論佛骨刺潮州而以文行化俗使魏
博而以口舌解圍其見於樹立者卓有可
觀使唐果能相愈亦豈無所補乎修性狷
介彭思永蔣之奇輩屢譖之晚用韓琦之
punctuated:
一家，則修於愈庶乎及之矣。今考其遺文，愈之《原道》《原性》《師說》等篇，發明天地人物之理，往往有前人所未發者，程子所謂不可漫觀者是已。惜其因文見道，而無格致之學，故以博愛爲仁，則語用而遺體；性有三品，則泝流而失源。揆之以聖人之道，不能無牴牾焉。修之《本論》《易童子問》《詩本義》諸作，發明古今名物之理，往往有經傳所未及者，朱文公所謂平易說理者是已。惜其專意業文，而無濂洛之學，故以《繫辭》非孔子之經，《周禮》非周公所作。揆之於聖人之道，不能無枘鑿焉。

愈性鯁直，李逢吉、皇甫鎛輩深忌之。晚爲裴度所知，然卒不能薦之於朝，議者深爲之惜。然觀其始論宮市，繼論佛骨，刺潮州而以文行化俗，使魏博而以口舌解圍，其見於樹立者卓有可觀。使唐果能相愈，亦豈無所補乎？修性狷介，彭思永、蔣之奇輩屢譖之，晚用韓琦之
translation_en:
…a distinctive school of his own; thus Ouyang Xiu came close to matching Han Yu. Now, examining their surviving writings, Han Yu’s essays such as An Inquiry into the Way, An Inquiry into Human Nature, and On Teachers elucidate the principles of Heaven, Earth, human beings, and things, often revealing what earlier writers had left unexplained. These are what Master Cheng meant when he said they must not be read casually. Regrettably, Han Yu perceived the Way through literary composition but lacked the learning of investigating things and extending knowledge. Thus, in defining benevolence as universal love, he spoke of its function while omitting its substance; in dividing human nature into three grades, he traced the current but lost sight of its source. Measured against the Way of the sages, his views cannot be free of contradictions. Ouyang Xiu’s works, including Discourse on Fundamentals, A Boy’s Questions on the Changes, and The Original Meaning of the Odes, elucidate the principles underlying names and things past and present, often addressing matters beyond the scope of the classics and their commentaries. These are what Master Zhu, posthumously titled Wengong, meant by explaining principles plainly and accessibly. Regrettably, Ouyang Xiu devoted himself exclusively to literary composition and lacked the learning of the Lian and Luo schools. Thus he held that the Appended Statements was not a canonical text by Confucius and that the Rites of Zhou was not written by the Duke of Zhou. Measured against the Way of the sages, his views cannot be free of discrepancies, like tenons and mortises that do not fit.

Han Yu was upright and outspoken by nature, and men such as Li Fengji and Huangfu Bo deeply resented him. Late in life he gained Pei Du’s recognition, yet Pei ultimately failed to recommend him to the court, a circumstance commentators have greatly regretted on his behalf. Yet consider how he first remonstrated against palace purchasing and then against the Buddha’s bone; how, as prefect of Chaozhou, he transformed local customs through his writings and conduct; and how, as an envoy to Weibo, he resolved a siege through persuasion. His concrete accomplishments were outstanding and worthy of admiration. Had the Tang indeed been able to make Han Yu chief councilor, could he have failed to contribute? Ouyang Xiu was uncompromising and principled by nature, and men such as Peng Siyong and Jiang Zhiqi repeatedly slandered him. Late in life, through Han Qi’s …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
薦而與同登政府不可謂之不遇及觀其
遺司諫之書進朋黨之論議麟州之屯田
阻六塔之河道其見於建白者綽有可紀
則修之用於宋亦可謂無負矣然要其所
至則愈以文章名於唐而身繫安危如裴
度者終非愈之所優修以文章名於宋而
功在社稷如韓琦者每爲修之所服則天
下後世之公論不可誣矣愚生幸際
明時思樂泮水固將假文字以進身而欲效
===
其所欲爲者也其於韓歐二子未敢以爲
終身之地而於商之伊尹周之吉甫竊有
志焉執事幸毋以爲僭
第四問
蕭汝爲
同考試官教諭顧批粤中風俗人才評品精覈
而篇末數語尤精采動人非積學之士不能也
同考試官教諭閔批此策條答詳明措辭清雅篇
終又含蓄感慨不盡之意蓋尚友古人者也錄之以考其後
punctuated:
薦，而與同登政府，不可謂之不遇。及觀其遺司諫之書、進朋黨之論、議麟州之屯田、阻六塔之河道，其見於建白者，綽有可紀，則修之用於宋，亦可謂無負矣。然要其所至，則愈以文章名於唐，而身繫安危如裴度者，終非愈之所優；修以文章名於宋，而功在社稷如韓琦者，每爲修之所服，則天下後世之公論不可誣矣。愚生幸際明時，思樂泮水，固將假文字以進身，而欲效其所欲爲者也。其於韓歐二子，未敢以爲終身之地，而於商之伊尹、周之吉甫，竊有志焉。執事幸毋以爲僭。

第四問
蕭汝爲

同考試官教諭顧批：粤中風俗人才，評品精覈，而篇末數語，尤精采動人，非積學之士不能也。

同考試官教諭閔批：此策條答詳明，措辭清雅，篇終又含蓄感慨不盡之意，蓋尚友古人者也。錄之以考其後。
translation_en:
…recommendation, and entered the chief council together with him; one cannot say that Ouyang Xiu lacked recognition. When we examine his letter to the Remonstrator of the Right, his submitted discourse on factions, his discussion of agricultural garrisons in Linzhou, and his opposition to the river channel at Liuta, there is ample worth recording in his proposals to the throne. Thus it may also be said that Xiu did not betray the trust placed in him by the Song. Yet, assessing their ultimate achievements, Han Yu won fame in the Tang through his writing, but being a man upon whom the state's security depended, as Pei Du was, was never his particular strength. Xiu won fame in the Song through his writing, but he repeatedly acknowledged his admiration for men such as Han Qi, whose achievements sustained the state. The impartial judgment of the world and of later generations cannot be gainsaid.

I, an unworthy student, have fortunately encountered an enlightened age and delight in the waters of the school pool. Certainly I intend to advance through literary accomplishment, seeking to put my aspirations into practice. As for Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu, I would not presume to take their attainments as the ultimate goal of my life; rather, I privately aspire to emulate Yi Yin of the Shang and Jifu of the Zhou. May you, honored sir, not consider this presumptuous.

Fourth Question
Xiao Ruwei

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: His assessment of Guangdong's customs and talented men is precise and discriminating. The final few sentences are particularly brilliant and moving. Only a scholar of accumulated learning could accomplish this.

Comment by Associate Examiner Min, Instructor: This policy essay answers each point fully and clearly, with lucid and elegant wording. Its conclusion also conveys restrained but inexhaustible feelings of reflection and concern. He is surely one who seeks fellowship with the men of antiquity. I select this essay so that his subsequent progress may be assessed.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正何批博雅之才具見此策嶺南
佳士吾當於子拭目
考試官教授劉批辭嚴義正深得儒先探本
之意是用錄出
對風俗因地而異同知有以變之則無不
可同之地賢才因時而盛衰知有以興之
則無不可盛之時蓋風俗賢才固未可以
地與時論也亦在變之興之何如耳有化
導之方有轉移之術培植之旣固漸摩之
===
旣久則異可同衰可盛自有不言而化之
妙此其機也而神其機者固執事所謂存
乎其人也傳曰爲政在人經曰遐不作人
其有見於此歟敢摭其說以對風俗不以
人而變乎何東郊頑民乃卒化於三后協
心之日賢才不以人而興乎何孔門諸賢
乃並起於東魯洙泗之鄉是必有故矣今
之東廣古南粤地也而廣州等十府卽漢
交州所部南海等郡是已其地多民夷雜
punctuated:
考試官學正何批：博雅之才，具見此策。嶺南佳士，吾當於子拭目。

考試官教授劉批：辭嚴義正，深得儒先探本之意，是用錄出。

對：風俗因地而異同，知有以變之，則無不可同之地；賢才因時而盛衰，知有以興之，則無不可盛之時。蓋風俗賢才，固未可以地與時論也，亦在變之興之何如耳。有化導之方，有轉移之術，培植之旣固，漸摩之旣久，則異可同，衰可盛，自有不言而化之妙。此其機也，而神其機者，固執事所謂存乎其人也。傳曰：「爲政在人。」經曰：「遐不作人。」其有見於此歟？敢摭其說以對。風俗不以人而變乎？何東郊頑民乃卒化於三后協心之日？賢才不以人而興乎？何孔門諸賢乃並起於東魯洙泗之鄉？是必有故矣。今之東廣，古南粤地也，而廣州等十府，卽漢交州所部南海等郡是已。其地多民夷雜
translation_en:
Examiner He, School Instructor, comments: “Broad learning and cultivated talent are fully evident in this policy essay. Among the worthy scholars of Lingnan, you are one whose progress I shall watch with keen anticipation.”

Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “The language is solemn and the principles correct. It deeply grasps the intention of earlier Confucian scholars to investigate fundamentals; for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”

Response: Customs differ or resemble one another according to place. If one knows how to transform them, there is no place where they cannot be brought into accord. Worthy talent flourishes or declines according to the times. If one knows how to foster it, there is no time when it cannot flourish. Indeed, customs and worthy talent cannot be judged solely in terms of place and time; everything also depends upon how they are transformed and fostered. With methods of moral guidance and means of effecting change, once cultivation is firmly established and gradual nurturing has continued long enough, differences can be brought into accord and decline turned into flourishing. Then the subtle efficacy of transformation without words will naturally emerge. This is the pivotal mechanism; and what gives it its wondrous efficacy is precisely what you, honored examiners, mean by saying that it depends upon the person. The commentary says, “The conduct of government depends upon men.” The classic says, “Why not nurture men?” Do these words not reflect an understanding of this? I venture to draw upon their meaning in my response.

Are customs not transformed through human agency? Why, then, were the stubborn people of the eastern outskirts finally transformed when the three sovereigns acted with one heart? Is worthy talent not fostered through human agency? Why, then, did the worthies of Confucius’s school arise together in eastern Lu, in the region of the Zhu and Si rivers? There must surely be a reason for this.

Present-day eastern Guang is the territory of ancient Nanyue. Its ten prefectures, including Guangzhou, correspond to Nanhai and the other commanderies under the jurisdiction of Jiaozhou in the Han dynasty. In this territory, commoners and non-Han peoples largely intermingle…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
處其風俗不同自其變者言之廣之俗則
質直尚信韶之俗則淳樸愿愨惠之俗則
文物有加焉若他郡之美具載圖誌固不
得而盡述也自其未變者言之如信巫淫
祀喪用樂之類雖當
聖朝誕敷文德之時鄉士夫固敦尚名教矣其
比閭族黨之間深山邊海之區亦或有不
免者其故何哉以變之無其人耳使如執
事所謂常衮文翁者置為長民之吏則變
===
而通之革而信之尚何風俗之不與化推
移耶昔韓愈之治潮州也師延趙德潮人
化之遂篤於文行張紘之治雷州也禮明
宗子雷人化之悉更其舊習執是而徵諸
常衮文翁蓋先後一揆焉嗚呼先民不作
遺矩猶存安得若人者而為風俗之指南
哉其地多山川靈秀其人才間出自其賢
者觀之在漢則有若董正之高潔在唐則
有若張九齡之相業在宋則有若余靖之
punctuated: 處，其風俗不同。自其變者言之，廣之俗則質直尚信，韶之俗則淳樸愿愨，惠之俗則文物有加焉。若他郡之美，具載圖誌，固不得而盡述也。自其未變者言之，如信巫淫祀、喪用樂之類，雖當聖朝誕敷文德之時，鄉士夫固敦尚名教矣，其比閭族黨之間、深山邊海之區，亦或有不免者。其故何哉？以變之無其人耳。使如執事所謂常衮、文翁者，置為長民之吏，則變而通之，革而信之，尚何風俗之不與化推移耶？昔韓愈之治潮州也，師延趙德，潮人化之，遂篤於文行；張紘之治雷州也，禮明宗子，雷人化之，悉更其舊習。執是而徵諸常衮、文翁，蓋先後一揆焉。嗚呼！先民不作，遺矩猶存，安得若人者而為風俗之指南哉？其地多山川靈秀，其人才間出。自其賢者觀之，在漢則有若董正之高潔，在唐則有若張九齡之相業，在宋則有若余靖之
translation_en:
…live together, and their customs differ. Speaking of those customs that have been transformed, the people of Guangzhou are straightforward and value trustworthiness; those of Shaozhou are simple, sincere, and honest; and those of Huizhou excel still further in cultural accomplishments. The admirable qualities of the other prefectures are fully recorded in maps and gazetteers and cannot all be recounted here. Speaking of customs that remain unchanged, there are such practices as trusting shamans, offering improper sacrifices, and using music at funerals. Although this is an age when the sagely dynasty broadly extends its civilizing virtue, and the local gentlemen certainly esteem and uphold orthodox moral teachings, some among the neighborhood and lineage communities, and in the remote mountains and coastal districts, may still be unable to avoid these practices. Why is this? Simply because there are no suitable men to transform them. If men like Chang Gun and Wen Weng, whom you have mentioned, were appointed as officials governing the people, they would transform customs and make them workable, reform them and win people's trust. What customs, then, would fail to change along with this civilizing influence?

Formerly, when Han Yu governed Chaozhou, he invited Zhao De to serve as a teacher. The people of Chaozhou were transformed by his influence and became devoted to literary learning and moral conduct. When Zhang Hong governed Leizhou, he treated Ming Zongzi with honor [?]; the people of Leizhou were transformed by his influence and entirely changed their former habits. If we compare these examples with Chang Gun and Wen Weng, the earlier and later cases follow the same principle. Alas! Those worthy predecessors will not rise again, but the standards they left behind still survive. Where can we find such men to serve as guides for popular customs?

This land has many mountains and rivers endowed with numinous beauty, and talented men emerge from time to time. Looking at its worthy men, under the Han there was the lofty integrity of Dong Zheng; under the Tang, the achievements of Zhang Jiuling as chief minister; and under the Song, there was Yu Jing's…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
邊功焉其事行之詳具載史傳亦不得而
槩舉也自其賢而繼出者觀之如關敏鄧
顒陳鼎之輩正值
聖朝開國承家之日關敏固闔門死忠矣而鄧
顒委身濟難之烈陳鼎蹇諤不阿之行是
皆人所難者其故何哉以興之有其人耳
誠如執事所謂董逸民張文獻者首開南
粤之荒則高山仰止景行行止尚何賢才
之不項背相望耶昔言偃載道而南至宋
===
范仲淹諸賢輩出而吳遂爲文物之望陳
良游學於北至宋周茂叔大儒特起而楚
遂爲道學之邦執是而徵之董正九齡蓋
古今一律焉嗚呼不有先覺孰開我人安
得數公者而爲人物之標的哉愚也仰往
哲之孤高悼末俗之簡陋而欲振衣於千
仞之崗久矣倘與其進吾將過闕里而弔
古循東郊而問俗不知尚有往日其人否
乎謹對
punctuated:
邊功焉。其事行之詳，具載史傳，亦不得而槩舉也。自其賢而繼出者觀之，如關敏、鄧顒、陳鼎之輩，正值聖朝開國承家之日。關敏固闔門死忠矣，而鄧顒委身濟難之烈、陳鼎蹇諤不阿之行，是皆人所難者，其故何哉？以興之有其人耳。誠如執事所謂董逸民、張文獻者，首開南粤之荒，則高山仰止，景行行止，尚何賢才之不項背相望耶？昔言偃載道而南，至宋范仲淹諸賢輩出，而吳遂爲文物之望；陳良游學於北，至宋周茂叔大儒特起，而楚遂爲道學之邦。執是而徵之董正、九齡，蓋古今一律焉。
嗚呼！不有先覺，孰開我人？安得數公者而爲人物之標的哉？愚也仰往哲之孤高，悼末俗之簡陋，而欲振衣於千仞之崗久矣。倘與其進，吾將過闕里而弔古，循東郊而問俗，不知尚有往日其人否乎？謹對。
translation_en:
…achievements on the frontier. The details of their deeds and conduct are fully recorded in histories and biographies; I cannot enumerate even their broad outlines here. Looking at the worthy men who followed them, such figures as Guan Min, Deng Yong, and Chen Ding lived precisely when our sagely dynasty was founding its state and establishing its ruling house. Guan Min and his entire household indeed died in loyalty; Deng Yong’s heroic devotion in overcoming calamity and Chen Ding’s forthright, unyielding conduct were likewise things difficult for anyone to achieve. Why was this so? Simply because there were men to inspire them. As you, honored examiner, have indeed said, Dong the Recluse and Zhang Wenxian first opened up the uncultivated southland of Yue. Thus, “We look up to the lofty mountain; we travel along the great road.” How, then, could worthy talents fail to follow one another in close succession? Long ago, Yan Yan carried the Way southward; by the Song, Fan Zhongyan and other worthies emerged in succession, and Wu consequently became a renowned center of cultural achievement. Chen Liang traveled north to study; by the Song, the great Confucian Zhou Maoshu arose in distinction, and Chu consequently became a land of Learning of the Way. Applying these examples to Dong Zheng and Zhang Jiuling, we find the same pattern in ancient and later times.
Alas! Without those who awaken first, who would enlighten us? Where might we find men like these gentlemen to serve as models for others? In my humble ignorance, I admire the solitary eminence of past sages and lament the crudeness of the customs of this declining age. I have long wished to shake out my robes upon a ridge a thousand ren high. If you favor my advancement, I shall visit Queli to pay homage to antiquity and travel through the eastern suburbs to inquire into local customs. I wonder whether men like those of former days may still be found there. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第五問
潘濂
同考試官訓導陳批時務一策正欲觀士子識
見何如此荅考究得實處置有方决非迂腐之士也
同考試官訓導楊批論馭兵卹民二事援古證今
卓有所見所謂識時務者在俊傑子足當之矣
考試官學正何批議處時事俱合機宜足見
學識
考試官敎授劉批論時事有根據有識見
===
凡士哉
天下之事所以防其患者在有其道所以
任其責者在得其人夫法敝而爲之立患
生而爲之防此理也亦勢也然非得人以
任之則膠膠擾擾紛變於吾前者日不知
其幾而天下之事始多矣自今觀之民惟
邦本本固邦寧民不可以不卹也天下雖
安忘戰則危兵不可以不馭也今之談者
動曰卹民在守令而難其人馭兵在將帥
punctuated:
第五問
潘濂
同考試官訓導陳批：時務一策，正欲觀士子識見何如。此荅考究得實，處置有方，决非迂腐之士也。
同考試官訓導楊批：論馭兵卹民二事，援古證今，卓有所見。所謂識時務者在俊傑，子足當之矣。
考試官學正何批：議處時事，俱合機宜，足見學識。
考試官敎授劉批：論時事，有根據，有識見，凡士哉！
天下之事，所以防其患者，在有其道；所以任其責者，在得其人。夫法敝而爲之立，患生而爲之防，此理也，亦勢也。然非得人以任之，則膠膠擾擾、紛變於吾前者，日不知其幾，而天下之事始多矣。自今觀之，民惟邦本，本固邦寧，民不可以不卹也；天下雖安，忘戰則危，兵不可以不馭也。今之談者動曰：卹民在守令，而難其人；馭兵在將帥
translation_en:
Fifth Question
Pan Lian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: This policy question on current affairs was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ discernment. This answer investigates the facts thoroughly and proposes well-considered measures. Its author is certainly no pedantic scholar.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: In discussing the two matters of controlling troops and caring for the people, he invokes antiquity to substantiate his arguments about the present and displays outstanding insight. As the saying goes, those who understand the affairs of their times are men of exceptional talent. You fully deserve that description.

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: His proposed handling of current affairs accords throughout with the requirements of the circumstances and amply demonstrates his learning and discernment.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: His discussion of current affairs is well grounded and discerning. An ordinary scholar indeed [?]!

In the affairs of the realm, preventing troubles depends on having the proper methods; entrusting responsibility depends on obtaining the right people. When laws become defective, laws must be established; when troubles arise, safeguards must be devised. This is both a matter of principle and a necessity imposed by circumstances. Yet unless the right people are found to take responsibility, countless disturbances and tangled changes will unfold before us each day, and the realm’s affairs will become increasingly troublesome. Looking at the present situation: the people alone are the foundation of the state; when that foundation is firm, the state is at peace. Thus the people must be cared for. Though the realm may be at peace, forgetting warfare brings danger. Thus troops must be kept under control. Those who discuss these matters today readily say: caring for the people rests with prefects and magistrates, but suitable men are difficult to find; controlling troops rests with commanders …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而難其人此非天下之通論也天生一世
之材自足以效一世之用顧在任之何如
爾載觀古之人孝武窮征遠討海内虚耗
而東方朔進薄其賦歛之言德宗剛愎自
任藩鎮離心而陸贄獻輕稅薄征之諫元
氣欲惜賦歛當輕此胡安國上時政之忠
議也紀綱欲立民力湏寬此朱熹應直言
之正論也是數君子其知國之所恃在民
民之所恃在守令者乎趙充國以四萬騎
===
屯沿邊九郡而單于引去李德裕以十一
軍控制西北二邊而南詔請還監俘州郡
脩治器械而虜人遠遁此馬知節之謀略
可嘉也閱延州兵日夜訓練而敵人相戒
此范仲淹之威望可畏也是數君子其知
民之所衞在兵兵之所馭在將帥者乎方
今
皇風清穆海宇輯寧干戈積府庫之塵閭里興
載芟之頌太平之治復見於
punctuated:
而難其人，此非天下之通論也。天生一世之材，自足以效一世之用，顧在任之何如爾。載觀古之人，孝武窮征遠討，海内虚耗，而東方朔進薄其賦歛之言；德宗剛愎自任，藩鎮離心，而陸贄獻輕稅薄征之諫。元氣欲惜，賦歛當輕，此胡安國上時政之忠議也；紀綱欲立，民力湏寬，此朱熹應直言之正論也。是數君子，其知國之所恃在民，民之所恃在守令者乎？趙充國以四萬騎屯沿邊九郡，而單于引去；李德裕以十一軍控制西北二邊，而南詔請還監俘；州郡脩治器械，而虜人遠遁，此馬知節之謀略可嘉也；閱延州兵，日夜訓練，而敵人相戒，此范仲淹之威望可畏也。是數君子，其知民之所衞在兵，兵之所馭在將帥者乎？

方今皇風清穆，海宇輯寧，干戈積府庫之塵，閭里興《載芟》之頌，太平之治復見於
translation_en:
…and that suitable men are hard to find. This is no sound general judgment of the affairs of the realm. The talent Heaven produces in any age is sufficient to meet that age’s needs; it depends only on how that talent is employed. Consider further the men of antiquity. When Emperor Xiaowu exhausted his forces in distant campaigns and depleted the resources of the realm, Dongfang Shuo urged him to reduce taxation. When Emperor Dezong stubbornly trusted his own judgment and the regional military commands grew estranged, Lu Zhi remonstrated with him to lighten taxes and levies. To preserve the state’s vital energies, taxation must be light: this was Hu Anguo’s loyal counsel in his submission on current government. To establish sound governing principles and discipline, the burdens on the people’s strength must be eased: this was Zhu Xi’s upright argument in response to a call for frank advice. Did not these gentlemen understand that the state depends upon the people, and that the people depend upon prefects and county magistrates?

Zhao Chongguo stationed forty thousand cavalrymen in nine frontier commanderies, and the chanyu withdrew. Li Deyu used eleven armies to control the western and northern frontiers, and Nanzhao requested permission to return captives [?]. When the prefectures and commanderies put their weapons and equipment in good order, the enemy fled far away: Ma Zhijie’s strategy in this deserves praise. When the troops at Yanzhou were inspected and trained day and night, the enemy warned one another to be on guard: Fan Zhongyan’s prestige in this inspired awe. Did not these gentlemen understand that the people are protected by soldiers, and that soldiers are controlled by their commanders?

Today, imperial influence is pure and harmonious, and all within the seas is at peace. Shields and spears gather dust in the arsenals, while the villages raise songs of praise like “They Cleared Away the Grass” (Zai shan). An age of great peace is seen once more in…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今日矣往年湖湘歲歉致厪
當宁之憂於是竭府庫停起運而所以賑卹
吾民者至矣執事猶懷意外之患而以諸
路水旱爲慮愚以爲人君有憂勤惕厲之
心自足以感召和氣固無是矣萬一有之
則古人救荒之政具在或發倉廩以賑乏
或爲粥溢以救殍或興工作以聚失業或
弛刑禁以釋無辜罷不急之務去無名之
征募商糶粟可行也諸路借運可行也何
===
患救荒之無其策哉近時襄漢有警致煩
宵旰之憂於是調土兵募民兵而所以捍衞
吾民者至矣執事猶抱意外之虞而以他
處盜賊繼起爲念愚以爲人君有神武不
殺之威自足以戡定禍亂固無是矣萬一
有之則古人禦寇之法具在先加威武以
懾其心次示招安以弛其計多方間諜擣
虛攻盈居則謹烽堠出則禁侵掠賊勢少
緩則一路之兵可捍禦也賊勢衆大則諸
punctuated:
今日矣。往年湖湘歲歉，致厪當宁之憂，於是竭府庫，停起運，而所以賑卹吾民者至矣。執事猶懷意外之患，而以諸路水旱爲慮。愚以爲人君有憂勤惕厲之心，自足以感召和氣，固無是矣。萬一有之，則古人救荒之政具在：或發倉廩以賑乏，或爲粥溢以救殍，或興工作以聚失業，或弛刑禁以釋無辜。罷不急之務，去無名之征，募商糶粟可行也，諸路借運可行也，何患救荒之無其策哉？
近時襄漢有警，致煩宵旰之憂，於是調土兵，募民兵，而所以捍衞吾民者至矣。執事猶抱意外之虞，而以他處盜賊繼起爲念。愚以爲人君有神武不殺之威，自足以戡定禍亂，固無是矣。萬一有之，則古人禦寇之法具在：先加威武以懾其心，次示招安以弛其計，多方間諜，擣虛攻盈，居則謹烽堠，出則禁侵掠。賊勢少緩，則一路之兵可捍禦也；賊勢衆大，則諸
translation_en:
…today. In past years, poor harvests in Huxiang caused His Majesty concern. The treasury and granaries were accordingly emptied, and scheduled shipments of revenue were suspended: the measures taken to relieve our people were most thorough. Yet you, honored examiners, remain apprehensive of unforeseen troubles and concerned about floods and droughts in the various circuits. In my humble view, when a ruler is concerned, diligent, vigilant, and earnest, this alone suffices to summon harmonious influences; such disasters should surely not occur. Should they nevertheless occur, the famine-relief measures of the ancients are all available: opening granaries to relieve the needy, preparing gruel [?] to save those dying of hunger, undertaking public works to gather those deprived of their livelihoods, or relaxing penal prohibitions to release the innocent. Suspend nonessential undertakings and abolish unjustified levies. Recruiting merchants to sell grain is practicable, as is borrowing supplies from the various circuits and transporting them. Why fear that there is no policy for relieving famine?
Recently, alarms in the Xianghan region troubled His Majesty, keeping him awake before dawn and delaying his meals until late. Indigenous troops were accordingly mobilized and civilian militia recruited: the measures taken to defend our people were most thorough. Yet you remain apprehensive of unforeseen dangers and concerned that bandits elsewhere may rise in succession. In my humble view, when a ruler possesses the awe-inspiring authority of divine martial prowess without killing, this alone suffices to quell calamity and disorder; such troubles should surely not occur. Should they nevertheless occur, the methods of the ancients for resisting bandits are all available: first exert military might to strike fear into their hearts, then offer amnesty and submission to weaken their resolve; employ spies through many channels, strike where they are undefended, and attack where their forces are concentrated. When stationed, maintain vigilant beacon posts; when marching out, prohibit encroachment and plunder. If the pressure from the bandits abates somewhat, the troops of a single circuit can hold them off; if the bandits are numerous and powerful, then the various…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
路之兵可召集也孰謂禦寇之無其略哉
雖然此特其法爾而所以行夫法者顧在
於得人耳先儒謂斯民之休戚係守令之
賢否方今天下民力之匱竭不但湖湘爲
然也若郡縣之守令果得人如召信臣之
在南陽爲民興利而躬勸農桑卓茂之在
密邑勞心撫字而視民如子賈琮之在交
趾蠲復傜役而謳歌四起則必有以培植
乎元氣而黎民享其安矣先儒謂天下無
===
必勝之兵而有不可敗之將方今天下軍
士之消耗不但襄漢爲然也若邊陲之將
帥果得人如郭子儀之屯涇陽馭下以恕
而將士樂用李光弼之代朔方號令精明
而人心自服曹彬監征蜀之軍申令戢下
而所在秋毫無犯則必有以振揚乎威武
而軍士樂於用矣然守令之賢否將帥之
勇怯則又在乎
朝廷愼選作興何如耳此廟堂密勿之至計
punctuated:
路之兵可召集也。孰謂禦寇之無其略哉？雖然，此特其法爾，而所以行夫法者，顧在於得人耳。先儒謂：「斯民之休戚，係守令之賢否。」方今天下民力之匱竭，不但湖湘爲然也。若郡縣之守令果得人，如召信臣之在南陽，爲民興利而躬勸農桑；卓茂之在密邑，勞心撫字而視民如子；賈琮之在交趾，蠲復傜役而謳歌四起，則必有以培植乎元氣，而黎民享其安矣。

先儒謂：「天下無必勝之兵，而有不可敗之將。」方今天下軍士之消耗，不但襄漢爲然也。若邊陲之將帥果得人，如郭子儀之屯涇陽，馭下以恕而將士樂用；李光弼之代朔方，號令精明而人心自服；曹彬監征蜀之軍，申令戢下而所在秋毫無犯，則必有以振揚乎威武，而軍士樂於用矣。然守令之賢否、將帥之勇怯，則又在乎朝廷愼選作興何如耳。此廟堂密勿之至計，
translation_en:
…the troops of the various routes can be summoned and assembled. Who could say that there is no strategy for resisting bandits? Yet these are merely methods; putting them into practice depends upon obtaining the right men. Earlier Confucian scholars said: “The well-being or suffering of these people depends upon whether their prefects and magistrates are worthy.” Today, the exhaustion of the people’s resources throughout the realm is by no means confined to Huxiang. If truly suitable men were appointed as prefects and magistrates, they would be like Shao Xinchen in Nanyang, who promoted measures benefiting the people and personally encouraged farming and sericulture; Zhuo Mao in Mi, who devoted himself to caring for the people and treated them as his children; or Jia Cong in Jiaozhi, who remitted corvée obligations, so that songs of praise arose on every side. They would surely find ways to nurture the fundamental vitality of the realm, and the common people would enjoy peace.

Earlier Confucian scholars said: “There are no armies in the world certain of victory, but there are generals who cannot be defeated.” Today, the depletion of military manpower throughout the realm is by no means confined to Xianghan. If truly suitable men were appointed as frontier commanders, they would be like Guo Ziyi when stationed at Jingyang, who governed his subordinates with forbearance, so that officers and soldiers served willingly; Li Guangbi when he took over command at Shuofang, whose orders were precise and clear, so that men submitted of their own accord; or Cao Bin, who supervised the army campaigning against Shu, reiterated his orders, and restrained his subordinates, so that wherever they went they did not encroach upon even a hair’s breadth of the people’s property. They would surely find ways to revive military might, and the soldiers would serve willingly. Yet whether prefects and magistrates are worthy or unworthy, and commanders brave or cowardly, depends in turn upon how carefully the court selects them and encourages their efforts. This is a matter for the court’s most painstaking and confidential deliberation…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下經久之遠圖顧草茅賤士何足以語
此然竊有志焉惟執事進敎之可也
punctuated: 天下經久之遠圖。顧草茅賤士，何足以語此？然竊有志焉，惟執事進敎之可也。
translation_en: …a far-reaching plan for the enduring stability of the realm. Yet how could a humble scholar outside official service such as myself be qualified to speak of this? Still, I privately aspire to this end, and ask only that you, honored examiners, offer me further instruction.

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
我
太祖高皇帝奄有天下之初規畫庶
務而於設科取士則尤加之意
焉是故三載一舉行之其制大
備于洪武甲子條貫截然著為
令典歷世守之而無敝也迺今
===
正德庚午適當天下鄉試之期
洽膺聘而来濫竽取士之柄事
既竣刻士之邑里名氏并文之
粹者與夫内外執事之職名為
鄉試錄將獻諸
天子傳之天下洽竊序其後曰惟天
生賢與賢之用世要皆非偶然
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

我太祖高皇帝奄有天下之初，規畫庶務，而於設科取士，則尤加之意焉。是故三載一舉行之，其制大備于洪武甲子，條貫截然，著為令典，歷世守之而無敝也。迺今正德庚午，適當天下鄉試之期，洽膺聘而来，濫竽取士之柄。事既竣，刻士之邑里名氏，并文之粹者，與夫内外執事之職名，為鄉試錄，將獻諸天子，傳之天下。洽竊序其後曰：「惟天生賢，與賢之用世，要皆非偶然
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

When our Emperor Taizu Gao first came into possession of all under Heaven, he planned the many affairs of government, giving particular attention to establishing examinations for selecting men of talent. These were therefore held once every three years. The system became fully developed in the jiazi year of the Hongwu reign (1384), with clearly defined regulations embodied in authoritative statutes. Successive generations have observed them without ill effect.

Now, in the gengwu year of the Zhengde reign (1510), when the time arrived for Provincial Examinations throughout the realm, I, Qia, came in response to an invitation and, unworthily occupying my position, assumed responsibility for selecting men of talent. Once the work was completed, the candidates’ home localities and names, together with the finest of their compositions and the titles and names of officials serving inside and outside the examination compound, were engraved for printing as the Record of the Provincial Examination. It is to be presented to the Son of Heaven and circulated throughout the realm. I, Qia, venture to append this postface: “Heaven’s bringing forth worthy men, and worthy men’s entering the service of the world, are, in essence, never matters of chance …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者東廣古南粵地也歷秦與漢
土地開拓積數百年而文獻張
公出焉東南文運藉是一倡自
夫辨邪之智識事君之忠藎當
時人物卒難並埒又積數百年
而忠襄余公出焉其文章尚矣
在朝也著蹇諤之風在邕州也
===
收經營之績至今人誦之不已
要之天有意於二公故其出而
用世也如此夫豈偶然者哉矧
我
國家
聖聖相承道化浹洽天心克眷畀以
才賢宜乎數十年来賢人君子
punctuated: 者。東廣，古南粵地也。歷秦與漢，土地開拓，積數百年，而文獻張公出焉。東南文運，藉是一倡。自夫辨邪之智識、事君之忠藎，當時人物卒難並埒。又積數百年，而忠襄余公出焉。其文章尚矣；在朝也，著蹇諤之風；在邕州也，收經營之績。至今人誦之不已。要之，天有意於二公，故其出而用世也如此，夫豈偶然者哉？矧我國家，聖聖相承，道化浹洽，天心克眷，畀以才賢。宜乎數十年來，賢人君子
translation_en: …were no mere accidents. Eastern Guangdong was the land of ancient Nanyue. Through the Qin and Han dynasties, its territory was opened up and extended; after several hundred years, Lord Zhang, posthumously titled Wenxian, emerged there. Through him, the literary fortunes of the southeast received their first great impetus. As for his discernment in distinguishing the wicked and his devoted loyalty in serving his sovereign, the figures of his day could scarcely equal him. After several hundred more years, Lord Yu, posthumously titled Zhongxiang, emerged there. His literary accomplishments were outstanding; at court, he became known for forthright remonstrance, and in Yongzhou, he achieved success in administering affairs. To this day, people never cease praising him. In essence, Heaven had a purpose for these two men; hence their emergence and service to the world took this form. How could these have been mere accidents? How much more is this true of our dynasty! Sage sovereign has succeeded sage sovereign, the transforming influence of the Way has spread everywhere, and Heaven has shown its favor by bestowing talented and worthy men. It is fitting, then, that over the past several decades, worthy men and gentlemen…

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以文章魁天下類是者恒多夷
考其政事叅預舘閣職司臺諫
者足以羽儀乎
天朝布列方嶽分牧郡縣者又足以
鎭重乎外服故嘗論天下士必
先焉論科目得人而莫敢少焉
諸士子獲取於是矣行將角天
===
下士則夫奉
廷對服官序實昉於此將何以為
之地耶必曰不徒以文章為也
行檢其郛郭不徒以政事為也
學術其基本近師之今之前輩
是也遠師之文獻忠襄公是也
等而上之則雖伊傅周召亦吾
punctuated: 以文章魁天下，類是者恒多。夷考其政事，叅預舘閣、職司臺諫者，足以羽儀乎天朝；布列方嶽、分牧郡縣者，又足以鎭重乎外服。故嘗論天下士，必先焉；論科目得人，而莫敢少焉。諸士子獲取於是矣，行將角天下士，則夫奉廷對、服官序，實昉於此，將何以為之地耶？必曰：不徒以文章為也，行檢其郛郭；不徒以政事為也，學術其基本。近師之，今之前輩是也；遠師之，文獻、忠襄公是也。等而上之，則雖伊、傅、周、召，亦吾
translation_en:
… have led the realm in literary accomplishment; men of this kind have always been numerous. On examining their achievements in government, those serving in the academies and literary offices, or holding posts as censors and remonstrance officials, have brought distinction to the imperial court; those stationed throughout the provinces or governing prefectures and counties have lent stability and dignity to the territories beyond the capital. Thus, whenever discussing the scholars of the realm, I have given these men precedence; when discussing the examination system’s success in obtaining worthy men, none dares disparage them.

You scholars have now been selected here and will soon compete with scholars from throughout the realm. Answering questions at court and entering the ranks of official service truly begin here. What, then, will you lay as your foundation? Surely the answer must be: literary accomplishment alone will not suffice; disciplined conduct must be your enclosing walls. Administrative achievement alone will not suffice; learning must be your foundation. For models close to your own time, there are the senior men of today; for models from further back, there are Lords Wenxian and Zhongxiang. Ascending still higher, even Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao would be my …

title: 正德五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
儔匹爾烏可以多讓哉使畫於
一得沾沾然自喜而不知所以
求進焉則天之生賢何如國家
之取士何如乃以是而自處哉
其為科目之玷也固矣洽用是
以相告云
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正
===
何洽謹序
punctuated:
儔匹爾，烏可以多讓哉！使畫於一得，沾沾然自喜，而不知所以求進焉，則天之生賢何如？國家之取士何如？乃以是而自處哉！其為科目之玷也固矣。洽用是以相告云。
山東東昌府臨清州儒學學正何洽謹序。
translation_en:
…peers—how could one concede much to them! If one confines oneself to a single achievement, smugly delights in it, and does not know how to seek further progress, then what becomes of Heaven’s purpose in bringing forth worthy men? What becomes of the state’s purpose in selecting scholars? How could one be content with such a position! Such a person would assuredly be a blemish upon the examination system. I, Qia, therefore offer these words to you all.
Preface respectfully composed by He Qia, Instructor of the Confucian School of Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
